title: Write the sandbox threat model and security design doc (GATE)
description:
Nothing else in the sandbox track may start until this is written and reviewed. The user explicitly asked for code execution to be carefully examined security-wise.

Must cover, concretely:
- Why in-process execution is unacceptable: chat-backend runs as ROOT (suite docs/project-spec.md:362 - it raises ulimit and owns root-owned chat-data PVC files), and ENABLE_SCRIPT_EXECUTION is false in production today. sandbox_tools.py:21 _ALLOWED_ENV_KEYS is an allow-list precisely because a deny-list previously leaked INTERNAL_API_SECRET.
- Isolation boundary: separate pod, non-root, read-only rootfs, drop ALL capabilities, RuntimeDefault or stricter seccomp, no shell, gVisor/sandboxed-node evaluation, memory/CPU/pid limits, wall-clock timeout, output size caps.
- Egress: deny by default. The sandbox reaches db-api and results-api ONLY, never the internet, never the chat-data PVC, never the Keycloak/postgres services.
- Credentials: the sandbox must NOT hold INTERNAL_API_SECRET. Design a short-lived per-request scoped token. Note the precedent problem at suite docs/project-spec.md:237 - mcp-server sits on both sides of the db-api NetworkPolicy, so a NetworkPolicy alone is not a boundary.
- MCP exposure: per explicit user requirement, code execution must NOT be reachable via /mcp. Enumerate every layer enforcing this (tool registration, NetworkPolicy, and a test).
- Abuse cases: crypto mining, data exfiltration via db-api, resource exhaustion starving chat-backend on a shared node, prompt-injected scripts from user-supplied attachments or tool results.

Deliverable: docs/code-execution-security.md in genetics-results-suite, plus a new documentation-ownership row in CLAUDE.md.
close_reason:
Design of record written: docs/code-execution-security.md (892 lines), plus a CLAUDE.md documentation-ownership row and the docs/ tree entry in project-spec.md. Committed 6f7f520.

Two reviewers (codebase-accuracy + adversarial security), two fix rounds. Round 1's fixes introduced two new breaks which round 2 closed; stopped at two rounds per policy rather than a third.

WHAT REVIEW CAUGHT THAT NOTHING ELSE WOULD HAVE:
- The central isolation claim was unsound. Dedicated KSA with no Workload Identity binding only holds under GKE_METADATA node mode; a pool built from the first spec would default to GCE_METADATA + the Compute default SA, exposing the raw metadata server. GKE_METADATA needs cluster-level WI, which gke.tf gates on manage_iam, so it fails at APPLY not plan - and the cheap escape re-introduces the hole.
- results-api accepts a forged X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email from any namespace pod (from-less ingress rule + header fallback). Filed as genetics-results-suite-fad; .8/.9 blocked on it.
- Routing JWTs by dot-count would have 401'd every Google Identity Token. Now discriminates on the JOSE alg header.
- Pod-level /tmp emptyDir was a sequential cross-conversation channel; concurrency 1 bounds concurrent leakage, not sequential.
- read_artifact reusing SUBAGENT_ALLOWED_PATHS (=/data) would have handed the model a read primitive over chat_history.db and llm_config.db.
- The db-api ingress policy admits only chat-backend and mcp-server, so the sandbox egress allow-list alone left the primary data path dead. Both reviewers found this independently.
- The TOOL_PROFILE argument for MCP exclusion was backwards: mcp-server passes no profile, tool_profile=None means NO filtering, so _mcp_disabled membership is the sole registration-layer control.

DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS FROM THE TICKET:
- DNS eliminated (hostAliases as v1 default) rather than allowed with tunnelling booked as residual. Rationale: ~200 KB/s sustained exfiltration falsified two load-bearing controls. Reversible - the doc carries an explicit revert clause. USER HAS NOT RULED ON THIS.
- gVisor on a separate pinned 1-node pool. USER HAS NOT RULED ON THIS EITHER; it is a permanent extra node.

LEFT UNDONE: wording/stale-count/citation drift batched as genetics-results-suite-5r2. The doc's node-pool sizing assumes a pinning that is not actually in effect - genetics-results-suite-262 blocks .10.

CAVEAT FOR IMPLEMENTERS: 892 lines of design that has never met an implementation. Expect .6/.7 to find over-specification; prefer amending the doc over silently diverging.

title: OPERATOR: live NetworkPolicies are not the committed ones and admit every source on port 4000
description:
Found while validating genetics-results-suite-rhh. UNRELATED to that change, and more serious than it.

THE ENFORCED NETWORK POLICY IS NOT THE COMMITTED ONE, AND THE ENFORCED ONE IS WIDE OPEN.

MEASURED, read-only, 2026-08-13:
  kubectl get networkpolicy allow-ingress-results-api -n genetics -o yaml
    creationTimestamp: "2026-04-08T12:53:06Z"
    generation: 1
    ingress:
    - ports: [{port: 4000}]              # <-- NO `from:` - admits EVERY source
    - from: [chat-backend, mcp-server]
      ports: [{port: 4000}]
The committed k8s/network-policies/policies.yaml has ONE rule with FIVE podSelectors. The live object has a from-less rule that admits everything on 4000, plus a narrower one that is therefore redundant.

`generation: 1` since 2026-04-08 means the object has NEVER BEEN MODIFIED since creation. scripts/deploy.sh:424 is what applies these policies, so NO FULL deploy.sh RUN HAS HAPPENED IN FOUR MONTHS, and the committed policy has never been in effect.

THE SAME SHAPE APPEARS ON allow-ingress-frontend, allow-ingress-bff AND allow-ingress-chat-backend - all ports-only, i.e. effectively unrestricted ingress.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS:
1. Several documents in this repo cite k8s/network-policies/policies.yaml as THE bound on who can reach a service. Those citations describe a policy the cluster is not enforcing. genetics-results-suite-rhh's first draft did exactly this and had to be reworded to argue from the actual pod inventory instead.
2. scripts/test-network-policies.py validates the COMMITTED union and exits 0. It cannot detect that the committed union is not what is live - it reads manifests, never the cluster. genetics-results-suite-r22 closed ten fail-open paths in that harness; this is a different gap, outside it by construction.
3. The sandbox rollout (genetics-results-suite-4h6.7, 4h6.26, 4h6.27) rests on NetworkPolicy as the isolation boundary. If policies are not actually applied, that boundary does not exist at deploy time.

TO DO:
1. Diff every live policy against the committed one and record the drift. Read-only; do this first.
2. Work out WHY they were never reapplied - whether deploy.sh has genuinely not run in four months, or whether something makes the apply a no-op or skips it.
3. Apply the committed policies. This is a LIVE CLUSTER OPERATION and the user has held those back, so it needs their go-ahead - flag it rather than doing it.
4. Add a check that compares live policies against committed ones, or make test-network-policies.py able to run in a live mode. A harness that validates a file nobody applied is a harness that reports green on an unenforced control.
5. Then re-check every doc that cites policies.yaml as a bound.

DO NOT let this ride along with a feature bead - it needs its own window and its own verification.

title: The sandbox limits bind only requests that volunteer a token; seven public routes are unbounded
description:
Found by a blind validator during genetics-results-suite-4h6.29, deliberately NOT fixed there because closing it needs a design decision rather than a fix round.

MEASURED. results-api's four per-execution counters (aggregate bytes, request count, per-jti concurrency, pod-wide concurrency) are keyed on resolving a sandbox principal from the Authorization header. With NO header, _sandbox_principal returns None and admit() is never called. Seven routes are @is_public and answer 200 with no credential:
  /api/v1, /healthz, /api/v1/auth, /api/v1/variant_sets, /api/v1/variant_sets/{name}, GET /api/v1/rsid/variants, POST /api/v1/rsid/variants
20 of 20 unauthenticated requests were served with the execution map EMPTY.

AND THE SANDBOX CAN REACH THEM. k8s/network-policies/sandbox-policy.yaml egress allows app: results-api on port 4000 DIRECTLY, bypassing auth-gateway. So sandbox code that simply omits the header gets unbounded request rate, aggregate egress and concurrency - including sidestepping the pod-wide concurrency limit whose stated job is protecting a replicas: 1 pod with an 8Gi limit. No rate limiter exists anywhere else in the app (no slowapi, no rate_limit references in app/).

app/core/limits.py argued that omitting the header cannot buy a looser limit. That holds for the per-response BYTE CAP (those handlers are individually bounded) and is FALSE for the four counters. Its comment was corrected in 4h6.29; the hole was not.

THE DESIGN DECISION, which is why this is not a fix round: results-api cannot distinguish an unauthenticated sandbox request from an unauthenticated browser request. Both arrive at :4000 in-cluster. Options, none obviously right:
(a) require the sandbox token on ALL routes when SANDBOX_ENABLED - but the public routes are public for the browser, and results-api cannot tell who is calling;
(b) remove results-api:4000 from the sandbox's egress allow-list and force sandbox traffic through a path that always carries the token - this is the structural fix and it is a NetworkPolicy change, so it belongs with the sandbox rollout;
(c) add a pod-wide bound on UNAUTHENTICATED requests (concurrency + rate) that protects the pod regardless of caller - cheap and caller-agnostic, but set too low it 429s real browser users on public routes;
(d) accept it and rely on the individual handlers' own bounds - which is the status quo and is what 4h6.29 documented as not being a complete bound.
(b) is probably right and probably free, since the sandbox has no reason to call an unauthenticated route. Verify that before choosing.

DO THIS BEFORE THE SANDBOX IS DEPLOYED. Production impact is nil today (no sandbox Deployment, SANDBOX_ENABLED false on both services) and this is the last moment it is free.
close_reason:
PARTIALLY CLOSED - read this before assuming the hole is shut. Landed as genetics-results-api fb60788 and suite 3ae40c7 + 7104e81. Nothing applied; SANDBOX_ENABLED is "false" on both services and the false branch is byte-identical to before.

THIS BEAD'S OWN PREFERRED OPTION WAS REFUTED. I filed it recommending option (b) - remove results-api:4000 from the sandbox egress allow-list - on the stated assumption that "the sandbox has no reason to call an unauthenticated route". IT DOES: GeneticsClient.search(rsids=...) -> ToolExecutor.lookup_variants_by_rsid -> GET /v1/rsid/variants, which carries @is_public at app/routers/rsid.py:81. And there is nowhere to move it: the sandbox is denied auth-gateway by design and auth-gateway would not validate a sandbox HS256 token; a dedicated port would need a second listening socket in results-api, since egress on this dataplane evaluates the destination POD port. Independently, 16 of 25 SDK functions target results-api, so removing the rule breaks far more than that one call. scripts/test-network-policies.py now carries that reasoning inline so the next person to tighten the policy learns it before deleting the entry.

WHAT SHIPPED: a corrected option (a). When SANDBOX_ENABLED is true, is_public_endpoint collapses the anonymous surface to ALWAYS_ANONYMOUS_PATHS = {"/healthz"}. Every data-path route then requires A principal - not specifically the sandbox's - which answers the objection I raised in the bead ("results-api cannot tell a browser from the sandbox") by not asking it to.

THE HOLE IS NOT CLOSED, AND THE FIRST DRAFT CLAIMED IT WAS. A blind validator MEASURED it against the real ASGI app with SANDBOX_ENABLED=true, REQUIRE_AUTH=true:
    no header                                     -> 401
    Authorization: Bearer <INTERNAL_API_SECRET>    -> 200, user_email=mcp-tool
    sandbox_budget._executions afterwards          -> {}
INTERNAL_API_SECRET satisfies is_internal_caller, so get_verified_user returns "mcp-tool" and the request enters the handler - but _sandbox_principal only accepts an HS256 sandbox token, so admit() is NEVER CALLED. Requiring "a principal" is satisfied by a credential that bypasses the accounting entirely.
NOT HYPOTHETICAL: sdk/client.py states outright that the client attaches INTERNAL_API_SECRET to every request and that a script which can import the module can also read os.environ. So on the day the flag flips, a sandbox script sheds all four per-execution counters by sending the internal secret INSTEAD of no header. The change converts "omit the header" into "send the other header".
IT CLOSES WHEN: genetics-results-suite-4h6.7 stops handing the sandbox that secret (Deployment) AND genetics-results-suite-4h6.14 makes the SDK send its per-execution token (transport). Both are named in app/dependencies.py, app/core/limits.py and app/core/sandbox_budget.py, and in docs/code-execution-security.md limitation 1, which now reads PARTIALLY closed.

THE DOCUMENTED ROLLOUT HAZARD WAS BACKWARDS AND THE TRUE ONE IS WORSE. The docs said flipping SANDBOX_ENABLED before 4h6.14 lands makes "every SDK call 401". Measured false - they return 200 as mcp-tool. The real hazard is that the SDK KEEPS WORKING while contributing nothing to the budget, so the flip LOOKS SUCCESSFUL and the control is inert. Anyone planning the rollout against the old sentence would have planned against the wrong risk.

THE MISSING TEST IS THE ONE THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT ALL OF THIS. Every original test checked a boolean predicate; none drove a request through the app and inspected whether it was ACCOUNTED - which is exactly why the bypass was invisible to a green suite. test_an_internal_secret_caller_is_served_but_not_accounted now does, encodes the CURRENT behaviour, and is documented as EXPECTED TO FAIL when 4h6.7/4h6.14 land - that failure is the signal the hole closed.

ALWAYS_ANONYMOUS_PATHS WAS UNPINNED - a security WIDENING passed every test. Measured: setting it to {"/healthz", "/api/v1/variant_sets", "/api/v1/auth", "/api/v1"} left all 8 tests green, because the surface test asserted `anonymous == set(ALWAYS_ANONYMOUS_PATHS)` - tautological against the very constant it should pin - and despite its name never named /healthz. Now pinned by name; the same mutation fails 2 tests.

THE LOAD-BEARING EMPIRICAL CLAIM IS UNPROVABLE FROM TELEMETRY, and the docs no longer pretend otherwise. They asserted the measured calls "every one of them arriving through auth_request /oauth2/auth and then the BFF". The usage log CANNOT show that: middleware_usage_logging attributes only via the internal secret plus an allow-listed X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email, and its fallback reads state.authenticated_user - which on an @is_public route is NEVER SET, because auth_required returns at is_public_endpoint before get_verified_user runs. The fallback is dead on precisely these seven routes, so an internal-secret caller logs IDENTICALLY to an anonymous one. Measured: 246/246 NULL user_email on GET /api/v1/rsid/variants over 90 days, 8/8 on variant_sets/{name}. The guarantee is ARCHITECTURAL - auth-gateway's location /api/ routes to @api_bearer or auth_request+BFF, and bff/upstream.ts:58 attaches its own bearer - and is now stated as such.

VERIFIED AND SOUND: path handling is clean (no case, percent-encoding, traversal or double-slash variant reaches a handler anonymously; the comparison is against the resolved route.path, not the raw URL). /healthz is a constant JSONResponse with no data path. No probe, GCP LB health check or monitoring script targets any of the other six - the monitors' only other results-api route is /api/v1/datasets, which was never @is_public. Nothing entering the cluster from outside can be anonymous at results-api.

FILED SEPARATELY: (1) the SANDBOX_ENABLED overload - disabling the sandbox during an incident silently RE-OPENS all six routes, so the incident lever and the security lever are the same switch and the security side fails open; (2) mcp-server's executor.py:290-292 builds `{"Authorization": ...} if api_secret else {}` - a silent no-header fallback that is the one place a genuinely anonymous in-cluster caller could exist today, invisible in the log, becoming a bare 401 after the flip.

227 -> 236 passed in the offline lane; tests/test_anonymous_surface.py 8 -> 9.

title: OPERATOR ACTION: apply the hla_associations_v expand phase to BigQuery
description:
The committed schemas/hla_associations_v.sql (genetics-results-db) renames five columns to the suite's house spelling, but the DEPLOYED view still emits the old ones. Nothing in any repo can close this - it needs the view applied against BigQuery, which the user has held back ("none of these updates should yet be applied on the live cluster").

MEASURED 2026-08-12 against the live view:
  deployed emits   mlogp, sebeta, af_alt, af_alt_cases, af_alt_controls   (all FLOAT64)
  docs describe    mlog10p, se, af, af_cases, af_controls

CONSEQUENCE TODAY, not hypothetically: ALL FIVE HLA worked examples in configs/datasets.yaml and in sandbox/schema/hla_associations_v.md fail against production with "Unrecognized name: mlog10p". Anyone - human or agent - who copies a documented HLA example gets an error.

THIS IS DELIBERATE, NOT DRIFT. It is the contract phase from suite 4277ffc (genetics-results-suite-5wm), whose commit message ends "NOT APPLIED to any cluster or to BigQuery" and which added a ~113-line rollout runbook to docs/project-spec.md (around lines 981-1070) containing a state table naming this exact failure and THE LITERAL EXPAND-PHASE SQL to run. Read that runbook before doing anything.

WHY IT HAS GONE UNNOTICED: nothing executes the worked examples. scripts/test-sandbox-docs.py contains no bq/bigquery/Client()/dry_run/subprocess reference at all; its only example check asserts the SQL's FIRST LINE appears textually in the rendered markdown. So the docs can describe a view that does not exist and every check stays green.

TO DO:
1. Run the expand-phase SQL from docs/project-spec.md's HLA rollout section. It is an expand, so the view emits BOTH spellings and nothing breaks at the moment it lands.
2. Verify the five worked examples actually run - that is the acceptance test, and it is the one thing no automated check covers.
3. Then the contract phase, on the runbook's schedule.
Do NOT apply schemas/hla_associations_v.sql directly - it is the CONTRACT phase and applying it first breaks any consumer still using the old names.

CONSIDER FILING: a harness check that dry-runs each worked example against BigQuery would have caught this on day one. It cannot live in test-sandbox-docs.py (that gates scripts/build.sh on a credential-free build host) but it could be a separate, credentialed check. Related: the enumeration-rot bead.

title: CONFIG_PROFILE selects the terraform backend independently of which tfvars is in place, so a cross-profile apply passes every guard
description:
Found by a reviewer while validating genetics-results-suite-82s. STRICTLY WORSE than the bug 82s fixed, and 82s's guard does not touch it.

The main checkout holds three files side by side: terraform/terraform.tfvars, terraform.tfvars.daly and terraform.tfvars.finngen. scripts/deploy.sh:20-21 lets CONFIG_PROFILE select the terraform BACKEND independently of which tfvars is actually in place.

So `CONFIG_PROFILE=daly ./scripts/deploy.sh` from the MAIN CHECKOUT, with the finngen tfvars in place, passes the shell guard AND the new lifecycle.precondition - both only check that terraform.tfvars EXISTS - and applies finngen values against the daly state. That is a cross-profile apply with every guard green.

Compare 82s, where the failure needed a worktree and produced obviously-wrong defaults. Here the values are all real and plausible, just pointed at the wrong cluster, so the plan looks reasonable.

TO DO:
1. Make the guard check IDENTITY, not existence: assert that terraform.tfvars matches the selected profile. Cheapest reliable form is probably a config_profile assertion - terraform already has var.config_profile, so a precondition comparing it against the profile deploy.sh selected (passed in as a -var, or read back from state) would fail closed on a mismatch.
2. Consider removing the bare terraform.tfvars in favour of an explicit -var-file per profile, so there is no ambiguous default file to get wrong. That is the structural fix; (1) is the cheap one.
3. Whatever is chosen must fail LOUDLY and BEFORE apply - see 82s's close reason for why a lifecycle.precondition alone renders the whole plan first, and why the shell guard in deploy.sh is what gives a genuinely early failure on the automated path.

PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by 82s. Verify the file layout in the main checkout before acting - it was read read-only from a worktree.
close_reason:
Landed as suite 71a0d47. NOT APPLIED - terraform was never run beyond `fmt -check`, which needs no backend and takes no state lock.

PREMISE CONFIRMED AND WORSE THAN THE BEAD STATED. The two profiles are not near-neighbours: project_id daly-finngenie vs phewas-development, region/zone us-central1-a vs europe-west1-b, static_ip_name, domains (3x broadinstitute.org vs finngenie.finngen.fi + finngenie.fi), manage_iam true vs false (+ explicit node_service_account), oauth_email_domain, app_name GeneGenie vs FinnGenie, max_node_count 2 vs 3. cluster_name is the only one that matches. The backend buckets differ too (genetics-results-terraform-daly vs genetics-results-terraform), so the mismatch really does mean applying against the wrong STATE. A cross-profile apply is a cross-PROJECT apply: everything ForceNew, plus 82s's node-pool replacement path.
terraform.tfvars is currently byte-identical to terraform.tfvars.finngen, and the live .terraform cache points at the finngen bucket - so the guard passes in the main checkout today. No self-inflicted breakage.

TWO GUARDS, DELIBERATELY ASYMMETRIC.
deploy.sh compares the config_profile INSIDE the file in place against the profile that selected the backend, aborting before `terraform init`. Those are independent exactly when CONFIG_PROFILE is set - the only case where the hazard exists. When it is unset, PROFILE was derived from that same file, so the check is a no-op BY CONSTRUCTION rather than a false sense of safety. It deliberately does NOT compare against BACKEND_FILE, which derives from PROFILE - that would be the env var against itself.
terraform/main.tf adds a second precondition comparing the bucket in .terraform/terraform.tfstate (written by init -backend-config=) against the bucket parsed from ${var.config_profile}.tfbackend. The backend cache is the one signal terraform has that is independent of every variable. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY by review, not accepted on the implementer's reasoning. Both deploy.sh branches use -reconfigure, which rewrites the cache before apply, so there is no stale-cache false pass or false fail on the scripted path; on a bare `terraform apply` the cache IS the state being written, which is the correct semantics.
It inherits every 82s limitation - full plan rendered before it fails, silent under -target, never evaluated on destroy - so it is the backstop and deploy.sh is the guard.

THE CHANGE INTRODUCED A REGRESSION AND REVIEW CAUGHT IT. Hoisting the config_profile parse out of its elif made it unconditional, and under set -euo pipefail a tfvars that EXISTS but has no config_profile line made grep exit 1, pipefail propagate, and the script die after printing one line with ZERO diagnostics. Measured old-vs-new: pre-change with CONFIG_PROFILE set it proceeded; post-change it died silently - including on the SKIP_TERRAFORM=true worktree flow that the whole 82s design exists to preserve. A guard script that exits 1 with no message is the worst available failure mode. Fixed with `|| true`: TFVARS_PROFILE already defaults to "", which never equals a valid profile, so it still fails closed with its real message.
Second fix: the sed was not end-anchored, so `config_profile = "finngen"  # active` parsed as `finngen  # active` and produced a SPURIOUS mismatch abort. Not hypothetical - terraform.tfvars.daly already uses trailing comments on oauth_email_domain and oauth_allowed_emails, so the style is live in that file and simply has not reached this line yet. Now restricted to non-quote characters and anchored past the closing quote.

VERIFIED, with stub terraform/kubectl FIRST on PATH and command -v checked (a real kubectl at /usr/bin/kubectl has already nearly been hit once this session):
  CONFIG_PROFILE=daly + finngen tfvars -> abort, full explanatory message, NO terraform invocation at all
  matching profile, and CONFIG_PROFILE unset -> proceed unchanged
  missing tfvars -> 82s's message verbatim, exit 1, no terraform call
  no config_profile line + CONFIG_PROFILE set -> now proceeds instead of dying silently
  trailing comment on the config_profile line -> parses cleanly, no spurious abort
  Finngen / 'finngen ' / bogus -> all caught, though by the PRE-EXISTING 'Backend config not found' check at deploy.sh:33, not the new guard. Fail-closed either way.
Both regexes reimplemented in Python against the REAL .tfbackend files: daly -> genetics-results-terraform-daly, finngen -> genetics-results-terraform. RE2 supports every construct used (\s, [^"]+, capture groups; no lookaround, no backrefs) and Go's leftmost-first greedy matching agrees with Python here. `terraform fmt -check -recursive` flags only the pre-existing gke.tf and logging.tf misalignment; main.tf is clean, which is real parse evidence since fmt builds the AST.

SKIP_TERRAFORM=true WITH A MISMATCHED PROFILE IS SAFE, verified rather than assumed - it was the obvious place for a hole. Every templated value (GCP_PROJECT, GCP_REGION, DOMAIN, DOMAINS, STATIC_IP_NAME, CONFIG_PROFILE, OAUTH_*) comes from `terraform output` against the SELECTED state, and the kubectl context itself is eval'd from that same state, so the result is an internally consistent deploy of the selected profile to that profile's cluster - not a cross-wired one. Residual worth knowing: CONFIG_PROFILE can arrive silently via .env (set -a at deploy.sh:12-14), so this can happen without anyone typing it. Checked - it is commented out at line 48 of the live .env.

RECORDED, NOT FIXED: require_tfvars=false now disables BOTH preconditions, so an operator silencing the profile check also silences 82s's existence check. A second variable would be the clean answer but that is a design change beyond this bead. Documented where require_tfvars is described.
Also nits, deliberately left: the bucket regex is unanchored, so a commented `# bucket = "..."` line preceding the real one in a .tfbackend would win (neither file has one); spurious-fail cases exist if someone inits with an inline -backend-config to a bucket no .tfbackend names, or renames a bucket after init.

STRUCTURAL FIX RECOMMENDED BUT DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: removing the bare terraform.tfvars in favour of an explicit -var-file per profile. It is the right end state, but terraform.tfvars is gitignored and main-checkout-only, so it needs the operator to reconcile an untracked file by hand on every machine, and any run that forgets the flag silently reverts to DEFAULTS - reintroducing exactly the 82s failure with no file-existence signal left to catch it. That needs a documented migration plus a terraform.tfvars-must-not-exist assertion to be safe. The identity guard closes the hole today with no operator action.

title: terraform run from a worktree sees enable_log_sinks=false and proposes DESTROYING both log sinks
description:
Found while validating genetics-results-suite-re3. NOT a defect in any committed file - a foot-gun in how the worktrees interact with terraform's variable defaults.

terraform/terraform.tfvars is gitignored and exists ONLY in the main checkout at /home/jkarjala/suite/genetics-results-suite/terraform/. It sets enable_log_sinks = true. It is ABSENT from .claude/worktrees/*, which is where all agent work happens.

CONSEQUENCE: `terraform plan` or `apply` run from a worktree picks up the variable DEFAULT (false) instead, and would propose destroying google_logging_project_sink.endpoint_access_to_bigquery and its sibling sink, plus the associated google_bigquery_dataset_iam_member. A plan that reads as a small filter change from the main checkout reads as a destroy from a worktree, and the difference is invisible unless you notice the count.

This is the same CLASS as genetics-results-suite-e47 (sync-datasets.sh resolves sibling repos from the repo root, so run from a worktree it silently skips). Both are 'the worktree is missing something the main checkout has, and the tool degrades silently instead of failing'. Worth fixing as a class rather than one at a time.

WHAT TO DO: decide between (a) a guard at the top of any terraform wrapper that refuses to run when terraform.tfvars is absent, (b) making enable_log_sinks have no default so terraform errors instead of defaulting to destroy, or (c) a documented -var-file pointing at the main checkout. (b) is the smallest and fails closed; (a) generalises to the other tfvars-dependent toggles.

Check whether any OTHER terraform variable has a default that is destructive when the tfvars file is missing - enable_log_sinks was found incidentally and is unlikely to be the only one. That audit is the real deliverable.

MEASURED: the live sink exists with writerIdentity service-1021318262546@gcp-sa-logging.iam.gserviceaccount.com, which is the evidence that enable_log_sinks is true in the deployed profile. No terraform command was run from the worktree to confirm the destroy plan - deliberately, since plan takes a state lock. So the destroy behaviour is INFERRED from the variable default, not observed. Confirm it with a plan from the MAIN CHECKOUT before acting.
close_reason:
Landed as suite 51ec8f6. Nothing applied; terraform was never run against the real config, not even plan.

PREMISE CONFIRMED but the bead named the wrong worst case. enable_log_sinks does default to false and the live tfvars does set it true - but manage_iam is worse, and the run is not fully silent: project_id and domains have no default, so a worktree run prompts for them (and errors under -input=false). Once those two are answered, everything else defaults quietly.

THE AUDIT WAS THE DELIVERABLE and it is COMPLETE, not sampled: all 16 keys in the live terraform.tfvars diffed against variables.tf. Nine match their defaults, two prompt, FIVE diverge destructively:
  manage_iam false->true            creates a GSA and points node_config.service_account at it (gke.tf:59). ForceNew -> the GKE node pool is REPLACED. Also needs project IAM admin the terraform SA may not hold, so it can half-apply.
  node_service_account set->""      the same replacement by the other route, whenever manage_iam=false with no tfvars.
  enable_log_sinks true->false      destroys both sinks and both dataset IAM members. Neither dataset sets delete_contents_on_destroy, so a non-empty dataset fails the destroy MID-APPLY - ingestion already stopped, apply exits non-zero after the damage. Worse than a clean revert.
  config_profile finngen->daly      no GCP resource changes; it poisons `terraform output`, which deploy.sh reads immediately after apply to template the k8s manifests. Deploys the daly dataset profile onto the FinnGen cluster.
  oauth_email_domain finngen.fi->broadinstitute.org   rewrites the auth-gateway allow-list. Locks out every real user and admits a different org.
Nothing was missed: manage_iam is the ONLY variable driving a count (7 resources), and every variable feeding a resource name or location already equals its default, so no destroy-and-recreate hides elsewhere. The nine that match are LUCK, not design - cluster_name/region/zone diverging would mean a full cluster rebuild, and the daly profile's tfvars may well differ.
The node-pool ForceNew is INFERRED, not measured - confirming it needs a real plan. It survives being wrong anyway: the new SA would not exist with Artifact Registry reader at the moment the pool switched to it, so the outcome is either replacement or a pool that cannot pull images.

FIX: a lifecycle.precondition on the existing static_ip data source asserting fileexists("${path.module}/terraform.tfvars"), gated on a new require_tfvars variable (default true). Central guard rather than removing five defaults, because removing defaults fixes today's five and re-breaks on the next variable added. No new resource, so no state footprint.
Plus a shell guard in scripts/deploy.sh, which closed a REAL HOLE found while auditing: the existing tfvars check at line 22 is only a FALLBACK for deriving the profile, so CONFIG_PROFILE=finngen ./scripts/deploy.sh from a worktree would have reached `terraform apply -auto-approve` with no tfvars.

COVERAGE IS MEASURED AND HONEST, which is the part worth keeping. In a throwaway config (terraform v1.15.5):
  FIRES on plan, apply, plan -refresh=false, and -chdir. path.module resolves to "." against terraform's working directory, and deploy.sh cds into terraform/, so it is correct on every real path. The read is never deferred - name = var.static_ip_name is always known.
  DOES NOT FIRE under `apply -target=...`. Measured, real: -target prunes the graph to the target and its dependencies, and the guarded data source is a dependency of nothing - even though a root output references it. A targeted apply from a worktree still runs on the destructive defaults. Direct consequence of the guard living on one data source.
  DOES NOT FIRE on destroy - data sources are not read in destroy plans. DELIBERATE: destroy is driven by state, not variable values, so a worktree destroy is no more dangerous than a main-checkout one and blocking it would break legitimate teardown for nothing.
  Both gaps are now documented rather than implied away.
  terraform output evaluates NO config and no preconditions - measured with tfvars deleted, returned the state value, exit 0. That is what keeps SKIP_TERRAFORM=true deploys working. rollout.sh does not invoke terraform at all; deploy.sh is the only script that runs the binary.

A FIRST DRAFT OF THE DOCS CLAIMED THE GUARD 'aborts the plan before any resource is planned'. Measured false and corrected before commit: terraform renders the COMPLETE plan - every diff, "Plan: N to add..." - and only then prints "Terraform planned the following actions, but then encountered a problem:". Nothing is applied, but the operator watches the full destroy/replace plan scroll past above the error, which is alarming if you do not know it is inert. A variable-level validation block behaves identically, so there is no earlier hook available; the shell guard is what gives a truly pre-terraform failure on the automated path.

require_tfvars is safe as an escape hatch: measured that both -var and TF_VAR_ set it, grep finds no script or manifest exporting it, and it is deliberately absent from terraform.tfvars.example so copying the example does not disable it. No CI in this repo invokes terraform.

FILED: the profile-mismatch hazard a reviewer found, which is strictly worse than this bead and untouched by this fix - the main checkout holds terraform.tfvars, .daly and .finngen side by side, and CONFIG_PROFILE selects the backend independently of which tfvars is in place, so a profile/state mismatch passes BOTH guards.

NOT DONE: terraform fmt -check flags pre-existing misalignment in gke.tf and logging.tf, unrelated and untouched. The two edited terraform files are clean.

title: Per-credential row and byte caps on db-api and results-api
description:
Split out of genetics-results-suite-4h6.9, which shipped the sandbox credential and the request.state hook but not the caps.

docs/code-execution-security.md section 4 ("Implementation note for the caps" through the numbers table) specifies:
- db-api: maximum_bytes_billed 50 GB per query, an aggregate 200 GB per jti (in-process LRU counter, 429 over budget, never a silent truncation), and a 25 000-row response cap.
- These are DEFAULTS for every request, relaxed to the operator-configured MAX_ROWS/MAX_BYTES_BILLED only for a request carrying a VERIFIED non-sandbox credential. A caller must never obtain looser limits by presenting a weaker credential or none at all.
- The row cap must be clamped IN THE HANDLER: QueryRequest.max_rows is a class-level Pydantic constraint evaluated at model-definition time and cannot vary per credential; tightening module-level MAX_ROWS would hit every caller in the process.
- results-api: its own row and response-BYTE caps (it serves the bulkiest payloads in the suite), with the BROADER relax condition — any verified non-sandbox principal (shared secret, Google id_token, or per-user API token), because auth-gateway's @api_bearer location routes real users straight here with no shared secret. An hmac-only rule would put verified humans on the tight sandbox defaults.

The hook already exists: db-api leaves the principal on request.state.principal (SandboxPrincipal | "internal" | None), results-api on request.state.sandbox_principal.

Files: genetics-results-db/api/main.py (execute_query and the QueryRequest handling), genetics-results-api/app/dependencies.py or a middleware.
close_reason:
Landed as db d72c8f8, results-api 3ca6b7f, suite c6d4098. Files only; NOTHING applied to any cluster. Full tier: review + blind validation in parallel, one large fix round, targeted re-review, then two doc-scope lines. No blocking findings survived.

WHAT SHIPPED. db-api: 25,000 rows and 50 GB maximum_bytes_billed per query, plus an aggregate 200 GB per jti across ALL FOUR BigQuery paths, 429 over budget and never a silent truncation. results-api: a 16 MiB response-byte cap and NO row cap, with the broader relax condition the spec asked for (shared secret OR Google id_token OR per-user API token, because auth-gateway's @api_bearer routes real users straight there). Tests: db-api 102 -> 122 collected / 106 passed; results-api 87 -> 113 auth+cap tests, 538 -> 549 collected.

PRODUCTION IMPACT TODAY IS NIL and that was verified, not assumed: no sandbox Deployment exists and SANDBOX_ENABLED is false on both services, so caps_for returns relaxed for 100% of traffic and the middleware is pure pass-through.

THE DESIGN'S CORE INVARIANT WAS BROKEN ON ONE ROUTE, found independently by both reviewers. POST /api/v1/rsid/variants is @is_public and parse_and_validate_rsids validated format without counting; the NetworkPolicy lets the sandbox reach results-api:4000 directly, bypassing auth-gateway's client_max_body_size. So a script PRESENTING its token got 16 MiB while the same script OMITTING the header got an unbounded response materialized in the pod - an absent credential buying a strictly looser cap than a sandbox one. Fixed with a UNIFORM MAX_RSIDS = 5000 on both verbs for every caller, not a sandbox special case, because uniformity is what makes the invariant hold. Regresses nothing: uvicorn selects h11 (httptools is not a dependency) whose 16 KiB request-line-and-header bound allows at most 4096 ids in a query string, and both production callers are GET.

THE FIRST VERSION'S PUBLIC-ROUTE JUSTIFICATION WAS FALSE, in the docs and in code comments: it claimed zero security delta because a sandbox script is capped on those routes either way. The script chooses whether to send the header. The relaxation now rests on the uniform bound instead.

THE AGGREGATE BUDGET GUARDED ONE OF FOUR PATHS while the constant's own comment and both docs claimed the whole execution. /stats and /tables/{t}/sample took the per-query cap and were never charged, and neither is cached - /stats runs an uncached GROUP BY over credible_sets_v every call, loopable for the whole wall clock at 50 GB a time outside the budget. WORSE: /schema queried at the RELAXED 100 GB ceiling from a sandbox request, twice the sandbox's own per-query cap, across all 15 views on a cache miss, uncharged. All four now route through one _run_internal_query that takes the TRIGGERING caller's ceiling and charges them. The cross-caller cache argument survives in narrower form - one caller's cap must not decide what a LATER caller finds, but may decide who pays - and was confirmed against the code: _VALUES_CACHE is written only on a non-empty result, so a job over the triggering ceiling leaves it unpopulated rather than poisoned.

THE CAP WAS A MEMORY AMPLIFIER ONLY THE SANDBOX COULD TRIGGER. Counting rows meant buffering 16 MiB, copying it, then json.loads on the event loop; for 25,000 wide rows the object graph is several times the bytes, against a replicas: 1 pod with an 8Gi limit that already preloads gene maps and the search index. Presenting the token could hurt the pod MORE than omitting it. DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE DESIGN: the results-api row cap is DROPPED, not fixed. The counter only ever recognised JSON while TSV is the default format of every bulk range endpoint, so it never fired where it mattered; the byte cap binds across all formats and bounds pod memory directly, and peak memory is now strictly lower than before this bead. The 25,000-row cap remains live on db-api.

A 429'd STREAM DID NOT STOP THE UPSTREAM WORK - measured, not argued: a 10 KiB cap against a 100 KiB response produced all 100 chunks. That generator is GCS range-reads plus the tabix worker pool, so the caps bounded what a script RECEIVED and not what results-api SPENT producing it. send_wrapper now raises past ExceptionMiddleware (never reaching ServerErrorMiddleware, so never a 500, never logged unhandled, never raisable on the relaxed path or at http.response.start); the generator stops at 11 chunks and the client still gets its 429. Asserted on ASGI spec_version 2.3 - what uvicorn 0.40 actually sends - as well as 2.4.

TWO COUNTER DEFECTS: the LRU trim ran only on the ALLOWED branch while the reject path inserted a zero-valued entry, so a flood of distinct jtis grew it unbounded; and a query raising between the pre-flight charge and the reconcile left the estimate charged forever, so a script's syntax errors ate its own budget. Reconcile now runs in a finally.

KEPT total_bytes_processed over total_bytes_billed and corrected the docs instead: a dry-run job reports zero billed bytes, so processed is the only figure available on both sides of a pre-flight charge and its reconcile, and mixing units would make the correction wrong by construction. They differ by at most 10 MB per query against a 200 GB budget.

THE COUNTER IS IN-PROCESS. db-api is replicas: 1 with no HPA anywhere in k8s/, so it is exact today - but that is a property of the manifest, not the design. The manifest now carries a comment at the replica count saying N replicas means N x 200 GB.

DOC CORRECTIONS EARNED IN REVIEW: the @is_public list is SEVEN routes, not five (/api/v1 and /healthz were missing); the route is /api/v1/auth, not /auth/status; and the user_email-is-NULL inference was REMOVED as unsupportable - genetics_api_logs.genetics_results_api returns zero rows for the last two days while Cloud Logging has entries from today, and all 2,812 rows over 30 days show NULL while a live entry today carries mcp-tool, which is a sink artefact. The responseSize finding stands (non-NULL on 0 of 2,812 rows), so the no-truncation conclusion now rests explicitly on the caps being unreachable by the largest response the code can produce - the largest configured variant set is 888 rows / 18.6 KB - rather than on size data that does not exist.

OTHER BEHAVIOUR CHANGES WORTH KNOWING: sandbox-principal resolution moved AHEAD of both short circuits in auth_required, which is what makes a sandbox token capped on public routes and under REQUIRE_AUTH=false; it 401s an invalid HS256 bearer where one previously passed, and nothing in the suite issues HS256 bearers. HTTPException is re-raised past the except Exception warning handlers in /stats and _get_categorical_values so the 429 reaches the caller - narrow by construction, since a BadRequest from BigQuery is not an HTTPException and still degrades. With INTERNAL_API_SECRET UNSET the three internal db-api paths now run at 50 GB where they used to run at 100 GB; production is unaffected (required secretKeyRef) but local dev gets the tighter ceiling, recorded in the _caps_for docstring.

LEFT UNDONE, filed as 4h6.29 (P2): results-api has NO per-execution aggregate byte budget, request-count limit or concurrency limit - the 120s wall clock is the only bound, and nothing limits how many concurrent requests one execution may make. Also noted and not acted on: _run_internal_query calls job.result() and its callers call it again (harmless, cached); a 413 on the rsid POST does not drain the body, so a still-uploading client may see a reset; and the cap-middleware containment test uses a bare FastAPI app, so containment through the real stack is argued rather than exercised, guarded only by a GZip-ordering assertion.

title: The MCP exclusion boundary is one hop: mcp-server can reach the sandbox through chat-backend
description:
Found reviewing genetics-results-suite-4h6.8. Both reviewers raised it independently.

k8s/network-policies/policies.yaml admits app: mcp-server to chat-backend:8000, and mcp-server's Deployment carries both INTERNAL_API_SECRET and CHAT_BACKEND_URL (confirmed against the live Deployment). chat-backend is the one pod admitted to the sandbox.

So the network layer closes mcp-server -> sandbox but NOT mcp-server -> chat-backend -> sandbox. The user's explicit requirement is that code execution not be reachable via MCP. Layer 2 as built guarantees 'mcp-server cannot open a socket to the sandbox', which is not the same claim.

docs/code-execution-security.md section 5 now says so in prose (landed with 4h6.8). This bead is the actual hardening.

WHAT TO DO: whatever chat-backend route dispatches to the sandbox must reject the marker-alone mcp-tool service identity. Note genetics-results-suite-th2 established that a valid INTERNAL_API_SECRET marker with no identity header resolves to exactly that identity, and mcp-server holds the secret. So the run_analysis dispatch path needs a real user identity, not merely an authenticated caller.

Depends on 4h6.14 existing (the run_analysis route). Section 5's layer enumeration should be updated again once this lands.

title: Deploy-window live verification of the sandbox NetworkPolicy
description:
Everything genetics-results-suite-4h6.8 could not test offline. Run these once the sandbox is actually deployed (needs 4h6.7 and 4h6.10). scripts/test-network-policies.py covers the manifest-level properties already; these four need a live pod and cannot be faked.

1. mcp-server -> sandbox must FAIL. The explicit requirement in 4h6.8 ('a test that asserts the mcp-server pod cannot open a connection to the sandbox Service') that could not be run because nothing was deployed. From the mcp-server pod, attempt a TCP connect to sandbox:8080 and confirm it times out / is refused.

2. Metadata server egress. UNRESOLVED and currently documented as NOT covered. From the sandbox, curl 169.254.169.254 with the Metadata-Flavor header and confirm it fails. Link-local/node-local traffic is the class already proven EXEMPT from NetworkPolicy on this dataplane in the INGRESS direction (kubelet probes from 169.254.4.6), so egress enforcement must not be assumed. If it turns out NOT to be blocked, docs/code-execution-security.md section 3 and docs/project-spec.md both already say so honestly, and the compensating control (node pool GKE_METADATA mode, no Workload Identity binding for the sandbox KSA) becomes the only one - verify that it holds.

3. ClusterIP vs pod IP in egress policy. sandbox-egress uses podSelector, which assumes Cilium translates the ClusterIP to a backend pod IP BEFORE egress policy evaluation. Confirm sandbox -> db-api:8080 and sandbox -> results-api:4000 actually connect. If they are dropped to a 10.20.x.x address, translation happens after policy and a Service-CIDR ipBlock is required.

4. Denials that must hold. From the sandbox, confirm all of these fail: any internet address (e.g. an s3 endpoint by IP - polars object_store is the path only this policy closes), kube-dns on 53, chat-backend:8000, mcp-server:8080, rag-service:8000, keycloak, and the Kubernetes API server. Also confirm DNS resolution of db-api/results-api works via hostAliases and does NOT stall (that is the /etc/nsswitch.conf 'files before dns' assertion from 4h6.6 paying off).

Expected during 1-4: db-api and results-api both return 401 to the sandbox. That is correct until 4h6.9 lands the scoped credential - reachability is what is under test here, not authorization.
notes:
WIDENED after the 4h6.8 review (2026-08-10). The metadata-server check must not be limited to 169.254.169.254 - the node IP (10.0.0.41 at time of writing) and the kubelet source 169.254.4.6 are the SAME unverified class, and 169.254.4.6 is already PROVEN exempt from NetworkPolicy in the ingress direction on this dataplane. Egress enforcement to link-local has never been tested here at all, so treat all node-local and link-local destinations as unknown until measured, not just the metadata IP.

Also verify, from inside the sandbox pod with the policy applied:
- ClusterIP translation order. A reviewer settled this from cilium-config (bpf-lb-sock-hostns-only true, so pod->ClusterIP is translated in the pod veth eBPF program, and bpf_lxc DNATs before resolving destination identity and before egress policy evaluation; Cilium v1.18.7-gke1.35). to: podSelector is therefore correct and NO Service-CIDR ipBlock is needed. This was reasoned, not observed - there is currently no pod in the cluster carrying an egress policy to watch. Confirm empirically, because if it is wrong the sandbox cannot reach db-api or results-api at all.
- NEVER fix a translation problem with a Service-CIDR ipBlock. 10.20.0.0/20 is every Service in the cluster including kube-dns, which reopens the DNS exfiltration path the whole design exists to close. The only admissible form is a /32 per allowed Service IP with its own port rule.
- hostAliases does not stall. Dropping rather than rejecting 53/UDP turns an unpinned name into a multi-second hang; 4h6.6 measured 86.7s against an unresolvable metadata name versus 7.4s against a blackholed pin.

title: chat-backend trusts an unvalidated X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email with no allow-list, granting admin and minting API tokens
description:
Found during genetics-results-suite-k4t. Same shape as the results-api bug fad fixed, but strictly worse.

genetics_mcp_server/auth/dependencies.py:auth_required treats INTERNAL_API_SECRET as an ALTERNATIVE identity (returns 'mcp-tool') rather than as a trusted-proxy MARKER. When the bearer is absent or does not match, control falls through to auth/core.py:get_authenticated_user, which returns whatever X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email says. No signature, no secret, and - unlike results-api's old path - NO allow-list at all: settings.allowed_emails / allowed_email_domains (config/settings.py) are read only by mcp_server.py, never by chat-backend.

Impact of forging one header from any pod that can reach chat-backend:8000:
- ADMIN. ENABLE_ADMIN_PAGE=true in prod and admin membership is tested against ADMIN_USERS using the forged string (auth/dependencies.py). Grants routers/admin.py GET /admin/sessions (every user's chat sessions), GET /admin/sessions/{id} (full transcripts), and the admin writes in routers/llm_config.py that mutate tool descriptions and global config - i.e. prompt injection into every user's chat.
- TOKEN MINTING. POST /chat/v1/tokens (routers/api_tokens.py) calls create_api_token(user, ...) and returns the PLAINTEXT token. mcp-server accepts that token via _validate_user_token, and results-api accepts it too, so the hole pivots into both.
- Per-user data. All 14 routes in routers/chat_history.py scope on the forged user; also download ownership (download_store.py) and user settings/instruction sets (routers/llm_config.py).
- GET /chat/v1/auth is fully unauthenticated (chat_api.py, @is_public) and reflects the forged identity plus is_admin - an unauthenticated oracle for enumerating ADMIN_USERS.

mcp-server does NOT share this bug: it reads no identity header anywhere, and its ASGI gate (mcp_server.py) fails closed to 401 without a Bearer.

CONTAINMENT ALREADY LANDED (k4t): allow-ingress-chat-backend now admits only auth-gateway, results-api and mcp-server (plus monitor additively), instead of every pod in the namespace. That is containment, not a fix.

FIX SHAPE (deliberately NOT done in k4t - it is not a one-line change and it is cross-repo):
1. genetics-mcp-server: make the identity header conditional on a valid INTERNAL_API_SECRET bearer, then run the resulting address through the allow-list, mirroring results-api's get_verified_user precedence order.
2. genetics-results-suite: auth-gateway must start sending that bearer on 'location /chat/v1/' and 'location = /status' (k8s/deployments/auth-gateway.yaml) - it does not today.
Step 2 must ship BEFORE step 1 or every browser chat request 401s. Same ordered-rollout hazard as the bff/results-api pair; document it the same way. auth-gateway is a ConfigMap-driven pod, so step 2 needs deploy.sh, not rollout.sh.
close_reason:
Landed as suite 84d7d69 (auth-gateway + chat-backend manifests, docs) and genetics-mcp-server cbff33b (auth precedence, /tokens/validate, tests). Files only; NOTHING applied to any cluster, per the standing hold. Full validation tier: test + sighted review + blind validation, then two fix rounds and a targeted re-review.

WHAT LANDED. chat-backend now honours X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email only behind a valid INTERNAL_API_SECRET marker, then runs the address through the allow-list, mirroring results-api's precedence from -fad including rejecting rather than downgrading a not-allow-listed identity. auth-gateway sends the marker on the two locations that proxy to chat-backend. 1249 -> 1274 passed, 74 deselected.

THE ONE REAL DEVIATION, and the most important thing here: THE MARKER DOES NOT RIDE Authorization, unlike results-api. Two reviewers reached this independently. chat-backend is replicas 1 / Recreate / 300s grace, auth-gateway is RollingUpdate ready in seconds, and deploy.sh fires every rollout restart before waiting on any -- so the gateway leads by up to five minutes no matter how the operator sequences it. Old auth_required checks the bearer FIRST, so with the marker on Authorization every browser user in that window collapses to the single identity mcp-tool, and sessions, messages, downloads and API tokens written then stay owned by mcp-tool PERMANENTLY and readable by everyone. Fixing the rollout does not un-mix that data. On a header the old backend does not know, the same window is byte for byte today's behaviour. Cost: two conventions in the suite. is_internal_caller accepts both transports so results-api and mcp-server are untouched.

THAT ALSO CLOSED A REGRESSION THE FIRST VERSION INTRODUCED. /tokens/validate is the only chat-backend route with no auth dependency; it gates itself on a raw Authorization bearer. Stamping the secret across the whole /chat/v1/ prefix made it callable by every logged-in browser user -- a token-to-identity oracle -- and every future internal-only endpoint under that prefix would have inherited the hole silently. Found by both reviewers. It now uses the shared helper and rejects when an identity header is present, since a genuine service call never sends one; both legitimate callers verified from their outbound code. Its duplicated hmac block also compared str, the same non-ASCII TypeError -fad fixed in results-api, sitting two files away.

THE ALLOW-LIST WAS NEVER WIRED. chat-backend received neither ALLOWED_EMAILS nor ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS, so making it load-bearing as this bead described would have rejected EVERY user -- worse than the bug. Wired to bearer-auth-allowed, the ConfigMap results-api and mcp-server already consume, rendered from the same terraform variables as oauth2-proxy, so the two allow-lists cannot diverge on this profile. allowed_email_domains defaults to finngen.fi, so emptiness cannot signal 'unconfigured'; hence allow_list_configured and a documented fail-open with a warning. The marker requirement, which is the half that closes the hole, applies unconditionally. Production has ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS=finngen.fi, so enforcement is live and the fail-open is not.

ROLLOUT, and it is NOT symmetric. Of the four states only ONE is harmful and gateway-first never enters it: gateway-only is byte-for-byte the old behaviour and a safe resting state, chat-backend-only is a TOTAL LOCKOUT of chat. auth-gateway is ConfigMap-driven so it needs deploy.sh, not rollout.sh. A collapsed single deploy.sh is a race, not a guarantee -- a stream-free chat-backend terminates in seconds and the gateway now has an extra initContainer in front of it -- so the worst case is a short 401 window inside a deploy that already interrupts chat. Rollback mirrors: chat-backend first, auth-gateway second. State table in docs/project-spec.md and README.md.

TWO nginx FACTS MEASURED AGAINST A REAL IMAGE, both of which the first version got wrong, and both with the same observable failure: initContainer reports success and every browser chat request 401s.
- nginx -t does NOT catch every bad secret. A backslash, a newline, a quote-escape or an embedded '; #' all render a VALID config delivering a wrong marker (nginx unescapes \t \r \n \" \' \\ inside quoted strings); an empty value drops the header entirely.
- nginx -t DOES reject most $ values as unknown variables, missing only suffixes spelling a real variable -- $http_foo and $arg_x pass and deliver the prefix -- which the open-ended $http_* / $arg_* / $cookie_* families make unbounded.
So the guard is a WHITELIST, ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9+/=_.-]*. openssl rand -base64 32 is entirely inside it, so it rejects nothing create-secrets.sh generates; it only constrains an operator-supplied value. nginx -t quotes the offending directive on failure, which would print the secret into Cloud Logging, so every branch discards output for the real render and re-tests with a placeholder -- including the config's own error_log /dev/stderr, which resolves through /proc/self/fd/2 that the redirect has already pointed at /dev/null.

VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY, not argued: both envsubst passes against the real file (placeholder survives pass 1 with zero sentinel leaks, all 21 nginx variables through both passes with unchanged counts, rendered diff exactly the injected lines); envsubst present in nginx:1.27-alpine and the initContainer command run inside it; a forged X-Internal-Auth defeated by proxy_set_header against a control location that omits it; 60 days of gateway logs showing no non-browser client on either chat location; and the browser being cookie-only across every chat call.

DELIBERATE: REQUIRE_AUTH=false, dev only, still honours the header unmarked -- that mode already authenticated everyone, so a marker would protect nothing.

LEFT UNDONE, filed: genetics-results-suite-eau (auth-gateway sets no securityContext on any container and project-spec claims otherwise -- pre-existing, but this change added a second container to that file), -zl2 (allow-list does not accept oauth2-proxy's leading-dot subdomain form; inert on finngen.fi, and results-api has it too), -7zr (comment nits).

This unblocks genetics-results-suite-4h6.8.

title: Update the datasets.yaml variant/chr guidance IN THE SAME WINDOW as the credible_sets swap - not before
description:
Identified by measurement during genetics-results-suite-4h6.18, 2026-08-10. Deliberately NOT done at that time, and this bead exists to explain why the obvious ordering is backwards.

configs/datasets.yaml in THIS repo is the canonical copy. Line 237, in the credible_sets_v example description, says:
  'Always add the chr filter next to variant - the table is partitioned by chr and without it the same query scans ~20x more data and can hit the bytes-billed limit'

THAT IS EXACTLY RIGHT TODAY AND BECOMES EXACTLY WRONG AFTER THE SWAP. Measured with real execution, cache off, projection SELECT dataset, trait, pip, mlog10p:

  shape                                   pre-swap view      post-swap layout
  WHERE variant = '12:111446804:T:C'      7,606,541,126 B      253,707,488 B
  WHERE chr = 12 AND variant = ...           367,715,852 B      288,326,272 B
  chr-filter ratio                        0.048 (20.8x saving)  1.136 (13.6% WORSE)

SO DO NOT MAKE THIS CHANGE BEFORE THE SWAP RUNS. Landing it early tells every agent to drop a filter that currently saves 20x, which degrades production queries and can hit the bytes-billed limit - the precise failure the note was written to prevent. The swap is PREPARED but NOT EXECUTED (genetics-results-db 68b4c40, runbook at docs/credible-sets-clustering-swap.md), so today the note is correct and must stay.

WHAT TO CHANGE, once the swap has actually landed and been verified:
- line 237: replace the 'always add the chr filter' clause with guidance that variant is now a clustering key and needs no chr companion; adding one is at best neutral and measurably slightly worse.
- line 242: the accompanying example SQL 'WHERE chr = 12 AND variant = ...' should drop 'chr = 12', otherwise it demonstrates the now-counterproductive pattern.
- line ~1137: an exact-variant lookup written the long way, 'AND cs.chr = 5 AND cs.pos = 1104823 AND cs.ref = 'C' AND cs.alt = 'T'', should become 'cs.variant = '5:1104823:C:T'' so it hits the clustering key.

LEAVE ALONE, verified as still correct: the range-scan examples at lines 272, 304, 315, 1196 and 1283 genuinely need chr = N for partition pruning and are unaffected - pos being the fourth clustering key only helps them. Line 1033 (rsid to variant translation) concerns variant_annotation_v, a different table. Lines 1052 and 1082 (join predicate, peak_to_gene guidance) stay valid.

CROSS-REPO: sibling repos hold GENERATED copies of datasets.yaml. genetics-results-db's local configs/datasets.yaml is gitignored and generated and carries the same note at the same line; it is fixed by sync-datasets.sh. Note genetics-results-suite-e47 - sync-datasets.sh resolves sibling repos from the repo root, so run from a worktree it silently skips, and a stale copy can reach a deployment via deploy.sh.

Depends on the swap. Blocks nothing, but if it is forgotten the agent guidance stays wrong in the expensive direction.

title: Run the suite from source on this dev VM to prove the fad deploy ordering before deploying
description:
Requested by the user 2026-08-10: verify locally before deploying anything.

MACHINE ASSESSMENT, measured not assumed: 4 vCPU, 31 GB RAM (19 GB available), Linux 6.8 GCP kernel - this machine appears to BE the VM docs/local-dev-vm.md describes. docker 23.0.1 and kubectl are present. kind, minikube, k3d, skaffold, tilt, podman and runsc are ALL ABSENT.

PREREQUISITE - DISK. /home is at 97 percent, 3.5 GB free of 97 GB. docker holds 18.13 GB of images and 5.14 GB of build cache, 100 percent reclaimable with nothing running. A prune returns roughly 23 GB but also discards the sandbox image built for 4h6.6 and every cached base layer, so the next build is slow. Ask before pruning wholesale; dangling-only is the conservative option.

WHAT TO RUN: the from-source path already documented in docs/local-dev-vm.md - results-api :2000, frontend :3000, chat-backend :4000, bff :5000, db-api :8080, all over localhost, no Docker and no Kubernetes.

THE PRIMARY GOAL is genetics-results-suite-fad's deployment ordering. Its state table is currently verified by executing the resolvers in isolation, which is real but is not a request crossing a real socket. Prove all four rows end to end:
  neither         -> works, header alone authenticates (the vulnerability)
  bff only        -> WORKS, resolves as mcp-tool, usage log still names the real user
  results-api only -> TOTAL LOCKOUT, 401 on every non-variants browser request
  both            -> works, real user is the authenticated identity
Do it by checking out the old and new revisions of each service, not by editing code.

CRITICAL GAP IN THE DOCUMENTED PATH: local-dev-vm.md's own first paragraph says there is NO auth-gateway and NO oauth2-proxy, and services talk over localhost with no login. That is exactly the chain fad modifies - X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email originates in auth-gateway's nginx, and the divert 'if ($http_authorization ~* "^Bearer ")' is what the bff guard must partition against. So the default setup SKIPS the code under test. Run nginx locally with the REAL auth-gateway config (k8s/deployments/auth-gateway.yaml) plus a stub identity source, or the exercise proves much less than it appears to.

WHAT THIS MACHINE CANNOT PROVE, do not pretend otherwise:
- NetworkPolicy enforcement. No local k8s installed, and even with kind or minikube the default CNI does not enforce policies. Worse, production is ADVANCED_DATAPATH (Dataplane V2), and the conclusion that kubelet probes bypass NetworkPolicy is SPECIFIC TO THAT DATAPATH. A local Calico or Cilium cluster can give a different answer and would mislead rather than inform.
- gVisor isolation for the sandbox. runsc is not installed, so the image would run under runc. The image builds and its ten assertions pass locally, which is genuine verification of the image, but the isolation boundary needs the real GKE Sandbox node pool.
Leave both to a staging deploy.

Also worth running here once it exists: the 4h6.4 replay benchmark, which defaults to --base-url http://localhost:8000 and hard-codes secret=true so it never writes to a user's history.
close_reason:
Doc changes landed as 8f8c92b. The task itself was VERIFICATION, not code: eight deploy-ordering state rows proven from source on this VM, over real sockets, through real nginx. ALL EIGHT PASS. Nothing was refuted; nothing applied to any cluster; no shared worktree was checked out, stashed or modified (confirmed clean afterwards).

METHOD, because it is what makes the result mean anything. Five throwaway `git clone --shared` copies under the scratchpad, each checked out to its own revision - never the shared worktrees. Module resolution asserted INSIDE each copy before any result was trusted (the 6o3 trap has bitten five times this session). Real nginx:1.27-alpine on host networking; nginx.conf pulled from the real ConfigMap with a YAML parser; pass 1 = deploy.sh's exact envsubst whitelist (${INTERNAL_API_SECRET} confirmed surviving it); pass 2 = the render-config initContainer's args[0] extracted VERBATIM from the Deployment and run inside the image, nginx -t included. Only 24 lines changed, all of them cluster-DNS upstreams, resolver and listen port. oauth2-proxy stubbed by a 202 + X-Auth-Request-Email responder. results-api ran with REAL data, REQUIRE_AUTH=true, ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS=finngen.fi.

-fad (bff -> results-api), 4/4 PASS. neither: 200, real user. bff only: 200, real user. results-api only: 401 on /resources AND /search. both: 200, real user. The "non-variants" qualifier proved exactly right - POST /api/v1/results, served from upstream.ts, returned 200 in ALL FOUR rows including the lockout row, because it already carried the token.

THE VULNERABILITY IS CONFIRMED OVER THE WIRE, not inferred. Direct to results-api, 7 probes per revision: on the OLD build the identity header ALONE with attacker@evil.example returned 200 - so the bead's "any string authenticated, the allow-list is never consulted" is fact. On the NEW build that same probe is 401, and marker + non-allow-listed identity is 401 rather than a downgrade, confirming the reject-not-downgrade decision row for row.

-th2 (auth-gateway -> chat-backend), 4/4 PASS, and the row that mattered is clean. auth-gateway only was BYTE-FOR-BYTE identical to the pre-change baseline in every observable, with the identity staying real.user@finngen.fi rather than collapsing to mcp-tool. That is the entire justification for riding the marker on X-Internal-Auth instead of Authorization, and it is now socket-verified rather than argued. chat-backend only is a total lockout: 401 on /chat/v1/tokens, /chat/v1/admin/sessions and /status.

THE th2 VULNERABILITY IS ALSO CONFIRMED LIVE. Forging X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email at the old chat-backend returned 200 admin, 200 on GET /admin/sessions, and POST /chat/v1/tokens returned A PLAINTEXT API TOKEN IN THE BODY. All three are 401 or authenticated:false on the new build. The /tokens/validate oracle regression that review caught mid-flight is confirmed to have BOTH existed and been closed: browser-shaped call via the gateway gets 403 Internal endpoint on new, 200 {"valid":false} on old.

Also verified: a browser cannot forge past the new gateway - sending either a forged identity header or a forged X-Internal-Auth still resolves to the real user, because proxy_set_header redefines. And the initContainer's secret whitelist, run against the real image, accepted a good secret and FATAL'd on empty, bad;#injected, has\"quote and has$http_foo.

BONUS, first time over a socket: 4h6.9's sandbox token. Minted with chat-backend's real mint_execution_tokens and presented to results-api - correct audience 200, db-api-audience token replayed at results-api 401 with InvalidAudienceError named in the log (same key, valid signature, so not a signature accident), tampered token 401.

HONEST GAPS, recorded rather than glossed:
- "bff only resolves as mcp-tool" has NO HTTP surface - no results-api endpoint echoes the verified identity. Established indirectly over sockets (a wrong bearer plus a valid identity header 401s on the old build, proving the bearer short-circuits the header path; marker alone logs mcp-tool) plus a code read. The literal string was not directly observed.
- The db-api half of the token replay is UNPROVEN - db-api was never started, so the mirror-image rejection is untested.
- 4h6.28's caps were not isolated as a distinguishable observable.
- The 4h6.4 replay benchmark was not run (budget).
- NetworkPolicy enforcement and gVisor isolation: COULD-NOT-TEST, deliberately. No local k8s, and kind/minikube's default CNI does not enforce policies at all; production is ADVANCED_DATAPATH and the kubelet-probe finding is specific to it, so a local Calico/Cilium answer would MISLEAD. runsc is absent. Both belong to 4h6.26 and a staging deploy.

DOCS CORRECTED, because the exercise proved the documented path skips the code under test. local-dev-vm.md now says so and carries the working recipe, the two undocumented prerequisites that abort a fresh clone (datasets.yaml is gitignored; the browser needs npm install), and a "what this VM cannot verify" section. That in turn exposed a claim that was FALSE in two places, found independently by two agents: the siblings' datasets.yaml copies are GENERATED AND UNTRACKED, not committed - so "the committed copies don't drift" was a guarantee that never existed, nothing detects a stale sibling copy, and deploy.sh's best-effort sync is not a backstop either, since sync-datasets.sh derives SUITE_DIR as the parent of scripts/ and from a worktree warns and exits 0 having copied nothing (confirmed by running it).

FILED: genetics-results-suite-r0l - results-api's /api/v1/auth is @is_public and returns get_authenticated_user, structurally the same oracle shape th2 closed on chat-backend. It SHOULD be inert after fad, but that is reasoning and it was flagged rather than probed. The same wrong sibling-copy claim in a deploy.sh comment is left to 7zr.

CLEANUP: all 9 processes and the nginx container stopped; the user's own running suite on 2000/3000/4000/5000/8080 was untouched and confirmed still listening. Scratchpad trimmed 1.7 GB -> 57 MB, keeping the scripts, rendered configs and service logs so the rig can be rebuilt. Disk back to 30 GB free.

title: SDK import closure drags config/settings.py into the sandbox image, disclosing every internal env var name
description:
Found 2026-08-10 while pruning the sandbox image for genetics-results-suite-4h6.6. The prune removed 86 of 115 genetics_mcp_server files. These are the ones that could NOT be removed, and the reason is a fixable import chain in genetics-mcp-server.

MEASURED IMPORT CLOSURE of genetics_mcp_server.sdk, determined empirically by importing and enumerating sys.modules - 13 modules: the package __init__; sdk __init__, _runner, client, errors; tools __init__, definitions, executor, phewas_categories, sql_safety, uniprot; config __init__, settings.

THE CHAIN THAT DRAGS IN SETTINGS:
sdk/client.py imports tools/executor.py, which has a module-level import of UniProtClient from tools/uniprot.py, which imports Settings from config/settings.py. Separately, ToolExecutor.__init__ calls get_settings() at runtime.

WHAT THAT DISCLOSES to prompt-injectable code running in the sandbox: config/settings.py names the complete internal configuration surface exactly - INTERNAL_API_SECRET, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, TAVILY_API_KEY, PERPLEXITY_API_KEY, BIGQUERY_API_URL, ADMIN_USERS, ALLOWED_EMAILS, ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS, GOOGLE_TOKEN_AUDIENCE, OAUTH_ISSUER, OAUTH_JWKS_URI, SUBAGENT_ALLOWED_PATHS - plus the on-disk paths of chat_history.db and llm_config.db. tools/executor.py ships too, and docs/code-execution-security.md itself records its f-string SQL interpolation sites as blocking 4h6.14, so it hands an attacker a map of the injection sites in the one backend the sandbox may reach.

VALUES are not disclosed - the sandbox has no Workload Identity and no access to the secret - but NAMES plus structure convert 'attacker must guess the internal model' into 'attacker reads it off local disk'.

GOOD NEWS for scope: auth/core.py is NOT in the closure and no longer ships. The X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email forging recipe is out of the image.

THE FIX IS IN genetics-mcp-server, not in the sandbox build. Two parts: first, put the Settings import in tools/uniprot.py behind an 'if TYPE_CHECKING' guard with a string annotation so it becomes a type-only dependency; second, make ToolExecutor resolve get_settings lazily at first use rather than in __init__, or inject it. Then re-derive the closure and tighten SDK_ALLOWLIST in sandbox/prune_venv.py, which is currently the thing keeping this honest.

VERIFY AFTERWARDS by re-running the sandbox build. sandbox/build-checks.py asserts the surviving module list equals the allow-list exactly, so a shrunken closure will FAIL the build until the allow-list is narrowed to match. That coupling is intended.

RELATED, same root cause, already worked around: with 4h6.11 landed, importing genetics_mcp_server.sdk FAILS with ModuleNotFoundError for dotenv, through this same config.settings chain. Worked around by pinning python-dotenv in sandbox/requirements.txt. Cutting the chain would remove that dependency too.
close_reason:
Landed as mcp-server 8813762 and suite 4977621. Files only; nothing applied to any cluster, no docker push. Full tier: review + blind validation in parallel, one fix round, targeted re-review. No blocking findings survived.

THE CLOSURE IS 11 MODULES, down from 13, measured by importing and enumerating sys.modules rather than reasoned about, and confirmed identically inside the built image. config/ is gone from disk there; `import genetics_mcp_server.config.settings` is a ModuleNotFoundError; python-dotenv came out of sandbox/requirements.txt and `import dotenv` in the image is likewise gone. docker build: 10 checks, 0 failures.

ONE IMPORT EDGE DID IT. tools/uniprot.py imported Settings at module level and sdk/client.py reaches it via tools/executor.py. Behind TYPE_CHECKING with a quoted annotation, the chain breaks.

But cutting the import alone was NOT sufficient: ToolExecutor.__init__ called get_settings(), so with the file pruned the first lazy call would still ModuleNotFoundError at runtime in the sandbox. Settings now resolve at first use with a frozen _PrunedInstallSettings fallback carrying Settings' own defaults; internal_api_secret is hard-coded empty there so the variable does not return to a shipped file through its own replacement.

THAT FALLBACK IS UNREACHABLE IN PRODUCTION - verified, not assumed. chat_api, llm_service and mcp_server all import config or config.settings at module scope before any ToolExecutor exists, so the module is in sys.modules and the import cannot raise. The only install where the file is genuinely absent is the sandbox. Its empty secret omits the Authorization header entirely and results-api answers 401 - loud, and not a regression, since the sandbox pod never held the secret (confirmed against the NetworkPolicy comments and a grep of k8s/, where INTERNAL_API_SECRET is injected into six workloads and never the sandbox).

THE FIX BROKE .env FOR DEV AND CLI CALLERS, and a reviewer DEMONSTRATED it rather than theorising. __init__ read GENETICS_API_URL, GENETICS_PUBLIC_API_URL and BIGQUERY_API_URL from os.environ, and the settings import used to be the FIRST statement of __init__, so its module-scope load_dotenv() ran before those reads. Deferring it inverted that. With a .env in cwd the executor came up on the hard-coded default URL WITH a valid secret attached, and bigquery_url None, silently disabling the BigQuery SQL tools. Affected scripts/analyze_variants.py and the standalone SDK path; production k8s was never affected since env comes from the pod. The three reads are now cached_property resolving through _endpoint_env, which calls the settings resolution for its ordering side effect first - one change covering both sites, adding no dotenv dependency to the SDK. Measured: base_url http://0.0.0.0:2000/api -> http://dotenv.example/api, bigquery_url None -> set.

INTENDED BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, recorded because it is real: env vars set AFTER construction but BEFORE the first URL read are now honoured; changed after the first read they are not. Previously all three froze at construction. Every monkeypatch.setenv and patch.dict(os.environ) in the test tree was grepped - none wraps a ToolExecutor construction for these three vars except the new closure test, which depends on the NEW behaviour.

THE GOAL IS ONLY PARTLY MET, and the doc now says so. The first version claimed the three endpoint URLs were 'the whole residual list'. Grepping the 11 shipped modules refutes it: executor.py names PERPLEXITY_API_KEY, TAVILY_API_KEY and LITERATURE_SEARCH_BACKEND in LIVE os.environ.get calls, and INTERNAL_API_SECRET appears by name in sdk/__init__.py and sdk/client.py prose and in stubs/genetics.pyi and stubs/client.pyi, which the Dockerfile copies into the final stage. Replaced with a table re-derived from the code.
DECISION: INTERNAL_API_SECRET STAYS NAMED, as an accepted residual with the reasoning written down. The stubs exist to be read by the model writing sandbox code, and a warning that does not name the variable is not checkable against the real deployment, so genericising it makes it ignorable; it discloses nothing derivable, since the SDK authenticates on the agent's behalf and the header rides every request; and 4h6.9 means the pod does not hold the value. Different calculus from settings.py, which named a dozen UNRELATED variables. No warning text was deleted.

WHAT GENUINELY STOPPED SHIPPING: ADMIN_USERS, ALLOWED_EMAILS, ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS, GOOGLE_TOKEN_AUDIENCE, OAUTH_ISSUER, OAUTH_JWKS_URI, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY, SUBAGENT_ALLOWED_PATHS, and the on-disk paths of chat_history.db and llm_config.db. auth/core.py, whose docstring is the header-forging recipe, was already out and is re-confirmed absent.
