tools/executor.py COULD NOT be removed: sdk/client.py imports ToolExecutor directly, every SDK method delegates to it, and MAX_ROWS reads ToolExecutor._MAX_SQL_LIMIT at module scope. Its f-string SQL sites still ship and remain 4h6.14's.

HARDENING THE FIX ITSELF: the except is narrowed to the two module names and no longer swallows a ModuleNotFoundError raised INSIDE settings.py's own import chain (today dotenv, tomorrow whatever it grows), and the fallback warns once, naming no variable, so an unintended engagement is visible rather than silent. client became a lock-guarded property with an explicit setter - cached_property lost its per-descriptor lock in 3.12, so two threads racing it built two clients and close(), reading __dict__, never closed the loser's pool, with mcp_server holding a module-level shared executor. Latent rather than live, since nothing awaits inside the descriptor. Double-checked locking verified correct: second check inside the lock, __dict__ write last so no half-built client can be cached, exception releases via the with, and a 16-thread race yields exactly 1 client.

THE NEW CLOSURE TEST WAS ITSELF IN THE 6o3 TRAP - the seventh time this session. Its subprocess resolved genetics_mcp_server from the ambient sys.path, which the editable install points at the MAIN checkout, with nothing tying it to the tree under test; it failed loudly today only because that checkout has no sdk/ yet. Every probe now asserts __file__ resolves under this worktree's src. Mutation-tested: re-adding a module-level config.settings import takes it from 9 passed to 4 failed.

Tests 1285 -> 1295 passed, 74 deselected. Counts in the docs re-derived: 48 modules installed, 11 in closure, 37 pruned; the previous 42/13/29 was already stale.

LEFT UNDONE, filed as genetics-results-suite-wvv (P3): four latent descriptor sharp edges on the new client property - del raises for want of a deleter, hasattr/getattr now constructs, _client_lock exists only via __init__, and base_url shadowing only propagates into public_url if assigned before public_url's first read. A reviewer grepped both repos and confirmed nothing does any of them today. Also noted there: ruff format would reformat executor.py, but it would have reformatted the pre-change file too, and no CI, pre-commit config or script runs it.

title: GOOGLE_TOKEN_AUDIENCE is the public gcloud CLI client ID, so the audience check binds nothing
description:
Found 2026-08-10 during the read-only investigation for genetics-results-suite-fad. Adjacent to that bead, deliberately not changed, and it needs a user decision.

The live results-api deployment sets GOOGLE_TOKEN_AUDIENCE to 32555940559.apps.googleusercontent.com. That is the PUBLIC gcloud CLI client ID, not a client ID belonging to this project.

Consequence: any Google identity token minted by 'gcloud auth print-identity-token' - by anyone, anywhere - carries that exact aud claim. So the audience check at genetics-results-api/app/core/auth.py:97-99 provides essentially no binding. Any authenticated Google identity in the finngen.fi domain can mint a token that passes it.

The allowlist (allowed_emails / allowed_email_domains, checked at auth.py:119) IS still applied on this branch, unlike the forged-header path in genetics-results-suite-fad. So this is not a full bypass - it means the audience check is decorative, and the whole weight of authorization rests on the domain allowlist alone. Anyone who can obtain a finngen.fi Google identity gets API access whether or not they were meant to.

THE DECISION: whether to mint a project-owned OAuth client ID and use that as the audience, which is what the check is for, or to accept that domain membership is the intended authorization boundary and remove the audience check rather than leaving something that looks like a control but is not one.

I have not touched this. Flagging because a control that appears to bind and does not is worse than an absent one - someone will reason about the system's safety assuming it works.

Verify the live value independently before acting (kubectl get deployment results-api -o yaml, and the manifest in k8s/deployments/results-api.yaml) - it was read once during an investigation focused on something else.
close_reason:
Landed as suite e83ae95, mcp-server 1c12497, results-api 8f8c430, browser 7722b10. Docs and user-facing guidance only; NO auth logic changed in any repo, GOOGLE_TOKEN_AUDIENCE unchanged, the Google id_token branch still works. Nothing applied to any cluster.

THE LIVE VALUE WAS RE-VERIFIED FIRST, as the bead asked. bearer-auth-allowed holds GOOGLE_TOKEN_AUDIENCE=32555940559.apps.googleusercontent.com, ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS=finngen.fi, ALLOWED_EMAILS=''. It originates from scripts/deploy.sh:74's hardcoded default, NOT from terraform - nobody ever overrode it.

USER DECISION (2026-08-10): push programmatic users to per-user API keys. A migration, not a removal.

THE INVESTIGATION CHANGED THE SHAPE OF THE DECISION, which is why it ran before asking. The bead framed it as 'mint a project-owned client id, or remove the check'. Option (a) does not work: `gcloud auth print-identity-token` on USER credentials cannot request a custom audience at all - deploy.sh:73's own comment already said so - so re-pointing the audience does not harden the flow, it deletes it for every human caller. That surfaced a third option the bead had not considered and the user took it: the per-user API key already exists, is issued by this deployment, is revocable and attributable, and was already the MCP dialog's primary path.

MEASURED, 2026-08-10, from Cloud Logging over 90 days: 1,943 non-mcp-tool requests from six @finngen.fi people, at least three using programmatic bearer access. ZERO 'token audience not allowed' rejections - the check has never rejected anything. Nothing automated depends on the deprecated path: no CI, no cron, and no code anywhere calls fetch_id_token, IDTokenCredentials, the metadata identity?audience= endpoint, or print-identity-token.
IMPORTANT CAVEAT, recorded rather than glossed: the logs CANNOT distinguish a Google id_token from a per-user API token - no field records credential type - so some of that programmatic traffic may already be on the recommended path and some may not. That is why this is a deprecation with the branch left working, not a switch-off.

THE REPLACEMENT CLAIM HAD TO BE CORRECTED, and that correction is the substance of this bead. The first version said the audience check buys cross-APPLICATION replay protection. A reviewer showed that overstates it in exactly the direction that matters: the pinned value is the gcloud CLI's PUBLIC client, which is the same audience every other homegrown service documenting the same one-liner receives - so the likeliest replay case is precisely the one the text implied was covered. It is CROSS-OAUTH-CLIENT protection: it rejects a token minted for a different client id, including ADC's 764086051850-..., and does nothing about a token the same user handed to another gcloud-audience service. Corrected at all seven sites (the reviewer's list of six missed one in mcp-server's env-var table); the old phrase now appears nowhere in any repo.
That correction is the whole point of the bead: a control that appears to bind and does not is worse than an absent one, and replacing one imprecise claim with another would have reproduced the defect.

THE MIGRATION HAS A HOLE AND THE DOCS NOW SAY SO. POST /chat/v1/tokens is behind auth_required, which needs the internal-secret marker PLUS an allow-listed oauth2-proxy identity header; a bearer that IS the internal secret yields mcp-tool rather than a person, so it cannot mint for a user either; and the gateway 401s a bearer-only caller into the login redirect before it reaches the backend. So a CI or service-account caller has NO path to the recommended credential without a human signing in through the browser once. After that the key works headlessly under the 90-day rolling idle expiry. Verified through all three gates in code.

TWO STALE CLAIMS THE DECISION MADE ACTIVELY MISLEADING, both fixed. Apple-only identities were documented as needing a generic OIDC verifier before programmatic access was possible; in fact the key dialog has no provider gating, minting authorization is the oauth2-proxy identity header plus the allow-list and is indifferent to the IdP, and redemption is a token-store lookup with no email check - so an Apple-only user can create and use a key today. The follow-up now scopes to the deprecated Google branch alone. And results-api's own project-spec still listed the id_token as a coequal credential with no deprecation marker.

VERIFIED BY REVIEW, not assumed: the 90-day rolling idle expiry is real (llm_config_db.py:1198, API_TOKEN_TTL_DAYS default 90, no override anywhere in k8s/ or scripts/); keys are shown once and revocable; they work for both /api and /mcp; 'Create a key above' is accurate in BOTH dialog boxes; the allow-list IS applied on the id_token branch, unlike the forged-header path -fad fixed; results-api has no Keycloak bearer path, so Keycloak is not the alternative; deploy.sh and the ConfigMap edits are comment-only and the new comments contain no $, so envsubst rendering is unaffected.

Measured numbers in the docs are dated 2026-08-10 and attributed to Cloud Logging, with an explicit warning not to re-derive them from the endpoint_access BigQuery sink - see the bead filed for that sink dropping user_email and lagging.

FILED ALONG THE WAY: genetics-results-suite-e22 (a gmail.com address in oauth2-proxy's logs, admitted or rejected unknown), and the endpoint_access sink bead.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER PICKS UP NEXT: gcloud credentials EXPIRED partway through this bead. kubectl and gcloud logging both fail now. The measurements above were taken while they were valid.

LEFT UNDONE deliberately: the id_token code path, GOOGLE_TOKEN_AUDIENCE's value, and the MCP_API_KEY shared-secret documentation all remain - the README now says that key is one deployment-wide value, neither attributable nor per-user revocable, and links to the per-user section. Nit not fixed: the dialog says a key grants access on 'your Google account's domain alone', which ignores the ALLOWED_EMAILS individual-address branch - accurate for this deployment.

title: Four more from-less NetworkPolicy rules leave frontend, chat-backend and mcp-server open to any pod
description:
Found 2026-08-10 during the read-only investigation for genetics-results-suite-fad. Out of that bead's scope, which covers results-api and bff only.

k8s/network-policies/policies.yaml has FOUR more ingress rules with ports but no 'from' clause, which admits ALL sources in the namespace:
  allow-ingress-frontend      port 3000
  allow-ingress-chat-backend  port 8000
  allow-ingress-mcp-server    port 8080
  allow-ingress-auth-gateway  port 8080

Their inline comments all say 'from load balancer'. Only ONE of them is actually an LB backend.

VERIFIED: the only Ingress (genetics-suite, 35.201.123.9) has two rules, both backending auth-gateway:8080, and auth-gateway is the only NodePort service. So:
- allow-ingress-auth-gateway GENUINELY needs it. Scoping that one requires an ipBlock for the GCP health-check ranges 35.191.0.0/16 and 130.211.0.0/22, plus the node CIDR for NodePort SNAT - NOT a podSelector. Get this wrong and the site goes down.
- frontend, chat-backend and mcp-server are the same over-broad pattern with no LB justification. They are reachable by any pod in the namespace today.

Kubelet probes are NOT a justification either: proven empirically that they are exempt from NetworkPolicy on this cluster's ADVANCED_DATAPATH / Dataplane V2 - db-api and oauth2-proxy have httpGet probes, only podSelector-scoped policies, and have been Running for days.

WHY THIS IS P1 AND BLOCKS THE SANDBOX: epic genetics-results-suite-4h6 puts LLM-authored, prompt-injectable code in this namespace. Fixing only results-api and bff (which is all fad does) still leaves chat-backend:8000 and mcp-server:8080 reachable from the sandbox pod.

MUST CHECK BEFORE DECLARING THE EPIC SAFE: whether chat-backend and mcp-server share the forgeable X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email auth code that fad found in results-api. If they do, the identical bypass applies to them and the sandbox can forge an identity against them too. Trace it rather than assuming - fad found the results-api path was worse than described, in that the allowlist is never consulted on the fallback path so ANY email string authenticates.

Do the same investigate-then-scope sequence fad used. Do not change the auth-gateway rule blind.

title: DECISION: maxUnavailable 0 makes every PDB-protected node permanently unscaledownable
description:
Needs a user decision. Raised by validation of genetics-results-suite-262 on 2026-08-07, after that bead's own rationale was shown to be partly wrong.

WHAT WAS DECIDED EARLIER: keep autoscaling min 1 / max 3 rather than pinning min==max==2, and add a PodDisruptionBudget instead. The notes on 262 justified this as addressing a failure mode pinning does not, 'at no standing cost'.

THAT LAST CLAUSE IS WRONG, and this bead exists to put the real cost in front of the user.

THE MECHANISM, confirmed against primary Google docs by two independent agents:
GKE's autoscaler doc has two branches, and they are easy to conflate:
  'If there are Pods on a node that cannot move to other nodes in the cluster, cluster autoscaler DOES NOT ATTEMPT to scale down that node.'
  'If Pods CAN be moved to other nodes, but the node cannot be drained gracefully after a timeout period, the node is forcibly terminated. This timeout period is one hour for GKE versions 1.32.7-gke.1079000 or later.'
The one-hour force-termination applies ONLY to nodes already SELECTED for scale-down. maxUnavailable: 0 with replicas: 1 makes the budget permanently unsatisfiable, so the node lands in the FIRST branch and is never selected. There is NO time bound on that path. Surfaced as no.scale.down.node.pod.not.enough.pdb, which the docs warn is best-effort and expires from the console in 72 hours.

CONSEQUENCE: results-api is RollingUpdate, so during a rollout its replacement lands on the surge node; the old pod dies, node 1 frees up, but the new pod stays on node 2 and node 2 can never be reaped. The pool ratchets to 2 nodes and STAYS THERE. That silently reproduces the min==max==2 steady state the user explicitly rejected, as an undocumented side effect rather than a choice.

AND THE MITIGATING ARGUMENT DID NOT SURVIVE EITHER: the first draft claimed chat-backend was exempt because an RWO PVC pinned it to one node. Checked: k8s/volumes/pvc-chat-data.yaml is ReadWriteOnce on storageClassName standard-rwo, a ZONAL PD - it permits attach to any node in the zone, one at a time, and does not pin the pod. chat-backend has no nodeSelector, nodeName or affinity. So chat-backend's PDB can ratchet too. The only true weaker statement is that Recreate means it never CREATES a surge node itself, though it can be rescheduled onto one another deployment created.

WHAT IS NOT AT RISK, so the decision is about cost and not safety - node upgrades and auto-repair both carry a documented hard one-hour-per-node ceiling after which GKE forces through, control-plane upgrades never drain workload pods, and a PDB cannot be made undeletable. No security patch can be deferred beyond that bound by this configuration, and the cluster cannot be wedged.

THE OPTIONS:
(a) KEEP maxUnavailable: 0 on both and accept a permanently 2-node pool once a rollout surges. Costs roughly one extra e2-standard-4 continuously. Buys genuine protection against mid-SSE eviction during voluntary drains.
(b) KEEP it on chat-backend only, drop results-api to no PDB. results-api is the reliable ratchet (RollingUpdate, migrates every rollout); chat-backend only ratchets occasionally. results-api's justification was a startupProbe allowing ~5 min warm start, which is a slower-recovery argument, not a lost-work argument - a dropped SSE stream loses a user's in-flight answer, a restarted results-api just makes tool calls fail briefly.
(c) SET maxUnavailable: 1 on both. Be clear that this is protectively INERT on a single replica: desiredHealthy = replicas - maxUnavailable = 0, so disruptionsAllowed = 1 and every eviction is admitted immediately. It documents intent and unblocks the autoscaler, nothing more.
(d) Give chat-backend a second replica, which is the only structural fix and the only thing that makes a PDB mean anything. Honest caveat: with sticky SSE connections it protects NEW connections; streams pinned to the drained pod still die. The real fix for those is client-side resume (EventSource auto-reconnect plus Last-Event-ID), which is a browser-repo change.

NOT A SUBSTITUTE, checked and rejected: cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=false is strictly worse - it blocks node selection the same way and has no effect on upgrades or repair.

ALREADY DONE regardless of which way this goes: unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy: AlwaysAllow is set on both PDBs. Under the default IfHealthyBudget a CRASHLOOPING pod is also unevictable with maxUnavailable: 0 - providing no service and blocking maintenance simultaneously. That was a genuine deadlock and is fixed.

262 landed with maxUnavailable: 0 and documentation that now states this cost honestly. Nothing has been applied to the cluster - the manifest is file-only until someone runs deploy.sh.
notes:
USER DECISION 2026-08-10: option (c) - set maxUnavailable: 1 on BOTH PDBs. Do NOT keep 0. Do NOT drop either PDB. Do NOT add replicas.

The user chose this understanding that it is protectively INERT on a single replica: desiredHealthy = replicas - maxUnavailable = 0, so disruptionsAllowed = 1 whenever the pod is healthy and every eviction is admitted immediately. It documents intent and keeps the manifest as a placeholder for when a second replica exists; it does not protect a stream today.

Mid-stream eviction is therefore covered by what is ALREADY LIVE from commit 6db94e8: terminationGracePeriodSeconds 300, preStop sleep 10, uvicorn --timeout-graceful-shutdown 280. That half of the commit IS in the committed manifest, unlike the pinning.

Consequence accepted: no protection against voluntary eviction. Consequence avoided: no permanent 2-node ratchet, which was the reason 0 was rejected.

Nothing is to be applied to the live cluster.
close_reason:
Landed as suite abe5c5f. FILES ONLY - nothing applied to the cluster. The manifest reaches it only on the next deploy.sh.

USER DECISION IMPLEMENTED: maxUnavailable: 1 on both PDBs, chosen in full knowledge that it is protectively INERT on a single replica. desiredHealthy = replicas - maxUnavailable = 0, so disruptionsAllowed = 1 whenever the pod is healthy and every eviction is admitted immediately. The budgets document intent and become meaningful at a second replica; they do not protect a running stream today. Both PDBs kept, no replicas added, minAvailable not used.

WHY 0 WAS REJECTED, kept in BOTH files deliberately so nobody 'fixes' the inert budget back: maxUnavailable: 0 on replicas: 1 is permanently unsatisfiable, which puts the node in GKE's never-SELECTED-for-scale-down branch rather than the selected-then-force-terminated-after-an-hour branch. No time bound. results-api migrates to the surge node every rollout and pins it, so the pool ratchets to 2 nodes permanently - arriving sideways at the min==max==2 steady state the user rejected when it was proposed as a pinning.

WHAT ACTUALLY CUSHIONS MID-STREAM EVICTION is unchanged and was already live from 6db94e8, in the Deployment manifests rather than in the PDBs. Verified at the cited lines rather than assumed: terminationGracePeriodSeconds 300 (chat-backend.yaml:29), uvicorn --timeout-graceful-shutdown 280 (:37), and lifecycle.preStop.sleep.seconds 10 (:143-145). Reviewer confirmed that last one is the NATIVE sleep lifecycle action, not an exec shell sleep - PodLifecycleSleepAction went GA in k8s 1.30 and the cluster is v1.35.6-gke.1250000, so it is valid as committed.

unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy: AlwaysAllow KEPT on both, inert today, with its justification NARROWED after review caught it as factually wrong. The file had claimed removing it would reintroduce the crashloop deadlock 'the day someone raises replicas or switches to minAvailable'. The minAvailable half is right; the replicas half is not. At replicas: 2, maxUnavailable: 1, desiredHealthy = 1, so one CrashLoopBackOff pod beside one healthy pod gives currentHealthy 1 >= desiredHealthy 1 and IfHealthyBudget admits the eviction. The deadlock needs the budget AT ITS LIMIT - every replica unhealthy. The claim was unconditionally true under maxUnavailable: 0 (desiredHealthy == replicas) and was carried into the 1 framing without re-deriving. Two sentences three lines apart disagreed; they now agree on the correct version.

TWO MORE ORPHANS FROM THE REFRAME, both fixed: a sentence still naming the scale-down ratchet as something that exists (there is none at maxUnavailable: 1), and the Infrastructure bullet claiming graceful shutdown 'protects chat-backend from the subsequent scale-down'. It protects nothing from scale-down - the pod dies and the node goes away regardless. What it prevents is TRUNCATION of the in-flight stream, which the body text already said correctly.

REVIEWER CONFIRMED CORRECT: the YAML field set is identical to 0149f85 except the two intended scalar changes (nothing dropped, nothing added); policy/v1 accepts maxUnavailable alongside unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy (the mutual exclusion is minAvailable vs maxUnavailable); selectors still match the real pod labels at chat-backend.yaml:16 and results-api.yaml:14; both Deployments are still replicas: 1 so the premise the comments rest on holds; deploy.sh:329 applies the directory; the surge arithmetic table and the Open question block are untouched; docs/code-execution-security.md untouched.

VALIDATION GAP TO NOTE: kubectl apply --dry-run=client could NOT be run. It is not purely client-side in practice - it needs the API server for OpenAPI schema fetch and RESTMapper kind resolution - and this machine's GKE credentials have EXPIRED ('Reauthentication failed. cannot prompt during non-interactive execution'). Fallback was an offline yaml.safe_load_all parse plus a field-level diff against the version that DID pass a real dry-run at 0149f85. Since only a scalar moved from 0 to 1, schema acceptance is not in doubt - but re-run the real dry-run after gcloud auth login if belt-and-braces is wanted.

STILL FALSE ELSEWHERE, owned by genetics-results-suite-4h6.10: docs/code-execution-security.md:1193 asserts 'No PodDisruptionBudget in the namespace.' That has been false since 0149f85. It is in a residual-risk register rather than a design proposal, which is the kind of document people act on, so it is the weakest of the four deferrals to that bead. Note the risk it describes DOES still hold for the sandbox Deployment itself, which has no PDB.

title: get_hla_by_allele hands the model unlabelled positional lists
description:
Found by review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.25 on 2026-08-07. Confirmed empirically, not inferred.

This is the SAME defect genetics-results-suite-bef fixed for the five by-gene BigQuery tools. get_hla_by_allele landed on master in c8d8aa3, in parallel with bef's fix in 45c729e, so it never got the lesson.

db-api returns query rows POSITIONALLY with the column names in a separate key. executor.py:1452 assigns result.get('rows', []) straight into the payload, so the model receives:

  results[0] == ['K11_COELIAC', 'HLA-DQB1', 'DQB1*02:01', 1596.65, 0.0, 1.6397, ...]

with no 'columns' key anywhere in the payload. The model has to infer which number is mlogp, which is beta, which is sebeta, which is af_alt - and it will usually infer right, which is the uncomfortable part. Every other BigQuery tool zips rows into dicts via _bq_gene_payload (executor.py:363).

Check also whether the download link is broken the same way bef found: _convert_to_tsv's 'results' branch does results[0].keys(), which is an AttributeError on a list, swallowed by _process_download_hints so the user simply gets no link. bef fixed that by using the {columns, rows} form in _download_data. Verify whether get_hla_by_allele's _download_data has the same hole.

NOT fixed inside genetics-results-suite-4h6.25 because it changes live MCP tool output, which the epic forbids until the tool profile flips. The SDK is unaffected - it now takes the with_metadata/columns path.

FIX: apply _bq_gene_payload (or the same zip-with-length-check) exactly as bef did, including the loud failure on a columns/row length mismatch - zip truncates silently, and a row arriving as a dict would zip column names against dict KEYS and produce plausible-looking garbage.
notes:
USER DECISION 2026-08-10: FIX NOW. The epic's freeze on live MCP output was meant to protect the benchmark baseline, not to preserve a defect. The baseline shift is toward correct.

Scope is buc ALONE. The user chose the narrower option, so do NOT bundle genetics-results-suite-84o (the 'Read mlogp' description bug) into this - it stays a separate bead.
close_reason:
Landed as genetics-mcp-server a8420ac. 1244 -> 1249 passed, 74 deselected, ruff clean. Reviewed; no blocking findings.

Per the user's 2026-08-10 decision this DOES change live MCP tool output, which the epic otherwise freezes until the tool profile flips. Deliberate: the freeze protects the benchmark baseline, and this moves that baseline toward correct.

THE DOWNLOAD WAS ALSO BROKEN, and this was confirmed by EXECUTION before anything was touched, not by reading:
  results[0]: ['K11_COELIAC', 'HLA-DQB1', 'DQB1*02:01', 1596.65, 0.0, 1.6397, ...]
  download keys: ['results', 'filename']
  TSV RAISED: AttributeError 'list' object has no attribute 'keys'
Exactly bef's second failure mode - _convert_to_tsv's results branch does results[0].keys(), which is an AttributeError on a positional list, swallowed by _process_download_hints's bare except, so the user simply got no link. Filed separately as genetics-results-suite-71c: that bare except has now hidden this identical defect TWICE (bef, then buc) across ~25 _download_data producers, and the failure is indistinguishable from 'this result did not warrant a link', so nobody reports it.

SHAPED PER CONSUMER, following bef rather than inventing: model-facing results are dicts zipped from columns (that set is capped, so it is cheap, and it is what makes the values interpretable); _download_data uses the {columns, rows} form, avoiding materialising up to 100k dicts. Loud failure on a columns/row length mismatch, including a row arriving as a dict - which would otherwise zip column names against dict KEYS and produce plausible-looking garbage.

THE REFACTOR WAS THE REAL RISK, NOT THE FIX, and it was proven rather than argued. bef's validation is now shared as a static _positional_rows(query_result) -> (columns, rows, error) with _bq_gene_payload delegating to it, error strings kept byte-identical. The reviewer reconstructed the OLD _bq_gene_payload body verbatim from git show 45c729e and diffed its output against the new delegating version over 16 input shapes x with_metadata in {False, True} = 32 comparisons, 0 mismatches. Cases: normal, empty rows, empty columns, missing rows key, missing columns key, columns None, rows None, row too long, row too short, dict row, tuple row, second-row-bad, None row, string row, truncated present, [[]] with no columns. That mattered because the five by-gene tools are in production and their tests were written against the same code they would have been validating.

LOUD-FAILURE MATRIX VERIFIED on the real get_hla_by_allele: row too long / too short give the arity message; no column names gives its own; a dict row gives 'query result row is dict, expected a positional list'; a STRING row whose length happens to match the column count is caught by the isinstance check BEFORE the arity check, so it cannot slip through; empty rows correctly stay success=True with count=0 rather than erroring.

DOWNLOAD VERIFIED END TO END through the real _convert_to_tsv: header row equals columns exactly and value order matches (mlogp 1596.65 lands in the mlogp column, not shifted). Ran the full payload through the real _process_download_hints, which now produces a working link.

SDK CONFIRMED UNAFFECTED AND UNMODIFIED: git diff --stat over sdk/ is empty. Verified through the real client with a mocked upstream - 11 columns in query order, correct dtypes, an EMPTY result still retaining its schema (0, 11), truncated still raising GeneticsError, and a mismatch propagating as GeneticsError rather than a silently wrong frame. _frame's dict-row re-flattening against columns already handled the new shape.

THE TEST THAT HID THIS is gone. test_surfaces_rows mocked DICTS with columns: [] - a shape db-api never returns - which is precisely why the suite was green through the defect. Replaced with real positional fixtures. test_metadata_is_off_for_the_model_and_on_for_the_sdk was TIGHTENED rather than deleted: it still pins that columns/truncated stay off by default and on under with_metadata, and now also pins that the names reach the model on the rows themselves.

count is len(rows) and results is a 1:1 zip of the same rows, so count == len(results) before and after - the field did not silently change meaning. llm_service._count_result_items also unchanged.

SCOPE HELD: genetics-results-suite-84o (definitions.py:1278 still says 'Read mlogp' on the branch returning mlog10p) and genetics-results-suite-5wm (SDK per-branch column spellings) both deliberately untouched, per the user choosing the narrower option.

NOTED, NOT FIXED: MCP clients now receive both results (dicts) and _download_data (positional), since mcp_server.py strips neither - payload grows ~35% on a 2-row sample. That is the same tradeoff bef accepted for the five by-gene tools, so it is consistent rather than a regression.

title: hla() returns different column names depending on which selector was passed
description:
Found by review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.25 on 2026-08-07.

The SDK's hla() is the only collapse whose two branches read DIFFERENT stores, and they disagree on column names for the same quantities:

  hla(phenotype=...) -> results-api /v1/hla/{resource}, _HLA_HEADER_SCHEMA
    (genetics-results-api/app/routers/hla.py:30) spells them:
    mlog10p, se, af, af_cases, af_controls
  hla(allele=...)    -> BigQuery hla_associations_v
    (configs/datasets.yaml:831) spells them:
    mlogp, sebeta, af_alt, af_alt_cases, af_alt_controls

Trait column is 'phenotype' in both. Verified against the real schemas, not inferred.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE EPIC: the SDK is the surface a sandboxed script gets. A model primed on the MCP tool corpus writes
  hla(phenotype='K11_COELIAC').filter(pl.col('mlogp') > 7.3)
and gets ColumnNotFoundError - costing a retry iteration. Iterations are exactly what genetics-results-suite-4h6.23 measures, so this biases the code-execution arm downward: a measurement artefact, not a real difference. Concatenating results from the two branches also fails.

Made worse by genetics-results-suite-4h6.27: the get_hla_by_phenotype tool description actively tells the model to read 'mlogp', which is the WRONG spelling for that branch.

THE DECISION, which is why this is not being fixed inline: harmonising means renaming on the phenotype= branch in the SDK only (mlog10p->mlogp, se->sebeta, af->af_alt, af_cases->af_alt_cases, af_controls->af_alt_controls). That asserts the two backends' quantities are SEMANTICALLY IDENTICAL - in particular that results-api's 'af' is the ALT allele frequency and not something else. Confirm that against the munge code that produced both, do not assume it from the name.

Counter-argument on the other side: the SDK is documented as a thin adapter and no other function renames anything. Harmonising here makes hla() the exception.

Note exome() also splits across backends - check whether it faces the same divergence and what it does, so whichever way this goes is consistent.

Should be settled BEFORE genetics-results-suite-4h6.23 runs the benchmark, or the result carries a known artefact.
notes:
ID CORRECTION: the description refers to 'genetics-results-suite-4h6.27' for the wrong-spelling tool description. That was a placeholder written before the bead existed. The real ID is genetics-results-suite-84o.

Related: genetics-results-suite-84o (tool description names mlogp on the branch that returns mlog10p) must be resolved consistently with whichever way this bead goes.
close_reason:
Landed as db 7e44959, mcp 3da9f43, api 017bf11, munge 36d720b, suite 4277ffc. NOTHING APPLIED to any cluster or to BigQuery: setup_bigquery.sh was not run and no CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW was executed. The committed view definition is the CONTRACT phase and must not be applied directly - see below.

THE BEAD'S PREMISE WAS INVERTED BY INVESTIGATION, and the user was asked before implementing. The bead read as though hla_associations_v held the correct spelling. It does not: mlog10p/se/af is house style across the suite (counts mlog10p:mlogp ~786:130, se:sebeta ~333:45, af:af_alt ~128:39) and is what every ingest path already converts INTO. hla_associations_v was the exception. Following the bead as written would have renamed the CONFORMING surface. USER DECISION (2026-08-10): align hla_associations_v to house style.

Q1 SETTLED FIRST, as the bead asked: the quantities are semantically identical - same source rows, same munge pass, byte-identical values on matched rows, the difference introduced by an explicit 1:1 rename map. Independently corroborated: the five renames here are identical, source-for-target, to the column_mapping genetics-results-api's finngen_hla_sumstats ALREADY applies on the tabix path. So the BigQuery branch now reaches the names the other branch always served.

THE EXECUTOR CHANGE WAS BEHAVIOURAL, NOT COSMETIC, which is easy to miss when the bead is framed as a naming disagreement. get_hla_by_allele's SQL SELECTed, filtered on, and ORDER BY'd mlogp. All three renamed together; a partial rename would sort right and return nothing, or vice versa. The 4h6.25 guards (quote_literal on resource, sql_int clamping max_rows, _HLA_ALLELE_RE on the allele) are intact and untouched. The TSV download needed no change - its header comes from the query result's own `columns` key.

VIEW VERIFIED AGAINST LIVE, not assumed: bq show --schema gives 14 columns; the explicit list reproduces all 14 in that exact order, none dropped or reordered, CASE...AS resource intact. Dry-run clean, live sample values correct, generate_resource_sql.py lint still OK.

TWO FAKE TESTS IN ONE TASK - the substance of this bead's validation.
(1) mcp's phenotype-branch test mocked the HTTP client with a row dict authored inside the test file, then asserted the executor did not rename it. True by construction. Its docstring claimed "nothing else pinned it, so a rename there would land silently", which remained literally true AFTER the change.
(2) The two validators then CONTRADICTED each other on whether genetics-results-api pinned those names instead. Resolved by RUNNING it rather than picking a side: that repo's test_hla.py is pure live-server integration - 13 failed, 2 passed with nothing on :4000, and the 2 pass only because they assert 404s. Both column assertions cited as proof sit inside failing tests. se/af/af_cases/af_controls were asserted by NOTHING in any repo.
FIXED: docstring reworded to claim only what it proves, and a real offline pin added at genetics-results-api tests/test_hla_column_names.py (8 tests, no network). Verified by ON-DISK mutation, not in-memory: se->sebeta fails 4 tests, deleting af_cases fails 3, reverting mlog10p in either profile's mapping fails 3 - each in only its own profile's parametrizations, so one profile cannot mask the other.
The allele branch was separately confirmed genuinely pinned by three on-disk mutations including an ORDER BY-only and a single-column change.

ROLLOUT - READ BEFORE APPLYING ANYTHING. Unlike fad/th2 this rename has NO safe single-sided state. View-first gives `Unrecognized name: mlogp` on every allele-branch call; code-first gives `Unrecognized name: mlog10p`. The halves ship by different mechanisms: the view by setup_bigquery.sh run BY HAND, and nothing in deploy.sh/build.sh/rollout.sh touches BigQuery at all.
The code half is THREE artifacts, not one: the mcp-server image, the SEPARATE sandbox image, and the datasets-config ConfigMap that ONLY deploy.sh recreates (scripts/deploy.sh:301). That ConfigMap is what the model reads to compose ad-hoc SQL, so an image-only rollout leaves the LLM writing mlogp against the new view. The earlier "roll mcp-server back to back" instruction was wrong on both counts and is corrected.
EXPAND/CONTRACT IS THE DOCUMENTED ROUTE and both validators recommended it independently. The transitional both-spellings state was verified to break nothing (TSV header comes from the query's own columns; the only SELECT * consumer is model-composed sandbox SQL whose schema doc names only house spelling; monitor issues only COUNT(*)/DISTINCT resource; generate_resource_sql.py lint reads only the CASE block; gen-sandbox-docs.py --check compares against datasets.yaml not the live view). Rollback decides it: an expanded view serves both generations, so the code half rolls back with a plain kubectl rollout undo and no BigQuery action. The LITERAL expand-phase SQL is in suite docs/project-spec.md because improvising it is how the CASE...AS resource block gets dropped.
CAVEAT recorded there: during the expanded state NOTHING reminds you the contract step is still owed - lint and gen-sandbox-docs.py --check both stay green.

THIS CHANGES LIVE MCP TOOL OUTPUT SHAPE for the allele branch: named rows and the TSV download header both derive from the view's column list, so any external consumer reading mlogp/sebeta/af_alt breaks at view-replacement time.

CORRECTED A CLAIM THE MODEL WOULD HAVE ACTED ON: the two hla() branches were documented as concatenating "directly". Statistic names now agree, but the column SETS differ (results-api 15 keys incl. resource/version/chr/pos; BigQuery branch 11, no version), so a bare pl.concat still fails on width. Fixed at the GENERATOR source - including configs/datasets.yaml:920, whose notes produce the very schema doc the model reads - then regenerated.

Tests: mcp 1297 passed / 74 deselected (unchanged); db 122 passed; api 263 passed (+8 new, against a pre-existing 282-failure live-server baseline); suite gen-sandbox-docs.py --check clean, test-sandbox-docs.py 13/13.

PROCESS INCIDENT, disclosed by the reviewer and independently verified by me: it ran `git checkout -- executor.py` during mutation testing, discarding the implementer's uncommitted change, then restored it. I confirmed restoration myself - blob hashes fe00489..12af937, the exact 5-line rename diff, internally coherent. No damage. The shared-tree rule was restated more forcefully for later agents.

doc-drift hook warned on configs/datasets.yaml. It does not apply: only prose notes strings changed - no data_type enum, no field list, no ALL_VIEWS entry - and the sandbox files are the regenerated schema doc and stubs, not the image/manifests/policy that code-execution-security.md describes.

FILED: genetics-results-suite-n3t (nothing detects a base-table column the now-explicit view silently drops - both validators raised it), genetics-results-suite-w09 (the api suite gives no offline signal at all; 282 live-server failures - this is what made the fake pin possible), genetics-results-suite-5wy (adding-datasets.md HLA checklist).

LEFT UNDONE deliberately: the drift detector and the adding-datasets.md checklist (both filed above), and the whole rollout - no cluster or BigQuery action was taken, per the user's standing constraint.

title: phenotypes/datasets drift check is blind to new tables - HLA already slipped through
description:
Found 2026-08-07 when HLA landed on master while the epic was in flight. This is a hole in the guard shipped by genetics-results-suite-4h6.19, demonstrated by a real case within hours.

WHAT HAPPENED
hla_associations landed in BigQuery (506,961 rows, dataset = 'finngen_hla', registered in configs/datasets.yaml by suite commit feb2254, table by db commit a8ca52e). The datasets table loaded by .19 has ZERO rows for finngen_hla, so the registry is already incomplete.

WHY THE GUARD MISSED IT
scripts/load_phenotypes.sh builds live_datasets from a HARDCODED UNION of nine table names. hla_associations is not among them, so the dataset never appears in live_datasets, so validate()'s live-minus-mapped check has nothing to compare and passes clean. The guard fails OPEN for the single case where drift is most likely: a brand-new table.

This is worse than the mapped-minus-live direction that .19's review added, because that one at least errors.

FIX
Derive the live-dataset UNION from the same VIEWS list that api/main.py exposes, rather than hardcoding table names. Then any newly exposed view is automatically in scope and a new dataset value fails the build until it is mapped. Keep the explicit exclusions (peak_to_gene, variant_annotation have no meaningful dataset column) as a named list with reasons, so the exclusion is a decision rather than an omission.

ALSO REQUIRED FOR HLA SPECIFICALLY
- add finngen_hla to BQ_DATASETS_BY_DATASET_ID in scripts/build_phenotypes.py
- add hla_associations to the live-dataset query
- reload phenotypes and datasets

NOTE A THIRD TRAIT-COLUMN CONVENTION
hla_associations names its trait column 'phenotype', not 'trait' or 'trait_original'. So a join from phenotypes is p.trait_original = h.phenotype. The .19 work already documents the trait-vs-trait_original trap prominently; this adds a third spelling and the datasets.yaml table block should say so, or an agent will write h.trait and get zero rows silently - the exact failure this epic keeps rediscovering.
close_reason:
Drift check scope now derived from VIEWS. db worktree e0cb42d, suite worktree b99b509. phenotypes 32,611 -> 35,327, datasets 888 -> 889. 65 tests pass. One reviewer verified against production, one fix round.

THE GUARD NOW ACTUALLY FAILS - verified empirically in three directions, not by reading: unmapped live dataset -> exit 1; real list -> exit 0 at 35,327/889; live list minus finngen_hla -> exit 1 with two errors. An injected view enters scope with no other edit. Scope went from 9 hardcoded tables to 12 derived views.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN BEAD, both right:
1. peak_to_gene was WRONGLY excluded - here and in .19, where the claim originated. It does carry a dataset column (constant FinnGen_ATACseq, already mapped). Only variant_annotation and gene_annotations genuinely lack one. I repeated the stale claim without checking. Now in scope.
2. phenotypes_v/datasets_v needed excluding for a reason nobody had noted: they are PRODUCTS of the build under test, so a VIEWS-derived scope is self-confirming unless they are excluded.

CAUGHT IN REVIEW: the fail-open reintroduced ONE LEVEL UP. The regex parsing VIEWS returned a SHORT list, silently, for 'VIEWS = [...] + EXTRA', 'VIEWS.append(...)' and 'VIEWS += [...]'. A short list is not a crash - it produces valid SQL over fewer views and the loader runs clean. Now ast-based, rejecting any rebinding, extension or method call on VIEWS. Three new tests, one per case.

HLA DECISION: finngen_hla gets its own 2,716 phenotype rows rather than resolving through FinnGen_R14. My bead suggested the opposite. All 2,712 HLA codes ARE R14 endpoints, so the premise held - but datasets carries a finngen_hla row and the documented join is p.dataset = <view's dataset> AND p.trait_original = <code>; without those rows it returns zero rows silently for the one dataset this bead exists to fix, and an agent would need to know out of band that finngen_hla is secretly R14. The implementer first argued from R12 precedent (2,315 shared codes); review judged that the weaker argument since R12 is a separate phenotype set that happens to share codes, and the comment now leads with the zero-rows argument instead.
Cost quantified: 2,716 rows (7.7%), no fan-out on the datasets side, and the trait_original-alone fan-out hazard worsens 2.34x -> 3.34x on a pre-existing hazard the docs already warn about.

HLA JOIN WARNING was needed and is now correct. Master's block gave no key. An earlier draft said USING fails because 'the column names differ on both sides' - factually wrong and wrong in the direction that matters, since hla_associations_v DOES carry a dataset column. Only the trait column differs.

uv.lock: REMOVED, not committed. No repo in the suite tracks a lock file, and the Dockerfile installs with 'uv pip install --system -r pyproject.toml' which ignores it entirely - committing it would imply a reproducibility the build does not have. Adding it to .gitignore would make that durable; not done, out of scope.

LEFT UNDONE: wording nits batched to genetics-results-suite-5r2. 4 of the 2,716 finngen_hla phenotype rows have no hla_associations rows (AB1_EBV, AB1_SYPHILIS, AB1_PNEUMOCYSTOSIS, C3_ASTROCYTOMA_WIDE) - they come from the R14 metadata file, a systemic property of building phenotypes from metadata rather than anything new here, 0.15%.
Side-finding filed: genetics-results-suite-e47 (sync-datasets.sh silently no-ops from a worktree, which is how the db repo ended up serving a registry missing hla_associations_v).

title: Five by-gene BigQuery MCP tools emit unlabeled rows and their download link raises
description:
Found while reviewing genetics-results-suite-4h6.11 on 2026-08-07, verified independently. PRE-EXISTING - the SDK work did not cause it.

db-api returns query rows POSITIONALLY, not as dicts: genetics-results-db/api/main.py:579 builds rows.append([_serialize_value(v) for v in row.values()]) and column names travel separately in a 'columns' key (main.py declares rows: list[list[Any]]).

Five executor methods take result.get('rows', []) and pass it on without ever carrying 'columns':
  executor.py:910   get_asm_qtl_by_gene            -> {gene}_asm_qtl.tsv
  executor.py:1053  get_open_chromatin_by_gene     -> {gene}_open_chromatin.tsv
  executor.py:1114  get_variant_effect_by_gene     -> {gene}_variant_effect.tsv
  executor.py:1193  get_mpra_by_gene               -> {gene}_mpra.tsv
  executor.py:1251  get_mpra_pip_concordance_by_gene -> {gene}_mpra_pip_concordance.tsv

TWO CONSEQUENCES, both live today:

1. The MODEL receives 'results': [[...], [...]] - bare positional lists with no column names. It has to guess which value is which column, for five tools covering ASM-QTL, open chromatin, variant effect and MPRA by gene.

2. The DOWNLOAD RAISES. Those five set _download_data = {'results': <list of lists>}, and llm_service.py _convert_to_tsv takes the 'results' branch, which does headers = list(results[0].keys()) - AttributeError on a list. The 'columns'/'rows' branch immediately above it would have worked, but these five do not populate it.

Note the other ~20 _download_data sites pass genuine list-of-dicts and are fine. Only the five BigQuery-backed by-gene tools are affected - they are the ones that go through query_database rather than results-api.

RECOMMENDED FIX (one change fixes the model surface, the download, and the SDK together): in those five methods, zip 'columns' with each row to build list-of-dicts before putting it in 'results'. That changes the MCP payload shape from list-of-lists to list-of-dicts for these five tools - which is why it needs a decision rather than being folded into .11 silently. The current shape is broken, so this is a bug fix rather than a behaviour change, but it does alter what the model sees.

genetics-results-suite-4h6.11 works around it on the SDK side only, leaving the MCP surface as-is.
notes: CORRECTION to the close reason: the beads-visibility defect was filed as genetics-results-suite-xwf, not 'nk8'. That ID was written before the bead was created and does not exist.
close_reason:
Fixed at the root on the user's explicit instruction. genetics-mcp-server worktree 45c729e. Suite 1194 -> 1208 passed, 74 deselected, 0 failed.

Right shape per consumer rather than one shape for both:
- model-facing results: dicts built by zipping columns positionally (capped set, cheap, and it is what makes values interpretable)
- _download_data: the {columns, rows} form that _convert_to_tsv already supported, avoiding materialising up to 100k dicts

llm_service.py needed NO change - the working branch was already there, immediately above the one these five were hitting. Verified by running real payloads through _convert_to_tsv and checking the TSV header, not by inspection.

A columns/row length mismatch now fails loudly rather than mislabelling, since zip truncates silently. Four cases covered including a row arriving as a DICT rather than a sequence, which would otherwise zip column names against dict keys and produce plausible-looking garbage.

No other executor method has the same shape problem - grep confirmed exactly five call sites; the other ~20 download sites pass genuine results-api JSON objects.

SDK unaffected in behaviour but needed one adjustment: _frame's orient='row' construction was wrong once these payloads carry dicts, and now re-flattens against columns so columns decides order and schema in every branch. with_metadata is KEPT - an empty result has no row to take names from, so columns is still what preserves schema, and truncated is still what makes the SDK raise instead of returning a silent prefix. All three SDK properties verified by existing tests.

Filed while fixing: genetics-results-suite-nk8 (agents dispatched into a sibling repo's worktree cannot see this beads database).

title: results-api trusts a forgeable identity header from any pod in the namespace
description:
Found by adversarial security review of the sandbox design (genetics-results-suite-4h6.5), verified independently 2026-08-07.

TWO pre-existing facts combine into an authentication bypass:

1. genetics-results-api/app/core/auth.py get_verified_user() falls back to get_authenticated_user() when no Authorization header is present. get_authenticated_user (line 30-36) reads the raw X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email header and does nothing but split it on ':'. There is no validation that the request came from auth-gateway.

2. k8s/network-policies/policies.yaml allow-ingress-results-api contains a rule with ports but NO from clause:
     ingress:
     - ports:
       - port: 4000
   A from-less rule admits ALL sources. So results-api on 4000 is reachable from any pod in the genetics namespace, bypassing auth-gateway entirely.

results-api runs REQUIRE_AUTH=true, so auth is genuinely enforced - which is exactly why the fallback matters. auth-gateway does handle the header correctly at the edge (blanks it at auth-gateway.yaml:120, sets it from the verified oauth2-proxy email at 145/163/178/210), so EXTERNAL traffic is safe. The hole is namespace-internal.

CURRENT SEVERITY: latent. Every pod in the namespace today runs trusted first-party code, so nothing exploits it.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: the code-execution sandbox (epic genetics-results-suite-4h6) puts LLM-authored, prompt-injectable code inside that namespace with results-api as an ALLOWED egress destination. That converts this latent hole into an exploited one: a script can skip its scoped token entirely, send X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email: accounts.google.com:anyone@finngen.fi with no bearer, and get fully authenticated results-api access - summary statistics, LD, sumstats ranges - under a forged identity, with no session attribution, no audience binding, no token lifetime and no cost cap.

FIX (do not do these blind - the from-less rule may be load-bearing for the GCP load balancer health checks, which is probably why it is there):
(a) make the X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email path conditional on a trusted-proxy marker that only auth-gateway can set, rather than on the header alone.
(b) tighten allow-ingress-results-api so the from-less rule is scoped, after confirming what actually needs it (LB health checks, bff, monitor).

Same pattern is worth checking on bff (allow-ingress-bff at policies.yaml:35-42 has the identical from-less shape on port 5000).
notes:
STEP 1 COMPLETE 2026-08-10, read-only investigation. Findings below; step 2 is now unblocked and FILE-ONLY (nothing applied to the live cluster).

MY LB-HEALTH-CHECK HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG. Health checks do NOT reach results-api and no ipBlock is needed. results-api is ClusterIP; the only NodePort service is auth-gateway; the only Ingress (genetics-suite, 35.201.123.9) has two rules, both backending auth-gateway:8080; backend-configs.yaml defines only auth-gateway-hc-config.

KUBELET PROBES ARE EXEMPT from NetworkPolicy on this cluster (ADVANCED_DATAPATH / Dataplane V2). Proven empirically: db-api and oauth2-proxy both have httpGet probes and only podSelector-scoped ingress policies, and both have been 1/1 Running for 2d22h. The inline comment on allow-ingress-bff claiming the from-less rule is needed for kubelet probes is FALSE.

WHAT THE FROM-LESS RULE IS ACTUALLY CARRYING - two pod sources, nothing else:
- auth-gateway, via its @api_bearer named location (auth-gateway.yaml:122 proxy_pass to results-api:4000). This is the programmatic bearer-token path.
- bff (bff.yaml:31 GENETICS_API_URL=...:4000/api). This is the browser /api/ path.
Neither appears in any 'from' clause anywhere, so deleting the from-less rule would kill the entire browser UI and all bearer-token clients.
chat-backend, mcp-server and monitor all survive without it - they are already explicitly allowed (monitor via its own monitor-policy.yaml, confirming this bead's suspicion).

CRITICAL MECHANICAL NOTE FOR STEP 2: allow-ingress-results-api is a TWO-RULE list and the from-less one is the SECOND. The fix is a MERGE of the two rules, not a deletion. Deleting the from-less rule alone leaves chat-backend/mcp-server working and SILENTLY KILLS THE UI.

allow-ingress-bff CONFIRMED identical from-less shape on port 5000. Sole caller is auth-gateway (auth-gateway.yaml:149). No other reference in k8s/** or the whole genetics-results-browser repo. bff is not probed by monitor either.

THE AUTH BYPASS IS REAL AND WORSE THAN THIS BEAD STATED. Traced: server.py:133 mounts the API router with Depends(auth_required) -> dependencies.py:47 -> require_auth is true -> not a public endpoint -> get_verified_user (auth.py:125) -> get_bearer_token_user returns None immediately with no Authorization header (auth.py:70-72) -> falls back to get_authenticated_user (auth.py:30-36), which does request.headers.get(...).split(':')[-1] with NO validation -> returns a non-None email -> authenticated.

THE ALLOWLIST IS NEVER CONSULTED ON THIS PATH. config.allowed_emails / allowed_email_domains are checked only at auth.py:119, inside the Google-JWT branch. So the forged identity is not even constrained to finngen.fi - ANY STRING WORKS. REQUIRE_AUTH=true does not block it; it is precisely what routes the request into get_verified_user.

Attacker needs one HTTP request and no token:
  GET http://results-api.genetics.svc.cluster.local:4000/api/v1/...
  X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email: accounts.google.com:anyone@finngen.fi

It also POISONS ATTRIBUTION: middleware_usage_logging.py:25-33 prefers the raw header over the resolved auth identity, so the forged email is what lands in endpoint_access.

BASELINE TRAFFIC, 7 days, 800 endpoint_access records: 780 as 'mcp-tool' (the shared internal secret), 7 real @finngen.fi emails, 13 blank. Nothing anomalous. The real-email rows are bff pass-throughs carrying BOTH the user header and the internal bearer, so auth actually resolved via the bearer.

PROPOSED SCOPED RULE for step 2 - merge into ONE rule with four podSelectors (auth-gateway, bff, chat-backend, mcp-server) on port 4000. No ipBlock. For bff: a single podSelector for auth-gateway on port 5000.

OUT OF SCOPE, FILED SEPARATELY - note these are the REAL ids; an earlier version of this note cited placeholders '8ma' and 'q7f' which never existed:
- genetics-results-suite-k4t: four MORE from-less rules (frontend:3000, chat-backend:8000, mcp-server:8080, auth-gateway:8080). Only auth-gateway genuinely needs one, and scoping IT needs an ipBlock, not a podSelector. Now blocks genetics-results-suite-4h6.8.
- genetics-results-suite-fdd: GOOGLE_TOKEN_AUDIENCE is the public gcloud CLI client ID, so the audience check binds nothing.

RE-READ policies.yaml IMMEDIATELY BEFORE EDITING - another agent is concurrently editing this repo.
close_reason:
Landed across THREE repos, all file-only, NOTHING APPLIED to the live cluster:
  genetics-results-api      a36d3d0  auth gate + allowlist + normalisation
  genetics-results-browser  078bb61  bff passthrough attaches the internal bearer
  genetics-results-suite    4f82a17  merged ingress rules + ordered-rollout docs
New worktrees were created for the api and browser repos on branch worktree-db-only-architecture; neither existed before.

*** DEPLOY BFF FIRST. THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THIS TICKET. ***
State table, every row verified by EXECUTING the relevant code (old auth.py from git for the bff-only row, not the new one):
  neither        -> works, but the header alone authenticates (the vulnerability)
  bff only       -> WORKS. Old API checks the bearer first -> mcp-tool; the usage log reads the header directly so attribution stays the real user. A valid RESTING state, not a brief window - no transitional dual-accept mode needed.
  results-api only -> TOTAL LOCKOUT. Every non-variants browser request 401s.
  both           -> works, real user is the authenticated identity again.
Rollback reverses: results-api first, bff second. deploy.sh restarts everything at once with NO ordering between them, so a combined full deploy is UNSAFE - bff must go via rollout.sh first. Recorded in suite docs/project-spec.md, suite README.md, a header comment in scripts/rollout.sh, the API spec and the browser repo's CLAUDE.md and README.

THE HOLE WAS WORSE THAN THIS BEAD STATED. Traced: server.py:133 -> dependencies.py:47 -> require_auth true -> get_verified_user (auth.py:125) -> get_bearer_token_user returns None with no Authorization header -> get_authenticated_user does headers.get(...).split(':')[-1] with NO validation -> authenticated. THE ALLOWLIST IS NEVER CONSULTED on that path (checked only at auth.py:119 inside the Google-JWT branch), so the forged identity was not even constrained to finngen.fi - ANY STRING authenticated. It also poisoned attribution, since middleware_usage_logging prefers the raw header over the resolved identity.

STEP 1 REFUTED THE ASSUMED REASON FOR THE FROM-LESS RULE. LB health checks do NOT reach results-api - it is ClusterIP, the only NodePort service is auth-gateway, and both Ingress rules backend auth-gateway:8080. So NO ipBlock was needed. Kubelet probes are EXEMPT from NetworkPolicy on this cluster's ADVANCED_DATAPATH, proven empirically (db-api and oauth2-proxy have httpGet probes, podSelector-only policies, Running for days). The allow-ingress-bff comment claiming probes needed it was false. What the rule actually carried: auth-gateway's @api_bearer location and bff, neither of which appears in any from clause anywhere.

THE MERGE WAS MECHANICALLY DANGEROUS: allow-ingress-results-api was a TWO-RULE list with the from-less one SECOND. Deleting it alone would have left chat-backend and mcp-server working and SILENTLY KILLED THE BROWSER UI.

TWO INDEPENDENT VALIDATORS CAUGHT A LOCKOUT IN THE FIRST VERSION, with live evidence rather than argument: named researchers (vivaswat.shastry@, masahiro.kanai@, mervi.aavikko@finngen.fi) in endpoint_access within the last two weeks on /api/v1/resources, /resource_metadata, /search, /credible_sets_by_region, /summary_stats - none @is_public. The premise that bff sends header and token together was FALSE. nginx diverts anything carrying Authorization to @api_bearer BEFORE bff, and bff's two upstream paths split: upstream.ts attaches the token but drops browser headers and serves only the three variants routes; passthrough.ts forwards the header and attached nothing. Fixed on the SENDING side.

PRECEDENCE, now the design of record:
  marker + allow-listed identity header -> that email
  marker + identity header NOT allow-listed -> 401
  marker alone (or a literally-empty header) -> mcp-tool
  Google JWT / user API token -> unchanged
  identity header alone -> 401  <- the hole
Reject-not-downgrade on the not-allow-listed case is deliberate: a downgrade would let any of the four workloads holding INTERNAL_API_SECRET launder a refused identity into a working, service-attributed request, with the refusal never surfacing.

MARKER STRENGTH, stated plainly: it is exactly as strong as INTERNAL_API_SECRET, which bff, chat-backend, mcp-server and results-api all mount. NOT a boundary against those four - a compromised mcp-server could still assert an allow-listed email, buying log attribution rather than authorization, since it already has identical API access as mcp-tool. IT IS a hard boundary against everything else in the namespace, which is the actual 4h6 threat: the sandbox has egress to results-api and no secret.

ALLOWLIST LOCKOUT RULED OUT BY OBSERVATION: live bearer-auth-allowed ConfigMap is ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS=finngen.fi, ALLOWED_EMAILS empty; oauth2-proxy is OAUTH2_PROXY_EMAIL_DOMAINS=finngen.fi with an empty allowed-emails file. Both render from OAUTH_EMAIL_DOMAIN/OAUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS at deploy.sh:67-70, and deploy.sh applies configs before rolling deployments, so there is no stale-ConfigMap window. PRECONDITION for the future: they are consumed by independently-applied objects, so a partial deploy can desync them.

ALSO FIXED: compare_digest ran on str, which raises TypeError on non-ASCII, in ASGI middleware BEFORE routing - a 500 rather than a 401; it compares bytes now. _email_allowed was case-sensitive while oauth2-proxy lowercases (User@FinnGen.fi admitted by one, rejected by the other), and a literal '*' means allow-all to oauth2-proxy but matched nothing here. The resolved identity is normalised to trimmed lower case in BOTH resolvers, so one person cannot split across several identity strings in endpoint_access. The bff guard keys on a Bearer PREFIX mirroring nginx's ~* '^Bearer ' exactly - case-insensitive, anchored, literal single space, not \s - so the divert and the guard partition the request space with no gap and no overlap; keying on header presence would have let Authorization: Basic suppress the marker and 401.

A VALIDATOR FINDING I REFUTED, recorded so it is not re-raised: it claimed the merged rule locks out the monitor CronJob. It does not - monitor-policy.yaml carries its own additive allow-ingress-results-api-from-monitor (app=monitor, port 4000) and NetworkPolicies union. The validator read only policies.yaml. Its underlying point was fair though, and the misleading 'exactly the four in-cluster callers' comment now names monitor-policy.yaml explicitly, because the dangerous reading is someone later deleting that rule as redundant.

DOC CORRECTION MADE: an earlier doc claim that an empty-valued identity header resolves to mcp-tool is FALSE in the reachable case. nginx omits a header set to '', so a literally-empty value is unreachable; an empty $email produces 'accounts.google.com:', which is truthy, resolves to '', fails the allowlist and 401s. Unreachable in production because oauth2-proxy cannot 200 /oauth2/auth without an email. Corrected rather than left asserting a safe outcome the code does not produce.

STILL OPEN, filed separately:
- genetics-results-suite-k4t (P1, blocks 4h6.8): four more from-less rules. Fixing only results-api and bff leaves chat-backend:8000 and mcp-server:8080 reachable from the sandbox, and someone must check whether they share this same forgeable auth code. auth-gateway's rule genuinely needs an ipBlock.
- genetics-results-suite-fdd (P1): GOOGLE_TOKEN_AUDIENCE is the public gcloud CLI client ID, so the audience check binds nothing.
- docs/code-execution-security.md records this hole as OPEN in three places, all now stale: ~586-591 ('it is a hole, not a pattern'), ~911-921 items 1 and 2, and the ~1379 table row 'Blocked on genetics-results-suite-fad'. Owned by genetics-results-suite-4h6.10.

Tests: API 436 -> 482 collected, 56/56 in the two server-free files (the rest need a live results-api). Browser bff 57 -> 60, typecheck clean.

title: Node pool pinning was never applied to any live profile - autoscaler eviction fix is not in effect
description:
Found while reviewing the sandbox security design (genetics-results-suite-4h6.5) on 2026-08-07.

Commit 6db94e8 'fix: stop autoscaler evicting chat-backend mid-stream' pinned min_node_count == max_node_count == 2 to stop the autoscaler adding a node for a rollout and then scaling it down ~15 min later, evicting chat-backend mid-SSE. Its own message says: 'terraform/terraform.tfvars is gitignored, so the pinning is captured in terraform.tfvars.example; the live tfvars has been updated separately and still needs a terraform apply.'

That never happened. Verified 2026-08-07:
- terraform/terraform.tfvars (active): min_node_count = 1, max_node_count = 3
- terraform/terraform.tfvars.finngen: min = 1, max = 3
- terraform/terraform.tfvars.daly: min = 1, max = 2
- terraform/terraform.tfvars.example (the ONLY one tracked in git): min = 2, max = 2
- kubectl get nodes: exactly ONE e2-standard-4 node running

So the pinning exists only in the tracked example and in docs/project-spec.md. No live profile has it, and terraform apply was never run. The eviction bug the commit describes is still live: a full deploy.sh surges to 3951m CPU / 13.6 GiB against one node's 3920m / 12.97 GiB allocatable, so the autoscaler still adds a node and still scales it back down.

The graceful-shutdown half of that commit (terminationGracePeriodSeconds 300, preStop sleep 10, uvicorn --timeout-graceful-shutdown 280) IS live - it is in the committed manifest. So the symptom is partly mitigated but the cause is not.

Also: docs/project-spec.md 'Node pool sizing' (~line 274-310) documents the 2/2 pinning as current fact. It is wrong, and the CLAUDE.md rule says a doc is stale the moment it enumerates something the code no longer matches.

Decide and then do ONE of:
(a) apply the pinning to the live tfvars profiles and terraform apply, or
(b) keep autoscaling and update docs/project-spec.md to describe reality, accepting the eviction risk or mitigating it another way (PodDisruptionBudget, which the namespace still lacks entirely).

Blocks genetics-results-suite-4h6.10 (node pool budget for the sandbox): the gVisor-on-a-separate-pool cost argument in docs/code-execution-security.md assumes the 2/2 pinning, and that premise is currently false.
notes:
USER DECISION 2026-08-07: keep autoscaling (min 1 / max 3), fix the docs to describe reality, and add a PodDisruptionBudget. Do NOT apply the min==max==2 pinning.

Rationale for the choice: the namespace has NO PodDisruptionBudget at all today and every deployment is replicas:1, so node auto-upgrade and repair interrupt chat regardless of whether the pool is pinned. A PDB addresses a failure mode pinning does not, at no standing cost. The graceful-shutdown half of commit 6db94e8 (terminationGracePeriodSeconds 300, preStop sleep 10, uvicorn --timeout-graceful-shutdown 280) IS live and already cushions the eviction symptom.

SCOPE OF THIS BEAD IS NOW:
1. Rewrite docs/project-spec.md 'Node pool sizing' (~274-310) to describe the real 1-3 autoscaling. It currently documents a 2/2 pinning as current fact, which is false in every live profile. Keep the surge-budget arithmetic (3951m vs 3920m, 13.60 vs 12.97 GiB) - that part is accurate and still explains why a rollout adds a node.
2. Add k8s/poddisruptionbudget.yaml covering at minimum chat-backend, and decide whether results-api/db-api/mcp-server need one. With replicas:1, minAvailable:1 blocks voluntary eviction entirely - confirm that is what is wanted versus maxUnavailable:0, and note it will make node drains require manual intervention.
3. Update terraform.tfvars.example so the tracked file stops claiming 2/2.

Do NOT run terraform apply for this bead.
close_reason:
Landed as 0149f85 (suite). FILES ONLY - nothing applied to the cluster, no terraform apply. The PDB manifest reaches the cluster only when someone next runs deploy.sh.

DELIVERED per the user decision in the notes (keep autoscaling 1/3, fix docs, add a PDB; do NOT pin min==max==2):
1. docs/project-spec.md 'Node pool sizing' rewritten for real 1/3 autoscaling.
2. k8s/disruption-budgets/budgets.yaml (new) - PDBs for chat-backend and results-api, maxUnavailable: 0, unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy: AlwaysAllow. Plural-named subdir matching the existing k8s/ convention.
3. scripts/deploy.sh - added the apply line. deploy.sh applies directories individually rather than k8s/ recursively, so without it the manifest would never reach the cluster.
4. terraform/terraform.tfvars.example - 2/2 -> 1/3.

THE BEAD'S ARITHMETIC WAS WRONG AND SO WAS THE DOC'S. The old section claimed peak 3951m / 13.60 GiB from a '2651m / 7.91 GiB steady state' that no profile produces. Re-derived from k8s/deployments/*.yaml and reproduced INDEPENDENTLY by a second agent against the live node: allocatable 3920m / 12.96 GiB (13591704Ki), namespace 1300m / 5.6875 GiB, system overhead 876m / 1.327 GiB. Recreate set is exactly chat-backend, rag-service, keycloak-postgres; the other 8 are RollingUpdate with no maxSurge override (25% of 1 rounds up to 1).

TWO CONCLUSIONS CHANGED:
- daly overshoots MEMORY ONLY, not both axes. ENABLE_RAG defaults false UNCONDITIONALLY at deploy.sh:8 and is NOT profile-derived (only ENABLE_KEYCLOAK is, line 98), so a default daly deploy is 10 deployments peaking at 3826m / 13.45 GiB - UNDER the 3920m CPU allocatable. Only ENABLE_RAG=true (4076m) overshoots CPU.
- finngen, the LIVE profile, FITS on one node: 3226m / 12.20 GiB, 0.76 GiB headroom. Left as an OPEN QUESTION in the doc rather than resolved: if finngen fits, the mechanism 6db94e8 describes should not have fired on the live profile, so the original eviction's trigger is unexplained. Three candidates named (CronJob overlap eating the sub-1 GiB margin - schedules verified non-coinciding, 30 2 * * * vs 0 */8 * * *; an auto-upgrade/auto-repair drain rather than a scale-down; a since-lowered request) with a discriminating test.

THE PDB COSTS MORE THAN THIS BEAD'S NOTES CLAIMED. The notes said 'at no standing cost' and that is FALSE. Filed as genetics-results-suite-0v5 (P1) for a user decision. GKE's autoscaler doc has two branches: a node whose pods CAN move but will not drain gracefully is force-terminated after one hour (>= 1.32.7-gke.1079000; cluster is v1.35.6-gke.1250000), but a node whose pods CANNOT move is NEVER SELECTED for scale-down, with NO time bound. maxUnavailable: 0 on replicas: 1 is permanently unsatisfiable, so it lands in the second branch. results-api is RollingUpdate and migrates to the surge node every rollout, pinning it: the pool ratchets to 2 nodes and stays, silently reproducing the min==max==2 steady state the user rejected.

THE EXEMPTION THAT WOULD HAVE MADE chat-backend FREE DOES NOT HOLD - I reported it as fact before checking, correcting here. k8s/volumes/pvc-chat-data.yaml is ReadWriteOnce on standard-rwo, a ZONAL PD from pd.csi.storage.gke.io: attached to one node at a time, not bound to one. The restored PV chat-data-restored-pv has NO nodeAffinity at all, not even topology.gke.io/zone. Neither deployment has nodeSelector, nodeName, affinity, topologySpread or tolerations. So chat-backend can ratchet too; Recreate only means it never CREATES a surge node.

GENUINE DEADLOCK FOUND AND FIXED, independent of 0v5: under the default IfHealthyBudget, 'healthy' means Ready, so at maxUnavailable: 0 a CRASHLOOPING pod is also unevictable - serving nothing while blocking maintenance. AlwaysAllow set on both, verified accepted at policy/v1 on this cluster via kubectl explain plus client dry-run. Its own hole is documented: the same Ready definition means results-api's ~5 min startupProbe window (failureThreshold 60, periodSeconds 5) is UNPROTECTED - exactly the window that PDB was justified by.

CLAIMS SCOPED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: the one-hour bound is documented for SURGE upgrades, which this pool uses (terraform/gke.tf sets no upgrade_settings). BLUE_GREEN differs - pods deleted in the delete-blue-pool phase, soak defaulting to 1h, extendable to 7 days. Node auto-repair marked UNCONFIRMED: Google documents the one-hour drain bound but does NOT say PDBs are honoured during it. Whether the autoscaler's scale-down simulation models unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy also could not be confirmed, so the manifest does not claim a crashlooping pod releases the ratchet.

CONFIRMED SAFE: PDBs cannot block deploy.sh rollouts - the Deployment controller deletes pods directly, bypassing the Eviction API. First-ever deploy fine (namespace from terraform/kubernetes.tf, applied first; a PDB may legally precede its Deployment). rollout.sh needs no change. No kubectl drain/cordon anywhere in scripts/. Selectors verified against the real pod templates - not silently useless. This config cannot wedge the cluster or defer a security patch: upgrades and repair have hard one-hour-per-node ceilings, control-plane upgrades never drain workload pods, and a PDB is deletable with one command.

LEFT TO genetics-results-suite-4h6.10: docs/code-execution-security.md is stale in four places (~207-209 and ~1043-1045 assert the 2/2 pinning and the wrong figures as the premise of the gVisor cost argument; ~214-216 cites the pinning rationale; ~1193 lists 'No PodDisruptionBudget in the namespace' as open, now false). title: Run the paired benchmark and decide the rollout on the numbers
description:
Run replay_benchmark.py with the code arm against the current all-tools arm.

Report DISTRIBUTIONS. A code-execution arm scores ~1 tool call by construction, so tool-call count alone is a dishonest win condition. The gate is the combination:
- iterations per turn (baseline median 2, p90 6, p95 8, max 25)
- total input+output tokens and USD (baseline mean 2.01 USD/turn; 13.5% of turns over 5 iterations consume 35% of spend)
- wall-clock to first token and to done (watch for regression on the 36% of turns that are single-iteration today - a sandbox adds fixed cost there)
- script failure rate and retry-loop count
- LLM-judge quality via analyze_conversations --force, which must not regress

Expected shape of the win, from the 2026-08-07 measurement: cost and tail latency, NOT a dramatic median tool-call drop. Median context grows 39k -> 117k tokens between iteration 1 and 7+ while the uncached share rises 11% -> 52%; keeping intermediate data out of context is the mechanism being tested.

Kill criterion: if the code arm does not beat the baseline on cost AND does not regress quality, keep it behind the profile rather than defaulting it on.
