title: Implement run_analysis: submit code, stream stdout, enforce caps
description:
The single tool that replaces the data-access grid. Submits model-authored Python to the sandbox, streams stdout back, and enforces wall-clock timeout, output size cap and memory limit per the security doc.

Failure handling matters as much as the happy path: the benchmark counts script failures and retries because a failing script costs a full model roundtrip, and the realistic risk is a bimodal distribution (most turns at 1-2 roundtrips, a tail at 8+ from debugging loops). Return errors as structured, actionable messages (traceback plus the relevant stub) so the model repairs in one attempt rather than three.

Files: genetics-mcp-server/src/genetics_mcp_server/tools/definitions.py, tools/executor.py, sandbox client (new).
notes:
HANDOFF FROM genetics-results-suite-4h6.9 (2026-08-10): the scoped credential exists; .14 calls it.

MINTING CONTRACT (genetics-mcp-server/src/genetics_mcp_server/sandbox_token.py):

    from genetics_mcp_server.sandbox_token import mint_execution_tokens
    minted = mint_execution_tokens(user=<authenticated email>, session_id=<chat session id>)
    minted.execution_id   # uuid4 - the jti of BOTH tokens
    minted.db_api         # aud: db-api
    minted.results_api    # aud: results-api
    minted.expires_at     # iat + 300

Optional execution_id= kwarg when .14 has already chosen the /scratch directory name. THE TWO MUST BE THE SAME VALUE - execution_id IS the /scratch/<id> directory name, and that identity is what makes the 4h6.12 log join close across chat-backend, the sandbox SDK and db-api.

RAISES SandboxTokenUnavailable when SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY is unset. Deliberately an exception, not a None: every fallback from 'no sandbox token' is either 'send no credential' or 'send the shared secret', which are the two outcomes the whole mechanism exists to prevent. Do NOT catch it and proceed - fail the execution.

WHAT .14 STILL OWNS (all of the transport; .9 implemented none of it):
- The tokens travel in the BODY of the POST from chat-backend to the sandbox, minted fresh per execution. NEVER pod env, never a ConfigMap, never a Secret - chat-backend cannot set env on a running pod, and putting them in the pod spec would turn a 5-minute per-execution token into a static pod-lifetime credential.
- The supervisor places them in the FORKED CHILD, never in its own environment (residual #7 - the supervisor holds no credentials at any point).
- Preferred over the child's environment: a mode-0600 file under /scratch/<execution-id> that the SDK reads once and unlinks, because /proc/<pid>/environ is readable by any process with the same uid. Under a distinct child uid the supervisor must chown it to the child at 0400 BEFORE the fork - see section 2's 'Permission contract'.
- The sandbox must receive NEITHER INTERNAL_API_SECRET NOR SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY. Only chat-backend (sign) and db-api/results-api (verify) mount the signing key; the sandbox Deployment (4h6.7) must mount neither.

VALIDATION ALREADY IN PLACE: db-api api/sandbox_auth.py (aud db-api), results-api app/core/sandbox_token.py (aud results-api). Both reject on expiry, wrong audience, wrong issuer, bad signature, missing claim, or backdated iat, with a hard 401 and no fallthrough.

NOT IMPLEMENTED BY .9, DO NOT ASSUME IT: the per-credential BigQuery row/byte caps (50 GB per query, 200 GB per jti, 25 000 rows, results-api response-byte ceiling) are genetics-results-suite-4h6.28. .14's own caps - wall-clock timeout, output size cap, memory limit - are unrelated and still .14's. The hook 4h6.28 will use already exists: db-api leaves the principal on request.state.principal, results-api on request.state.sandbox_principal.

DEPLOY: SANDBOX_ENABLED is 'false' in k8s/deployments/db-api.yaml and results-api.yaml. The deploy that creates the sandbox Deployment must flip it to 'true', and only after create-secrets.sh has run - with it true and either secret unset, both services sys.exit(1) by design.

=== HANDOFF FROM genetics-results-suite-0lf (2026-08-12), REQUIRED, NOT OPTIONAL ===
THE SDK MUST SEND ITS PER-EXECUTION TOKEN, NOT INTERNAL_API_SECRET. This transport is one of the two things that actually closes 0lf's hole; the other is 4h6.7 (the Deployment must stop giving the sandbox that secret).

WHY: results-api charges its four per-execution counters only when _sandbox_principal resolves an HS256 sandbox token. sdk/client.py today authenticates with INTERNAL_API_SECRET from env, which is_internal_caller accepts - so the request is served with NO ACCOUNTING. MEASURED: 200 with sandbox_budget._executions == {}.

TWO TRAPS, both measured:
1. THE ROLLOUT HAZARD IS NOT WHAT THE DOCS ORIGINALLY SAID. They claimed flipping SANDBOX_ENABLED before this lands makes every SDK call 401. It does not - they return 200 as mcp-tool. So the flip LOOKS SUCCESSFUL while the control is inert. Do not use a green smoke test as evidence that this landed; assert on the execution map.
2. mcp-server's executor.py:288-292 builds {"Authorization": ...} if api_secret else {} - a SILENT no-header fallback. Once the anonymous surface is closed that becomes a bare 401 with no local signal. Filed separately, but it sits directly on this transport's path, so fix or account for it here.

ACCEPTANCE: a request from the SDK must appear in sandbox_budget's execution map. A boolean check that "auth works" is exactly the test shape that let this bypass through unnoticed in the first place.

A TEST WILL FAIL WHEN YOU GET THIS RIGHT, deliberately:
  genetics-results-api tests/test_anonymous_surface.py::test_an_internal_secret_caller_is_served_but_not_accounted
Update it in the same commit.

title: Extract ToolExecutor data methods into an importable genetics SDK
description:
Turn the existing per-tool executor methods into a stable Python package the sandbox imports: genetics.credible_sets(gene=..), genetics.coloc(..), genetics.sumstats(..), genetics.ld(..), genetics.mpra(..), genetics.sql(..) etc. This is a refactor, not a rewrite - the HTTP/tabix/BigQuery logic in executor.py (4,679 lines) is kept, only the entry points change.

One function per data product, with the by_gene/by_variant/by_region/by_phenotype distinction becoming ARGUMENTS rather than separate names. That grid is what produced 42 near-duplicate tools in the first place.

Note five methods already issue server-written SQL against BigQuery (executor.py:878, 1021, 1080, 1159, 1197) - use them as the pattern, and fix their f-string SQL interpolation while moving them.

Files: genetics-mcp-server/src/genetics_mcp_server/sdk/ (new package), tools/executor.py.
close_reason:
genetics SDK landed. genetics-mcp-server worktree commit 5f1ba16. Suite 1024 -> 1165 passed, 74 deselected, 0 failed. Two reviewers (behaviour-preservation + adversarial security), one fix round.

17 SDK functions replace 42 entry points, THIN over the existing executor - no HTTP/tabix/BigQuery logic moved, because the 42 MCP tools stay the production surface until .16.

TICKET FRAMING CORRECTED: the grid does not collapse completely. mpra_pip_concordance is a JOIN of credible_sets_v and mpra_v with a different row shape, so it stays its own function. normalize_gene_symbols was initially omitted on the grounds its 'unresolved' list cannot be a DataFrame - review disagreed (one row per input with a null symbol is the tidy form) and it is now included, along with lookup_phenotype_names and get_dataset_display_names, without which a script cannot resolve the trait CODES that credible_sets/summary_stats/gene_burden return.

CAUGHT IN REVIEW - none of these failed a test:
- The five BigQuery paths returned TRANSPOSED, STRINGIFIED frames. db-api returns rows positionally with names in a separate key; the SDK used pl.from_dicts. It did not raise - it fabricated column_0/column_1 names and coerced everything to str. Green only because two test mocks disagreed about the same upstream.
- 61 caller-controlled URL path segments were unencoded, and httpx normalises dot segments: mpra(variant='../../admin/users') reached an arbitrary results-api endpoint on the same host WITH THE INTERNAL BEARER ATTACHED. Strictly wider than the SQL hole the task was written to close.
- configure() forwarded a caller-supplied base URL into the client carrying INTERNAL_API_SECRET - one injected line exfiltrated the shared secret.
- The SDK had reintroduced the silent 500-row prefix its own design note argues against, and discarded the truncated flag.
- exome(gene=, resources=) accepted and DROPPED resources, silently returning unfiltered results.

VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY, not by reading: percent-encoding does NOT break colon-separated identifiers (real uvicorn+FastAPI server; uvicorn unquotes scope['path'] before Starlette routes; no route uses a path converter; auth-gateway's proxy_pass has no URI part so nginx forwards verbatim). '.' and '..' now work where they used to 404. _gene_window_cte generates byte-identical SQL for all five methods. The MCP payload is byte-identical without with_metadata. The import-isolation test uses a real subprocess.

REFRAMING WORTH KEEPING: sql_safety guards the MCP surface, NOT the SDK. A script can call sql() with arbitrary SQL, so what actually stands between it and BigQuery is db-api's SELECT-only check, its table allow-list and MAX_BYTES_BILLED. The hardening is still worth having where values are model-chosen and there is no escape hatch.

CONSEQUENCE FOR .9/.14: configure() is concrete evidence for what code-execution-security.md asserts - if the SDK runs inside the sandbox, INTERNAL_API_SECRET must not be there at all, since a script that can import can read os.environ. The scoped token is load-bearing, not optional hardening.

LEFT UNDONE: genetics-results-suite-a6u (int(limit_sql) re-parses a SQL token; latent, unreachable today), genetics-results-suite-25p (no test proves URL round-trip against a real ASGI server), genetics-results-suite-bef (the MCP-side positional-rows bug, needs a payload-shape decision). title: Scoped short-lived credential for sandbox to db-api
description:
The sandbox must never hold INTERNAL_API_SECRET. That secret authenticates the service, not the request, and a script that can read it can reach db-api directly and forever.

Design and implement a per-request, short-lived, audience-scoped token minted by chat-backend and injected into the sandbox execution environment for the lifetime of one script. db-api validates it alongside the existing shared secret. Include an expiry short enough that a leaked token is worthless (minutes), and make the token carry the session id so db-api logs attribute queries to a conversation.

Note the fail-open behaviour in db-api today (docs/project-spec.md: unset INTERNAL_API_SECRET disables auth with a startup warning) - the new path must NOT inherit fail-open.

Files: genetics-results-db/api/main.py, genetics-mcp-server sandbox client, k8s manifests.
close_reason:
Landed as suite cbd2165, mcp-server e26fd82, db 2dc03be, results-api c70f7ee. Files only; NOTHING applied to any cluster, per the standing hold. Full tier: review + blind validation + test runner in parallel, one fix round, then a targeted re-review. No blocking findings survived.

WHAT LANDED. chat-backend mints one HS256 token per destination per execution -- audience-bound so a results-api token cannot be replayed at db-api, 300s TTL, carrying sub, the chat session id, and an execution id that is also the /scratch/<id> directory name so logs join across chat-backend, the sandbox SDK and both backends. db-api and results-api validate offline. SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY is deliberately NOT INTERNAL_API_SECRET; exactly three Deployments mount it (chat-backend signs, the two verifiers verify), mcp-server does not, and the sandbox holds neither.

Tests: MCP 1274 -> 1285 passed / 74 deselected; db-api 65 -> 102 passed; results-api 482 -> 516 collected with 87 auth tests green (that suite cannot run green on this VM - ~282 pre-existing data-dependent failures needing GCS or local data, spot-checked as unrelated).

ATTACKED WITH 30 HAND-ROLLED TOKENS against both validators with real PyJWT, not just the repo's own tests. Closed and confirmed: alg none; RS256/HMAC confusion; HS384/512 with the correct key; wrong key; empty signature; every required claim missing or null; missing/null/empty scope; cross-audience replay both directions; foreign iss; expiry; and a far-future exp with an ancient iat. That last is why the age check exists independently of exp - effective lifetime is 300s from iat regardless of what exp claims, boundary confirmed at 299 accept / 301 reject.

TWO MINTER INVARIANTS THE VALIDATORS WERE TRUSTING RATHER THAN ASSERTING, both found independently by two reviewers, neither forgeable without the key but both undercutting the attribution this credential exists to produce: an EMPTY-STRING sub, sid or jti validated (PyJWT's require option rejects only missing and null), and aud as a LIST validated (PyJWT treats list aud as membership), so one token could have been valid at BOTH backends - single-destination binding was a minter property, not a validator one. Both asserted now.

ZERO FORWARD CLOCK-SKEW TOLERANCE, fixed with leeway=5. PyJWT >= 2.10 raises ImmatureSignatureError when iat > now and leeway defaulted to 0, so any positive skew between chat-backend and a verifier rejected a freshly minted token. The doc's argument that the short TTL makes skew a non-issue covers exp, not iat. The 300s age bound is separate and stays exact - re-verified after the change - so the acceptance window grew only on the not-yet-valid side, to 305s of verifier wall-clock.

THE FAIL-OPEN IS ROUTED AROUND, NOT REMOVED. db-api still disables auth entirely with a startup warning when INTERNAL_API_SECRET is unset; that is pre-existing and out of scope. The sandbox branch sits AHEAD of that early return, so a malformed sandbox token can never degrade into the shared-secret comparison or into no-auth. require_sandbox_config() sys.exit(1)s when SANDBOX_ENABLED is true and either secret is missing, both-unset included, and a reviewer confirmed both calls are on the REAL startup path - db-api's main.py IS the entrypoint given CMD ["python","main.py"] over COPY api/ ., and results-api's runs at import of app.server, where run_server.py's except Exception does NOT swallow SystemExit.

THE OPERATIONAL HAZARD WAS THE SECRET ORDERING, NOT THE CODE ORDERING. The code claim held up under checking (the path is entirely new; minter-only and validators-only are both safe; a token meeting an old validator 401s). But the new secret gate made create-secrets.sh mandatory before the next deploy on every existing cluster, and that script implements reuse-or-generate for only five keys - an operator re-running it with just ANTHROPIC_API_KEY exported, exactly what the old error message invited, would have blanked admin-users, external-mcp-servers, the Slack webhook and four API keys. The gate now emits a targeted kubectl patch for the single missing key and names the clobber. Script untouched; -4pj owns fixing it.

SANDBOX_ENABLED IS NOW COUPLED TO THE SANDBOX EXISTING. test-network-policies.py, already a deploy gate from 4h6.8, asserts sandbox.yaml present => both verifier manifests set it true. Without that, landing 4h6.7 with the flags still false silently voids the whole fail-closed guarantee. IMPORTANT FOR 4h6.7: both flags must flip in the SAME commit that adds sandbox.yaml or every deploy aborts with exit 1 - verified both ways on a scratch copy, and recorded in 4h6.7's notes because the first symptom is an aborted deploy with no obvious cause.

DELIBERATE SCOPE SPLIT: the design doc's per-credential BigQuery caps (50 GB/query, 200 GB per jti, row and response-byte ceilings, plus a defaults-not-penalty inversion that changes behaviour for EVERY caller of both services) are NOT implemented. No bead owned them and the blast radius is far wider than a credential. Filed as 4h6.28; this bead ships the request.state hook they need. So the credential lands WITHOUT the spend controls the doc pairs it with.

OTHER DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS, all recorded in an 'As built' subsection of the doc: iss is required rather than optional; iat age is checked explicitly because PyJWT accepts an ancient iat when exp is future; scope is required-present but kept out of the decoder's require list so its absence logs distinctly; results-api reports sandbox:<user> rather than the bare email so a script is never mistaken for a verified human.

ACCEPTED RESIDUALS, now written down rather than implicit: the symmetric key means a compromise of db-api OR results-api can MINT tokens impersonating chat-backend (Ed25519 with the private half at chat-backend would remove this while keeping offline validation); rotation is NOT atomic across the three Deployments, so every sandbox execution 401s across a rolling restart; jti is recorded but not consumed, so a leaked token is replayable within its 300s window; and @is_public routes skip auth_required entirely, which is an ATTRIBUTION gap as well as an authorization one - no principal, no sid/jti on endpoint_access for those five routes, and 4h6.28's caps will not key there.

ONE REAL BUG FOUND IN THE LOGGING: the sandbox authorization line passed a string message, so GCPJsonFormatter copied only names in EXTRA_LOG_FIELDS and none of sub/sid/jti reached jsonPayload - the line went nowhere. Added the three names rather than dropping the extra, since endpoint_access does not cover the @is_public set. Verified there is exactly one extra= call site in the whole service and no dependency collides on those names.

NOT WIRED TO ANYTHING YET, by design: mint_execution_tokens has no caller. Transport into the sandbox - the POST body, the mode-0600 /scratch/<id> file, the chown-before-fork rule - is 4h6.14, handoff recorded in its notes. So 'the sandbox gets this instead of the shared secret' is unproven end to end until 4h6.7 and 4h6.14 land.

LEFT UNDONE, filed: 4h6.28 (the caps), 4pj (create-secrets.sh blanks eight optional secrets on re-run, plus its silent-regeneration-on-kubectl-failure path), zyi (db-api compare_digest on str - the last known instance of the bug fad and th2 each fixed elsewhere - and PyJWT being the only unpinned validator dep). Nits unfiled: the harness routes an unanticipated manifest shape to exit 1 rather than exit 2, and two stale docstring lines about where Google tokens are handled.

title: NetworkPolicy: sandbox egress allow-list, and mcp-server must not reach it
description:
Two directions, both required.

Egress FROM sandbox: db-api (8080) and results-api (4000) only. Deny all other egress including DNS-to-internet, so a script cannot exfiltrate query results or fetch code. Deny access to keycloak, keycloak-postgres, chat-backend and rag-service.

Ingress TO sandbox: chat-backend ONLY. mcp-server must be denied at the network layer, not just by omitting the tool - this is the user's explicit requirement that code execution not be reachable via MCP, and the suite spec already warns (docs/project-spec.md:237) that mcp-server sits on both sides of the db-api policy, so a tool-registration omission alone is not a boundary.

Add a test that asserts the mcp-server pod cannot open a connection to the sandbox Service.

Files: k8s/network-policies/sandbox-policy.yaml (new), docs/project-spec.md (Security section).
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-10.

Files: k8s/network-policies/sandbox-policy.yaml (new, 2 objects: allow-ingress-sandbox and
sandbox-egress), k8s/network-policies/policies.yaml (allow-ingress-db-api and
allow-ingress-results-api each gained an explicit 'app: sandbox' peer),
scripts/test-network-policies.py (new, offline), scripts/check-doc-drift.sh (sandbox ->
code-execution-security.md row, which CLAUDE.md's ownership table already declared but the
script did not mirror), docs/project-spec.md (Security section) and
docs/code-execution-security.md (three amendments, below).

LABEL CONTRACT (recorded in the policy file header, project-spec, and 4h6.7's notes):
app: sandbox / containerPort 8080/TCP / Service 'sandbox' 8080 -> targetPort 8080.

deploy.sh needed NO change: it already runs 'kubectl apply -f network-policies/' on the
whole directory.

DNS: doc and policy AGREE - no kube-dns rule, hostAliases instead. No contradiction found.

TESTING: scripts/test-network-policies.py runs offline (no cluster, no network) and asserts
across ALL files in k8s/network-policies/ (union semantics) that no rule selecting the
sandbox admits mcp-server or the monitor, no sandbox rule is from-less, egress is exactly

The LIVE mcp-server -> sandbox connection test the bead asks for could not be run (nothing is

metadata-server question and a check that Cilium translates ClusterIP -> pod IP before egress
policy evaluation (sandbox-egress uses podSelector and depends on that ordering).

NOT DONE HERE (owned elsewhere): the sandbox Deployment/Service (4h6.7), the node pool
(4h6.10), the scoped credential (4h6.9), the MCP tool-registration exclusion and its test
(4h6.16).

WHAT LANDED. k8s/network-policies/sandbox-policy.yaml (allow-ingress-sandbox + sandbox-egress), an app: sandbox peer added to allow-ingress-db-api and allow-ingress-results-api, scripts/test-network-policies.py as an offline manifest harness now gating deploy.sh, a check-doc-drift.sh row, and the project-spec Security section. Two SEPARATE egress rules, not one: `to` x `ports` cross-products within a rule, so a merged form would also have permitted db-api:4000 and results-api:8080. No ipBlock anywhere, which is the ONLY thing closing pl.write_parquet('s3://...') -- 4h6.6 established polars ships the Rust object_store with its own HTTP/TLS stack, so no image-level control touches it. Both rules pin TCP, so all UDP including DNS is denied, matching the doc's hostAliases decision.

THE REVERSE DIRECTION WAS REQUIRED AND IS EASY TO MISS: an egress allow-list alone leaves the data path dead, because each destination's own ingress policy must admit the sandbox too. Both amended inside the from: lists -fad and -k4t just scoped; neither became from-less, no port widened.

BOTH HALVES 401 TODAY. results-api requires -fad's marker, db-api requires the same bearer, and the sandbox deliberately holds neither. Reachability is in place; authorization is not, until 4h6.9. Recorded in both policy files and both docs rather than left to be rediscovered. The sandbox was NOT given the internal secret.

NO METADATA COVERAGE IS CLAIMED, and the doc's previous claim that default-deny covered it was an over-claim, now corrected. Nothing permits 169.254.169.254 so standard semantics deny it, but link-local is the same class already PROVEN exempt in the ingress direction on this dataplane, and egress enforcement to link-local has never been tested here. THE LOAD-BEARING CONTROL IS 4h6.10's GKE_METADATA POOL, so 4h6.10 must land before the sandbox ever runs untrusted code. 4h6.26 was widened to cover the node IP and 169.254.4.6, not just the metadata IP.

A LABEL MISMATCH IN 4h6.7 FAILS OPEN, ASYMMETRICALLY, and this is the most important thing for whoever does .7. This is the namespace's first and only egress policy -- 17 live policies, all Ingress -- so a pod missing the selector has NO egress policy applying and gets the allow-all default: full internet, DNS, metadata, API server, no event, no log. Ingress meanwhile fails closed and loudly, which invites precisely the wrong fix (relax ingress to match the pod, leaving egress uncovered). Contract is app: sandbox, containerPort 8080/TCP, Service sandbox 8080->8080, pinned in the policy header, project-spec and 4h6.7's notes, and the harness cross-checks the Deployment the day it appears.

THE HARNESS SHIPPED WITH TWO WAYS TO PASS WHILE mcp-server COULD REACH THE SANDBOX. Both found independently by two reviewers, both reproduced by mutation, both closed:
- policyTypes is OPTIONAL and Kubernetes INFERS it, so a policy admitting mcp-server with the field omitted was fully enforced by the API server and wholly invisible to the harness. Now inferred per SetDefaults_NetworkPolicy: Ingress ALWAYS, Egress only when egress is NON-EMPTY. The truthiness matters -- `egress: []` with no policyTypes would otherwise pass the deny-by-default check while the cluster left egress unrestricted.
- peer_selects returned False for any peer carrying a namespaceSelector, with an inline comment stating the wrong inference. `namespaceSelector: {}` matches every pod in every namespace, mcp-server included. IT WAS ALSO WIRED TO NOTHING -- no CI, and -rxw records no installed git hooks -- so the label-contract check would never have fired. Now gates deploy.sh before the network-policies apply AND before any deployment, so an abort cannot leave a sandbox pod running without its policy. Blocking on exit 1, warning on exit 2. Exit 2 had to be fixed in a third round: sys.exit(<str>) exits 1, so a machine without PyYAML would have aborted a production deploy while blaming a security control.

Now stated as settled with a /32-per-Service contingency and an explicit prohibition. Reasoned from config, not observed, because no pod in the cluster currently carries an egress policy; empirical confirmation is in 4h6.26. Also confirmed no other policy engine can widen any of this: enable-cilium-network-policy false, no CRD.

title: Build the paired A/B replay benchmark harness
description:
New scripts/replay_benchmark.py. POSTs recorded turn sequences to /chat/v1/chat with secret=true (chat_api.py:295, so nothing is persisted) under two tool_profile arms in a PAIRED design - both arms in one execution so model drift cannot confound the comparison.

Report DISTRIBUTIONS, not just medians: production is heavily tail-weighted (median 2 iterations but p95 8, max 25). Metrics per arm: iterations/turn, tool calls/turn, wall-clock to first token and to done, input/output/cache tokens, USD. Plus code-execution-specific counters: script failure rate (non-zero exit, timeout, exception) and retry-loop count, since a failing script costs a full roundtrip.

Baseline to beat, measured 2026-08-07 over 916 turns since 2026-05-01: iterations median 2 / p90 6 / p95 8; tool calls per turn median 4 / p90 12; mean 2.01 USD per turn; 13.5% of turns >5 iterations consuming 35% of spend; median context 39k tokens at iteration 1 growing to 117k at iteration 7+ with uncached share rising 11% -> 52%.

Files: genetics-mcp-server/scripts/replay_benchmark.py (new).
notes:
HANDOFF from .1 (2026-08-07): .4's plan is to POST with secret=true 'so nothing is persisted' (chat_api.py:295). With .1 landed, secret=true ALSO means no chat_turn_metrics row is written — .1 deliberately skips metrics entirely for secret chat because secret chat is a privacy promise to the user. So the replay harness CANNOT read its numbers out of chat_turn_metrics when running secret.

Two options, pick one and record it: (a) read iterations/tokens/cost off the SSE stream itself — llm_service.py already yields a 'usage' StreamChunk per iteration carrying iteration, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_input_tokens, total_output_tokens, context_window, context_percent; or (b) run non-secret against a throwaway copy of chat_history.db and read chat_turn_metrics.

(a) is probably better: it needs no DB at all and works against any deployment.

ENVIRONMENT TRAP: in a fresh genetics-mcp-server worktree, 'uv run pytest' resolved to the pyenv shim rather than the worktree venv and imported genetics_mcp_server from the MAIN CHECKOUT, silently testing unmodified source. Run 'uv sync --extra dev' first, then assert the module resolves inside the worktree before trusting any test result.
close_reason:
Paired A/B replay harness built. genetics-mcp-server worktree fbf121e. Suite 1165 -> 1194 passed, 74 deselected, 0 failed. One reviewer, one fix round.

BUILD ONLY - running it against a deployment is task .23, separately gated. Default base URL is localhost, --dry-run issues zero requests, secret=true is a hard-coded literal with no flag or env override.

THREE PREMISE CORRECTIONS:
1. The usage chunk's input_tokens is the WHOLE CONTEXT (input_tok + cache_read + cache_create), not billed input. Cached tokens are derived by subtracting total_input_tokens.
2. COST CANNOT BE COMPUTED EXACTLY FROM THE STREAM. Cache reads and creations are folded into one number and never separated, yet they differ by exactly 12.5x in price. The harness reports an INTERVAL (all-cached-as-reads to all-cached-as-creations) rather than fabricating a figure; since every per-token price lies between those, the true cost is provably inside it. This weakens the metric .23 gates on - production data shows the cache-read share swinging 11% to 52% across a turn, so the interval will not be narrow. Fix filed as genetics-results-suite-n3p: emit cache_read/cache_create on the usage chunk. Both are already computed and already logged one line away.
3. An unpriceable --model was silently priced as Sonnet by cost.py's fallback. Now warns and returns null.

CAUGHT IN REVIEW - either would have INVERTED the result:
- Replayed history dropped tool_results. Production pushes them back as a user turn (LLMChat.tsx ~595-599); without them _sanitize_tool_blocks strips every tool_use block from the replayed assistant turn as orphaned, so from turn 2 the model saw an answer from thin air. Tool results are the BULK of the context growth this epic exists to measure (39k -> 117k, uncached 11% -> 52%), and the bias was ASYMMETRIC - the arm making more tool calls lost more context, compressing the measured gap toward zero. A code-execution arm would have looked no better than the status quo.
- The paired design was never used in the ANALYSIS. Distributions were built per arm independently over ok turns, so an arm failing on the hard, late, expensive turns kept only its cheap early ones and its medians dropped BECAUSE it failed. Recording failures is not excluding them from the comparison. Matched subset (ok in both arms) is now the headline; marginals survive explicitly labelled not-comparable.

ALSO FIXED: a wedged stream could keepalive past the per-turn timeout forever (httpx read timeout is per-read and sse-starlette comments reset it, so the TimeoutError handler was dead code); a whole-case exception collapsed N turns into 2 records; a turn with no usage chunk contributed a fake tool_calls=0, which EVERY turn would do against a deployment defaulting to OpenAI (--provider added); MIN_N_FOR_PERCENTILE[90] was 11 not 10 through float error.

VERIFIED CORRECT BY REVIEW: tool calls counted from real tool_use blocks never the prose markers (.2's imitation finding); the cost interval is a true bound computed the right way round; semaphore scope makes arms of one case non-overlapping; arm alternation recorded per case; per-turn failure aborts only that case+arm.

DESIGNED-IN GUARDS: percentiles flagged unreliable when n(1-p) < 1 so a p90 from 9 cases is not presented as stable; script_runs/script_failures/retry_loops look for a chunk that does not exist yet and stay None with an explicit NOT MEASURED reason, so the eventual code-execution arm cannot win trivially on a silent zero.

LEFT UNDONE: wording nits - UNMEASURED_REASONS missing script_runs, the doc's section heading path, arm_order_per_case keyed on case_id (two cases sharing a session_id would collide), two different Ns on one screen, and no test asserting --dry-run issues zero requests. Fold into genetics-results-suite-5r2.

title: Record per-turn metrics in chat_history.db instead of only logs
description:
Today iterations/tokens/cost exist ONLY as a log line (llm_service.py:1011 'Chat complete: ... iterations=N total_input_tokens=..') scraped from the genetics_chat_logs sink. content_json cannot substitute: it flattens a whole turn into one assistant record, so parallel vs sequential tool calls are indistinguishable and roundtrips are NOT derivable from it (verified 2026-08-07: roundtrips-per-turn maxed at 1 for every session).

Add a chat_turn_metrics table to chat_history.db keyed by (session_id, message_id) holding: iterations, tool_call_count, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read, cache_create, cost_usd, wall_ms, tool_profile, model. Write it where the Chat complete line is emitted.

Files: src/genetics_mcp_server/db/chat_history_db.py (table + migration, follow the existing PRAGMA table_info pattern), src/genetics_mcp_server/llm_service.py (~line 1011).

This is the measurement substrate for the whole epic - do it first.
close_reason:
chat_turn_metrics table landed. genetics-mcp-server worktree commit 18f919d. Suite 993 -> 999 passed, 74 deselected, 0 failed.

THE TICKET'S KEYING PREMISE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED. (session_id, message_id) is unavailable at write time: PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON (chat_history_db.py:90) and the assistant chat_messages row is POSTed by the client only AFTER the stream ends, so an FK always aborts; and ChatPage.tsx handleFirstExchange creates the session only after the first exchange completes, so EVERY conversation's opening turn streams with session_id null. Both verified against genetics-results-browser. Surrogate PK + partial unique index on message_id instead. message_id alone suffices - it is the client-generated chat_messages PK.

CAUGHT IN REVIEW, NOT BY TESTS (suite was green before both):
- Cross-user overwrite: the upsert keyed on client-supplied message_id with no ownership scope. Reproduced empirically - user B overwrote user A's row, cost zeroed 9.99 -> 0.0, session reassigned, silently. Fixed with a user_id column (from auth_required, never the request body) guarding the DO UPDATE; a conflicting write from another user inserts nothing and logs.
- The write sat between the Chat complete log and the 'done' chunk that carries the content the client persists. sqlite's 5s busy timeout could delay every turn's stream terminator, and the await was a new cancellation point that could lose that chunk on disconnect - the exact opposite of this task's own constraint. Moved after the yield; chat_api's async for has no break/early return so the generator still runs it.
- message_id was unbounded; a 2,000,000-char id was accepted and persisted to the shared RWO PVC. Now max_length=64.
- turn-1 rows (session_id NULL) survived delete_session forever, so 'delete my conversation' left a permanent record that a conversation happened and what it cost.

VERIFIED CLEAN EMPIRICALLY, not by inspection: asyncio.to_thread + sqlite is safe because _connections is keyed on threading.get_ident() so no connection crosses a thread (24 threads, 0 errors, 25 connections); secret chat writes nothing; a DB failure is swallowed without breaking the stream; CancelledError still propagates.

DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS: metrics are NOT recorded for exception/timeout/client-disconnect endings (they never reach the Chat complete line either, and partial accumulators would bias cost-per-turn downward). Max-iterations IS recorded - it is the 13.5%-of-turns / 35%-of-spend tail the epic exists to measure.

title: ChatRequest.system_prompt lets any authenticated user replace the entire system prompt
description:
Flagged during planning of the Instructions epic (genetics-results-suite-s5y) and deliberately left out of its scope. Now in scope on its own.

genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/chat_api.py:215 declares ChatRequest.system_prompt, used verbatim at ~line 458:
    system_prompt = request.system_prompt or default_system_prompt(settings.app_name)
There is no allow-list, no admin gate, no length bound. Any authenticated caller can replace the ENTIRE system prompt for their turn - discarding every grounding, citation, truncation and out-of-scope rule the default prompt establishes.

This is a strictly larger hole than the feature built next to it. The Instructions epic went to some length to make user-authored text safe: the body is resolved server-side by id so it never travels on the request, it is capped, it is wrapped in an envelope with a trailing guardrail, and it is scoped to presentation only. All of that is bypassed by a field sitting two lines away that accepts arbitrary prompt text with no constraints at all.

SCOPING ALREADY DONE - nothing in the suite sends it:
- genetics-results-browser: zero references in src/ or bff/
- the only senders anywhere are tests (tests/test_chat_api.py:356 test_chat_custom_system_prompt, and the stream-truncation harness which passes system_prompt=None)
- llm_service.stream_chat(system_prompt=...) is a separate INTERNAL parameter that chat_api populates with the assembled default+verbosity prompt. That stays; only the request-level override is the hole.

Preferred fix: remove the field from ChatRequest entirely. Pydantic ignores unknown fields by default, so a caller still sending it is silently ignored rather than 422'd - a graceful removal with no client breakage.

Before removing, confirm there is no external consumer: the chat API is also reachable with a bearer API token (see the Authorization: Bearer path that bypasses the BFF), so check whether any script, notebook or sibling repo drives it directly. If a legitimate need exists, the fallback is an admin gate plus a length bound rather than leaving it open.
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit f8302b9. Suite 935 passed / 74 deselected across two seeds.

Removed rather than gated, after confirming across all six repos that nothing sends it - not the browser, not the BFF, not any script; only a test. Pydantic ignores unknown keys, so a caller still sending it is ignored rather than 422'd. A side benefit: block 0 of the two-block cached system prompt is now unconditionally identical across users, which its cache design already assumed.

THE SAME CAPABILITY EXISTED IN A SECOND FORM, found independently by both reviewers and fixed here too: the Anthropic path filtered client-sent system-role messages but the OpenAI path did not, and provider is client-selectable with OPENAI_API_KEY wired into the pod, so a system-role message landed AFTER the server prompt where recency favours it. Rather than filter per provider, ChatMessage.role is now Literal['user','assistant'] - the authority boundary is the request model. Both provider filters stay as defence in depth because stream_chat is reachable with raw dicts.

422 rather than a silent drop: the history endpoint already rejects those roles, so no caller has reason to send one, and quietly discarding an injection attempt hides it from the caller and the logs.

Verified no real flow breaks: the browser builds message history only from stored rows plus hardcoded user literals; chat_history.py:414 rejects non-user/assistant at persistence and add_message has exactly one caller, so no system-role row can exist to be replayed; fork copies roles from rows that already passed that check.

Corrected a false claim I had put in the bead and the docs: the chat API is NOT reachable with a per-user API token. auth_required accepts the IAP/oauth2-proxy header or a Bearer INTERNAL_API_SECRET resolving to identity 'mcp-tool'; per-user tokens are validated only by the internal-only /tokens/validate that the /mcp path consumes. The security argument is unaffected - any IAP-authenticated user could already do it.

Follow-ups filed: the tool-descriptions authz gap, and the assistant-role length bound.

title: mcp-server cannot reach db-api: all BigQuery-backed MCP tools fail
description:
The standalone mcp-server (/mcp path, used by external MCP clients) has NEVER been able to reach db-api, so every BigQuery-backed tool returns 'BigQuery API URL not configured'.

Confirmed failing live on daly (2026-07-21): query_bigquery, get_bigquery_schema, get_asm_qtl_by_gene, get_open_chromatin_by_gene, get_variant_effect_by_gene.

Two independent causes, BOTH must be fixed:
1. BIGQUERY_API_URL is set in k8s/deployments/chat-backend.yaml but has never existed in k8s/deployments/mcp-server.yaml (git log -S confirms no commit ever added it).
2. NetworkPolicy allow-ingress-db-api (k8s/network-policies/policies.yaml:137-151) admits only app=chat-backend; monitor-policy.yaml adds monitor. mcp-server is not permitted, so even with the env var set the call would be blocked.

Manifests are profile-independent => affects finngen AND daly equally.

chat-backend is unaffected (has the env var and is allowed by policy), so the web UI agent's BQ tools work; only the standalone MCP server is impacted.

Note these tools are BigQuery-by-design: results-api has no by-gene open_chromatin endpoint, so executor.py:824 resolves gene->coords via gene_annotations_v.

Decision needed: opening db-api to mcp-server is a network-isolation change, not just a config fix.
notes: Config fix committed cb18545 (BIGQUERY_API_URL on mcp-server.yaml + mcp-server podSelector on allow-ingress-db-api NetworkPolicy). Left OPEN: takes effect only after cluster rollout (scripts/rollout.sh mcp-server + re-apply NetworkPolicy). Close after deploy verifies BigQuery-backed MCP tools work.
close_reason: Verified fixed live on finngen (2026-07-24). After deploy: running mcp-server has BIGQUERY_API_URL set; allow-ingress-db-api NetworkPolicy admits app=mcp-server; from pod mcp-server-75fd7c8644 TCP connect to db-api:8080 succeeds (was TimeoutError), /health=200, and POST /query 'SELECT 1 AS ok' returns 200 rows=[[1]]. BigQuery-backed MCP tools can now reach db-api.

title: Phase 0: decide ChromBPNet row-scale thresholding policy
description: Count ChromBPNet variant-score rows (132 contexts x variants, potentially billions). Decide thresholding (significant/non-zero only, or top-N per context) before sizing tabix/BQ. Biggest scale risk. Gates the Marderstein munge task.
design:
RECOMMENDED DEFAULT thresholding policy (empirical cutoff + row counts to be CONFIRMED once data is downloaded — blocked on .1). Keep this task OPEN.
Problem: ChromBPNet = 132 contexts x all variants (~3 billion predictions in the paper). Do NOT store the full cross-product.
Default:
- ChromBPNet -> variant_effect (model=chrombpnet), LONG. Emit a row only for (variant, context) pairs that pass a significance/effect threshold, NOT all 132 contexts per variant. Prefer the per-context significance calls provided by the Synapse release if present; else keep per-context empirical mlog10p >= 3 (p <= 1e-3) OR abs(chrombpnet_logfc) in the top 1 percent per context. Always set is_significant and mlog10p so the cutoff is transparent and re-filterable.
- Retain a variant if significant in ANY context (so by_variant lookups return it); emit its passing contexts, plus optionally its single top context.
- FLARE -> variant_effect (model=flare): keep the FULL released FLARE prioritized-variant set (already curated and far smaller); pan-context rows with cell_type/tissue NULL.
Rationale: bounds storage to variants with a real predicted effect somewhere (millions, not billions) — exactly what the query needs. Empirical step (after .1): count rows at this cutoff, confirm the significance fields the release actually provides, adjust cutoff to a sane table size.
close_reason: Decision made: default thresholding policy adopted (recorded in --design). Empirical row-count confirmation happens inside the Marderstein munge task (.13), which applies and tunes the default; no separate gate needed.

title: mcp-server's executor sends no Authorization header at all when INTERNAL_API_SECRET is unset
description:
Found while validating genetics-results-suite-0lf.

genetics-mcp-server, src/genetics_mcp_server/tools/executor.py:288-292 builds its headers as roughly:
    {"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_secret}"} if api_secret else {}
A silent no-header fallback. If INTERNAL_API_SECRET is ever unset or empty in an mcp-server or sandbox environment, every call goes out ANONYMOUS instead of failing.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW, and why it is worth fixing before the sandbox ships:
1. It is the ONE place a genuinely anonymous in-cluster caller of results-api could exist today. 0lf's architectural argument ("nothing entering from outside the cluster can be anonymous at results-api") holds; this is the in-cluster exception.
2. It is INVISIBLE in telemetry. The usage log's fallback reads state.authenticated_user, which on an @is_public route is never set, so an anonymous caller logs identically to an internal-secret one - measured 246/246 NULL user_email on GET /api/v1/rsid/variants over 90 days. You cannot tell from the logs whether this is happening.
3. After 0lf's change, when SANDBOX_ENABLED flips those calls become a bare 401 with no local signal explaining why - a misconfiguration presenting as an auth failure at the far end.

This is the same defect class as genetics-results-suite-4h6.9's "never fall back to no credential" contract; read that bead's reasoning before fixing.

FIX: fail loudly at startup rather than silently at request time. Assert INTERNAL_API_SECRET is present and non-empty when the executor is constructed (or at import, matching whatever that repo does elsewhere), with a message naming the variable. Do NOT just make the request raise - a startup assertion turns a latent runtime failure into an immediate, obvious one.
Check whether the same shape exists elsewhere in that repo while you are there.

title: SANDBOX_ENABLED gates the anonymous surface, so disabling the sandbox re-opens six routes
description:
Found while validating genetics-results-suite-0lf, and flagged independently by both validators.

0lf made results-api's anonymous surface collapse to /healthz when SANDBOX_ENABLED is true. is_public_endpoint keys DIRECTLY on config.sandbox_enabled, so the incident lever and the security lever are now the same switch - and the security side FAILS OPEN.

Setting SANDBOX_ENABLED=false to kill the sandbox during an incident silently re-opens all six routes to anonymous access: /api/v1, /api/v1/auth, /api/v1/variant_sets, /api/v1/variant_sets/{name}, and GET+POST /api/v1/rsid/variants. Nobody flipping that flag under pressure will expect it, and the variable name does not advertise it.

The two controls can also legitimately differ: you may want the anonymous surface closed as defence in depth with NO sandbox, or the sandbox live while an external integration still calls /api/v1 anonymously. There is no independent override today.

FIX, cheapest first:
(a) a separate ANONYMOUS_SURFACE_MINIMAL flag defaulting to on, with SANDBOX_ENABLED merely FORCING it - decouples the two at no cost and keeps the safe default;
(b) make the collapse one-way for the process lifetime, so a flag flip cannot widen it;
(c) leave it and document - not recommended, because the failure is triggered by a routine operational action.
(a) is the obvious one. The counter-argument in the current docstring - that the flip should ride the deploy that creates the sandbox - argues for a DEFAULT, not for a hard coupling.

Do this BEFORE the flag is ever flipped in anger. Production impact is nil today (SANDBOX_ENABLED is "false" on both services), and this is the cheapest moment.

So disabling the sandbox during an incident can no longer widen the surface, which was the whole bead. The regression itself is pinned - reverting the operator to `if config.sandbox_enabled:` fails 4 tests.

THE DEFAULT IS ON, AND THAT CHANGES BEHAVIOUR AT THE NEXT results-api DEPLOY rather than at sandbox rollout. The manifest already declares it with a comment, so the "visible in a manifest diff" goal is met either way.

THE ORDERING IS THREE SERVICES, NOT TWO, AND NOTHING ENFORCES IT:
    browser BFF  ->  mcp-server  ->  results-api

title: Run auth-gateway's nginx as uid 101 so the master is non-root, not just capability-reduced
description:
Follow-up to genetics-results-suite-eau, which hardened auth-gateway's containers but left the nginx MASTER running as root.

WHY THIS IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. eau measured both states: the nginx WORKER - the process that parses internet traffic - was already Uid 101 / CapPrm 0 / CapEff 0 even under the empty securityContext, because setuid() from root without PR_SET_KEEPCAPS clears the capability sets. eau improved the MASTER (CapEff 0xa80425fb -> 0xc1, NoNewPrivs 0 -> 1), which never touches attacker input. So the gateway is not meaningfully harder to exploit than before eau; it is only less useful once exploited. Making the master non-root is what changes that.

WHAT IT TAKES, measured not guessed: `--user 101:101` with the unchanged config FAILS at mkdir("/var/cache/nginx/client_temp") (13: Permission denied), because /var/cache/nginx is root:root 0755 in the nginx:alpine image and client_temp does not exist. So it needs an emptyDir mounted over /var/cache/nginx plus runAsUser: 101 (and runAsNonRoot: true). Once the master is non-root it never chowns or setuids, so CHOWN, SETUID and SETGID can ALL be dropped - the whole `add:` list eau had to keep goes away.

Consider readOnlyRootFilesystem in the same pass, since the tmpfs work overlaps: nginx also wants a writable pid path (the config already sets pid /tmp/nginx.pid) and /var/run.

RISK, and why eau deferred it: this is the internet-facing pod and the change is larger than adding a securityContext. Test it the way eau did - locally with docker against the REAL rendered ConfigMap (extract data["nginx.conf"], run deploy.sh's substitution with both injectable fragments populated, stub all eight cluster-local names with --add-host) and drive real traffic: /healthz, the auth_request subrequest path, the Bearer bypass, and a 20 MB POST to force a client_body_temp write. eau's scratch scripts show the shape.

Rollout is safe by construction: replicas: 1 with no strategy block gives maxUnavailable 0 / maxSurge 1, so a failure leaves the current gateway serving. But deploy.sh runs `kubectl rollout status ... || true`, so a stall does not fail the deploy loudly - watch it.

title: create-secrets.sh dies with exit 2 and no message when terraform.tfvars is absent, which is the normal case in a worktree
description:
Found while fixing genetics-results-suite-4pj; pre-existing, untouched there. Same worktree/tfvars family as genetics-results-suite-82s.

scripts/create-secrets.sh:33 derives the config profile with:
  PROFILE="$(grep -E ... "${TFVARS}" 2>/dev/null | sed ...)"
The script runs under `set -euo pipefail`. When terraform/terraform.tfvars is absent, grep exits 2, pipefail propagates it, the assignment fails, and set -e kills the script.

MEASURED: EXIT=2, zero kubectl calls, zero applies, and NO MESSAGE AT ALL - it dies before even the "Creating genetics-secrets..." echo. The 2>/dev/null suggests the author intended a missing file to be tolerated, so this is likely not the intended behaviour.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS:
- terraform.tfvars is gitignored and main-checkout-only, so absent is the NORMAL case in any .claude/worktrees/* checkout.
- create-secrets.sh runs BEFORE deploy.sh in the normal flow, so this silent exit-2 is the FIRST thing an operator hits - earlier than the clear, explicit tfvars guard that deploy.sh:22-25 already has and that 82s extended.
- It is fail-safe, not dangerous: nothing is written and no cluster call is made. The defect is purely diagnostic - an operator sees an exit code and nothing else.

FIX: give it the same explicit guard deploy.sh has - test -f the tfvars and print a real error naming the file and the main-checkout/worktree distinction - or make the PROFILE derivation tolerate a missing file if that was the intent. Decide which, since they differ: one refuses to run without tfvars, the other runs with a default profile.

INFERRED, worth checking in the same pass: scripts/build.sh:20 and build-all.sh:21 carry the same grep-under-pipefail pattern, but wrapped in ${APP_NAME:-...}, so they only abort when APP_NAME is unset. Confirm before changing.
close_reason:
Landed as suite 9c0659e.

PREMISE CONFIRMED EXACTLY as the bead measured it: from this worktree, create-secrets.sh exits 2 with ZERO bytes of output and never calls kubectl - it dies before its first echo, because grep on a missing terraform/terraform.tfvars exits 2, pipefail propagates, and errexit kills the assignment.

THE OPEN DECISION, resolved: REFUSE, do not default. The script writes per-profile cluster secrets, so guessing the profile is the wrong failure mode. It now mirrors deploy.sh's guard - CONFIG_PROFILE wins if set, else the tfvars if present, else an error naming the file and the main-checkout/worktree distinction, exit 1.
CALLER ANALYSIS (the e47 lesson - a nonzero exit is only safe if you check who is under set -e): NOTHING executes create-secrets.sh. Every occurrence in the repo is prose - deploy.sh:205/213/233 only mention it in error text, README, project-spec, keycloak-apple-signin, code-execution-security, auth-gateway.yaml and test-network-policies.py are all strings. Operator-invoked only, so exit 1 cannot trip a caller.

THE BEAD'S INFERENCE ABOUT build.sh/build-all.sh WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE MECHANISM AND WRONG ABOUT THE CONSEQUENCE, which is the more valuable finding here. It reasoned they were safe because the grep is wrapped in ${APP_NAME:-...} so they "only abort when APP_NAME is unset". True - but UNSET IS THE NORMAL INVOCATION. MEASURED: `env -u APP_NAME bash scripts/build.sh monitor` -> exit 2, no output; build-all.sh -> exit 2 right after the worktree warning. So every build from a worktree died silently, not latently. Fixed with `|| true` inside the substitution so the documented FinnGenie fallback is finally reachable; verified APP_NAME can never go empty into a name (${APP_NAME:-FinnGenie} catches it and it is only ever a --build-arg, never an image tag or k8s object name).
SIDE EFFECT WORTH RECORDING: check-worktree-paths.sh:107-108 asserts these scripts "just silently fall back to APP_NAME=FinnGenie". That was FALSE when written and is TRUE now - an executable preflight's claim became correct retroactively. It needed no edit.

REVIEW CAUGHT THE GUARD REINTRODUCING THE SAME DEFECT ONE LAYER DOWN, which is the pattern this whole family keeps producing. PROFILE was never validated, so THREE paths silently resolved to "not daly" and skipped keycloak-secrets with no error: CONFIG_PROFILE=typo, the case slip CONFIG_PROFILE=Daly, and - worst - a tfvars PRESENT but lacking a config_profile line, which the new `|| true` turned from an exit-1 into a silent empty string. create-secrets.sh had become the ONLY entry point in the suite accepting an arbitrary profile; deploy.sh does not have the hole (an empty profile becomes ".tfbackend", which does not exist) and terraform/variables.tf:71 validates contains(["daly","finngen"]). PROFILE is now validated against that same set, empty rendered visibly as <empty>. The error text already advertised "(daly|finngen)" as a constraint it did not enforce; it does now.
Concrete failure that is now impossible: an operator on daly runs CONFIG_PROFILE=Daly, the output reads like a normal finngen run, and deploy.sh later takes the real profile from terraform output and starts keycloak with no secret to mount.

DELIBERATE SCOPE ADDITION, flagged rather than slipped in: a PRE-EXISTING greedy sed, folded in because it lands on the exact lines being changed and corrupts a --build-arg through the DOCUMENTED flow. build.sh:23, build-all.sh:31 and create-secrets.sh:44 used "\(.*\)" where deploy.sh:39 uses "\([^"]*\)".*. terraform.tfvars.example:13 SHIPS a trailing comment containing quotes, and deploy.sh:39 tells operators to copy that example. MEASURED against that exact line: APP_NAME=[FinnGenie" # product/brand name shown in UI and assistant persona (e.g. "GeneGenie for daly)], and config_profile likewise resolving to [daly" # ...] -> keycloak silently skipped. The review's judgement that "pre-existing and harmless" was wrong is correct. All three now use deploy.sh's spelling, so the suite has one.

NEW CAPABILITY, deliberate and bounded: CONFIG_PROFILE now lets create-secrets.sh run from a worktree with no tfvars, which was previously impossible (it died at exit 2 before any kubectl call). Precedence matches deploy.sh:34-41 exactly, the target cluster comes from kubeconfig not from this flag, every key is reuse-first so a re-run is non-destructive, and the value is now validated.

VERIFIED BY REPRODUCTION THROUGHOUT, never by reading, with stub kubectl/gcloud/docker PROVEN first on PATH via command -v (a previous agent reached the live GKE endpoint by assuming kubectl was absent when a real one sat at /usr/bin/kubectl): worktree/no-tfvars -> exit 1 with the message, zero kubectl calls; CONFIG_PROFILE=daly -> all three secrets written incl. keycloak; typo/Daly/tfvars-without-config_profile -> exit 1 loudly; commented and plain tfvars lines both extract correctly; no-tfvars build -> APP_NAME=FinnGenie. bash -n clean on all three scripts.

LEFT UNDONE, filed as genetics-results-suite-<sed-bead>: the `\s` in these sed BREs is a GNU extension that silently fails on BSD/macOS sed, and build.sh (unlike build-all.sh:25) does not call check-worktree-paths.sh, so a single-service build from a worktree falls back to FinnGenie with no warning at all. Also unfiled-but-noted: an unreadable (chmod 000) tfvars is now masked into the FinnGenie fallback rather than exiting 2 - accepted, since the prior behaviour was a silent exit 2 anyway.
DOC NIT LEFT FOR THE BATCH: project-spec.md's new text says "the same main-checkout/worktree message deploy.sh prints" - it is modelled on deploy.sh's apply guard, not identical to either of deploy.sh's two messages.

title: bd exports issues.jsonl to the main checkout, so every beads commit from a worktree is a silent no-op
description:
Found while committing genetics-results-suite-e22/re3. This is the THIRD instance of the same class as genetics-results-suite-e47 (sync-datasets.sh resolves sibling repos from the repo root) and genetics-results-suite-82s (terraform.tfvars is main-checkout-only): a tool run from a worktree silently resolves a path to the MAIN CHECKOUT and degrades without erroring.

MEASURED. `bd` prints "Exported N issues to /home/jkarjala/suite/genetics-results-suite/.beads/issues.jsonl" - the MAIN CHECKOUT path - even when invoked from .claude/worktrees/db-only-architecture. Byte comparison right now:
  worktree .beads/issues.jsonl   377,580 bytes, 180 issues
  main     .beads/issues.jsonl   692,758 bytes, 232 issues
The worktree copy is TRACKED and NOT gitignored (git check-ignore returns nothing), so it looks like the file under version control - but nothing ever writes to it from here.

CONSEQUENCE: every `git add .beads/issues.jsonl && git commit` step performed from this worktree this session was a NO-OP. git reports 'nothing to commit, working tree clean' immediately after a bd close, which reads as 'already up to date' rather than 'you staged a file nobody wrote'. The branch's committed bead state is 52 issues stale and drifts further with every close.

WHY IT IS PROBABLY NOT LOSING DATA TODAY: the authoritative store is Dolt, not the jsonl - the jsonl is an export for git-based sync. So bead state survives in Dolt regardless. INFERRED, not measured: nobody is currently reconstructing state from the git copy. Confirm that before deciding this is cosmetic.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS: the failure is silent and the misleading signal ('working tree clean') is the one an agent or a human uses to conclude the step succeeded. Anyone who ever restores bead state from this branch's git history gets a snapshot missing everything closed since the worktree was created.

TO DO:
1. Decide whether the worktree's .beads/issues.jsonl should be gitignored (making the no-op honest), or whether bd should export relative to the invoking worktree.
2. If bd's behaviour is intentional (single canonical export next to the Dolt store), remove the 'git add .beads/issues.jsonl' step from the session-close protocol in CLAUDE.md, since it cannot do anything from a worktree and its apparent success is misleading.
3. FIX THE CLASS, not the instance. Three independent tools now degrade this way from a worktree, and each was found by accident rather than by a check. A single preflight that asserts 'this tool resolves paths inside the worktree I am in' would have caught all three. That is the real deliverable; the beads instance is the cheapest place to notice it.

Cross-reference genetics-results-suite-e47 and genetics-results-suite-82s - do not fix in isolation.
close_reason:
Landed as suite 9ee7799.

THE PREMISE HELD, and the drift was real: the branch's committed export had 180 issues against a live 239.

BUT THE FIRST DIAGNOSIS WAS TOO PESSIMISTIC, and the correction is the useful part. bd's export path is not a bug and is not configurable BECAUSE ONE DOLT DATABASE IS SHARED BY EVERY WORKTREE - a worktree gets no .beads/embeddeddolt of its own (verified in a throwaway repo; confirmed on the real one, present in the main checkout, absent here). Making bd export per-worktree would produce N snapshots, each COMPLETE rather than partial, differing only in WHEN they were taken, and conflicting on every merge.
THE REMEDY IS THEREFORE NEARER THAN IT LOOKED: because the store is shared, `bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl` run FROM the worktree produces the correct, current file - verified byte-identical (md5 8ceb65cc...) to the main checkout's. So a worktree CAN refresh its own committed export, and this commit does exactly that. The docs' original "refresh from the main checkout" left the reader believing the situation was unfixable from where they stand. The preflight now PRINTS that command, so the warning is actionable rather than merely informative.

THE ONE GENUINELY DANGEROUS FACT, measured not assumed: a stale jsonl is INERT under `bd hooks run post-checkout`, `post-merge`, and a REAL git merge of a branch whose issues.jsonl differed - a closed issue stayed closed. But `bd import` upserts blindly and DID revert a closed issue to open. Reproduced independently by a reviewer on bd 1.0.3. Nothing in this repo - script, hook, doc or CLAUDE.md - instructs anyone to run it (grep confirms the only hits are the two new lines describing the danger), so it is latent. It is now written down BEFORE someone reaches for it as a "restore" step.

ALTERNATIVES REJECTED WITH REASONS, so nobody retries them:
- Gitignoring the worktree copy: IMPOSSIBLE. .gitignore does not affect tracked files. Making it work needs `git rm --cached`, which removes the file from the branch and, on merge to master, from the main checkout where it IS live. --skip-worktree is per-clone local state nothing carries, and would hide real changes in main.
- Per-worktree bd export: actively harmful, per the shared-Dolt finding.
- Blanket removal of the `git add .beads/issues.jsonl` step: wrong as stated - from the main checkout that step works and is the only thing that refreshes the committed export. See the user-decision note below.

THE CLASS FIX IS THE REAL DELIVERABLE, as the bead argued. Four tools now degrade silently from a worktree - bd's export, sync-datasets.sh's sibling resolution (e47), terraform.tfvars (82s), core.hooksPath (rxw) - each found by accident rather than by a check. scripts/check-worktree-paths.sh covers all four, reusing the --check pattern install-git-hooks.sh established (rxw), invoked `|| true` from deploy.sh:23 and build-all.sh:25.
Each detection was spot-checked against the REAL failing condition rather than a proxy: for sync-datasets it compares $toplevel/../$sib against $main_root/../$sib, which is exactly what SUITE_DIR resolution does.

THE FIRST VERSION FAILED ITS OWN DESIGN RULE AND REVIEW CAUGHT IT. Its header says "an alert that fires every time is an alert nobody reads", but the beads detection was purely STRUCTURAL - worktree has issues.jsonl, worktree has no embeddeddolt, main has one - which is true in EVERY worktree PERMANENTLY, stale or not. The line counts it computed were only used in the message and never compared. MEASURED: with the two files made byte-identical it still reported a problem. That single item would have turned a four-item preflight into wallpaper on every deploy and every build, and it was the item the whole bead is about. Now gated on cmp -s: a refreshed worktree drops from 4 findings to 3, demonstrated in both directions.

VERIFIED COMPOSING with the three other preflights now at the top of deploy.sh (82s, hi0, rxw). Under set -euo pipefail with the script missing (127), mode-000 (126), exit 1 and exit 2, all four survive and the deploy exits 0 - so no deploy can fail because of a warning. No duplicated work either: the hooks branch is skipped when hooks_path is empty, so an unwired checkout gets ONE warning, not two. The preflight is genuinely read-only, traced and then measured (git config, git status and both issues.jsonl md5s byte-identical after a run).

ALSO FIXED: CLAUDE.md's documentation-ownership table enumerated deploy.sh, rollout.sh and build*.sh and listed neither install-git-hooks.sh nor check-worktree-paths.sh, while check-doc-drift.sh's header says its mappings mirror that table. That is the enumeration-rot class the table exists to prevent, in the table itself. Now matches the drift script's regex exactly.

NEEDS THE USER'S DECISION, raised to them separately: the session-close protocol in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (the user's GLOBAL file, deliberately not edited) says to stage and commit beads state. From a worktree `git add .beads/issues.jsonl` stages nothing unless `bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl` is run first. Suggested wording is in the report.

NITS RECORDED AS COMMENTS, no handling added:
- the sync-datasets detection misses the INVERSE and worse case - if a directory of that name happens to exist beside the WORKTREE, sync copies into the wrong tree and this check stays silent;
- the hooks comparison only considers hooks present on BOTH sides, so a hook added on the branch is missed, and a hooks_path pointing somewhere other than the main .beads/hooks makes the message misattribute the difference to "your edit".

title: OPERATOR: retire or rename genetics_api_logs.genetics_results_api, the decoy table
description:
Follow-up to genetics-results-suite-re3, which explains the mechanism. Cannot be done by an agent: it is a live BigQuery and GCE operation, and the user has held back all live changes.

The trap re3 documented is only half-closed. The committed terraform filter change (suite f6c766c, NOT YET APPLIED) stops NEW rows reaching phewas-development.genetics_api_logs.genetics_results_api. It does nothing about the 224,156 rows already there, or about the table's NAME - which matches the service exactly and is why two separate investigations reached for it. As long as a table named after the service sits next to the real one, the next reader repeats the mistake.

OPERATOR ACTIONS, in order:
1. terraform apply the sink filter change from the MAIN CHECKOUT, not from a worktree - see the tfvars bead, running it from a worktree would propose destroying both sinks.
2. Decide the fate of the developer machine feeding it. It is still emitting (1,377 rows on 2026-08-11) and it is the results-api test suite, not a server. Nothing needs to stop on its account, but confirm nobody depends on that feed.
3. Drop or rename genetics_api_logs.genetics_results_api. Before dropping, note the HISTORY ASYMMETRY: stdout begins 2026-03-06, the decoy begins 2026-01-06, so anything reaching back past March exists only in the table being dropped. If that history matters, rename rather than drop (e.g. dev_test_traffic_legacy).
4. Consider an authoritative view over the real table, e.g. a view on genetics_api_logs.stdout filtered to resource.labels.container_name='results-api', so the obvious thing to query is also the right thing. db-api shares stdout, so an unfiltered query mixes two services.

Do NOT do (3) before (1), or the sink recreates the table.

title: db-api's endpoint_access log lines carry no principal and no endpoint_path, so its rows are unattributable
description:
Found while validating genetics-results-suite-re3.

db-api and results-api both emit jsonPayload.log_type='endpoint_access' and both land in phewas-development.genetics_api_logs.stdout. But db-api's rows are structurally anonymous: 1,101 rows, ZERO non-null user_email, log_source NULL, endpoint_path NULL. genetics-results-db/api/main.py never puts a user or principal key in the payload at all.

Consequence: any 'who used what' question answered from that table is silently results-api-only. The two services' rows happen to be separable via endpoint_path IS NULL, which is an accident of the missing field rather than a designed discriminator - if db-api ever starts emitting endpoint_path, every existing query that relied on that split silently changes meaning.

WHAT TO DECIDE FIRST, before writing code: is db-api even supposed to be attributable? It sits behind results-api and the internal API secret rather than in front of users, so its caller may legitimately be a service rather than a person. If so the right fix is a service identity plus an explicit discriminator field, NOT a user_email.

TO DO once decided:
1. Add an explicit service discriminator to both services' endpoint_access payloads (e.g. service='db-api' / 'results-api') so the split does not depend on a NULL.
2. Add endpoint_path to db-api's payload.
3. Add whatever principal is meaningful for db-api.
4. Update docs/project-spec.md 'Log sinks', which currently documents the endpoint_path IS NULL split as the way to separate them - that note becomes wrong the moment (2) lands, and they must move together.

Cross-repo: the code change is in genetics-results-db, the doc is here. Per this repo's cross-repo documentation rule, both in the same session.
close_reason:
Landed as genetics-results-db 554d467 and genetics-results-api 653264c, with the suite docs in aba3f82. Batched with genetics-results-suite-1ot.

PREMISE HELD. db-api's endpoint_access rows were structurally anonymous - 1,101 rows, zero non-null user_email, log_source and endpoint_path NULL - so the two services separated on `endpoint_path IS NULL`, an accident of a missing field that would have silently INVERTED the moment db-api started emitting it.

THE FIRST ATTEMPT REUSED log_source AS THE DISCRIMINATOR AND THAT WAS THE WRONG CALL, though a defensible one. It is a strict improvement over a NULL accident, but it repeats the exact failure class this bead exists to fix: log_source is derived as f"genetics-results-api-{deploy_env}" from DEPLOY_ENV, its current value 'finngenie_prod' contains no service name, it is asymmetric between the two services (genetics_db_api_prod with underscores vs genetics-results-api-dev1 with hyphens - they do not even share a parse), and IT HAS ALREADY BEEN RENAMED ONCE (~2026-06-03). The draft docs conceded it in a sentence - "any historical query must enumerate values rather than assume one" - printed next to the advice to rely on it, which is an admission the discriminator is unstable.
RESOLVED: both services now emit a CONSTANT, non-env-derived `service` field. log_source is kept and re-scoped to the environment axis. Tests in both repos assert `service` survives a log_source/DEPLOY_ENV rename, which is the property that was missing.

THREE ERAS, all three needed by any query spanning a boundary, and a query keyed on ONE returns a silently wrong subset rather than an error - so they must be OR'd:
  from 2026-08-12    jsonPayload.service = 'db-api' | 'results-api'         the stable split
  back to 2026-03-06 enumerate log_source ('genetics_db_api_prod'; 'finngenie_prod' OR 'genetics-results-api-prod')
  before that        endpoint_path IS NULL identifies db-api                an accident of a missing field
Recorded in the suite's docs/project-spec.md 'Log sinks' and mirrored in the db repo's own spec, per the cross-repo rule.

NO MIGRATION NEEDED, and this was verified rather than hoped: the sink's BigQuery schema AUTO-EVOLVES. Proven from data - db-api's own sql/dry_run/estimated_cost_usd columns exist because db-api created them - so `service`, `endpoint_path`, `http_method` and `principal` get columns on the first row after rollout.

ALSO ADDED to db-api: endpoint_path (route template), http_method, and principal via a new _access_log_fields() helper across all five endpoint_access sites.
principal is one of exactly THREE literals - "internal" / "sandbox" / "unauthenticated" - naming the credential that authorised the call. NO user_email is invented: db-api sits behind results-api and the internal API secret, so its caller is a service, not a person, and the bead's framing of that decision was correct.
Review verified every branch: principal cannot contain a secret, a token or a user identifier (_INTERNAL_PRINCIPAL is a bare constant, not the secret), and _access_log_fields() cannot raise on ANY path - Any is imported, sandbox_auth is imported unconditionally rather than gated on SANDBOX_ENABLED, request.state access goes through getattr with a default, request is None is guarded and unit-tested, and endpoint_path/http_method are string literals at all five call sites. That mattered because an exception in a logging helper would take down the endpoint it logs.

Renamed the two sandbox-branch log lines' "path" key to endpoint_path so all five sites agree. NOTE A WRONG EXPLANATION THAT WAS CAUGHT BEFORE IT SHIPPED: an agent claimed "path" matched no column so the field was being silently dropped. False - the sink auto-evolves, so a `path` row would have CREATED a `path` column. The real reason is that those lines are in the sandbox branch, which has never fired. The wrong framing never reached any file; it existed only in a report.

Tests: db 138 -> 140 passed; results-api gained tests/test_usage_log_payload.py (6 tests) which the repo's fixture rule files into the credential-free offline lane - 188 passed / 382 deselected there, full suite 570 collected exit 0.

FILED: results-api's test_api_auth.py reads INTERNAL_API_SECRET at MODULE IMPORT in api/main.py, so any future test module importing api.main at module scope freezes the secret to '' and breaks it with a confusing failure. The new test file works around it with a lazy fixture import; the durable fix is a conftest.py setting the env var before collection, or reading the secret at request time.

title: code-execution-security.md's per-endpoint request-frequency table is measured from the wrong BigQuery table
description:
Split out of genetics-results-suite-re3, which established the cause. Deferred deliberately because it needs re-measurement, not a wording fix.

That table is NOT the production service - it is fed by a developer machine running the results-api TEST SUITE (sourceLocation.file points inside a genetics-results-api worktree's tests/ dir; 1,638 entries in one second). See docs/project-spec.md 'Log sinks' for the full explanation of why the table with the service's name is the decoy.

So every number in the table at lines ~1105-1116 measures test traffic, inside a SECURITY document.

  /api/v1/rsid/variants        table says 140 + 14   production: 66

  /api/v1/variant_sets         table says 7          production: 0

close_reason:
Landed as suite aba3f82. Batched with genetics-results-suite-tcs (same logging surface).

RE-MEASURED against genetics_api_logs.stdout with LITERAL window bounds [2026-07-13, 2026-08-12), not a rolling window:
  GET  /api/v1/rsid/variants        was 140    ->  64   (last hit 2026-08-11 10:28:48)
  POST /api/v1/rsid/variants        was 14     ->   0   never seen, ever
  GET  /api/v1/variant_sets/{name}  was 14     ->   3   (last 2026-08-07 18:37:48)
  GET  /api/v1/variant_sets         was 7      ->   0   never seen, ever
  GET  /api/v1/auth                            ->   0 in window, 1 ever, 2026-03-07 16:36:29
  GET  /api/v1        "not in the sink"        ->   0 in window, 4 ever, last 2026-05-20 19:08:30
Independently re-run by a reviewer; every figure reproduced exactly, including the two "1 ever"/"4 ever" timestamps to the second.

THE FIRST RE-MEASUREMENT WAS ITSELF UNREPRODUCIBLE, and catching that is the durable part. The doc labelled the window "the 30 days to 2026-08-12" but printed a query using TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY). Those disagree by nine hits: the calendar window the LABEL describes gives 64, the rolling query gives 55. Since this was the SECOND correction of these numbers and the doc's entire selling point is that they can be re-run, a reader re-running it tomorrow would have got a THIRD number with no way to tell whether the doc was wrong again. Bounds are now literal in the printed query, the label states the window in the same form, and a short paragraph names the drift so a future correction reads as anticipated rather than as a third mistake.

THE BEAD WAS WRONG ABOUT ONE ROW, AND THE CORRECTION IS BETTER THAN WHAT IT ASKED FOR. It said the "/api/v1, /healthz - not in the sink" claim is wrong. It is wrong for /api/v1 ONLY. /healthz is in usage_logging_excluded_paths (genetics-results-api/app/config/common.py:22, alongside /api/v1/docs, /redoc, /openapi.json, /favicon.ico), so its absence is BY DESIGN and its count can never be derived from this sink. Confirmed against source by two agents, and corroborated by zero rows over all history. The doc now says exactly that rather than implying disuse.

DIAGNOSIS PARAGRAPH RE-STATED: conclusion kept (don't trust the table), reason replaced. It was "a sink artifact"/"it lags" with a 2,812-row measurement; the real reason is that it was a different machine's log. The httpRequest.responseSize claim is now structural (the middleware emits a jsonPayload-only record, so it is NULL on every row of this sink) rather than a decoy-table row count.
code-execution-security.md:933 now names the table instead of pointing at "the genetics_api_logs sink".

sid/sub/jti CONFIRMED ABSENT from stdout's 19 leaf jsonPayload columns - and the answer is better than "not present". db-api DOES log all three in require_auth's sandbox branch, so the code is correct; they have never reached the sink to GROW its schema, because there is no sandbox Deployment and SANDBOX_ENABLED is "false". Recorded, so nobody assumes the sandbox-attribution fields this document describes are queryable in BigQuery.
Worth knowing for anyone reasoning about this sink: it AUTO-EVOLVES. Proven from data - db-api's own sql/dry_run/estimated_cost_usd/bytes_processed columns exist precisely because db-api created them. So "no column" always means "no row has ever carried that key", never "the sink dropped it".

THE SECURITY ARGUMENT WAS NOT RE-OPENED and survives, as scoped. Verified by review rather than assumed: the load-bearing argument is the response-size analysis (888 rows / 18.6 KB against a 16 MiB cap; MAX_RSIDS=5000), independent of the sink, and the document already withdrew the user_email inference and said the no-truncation conclusion rests on the caps being unreachable rather than on logged size data.

title: HLA TSV serializer does not validate against _HLA_HEADER_SCHEMA, so schema/emitter drift is uncaught
description:
Found during genetics-results-suite-w09's mutation testing, and it is exactly the concern bead 5wm raised about the download header.

Renaming mlog10p to mlogp in app/routers/hla.py's _HLA_HEADER_SCHEMA makes test_single_phenotype[json] fail - but test_single_phenotype[tsv] STILL PASSES. The JSON path validates against the schema (server logs 'error streaming or parsing data: Header mlog10p not found in header schema' and returns 500); the TSV serializer does not consult it and emits the underlying column unchanged.

So the TSV test's `assert "mlog10p" in header` pins the EMITTED TSV header - a rename of the real data column would be caught - but a divergence BETWEEN the schema and the TSV emitter is caught by nothing.
