That matters because 5wm established that the TSV download header and the JSON named rows both derive from the same column list, so a change reaching one and not the other is the live failure mode.

Note also: under the rename, test_single_phenotype[json] fails at tests/test_hla.py:64 with `assert 500 == 200`, not at the mlog10p membership assertion on :76. The rename IS caught, but one line earlier than the test appears to promise - worth knowing before citing :76 as the pin.

FIX: assert the TSV header equals list(_HLA_HEADER_SCHEMA), so schema and emitter cannot drift apart.

Related: genetics-results-suite-5wm, genetics-results-suite-w09.
close_reason:
Landed as api a56c31e. Batched with genetics-results-suite-917.

Added tests/test_hla.py::TestHlaAssociations::test_tsv_header_matches_the_header_schema, asserting result["header"] == list(_HLA_HEADER_SCHEMA) - full ORDERED equality, not a set or subset comparison. Empirically the served TSV header already equals the schema key order exactly, so strict equality holds rather than needing to be weakened.

JUDGEMENT CALL: pinned by TEST, not by making the serializer validate. The request path is unchanged.
Verified against the code rather than asserted: range_response's tsv branch (app/core/responses.py:80-97) never reads header_schema - it wraps the byte stream in TimedStreamingResponse after optional row filters; only the json branch passes it to tsv_stream_to_list (line 105). The TSV header's content and order come from the file's column_mapping/union_output_columns, so the schema is NOT the TSV path's source of truth.
Validating there would mean buffering the header line out of the stream, comparing, and re-injecting it - new latency and a new 500 mode on the download path - and would convert an additive, backward-compatible upstream column into an OUTAGE on the download route. The schema's job on the JSON path is type coercion, not an output contract for TSV. The invariant actually at stake is code-vs-code (schema list vs emitted columns), which a test pins at zero runtime cost and with a far clearer failure message than a 500. Review agreed and confirmed the characterisation of the TSV path.

MUTATION-PROVEN, including the case that distinguishes a real pin from a weak one: renaming mlog10p fails it, deleting info fails it, and - the important one - a PURE REORDER of beta and se with no rename also fails it, at "At index 9 diff: 'beta' != 'se'". So ordering is genuinely pinned, not incidentally satisfied.

WHY THIS EXISTED: renaming mlog10p in _HLA_HEADER_SCHEMA made test_single_phenotype[json] fail while test_single_phenotype[tsv] STILL PASSED, because the JSON path validates against the schema and 500s while the TSV path never consults it and emits the underlying column unchanged. So schema/emitter DIVERGENCE was caught by nothing - precisely the download-header concern genetics-results-suite-5wm raised, confirmed by mutation during w09 rather than by argument.

Worth knowing for anyone citing the JSON test: under that rename it fails at tests/test_hla.py:64 with `assert 500 == 200`, NOT at the mlog10p membership assertion on :76. The rename is caught, but one line earlier than the test appears to promise.

The test takes server_url so the fixture files it in the integration lane and it runs under plain pytest. Note that post-917 its `from app.routers.hla import _HLA_HEADER_SCHEMA` is no longer itself a reason for that lane.

Suite: 564 passed (563 + this test).

title: app/core/streams.py constructs DatasetMapping() at import, forcing 4 test modules out of the offline lane
description: Follow-up from genetics-results-suite-w09. app/core/streams.py:13 does a module-level dataset_mapping = DatasetMapping(), whose __init__ calls _init_dataset_to_resource_mapping -> read_file(path) over dataset_mapping_files, and read_file handles gs:// - so merely IMPORTING the module reads GCS. Anything whose import chain reaches it needs credentials even when it needs no server. Consequence today: tests/conftest.py must exclude 4 modules from the offline lane (test_coding_filter.py, test_data_types_filter.py, test_dataset_display_names.py, test_sumstats_column_alignment.py, 26 tests) and 6 tests are hand-marked integration purely for this reason. PAYOFF if fixed: those 4 modules plus 6 of the 7 hand-marked tests move back to offline. It would NOT move tests/test_sandbox_token_auth.py::test_alg_none_is_not_accepted, which is network-bound for an unrelated reason (verifying an alg:none token makes PyJWT fetch Google's OAuth signing certs). DO NOT USE A MODULE-LEVEL __getattr__ - a reviewer established this does not work here: PEP 562 module __getattr__ does NOT fire for bare global-name lookups inside the module's own functions, and all ten consumers of dataset_mapping are internal to streams.py (lines 126, 280, 298, 346, 409, 412, 475, 478, 504, 507; grep finds no importer elsewhere in app/). Deleting the global and adding __getattr__ would turn all ten into NameError at request time. USE A CACHED ACCESSOR instead - app/core/service_container.py:149 already does exactly that for the same object, and app/services/data_access_coloc.py:203 constructs another independently, so there are already three constructions and only this one is eager. Also worth addressing while in here: the conftest lane classification is FAIL-OPEN for new GCS-touching tests (a new test taking no server_url but constructing DatasetMapping lands in offline and breaks the credential-free run for everyone - loudly, not silently-green), and _NEEDS_GCS_AT_IMPORT is keyed on bare filenames so it stops matching if a module moves into a subdirectory. Fixing the eager construction removes the need for that list entirely.
close_reason:
Landed as api a56c31e. Batched with genetics-results-suite-7yg. Nothing applied to any cluster.

DONE: app/core/streams.py's module-level DatasetMapping() (a GCS read at import) is now a cached get_dataset_mapping(), following the pattern app/core/service_container.py:149 already uses for the same object.

The bead's warning was honoured and verified rather than trusted: a module-level __getattr__ does NOT work here, because PEP 562 __getattr__ never fires for bare global-name lookups inside the module's own functions, and all ten consumers are internal to streams.py. It was checked with a minimal reproduction before committing to the alternative.

The ten consumers are per-row filter_fn/transform_fn closures, so the accessor is bound ONCE per enclosing stream builder (5 sites: tsv_line_iterator_simple, tsv_line_iterator, tsv_line_iterator_qtl, tsv_line_iterator_coloc, tsv_line_iterator_coloc_by_trait) instead of per row. Closure bodies are textually unchanged and per-row cost drops from a global-dict lookup to a cell deref. Review verified independently by symtable: local+assigned in all 5 enclosing scopes, free+referenced in all 10 inner scopes, ZERO is_global() occurrences left, no stale importer anywhere in app/, tests/ or scripts/. All 5 bindings are on the straight-line prologue before any closure def, with no branch, early return or try in between, and none of the 5 is a generator - so there is no NameError path, which was the specific failure the __getattr__ approach was rejected for.

PAYOFF COLLECTED - the point of the bead, not a bonus. The whole exclusion mechanism (_NEEDS_GCS_AT_IMPORT, _offline_only, pytest_ignore_collect, pytest_report_header) was DELETED rather than emptied, plus 4 hand-written integration marks covering 6 tests. test_alg_none_is_not_accepted stays marked - it fetches Google's OAuth signing certs, unrelated to any of this.
The bead's arithmetic needed correcting: of the 26 tests in the four excluded modules only 20 are offline; the other 6 take server_url and merely changed lanes. 156 + 20 + 6 = 182. Verified against the actual collection, so nothing silently stopped running.

THE FIRST ATTEMPT REGRESSED THE VERY PROPERTY IT WAS FIXING, and how it was caught is the lesson. DatasetMapping was NOT the only credential-requiring import: streams.py:10 calls setup_logging() at module scope, and with the default DEPLOY_ENV=dev1 that constructs google.cloud.logging.Client(). Removing the exclusion list therefore replaced a loud, announced exclusion with a HARD COLLECTION ERROR - 556 collected, 1 error, Interrupted; the offline lane ran ZERO tests.

WHY IT WAS MISSED, and this now applies to every "credential-free" claim in this repo: it was measured by unsetting GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS and pointing CLOUDSDK_CONFIG at an empty dir. THIS MACHINE IS A GCP VM, so google.auth.default() falls back to the instance metadata service and that is not credential-free at all. Worse, google-auth infers GCE residency from /sys/class/dmi/id/product_name and returns compute_engine.Credentials WITHOUT touching the network, so even pointing the metadata host at a dead port is not sufficient here. A genuine check needs env -i with an empty HOME, no GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, no CLOUDSDK_CONFIG, and the metadata host blocked - and even then the failure SHAPE differs by host: OSError("Project was not passed and could not be determined from the environment") on this GCE box, DefaultCredentialsError elsewhere. The two environments used between implementer and reviewer exercise both branches, which is why both are in the catch.

FIXED AT THE ROOT rather than by restoring the exclusion list. app/core/logging_config.py now degrades to stdout when cloud logging cannot authenticate: catches both failure shapes, CLEARS the stdout handler that _setup_cloud_logging_api installs BEFORE constructing the client (a naive fallback double-logged every line - caught by probe, not by reasoning), and emits one WARNING after handlers exist so a real production auth failure is loud rather than swallowed.
_logging_initialized moved from BEFORE the risky call to after setup completes. The early latch was itself a bug: an escaping exception left the flag set, so every later importer silently skipped setup - which is exactly why this presented as 1 error instead of ~15, and why the failing module's identity followed collection order (deterministic today only because pytest-randomly is not installed).

MEASURED, credential-free, in the reviewer's own harness (not the implementer's):
  collect-only:  556 + 1 error, Interrupted  ->  564 collected, 0 errors
  -m offline:    zero tests run              ->  182 passed, 382 deselected
With credentials: 564 passed; handlers ['StreamHandler', 'CloudLoggingHandler'], no fallback warning, no extra handler - production path unchanged. Forced fallback leaves exactly ONE handler, verified.

KNOWN TRADE-OFF, recorded not fixed: OSError subsumes ConnectionError/TimeoutError, so a transient network blip at startup degrades that process to stdout-only for its whole lifetime with no retry - and on the dev VM stdout is not the collected sink, so the single WARNING announcing the degradation lands in the sink that was just lost. Low probability and strictly better than the previous hard crash at import. If it ever matters, surface "fell back to stdout" as a startup-check condition rather than narrowing the catch.
Also noted: the late latch theoretically lets two threads both pass the guard, but all four module-scope callers run at import and server.py:42 latches before the lifespan spawns any asyncio.to_thread work, so none reaches it unlatched. The old early latch had the mirror-image bug (a second caller logging into a handler-less root), so the new ordering is the better trade.

FILED: genetics-results-suite-uc9 - three independent DatasetMapping() constructions remain (streams.py via the accessor, service_container.py:149, data_access_coloc.py:203, the last of which builds one PER REQUEST). Consolidation was explicitly out of scope here and is now clean to do, since none is eager any more.

title: genetics-results-api test suite gives no offline signal: 282 failures without a live server
description: Discovered while validating genetics-results-suite-5wm. The genetics-results-api suite runs 282 failed, 263 passed, 12 skipped with nothing listening on :4000. Nearly the whole suite is live-server integration: tests take a server_url fixture and call requests.get, and tests/conftest.py only reads a --server-url option defaulting to http://localhost:4000 -- there is no app-startup or TestClient fixture anywhere. Consequences seen concretely: tests/test_hla.py asserts mlog10p at :76 and af_cases at :138, and a reviewer cited those as proof the HLA column names were pinned; they are not, because both assertions sit inside failing tests. The 2 tests in that file that pass do so only because they assert 404s, which everything returns. So 'the api suite is green' has never been a meaningful statement, and any claim of coverage in this repo needs checking against whether the test can run at all. Also note port 4000 is currently held by a DIFFERENT service (the Genetics Chat API), so even running a server locally does not make test_hla.py pass. FIX DIRECTION: add a TestClient-based conftest fixture so the routers can be exercised in-process, or split the suite into offline and integration markers so CI has a real signal. See tests/test_hla_column_names.py (added by 5wm) for the offline pattern.
close_reason:
Landed as api df3e1da. Nothing applied to any cluster.

RESULT: pytest goes from 282 failed / 269 passed / 12 skipped to 563 PASSED. `pytest -m offline` with credentials pointed at nonexistent paths runs 156 tests in 2.5s.

THE PROBLEM WAS WORSE THAN THE BEAD DESCRIBED. The bead said the suite gives no offline signal. It also gave a WRONG signal: port 4000 is held by a DIFFERENT service (the Genetics Chat API), so a large part of the suite was not failing to connect - it was receiving real HTTP 404s from an unrelated process and asserting on them. The recorded 282/269/12 baseline had nothing to do with the expired credentials it was first measured under; re-measured with ADC working, it was identical apart from 269 vs the previously noted 263.

WHY IT MATTERED CONCRETELY, and why this bead was filed: during genetics-results-suite-r0l a reviewer cited tests/test_hla.py:76 (mlog10p) and :138 (af_cases) as proof the HLA column names were pinned. Both sit inside tests that never executed.

APPROACH: --server-url now defaults to None. Omitted, the session fixture boots the REAL app in-process on an ephemeral free port - uvicorn in a daemon thread, full lifespan (tabix header warming, gene maps, search index, gene-disease load, cross-resource smoke query), ~25s on top of a ~7s import - and yields that URL, so EXISTING TESTS RUN UNCHANGED with no rewriting. Passed explicitly, it is yielded untouched and nothing boots: verified `--server-url http://127.0.0.1:9 tests/test_health.py` fails in 1.0s with no app boot and no port bound. tests/run_tests.sh passes --server-url in all seven of its modes, so it is unaffected.
loop="asyncio" matches run_server.py deliberately - uvloop breaks `tabix -R /dev/stdin`.

TWO LANES ASSIGNED BY FIXTURE, NOT BY MEMORY (pytest_collection_modifyitems): takes server_url -> integration; anything else -> offline. So a NEW UNMARKED TEST LANDS IN THE CREDENTIAL-FREE LANE that runs in both modes - it cannot silently join a never-runs pile, which is precisely how this repo got here. Verified by experiment with a probe module, and the partition is total: 563 = 156 offline + 381 integration, no unclassified remainder.

THE GREEN IS REAL, not asserted. Review mutated three areas the implementer had NOT used: healthz's response string, rsid lowercasing (2 tests), and the HLA schema - each produced failures in previously-dead tests, with real data in the payloads and "Startup smoke query passed" in the log. The 12 former skips were RUNTIME skips conditioned on the server's own answers ("No resources available", "No HLA resources configured"); they fired against the wrong service and now do not, so the accounting is consistent rather than a re-labelling.

REVIEW CAUGHT A NEW WAY FOR GREEN TO UNDER-REPORT - this bead's own failure class, reintroduced by the fix. _offline_only() substring-matched the -m string, so `-m "not offline"` satisfied it: pytest_ignore_collect silently removed the 26 tests in the four GCS-at-import modules while the report header asserted the opposite of the run requested. Fixed to an exact match; all four spellings verified (bare 563 collected; -m offline 156/537; -m "not offline" 387/563; -m "not integration" 176/563).

KNOWN LIMITATION, DOCUMENTED NOT HIDDEN: app/core/streams.py:13 constructs DatasetMapping() at MODULE IMPORT and that reads GCS, so anything whose import chain reaches it needs credentials even with no server. Four modules are therefore excluded from the offline lane only (announced by name in the report header, still run in the default lane) and seven tests are hand-marked integration. THE LIST IS FAIL-OPEN: a new test taking no server_url but constructing DatasetMapping lands in offline and breaks the credential-free run for everyone - loudly, not silently-green, so a maintenance wart rather than a coverage hole. The real fix is genetics-results-suite-917.

CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER CLAIM IN THIS EPIC: genetics-results-suite-5wm's tests/test_hla_column_names.py was reported as 8 fully offline tests. It is not - 4 of them reach app.routers.hla and therefore streams.py, and are now marked integration. Three modules' docstrings claimed they "need neither a live server nor GCS access"; that was false and is corrected.

FILED: genetics-results-suite-917 (make the DatasetMapping construction lazy - and NOTE the reviewer established a module-level __getattr__ will NOT work, since PEP 562 __getattr__ does not fire for bare global lookups inside the module's own functions and all ten consumers are internal to streams.py; use a cached accessor as service_container.py:149 already does) and genetics-results-suite-7yg (the HLA TSV serializer does not validate against _HLA_HEADER_SCHEMA, so a schema/emitter divergence is caught by nothing - directly the download-header concern 5wm raised).

NON-BLOCKING, recorded not fixed: `pytest -n auto` with no --server-url boots one full app copy PER xdist worker (~25s and a burst of GCS reads each). run_tests.sh is unaffected because it always passes --server-url, and the default addopts has no -n, so bare pytest is serial. _free_port() has a benign bind/close/hand-off TOCTOU race. Interpreter shutdown prints a cosmetic aiohttp ClientSession.__del__ ImportError that does not affect exit codes.

SCOPE HELD: no attempt was made to convert the ~282 live-server tests to offline - that was explicitly not the deliverable. The deliverable is that bare `pytest` now fails when something is broken, and that it is obvious which tests need what.

title: hla_associations_v silently drops new base-table columns; nothing detects it
description: genetics-results-suite-5wm changed schemas/hla_associations_v.sql from 'SELECT *, CASE...' to an explicit 14-column list because aliasing required it. It is now the ONLY one of the 15 views that pins its base columns (11 of 15 use SELECT *; the rest are joins). If a column is added to the hla_associations base table it will silently not surface, and nothing anywhere notices: no script in the suite reads INFORMATION_SCHEMA; scripts/generate_resource_sql.py lint extracts only the CASE...END AS resource block and passes clean on an under-wide list; scripts/monitor/bq_summary.py issues only COUNT(*) and SELECT DISTINCT resource. The trade-off is documented in the .sql header and genetics-results-db docs/project-spec.md but only as prose. FIX: add a test in genetics-results-db asserting the identifiers in schemas/hla_associations_v.sql cover every field name in SCHEMAS['hla_associations'] in scripts/load_data.py (~line 288-303), which is the in-repo authority for the base table's 14 columns. Both validators on 5wm raised this independently.
close_reason:
Landed as db 01a8325. Batched with genetics-results-suite-5wy (suite 11db632), both being 5wm follow-ups.

WHAT IT DETECTS: 5wm made hla_associations_v the only one of 15 views pinning its base columns, so a column added to the hla_associations base table silently stops surfacing. tests/test_hla_view_columns.py (6 tests) now catches that offline.

DESIGN, chosen deliberately: parse schemas/hla_associations_v.sql rather than restate the column list in the test. A declared list only proves the test agrees with itself; the .sql is the artifact actually applied to BigQuery. The test compares the SOURCE half of each alias (the `mlogp` in `mlogp AS mlog10p`) against SCHEMAS["hla_associations"] in scripts/load_data.py, which was verified to match both the DDL and the live table, in order. Checking the source half is the point - a naive "every base name appears somewhere in the file" check would pass if someone deleted the `mlogp AS` half and kept the alias.

OFFLINE BY CONSTRUCTION, verified not assumed: load_data.py was imported with socket.socket and socket.create_connection replaced by raising stubs; no socket opened, and bigquery.Client is constructed only inside a __main__-guarded main(). This deliberately avoids repeating the genetics-results-api pattern where the whole suite requires a live server and therefore asserts nothing - see genetics-results-suite-w09.

REVIEW FOUND A FALSE GREEN IN THE FIRST VERSION AND DEMONSTRATED IT. _strip_comments handled only `--`, and the select list was located with the FIRST \bSELECT\b in the file. A view file that genuinely dropped `info` but carried a leading /* */ comment holding the previous complete list PASSED ALL SIX TESTS - the exact regression the test exists to catch, in the shape you naturally get while editing a view. Not hypothetical: this file's own header comment discusses `SELECT *` and is safe today only because it happens to be a `--` comment; reflowing it to /* */ would have armed the trap.
FIXED BOTH HALVES: /* */ stripped inside the same quote-aware scan (a /* inside a string literal is literal; the block becomes a single space so `mlogp/**/AS` cannot fuse; an unterminated /* is left verbatim for the backstop), a surviving /* or */ fails the test, and the select list is anchored to `CREATE [OR REPLACE] VIEW ... AS SELECT` with NO fallback to the first SELECT.
Also fixed a second parser bug the review found: the top-level-FROM guard treated `_` as a non-word char, so `dataset_from,` parsed as `dataset_` and silently dropped every column after it.

RE-PROBED ADVERSARIALLY by the same reviewer that found the false green - 27 cases, zero silently-wrong results. Clean on: /* */ containing a comma, FROM, a commented-out column, or a whole `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW ... AS SELECT`; a block between AS and SELECT; `--` inside /* */ and vice versa; block comments splitting tokens; the anchor text inside a string literal; CREATE VIEW without OR REPLACE; dataset_from / from_dataset / _from / fromage. Fail-closed (acceptable) on: unterminated /*, /* or */ inside a string literal, a bare SELECT with no CREATE...VIEW, and OPTIONS(description="... AS SELECT ...") preceding the real anchor. Nested /* /* */ parses per real BigQuery semantics (BQ does not nest; first */ closes) - the probe's expectation was wrong, not the parser.

FAILS CLOSED THROUGHOUT: unparseable file, missing anchor, unclassifiable select item, SELECT *, DISTINCT, backticked or qualified names, and duplicate source columns are all failures, never skips. The derived-output set is pinned to {resource} so a new computed column forces a deliberate revisit rather than silently widening.

PROVEN ON DISK, NOT IN MEMORY - the standard this session had to adopt after two separate tests were found asserting against their own fixtures. Dropping `info` fails; dropping `info` WITH the block-comment decoy fails; replacing `mlogp AS mlog10p` with `mlog10p` fails; adding a fake 15th field to SCHEMAS fails. Reflowing the real header comment into /* */ still PASSES, so the test is not fail-closed against ordinary cosmetic edits.

Tests: db 128 passed (baseline 122 + 6 new).

LEFT UNDONE deliberately, non-blocking: with TWO `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` statements in one file the anchor takes the first, so it would validate the wrong statement. A false green would additionally require that first view to independently carry all 14 columns with all 5 correct aliases, and hla_associations_v.sql is a single-statement file by construction. Cheap hardening if it ever matters: make the anchor require the view name hla_associations_v.
Also not done: adding the new test to the tests/ listing in genetics-results-db docs/project-spec.md - that listing already names only 2 of 8 test files, so it reads as illustrative, and making it exhaustive is a bigger edit than this bead owns.

SCOPE NOTE: the implementer also extended the db docs/project-spec.md sentence at ~line 399 to name this test as the detector, since the bead observed the trade-off was documented there only as prose and CLAUDE.md requires spec files to track the change.

title: A gmail.com address appears in oauth2-proxy logs; confirm it was rejected
description:
Noticed during the genetics-results-suite-fdd investigation and NOT chased down, because the log line did not say whether the request was admitted or rejected.

Over 180 days oauth2-proxy logged 12 distinct addresses: 11 @finngen.fi and one oonatoyou@gmail.com.

WHY IT IS PROBABLY FINE: results-api reads ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS=finngen.fi and ALLOWED_EMAILS='' from the live bearer-auth-allowed ConfigMap, so it would reject that address. But oauth2-proxy has its OWN list - --authenticated-emails-file=/etc/oauth2-proxy/allowed-emails.txt, populated from the oauth_allowed_emails terraform variable, which is empty in the live ConfigMap - and that file was not read. The two lists are separate mechanisms and only coincide because both render from the same terraform variables on this profile.

WHAT TO DO: read the live allowed-emails.txt, then check Cloud Logging for that address to establish whether it ever got a 202 from the auth_request subrequest or only 401s. If it was admitted at the gateway, work out what it could reach - note the gateway admits browser traffic to bff, frontend and chat-backend, not only results-api, and chat-backend's own allow-list only arrives with genetics-results-suite-th2, which is not deployed.

Filed as a question rather than a finding. It may simply be a failed login attempt.
close_reason:
ANSWER: REJECTED. Blast radius ZERO. Landed as suite f6c766c (batched with genetics-results-suite-re3; the code change in that commit belongs to re3, e22 was a question and needed no code).

MEASURED trace for oonatoyou@gmail.com, 2026-08-07T01:01:52, request id d0009832, independently re-run by a second agent rather than taken from the first:
  01:01:52.504  GET /oauth2/callback, Google userinfo "email": "oonatoyou@gmail.com", "verified_email": true
                -> [AuthFailure] Invalid authentication via OAuth2: unauthorized, callback returns 403
  01:01:53.847  GET /oauth2/auth (the nginx auth_request subrequest) -> 401, 13 bytes, identity logged as '-'
  01:01:54.016  GET /oauth2/start?rd=/favicon.ico -> 302 back into the login flow
No 202 at any point, no _oauth2_proxy session cookie ever minted, so NO upstream was reached - not bff, not frontend, not chat-backend, not results-api. Google sign-in itself succeeded; oauth2-proxy's own email check is what rejected it. Five other non-finngen.fi addresses in the window show the identical AuthFailure pattern.

THE LOAD-BEARING STEP WAS THE EMPTY-FILE SEMANTICS, and it was settled from SOURCE, not inferred. The bead correctly identified that oauth2-proxy has its own list (--authenticated-emails-file=/etc/oauth2-proxy/allowed-emails.txt) separate from results-api's, and that the file had not been read. LIVE VALUE: ConfigMap oauth2-allowed-emails = {"allowed-emails.txt": ""} - EMPTY. That is ambiguous on its face: an empty allow-list could mean 'allow nobody'.
It does not. oauth2-proxy v7.14.3 validator.go computes valid = isEmailValidWithDomains(...) and only then, if false, valid = validUsers.IsValid(email) - a UNION. An empty file makes IsValid always false, which is INERT, not deny-all. Live: OAUTH2_PROXY_EMAIL_DOMAINS=finngen.fi, image quay.io/oauth2-proxy/oauth2-proxy:v7.14.3.
Corroborated behaviourally so the two explanations are distinguishable rather than merely consistent: /oauth2/auth returned 202 seventy-five times in three days with that same empty file mounted, which deny-all semantics would make impossible.

results-api's own list checked LIVE rather than assumed, per the bead: bearer-auth-allowed ConfigMap has ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS=finngen.fi, ALLOWED_EMAILS="". So it would have rejected the address too - but that never came into play, because the gateway rejected first.

CORRECTION TO THE BEAD, and it matters for any future question of this shape: the _Default log bucket retention is 30 DAYS (measured, unlocked). The bead's 'over 180 days oauth2-proxy logged 12 distinct addresses' was never answerable from that bucket - a --freshness=180d query returns only what survived retention and says nothing about the difference. The oldest AuthFailure retrievable is 2026-07-14. So the verdict above is unambiguous WITHIN THE 30 DAYS the default bucket can answer for; within it, that address appears exactly twice, both from the single rejected attempt. A 400-day global bucket exists but gcloud logging read does not query it unless the bucket/view is named explicitly. If certainty over the full 180 days is ever wanted, that is the (read-only) query to run - it was skipped here to stay in budget, and the verdict does not depend on it since a rejection is what was found.

It was a failed login attempt, as the bead's optimistic reading guessed - but now with the 401 on record rather than assumed, which was the whole point of filing it.

title: The endpoint_access BigQuery sink drops user_email, making it useless for auth questions
description:
Found during the genetics-results-suite-fdd investigation, unrelated to that bead's decision.

phewas-development.genetics_api_logs.genetics_results_api holds 223,063 rows since 2026-01-06 with only 18 non-null user_email, the last on 2026-03-12. The column EXISTS in the schema. Live Cloud Logging over the same window has the identities - a 90-day query returned 1,943 requests from six named finngen.fi people - so something is dropping the field between the log sink and BigQuery.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: this is the table anyone would naturally query to answer 'who uses this API and how'. Two separate investigations this session hit it. 4h6.28's implementer measured public-route response sizes against it, and a reviewer found httpRequest.responseSize is non-null on 0 of 2,812 rows there. A 4h6.9 reviewer independently found the same table returns zero rows for the last two days while Cloud Logging has entries from today, and concluded a doc claim built on it was unsupportable. So the sink is BOTH lagging AND lossy, and it has already produced one wrong doc claim that had to be removed.

The middleware itself is fine - app/middleware_usage_logging.py:88-98 emits user_email, endpoint_path, http_method, status_code, duration_ms, and Cloud Logging receives them. Suspect the sink filter or the BigQuery schema mapping in terraform.

Until this is fixed, treat that table as unusable for attribution questions and query Cloud Logging directly. Say so wherever the table is cited.
close_reason:
THIS BEAD'S PREMISE WAS WRONG. The sink is neither lossy nor lagging. Landed as suite f6c766c, batched with genetics-results-suite-e22. NOT APPLIED - the live sink still carries the old filter.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE: phewas-development.genetics_api_logs holds TWO tables, and a Cloud Logging sink names its BigQuery table after the LOG ID, not after the service.
  genetics_api_logs.stdout               GKE containers -> logs/stdout. results-api AND db-api.
                                         53,216 rows, 12,121 non-null user_email, max timestamp ~90s behind wall clock.
  genetics_api_logs.genetics_results_api a developer machine -> logs/genetics-results-api.
                                         224,156 rows, 18 non-null user_email.
So the table whose name MATCHES THE SERVICE is the decoy, and it is the one every prior investigation reached for. Both symptoms this bead reported are artefacts of querying a dev box instead of the cluster:
  'drops user_email' -> that machine's traffic is unauthenticated, so NULL is correct for it
  'lags two days'    -> a genuine gap in that machine's own traffic, not a streaming-buffer or partition-decorator artefact
The 18 non-null rows and their 2026-03-12 cutoff are the TAIL OF THE MARCH GKE CUTOVER, not a regression: stdout's first row is 2026-03-06.

THE EXCLUDED PRODUCER IS NOT LEGACY - the first draft said so and it was wrong. Its sourceLocation.file is /home/jkarjala/suite/genetics-results-api/.claude/worktrees/db-only-architecture/tests/../app/middleware_usage_logging.py and it emitted 1,638 entries inside ONE SECOND today. It is the results-api TEST SUITE on a developer box, still emitting (1,377 rows on 2026-08-11). Both the terraform comment and project-spec now say that, and say plainly that applying the filter stops that feed DELIBERATELY and with no replacement. It is an exclusion of test noise, not the retirement of something dead - if that framing is lost, the next reader reads it as a data loss.

FIX (files only, nothing applied): terraform/logging.tf's endpoint_access sink filter gains AND resource.type="k8s_container" AND resource.labels.namespace_name="genetics".
VERIFIED EXHAUSTIVELY, NOT SAMPLED - the shape of the old filter is what made that possible. Because it was project-wide, aggregating the sink's OWN OUTPUT enumerates exactly what it matched. Four producer shapes over full history: gce_instance/genetics-results-api (224,156, excluded), global/same log_source (284, excluded), k8s_container/genetics/results-api (53,216 minus db-api's, kept), k8s_container/genetics/db-api (1,101, kept). A 30-day query for endpoint_access EXCLUDING the known three returns ZERO rows. Code-side cross-check: only two files in the suite emit log_type='endpoint_access' and both run only in namespace genetics. Two independent validators measured this separately and agreed nothing wanted is lost.
Sink mechanics confirmed: writerIdentity unchanged by a filter edit so the dataset IAM member will not churn; bigquery_options.use_partitioned_tables=true already matches live; a filter applies at ROUTING time only, so the existing 224k rows stay and the table simply stops growing.

RULED OUT WITH EVIDENCE, so nobody re-checks them: schema mapping/drift (jsonPayload.user_email STRING NULLABLE present in BOTH tables' auto-evolved schema, and stdout populates it); middleware broken (VERIFIED not assumed - a live entry from today carries user_email 'mcp-tool'); a code change at 2026-03-12 (it is the cutover boundary).

THE 284-ROW resource.type='global' FINDING IS THE ONE WORTH REMEMBERING. Same process, same log_source, different resource type - the Cloud Logging client library falls back to 'global' when metadata detection does not resolve. Harmless here because it is the same unwanted producer, but it is a live demonstration that the label this new filter leans on CAN fail to hold. If results-api ever runs somewhere the GKE resource is not detected, the identical silent drop hits a WANTED producer, and the sink has no volume alerting to catch it. A negative filter (NOT resource.type='gce_instance') would have avoided inheriting that fragility; it was considered and deliberately not taken, since it fails open on any future junk producer instead. Recorded as a known trade-off, not an oversight.

BONUS CORRECTION: httpRequest.responseSize is not dropped, IT NEVER EXISTED. NULL on all 278,757 rows across both tables. The middleware logs a plain dict, and Cloud Logging populates the httpRequest struct only when a caller sets it. No sink change can produce it -> filed genetics-results-suite-fv5.

SECOND TRAP FOUND WHILE VALIDATING, same shape, now documented at docs/project-spec.md ~394: results-api's log_source was RENAMED genetics-results-api-prod -> finngenie_prod around 2026-06-03 (40,958 rows/95 emails before, 12,258/12,026 after). Filtering the old value silently returns nothing after that date and raises no error. Anyone repointing a query at stdout will hit this immediately.
Also: repointing is NOT a drop-in substitution. The dev table has 591 distinct endpoint_path values, stdout has 77 (541 dev-only, 27 stdout-only) - expected, since the test suite exercises the whole surface, but any query that assumed broad endpoint coverage changes meaning.

ALSO FIXED IN THE SAME COMMIT, both required rather than optional:
- docs/project-spec.md:661 still told the reader to distrust the sink because it 'drops user_email and lags'. Measurably false of stdout, and it is the EXACT confusion this change diagnoses, left standing 270 lines below the new explanation. The 90-day Cloud Logging figure it defends (1,943 requests, six @finngen.fi people) still stands and was not touched.
- README.md:426 per the doc-ownership table's terraform/** -> README.md rule.
- The identity claim at ~393 was scoped: db-api's 1,101 rows have ZERO non-null user_email STRUCTURALLY (genetics-results-db/api/main.py puts no principal in the payload), so 'identity' is a results-api-only property. The two separate on endpoint_path IS NULL - an accident of a missing field, not a designed discriminator -> filed genetics-results-suite-tcs.
Cross-check that the two spec regions now reconcile: 40,958 + 12,258 = 53,216 rows and 95 + 12,026 = 12,121 identities.

FILED: 82s (P1 - terraform from a worktree sees enable_log_sinks=false and would propose DESTROYING both sinks, since terraform.tfvars is gitignored and main-checkout-only; same class as e47), 1ot (code-execution-security.md's request-frequency table is dev-VM numbers inside a security doc - its security ARGUMENT survives, only the counts are wrong), tcs, 3sm (OPERATOR: retire/rename the decoy table - the filter only stops new rows, the misleading NAME is what actually repeats the mistake), fv5.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: terraform was never run, not even plan, because plan takes a state lock. docs/code-execution-security.md was left untouched - see 1ot.

title: results-api /api/v1/auth may be the same unauthenticated identity oracle th2 closed on chat-backend
description:
Flagged but NOT probed during genetics-results-suite-g9c's local verification. Recorded as an observation, not a finding.

app/routers/auth.py registers GET /auth under prefix /api/v1 and it is @is_public, so auth_required returns before any credential check, and the handler returns get_authenticated_user. That is structurally the same shape genetics-results-suite-th2 called out on chat-backend's GET /chat/v1/auth, where it reflected a forged identity plus is_admin and worked as an unauthenticated oracle for enumerating ADMIN_USERS.

WHAT SHOULD BE TRUE AFTER -fad: results-api's get_authenticated_user now requires the internal marker, so an unmarked caller should get null rather than a reflected identity, and results-api has no ADMIN_USERS equivalent, so even a reflection would leak less than chat-backend's did. That is reasoning, not measurement.

WHAT TO DO: probe it directly against the new build, on a real socket, the way g9c probed the other seven rows:
  no headers                          -> expect null / unauthenticated
  identity header alone               -> expect null, NOT the reflected address
  marker + allow-listed identity      -> expect that address
  marker alone                        -> expect the service identity
If the unmarked case reflects the caller-supplied address, it is a live information disclosure reachable from any pod in the namespace, and it becomes P1.

Note g9c also found this route is one of the seven @is_public routes 4h6.28 relaxed the caps for, so it is reachable without any credential by design - which is precisely why the reflection question matters.
close_reason:
Landed as api 6624eda, suite 65ccddc. Batched with genetics-results-suite-zyi. NO CODE CHANGE was needed; the deliverable is the measurement and a regression test. Nothing applied to any cluster.

VERDICT: NOT a live information disclosure. The bead asked for this to be probed rather than reasoned about, and that was the right instinct - an earlier bead this session was closed on exactly this kind of "it should be fine after -fad" reasoning and turned out to be wrong.

MEASURED, in-process through the full middleware stack AND over a real local socket (a free port; NOT 4000, which is held by the Genetics Chat API and would have answered for the wrong service). Identical results both ways:
  no headers                      -> HTTP 200 {"authenticated":false,"user":null}
  forged identity header alone    -> HTTP 200 {"authenticated":false,"user":null}   <- the case that mattered
  marker + allow-listed identity  -> HTTP 200 {"authenticated":true,"user":"real.user@finngen.fi"}
  marker alone                    -> HTTP 200 {"authenticated":false,"user":null}

get_authenticated_user demands the internal marker (genetics-results-suite-fad), so a forged X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email never reaches the response body. Unlike chat-backend's /chat/v1/auth, which th2 found reflecting identity plus is_admin, this one leaks nothing - and results-api has no ADMIN_USERS equivalent to enumerate anyway.

THE NULL IS A GENUINE FAIL-CLOSED, NOT AN ARTEFACT OF THE PROBE'S CONFIG - which is the thing worth having checked, because the measurement required stubbing (DEPLOY_ENV=test to avoid Cloud Logging, and an emptied dataset_mapping_files because that module reads GCS at import and this box's ADC is expired). Review re-drove the forged-header case under SIX config variants: baseline, REQUIRE_AUTH=false, empty INTERNAL_API_SECRET, empty allow-list, wildcard allow-list, and secret-unset with REQUIRE_AUTH=false. All six returned null. The reason is structural, not configurational: get_authenticated_user returns None at is_internal_caller() BEFORE the allow-list is consulted, and is_internal_caller itself returns False when the secret is unset. REQUIRE_AUTH is not read by the handler at all. So no stub could have disabled the check under test.

CASE 4 DEVIATES FROM THE BEAD'S STATED EXPECTATION and was pinned as measured rather than "fixed": marker alone returns null, not a service identity, because the handler calls get_authenticated_user (which only ever reports the proxied person) rather than get_verified_user (which would say mcp-tool). Changing it would make a credential-free-reachable route start reporting mcp-tool to any marker holder - strictly worse. Verified nothing downstream wants it: the only /v1/auth caller anywhere in the suite is genetics-results-browser src/store/useAuth.ts:55, and it hits chatApi, not results-api.

BEAD'S RELATED CLAIM CONFIRMED: /api/v1/auth really is one of the seven @is_public routes whose caps 4h6.28 relaxed - exactly 7 decorator sites (rsid GET+POST, variant_sets list+get, auth, root, healthz), matching the enumeration in app/core/limits.py. It is reachable with no credential by design, which is why the reflection question mattered.

REGRESSION TEST ADDED because an unmeasured property with no test needs measuring again - that is the whole reason this bead existed. tests/test_auth_endpoint_identity.py pins all four cases plus the non-allow-listed-identity rejection and the is_public premise. Deliberately OFFLINE - it mounts the router behind Depends(auth_required) as server.py does and drives it over ASGI, needing no GCS, no BigQuery and no live server, unlike essentially the rest of this repo's suite (see genetics-results-suite-w09). Mutation-proven twice by separate agents: removing the is_internal_caller guard makes test_forged_identity_header_alone_is_not_reflected fail with {"authenticated":true,"user":"attacker@finngen.fi"} - the exact oracle it claims to pin.

NON-BLOCKING, recorded not fixed: the test stubs allowed_email_domains={"finngen.fi"}, so it does not pin the wildcard deployment. With ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS="*" - a configuration _email_allowed explicitly supports - marker + non-allow-listed identity returns that address. That is by design and still requires the internal secret, so it is not an unauthenticated oracle.

ENVIRONMENT NOTE FOR WHOEVER PICKS UP NEXT: this machine's Google application-default credentials are EXPIRED. genetics-results-api's suite now aborts at COLLECTION (537 collected, 4 errors) because four modules read GCS at import time, so the 282-failed/263-passed/12-skipped baseline recorded in genetics-results-suite-w09 is currently unverifiable. `gcloud auth application-default login` restores it. The new test here is unaffected - it collects and passes standalone.

title: Add a column TYPE field to configs/datasets.yaml so the sandbox schema docs carry BigQuery types
description:
The generated sandbox schema docs (genetics-results-suite-4h6.13) give every column a description but no TYPE, so an agent writing SQL against them cannot know:

- cs_id is STRING, not an integer id
- chr is INT64, so 'WHERE chr = "chr5"' and 'WHERE chr = "5"' both fail
- gene_group_ids (gene_annotations_v) is an ARRAY and needs UNNEST, not '='
- which columns are FLOAT64 vs INT64 for rounding and division

Deliberately NOT done in 4h6.13: adding a field to datasets.yaml is a schema change, and CLAUDE.md's documentation-ownership table makes docs/datasets-yaml-schema.md and docs/adding-datasets.md wrong in the same commit unless they are updated with it. That was out of scope for a fix round.

Shape: tables.<view>.columns.<col> is currently a plain string. Either widen it to a mapping ({description:, type:}) with the string form still accepted, or add a parallel tables.<view>.column_types block. Populate it from genetics_results.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS rather than by hand, and add a check to scripts/test-sandbox-docs.py that every documented column has a type. Update docs/datasets-yaml-schema.md and docs/adding-datasets.md in the same commit, and check whether db-api's api/yaml_loader.py needs to tolerate the new shape.
close_reason:
Landed as suite 74bfc7f. Nothing applied to BigQuery or any cluster - one read-only SELECT against INFORMATION_SCHEMA.

SHAPE: a PARALLEL tables.<view>.column_types block, NOT a widened columns.<col> mapping. The deciding argument is a deployment fact rather than a code-edit count, and it was verified end to end by review:
configs/datasets.yaml reaches db-api as a ConfigMap (deploy.sh:343, unconditional and independent of any image build) on a path documented as needing NO image rebuild. So config and code SHIP SEPARATELY. A widened `columns` would therefore meet a running db-api pod whose image predates the change - yaml_loader.py:90-98 does result[name] = dict(cols) with no validation, main.py:758 drops the value into /schema's `description`, TableInfo.columns is list[dict[str, Any]] so Pydantic does not object, and the browser renders {column.description ?? "-"} as a bare React child at genetics-results-browser/src/features/chat/SchemaDrawer.tsx:370 -> "Objects are not valid as a React child", schema drawer dead. No amount of same-commit code fixing prevents that, BECAUSE THE TWO ARTEFACTS DEPLOY SEPARATELY. That is the whole argument.
Secondary: main.py:758 already emits a `type` key sourced from LIVE BigQuery field.field_type, so a `type` inside the description slot collides with an existing key from a different source.
An unknown sibling key is invisible to every existing reader - proven by RUNNING db-api's real yaml_loader.load_all() against the edited canonical file (all six loaded blocks unchanged, every column_descriptions value still str), not by reading it. Full consumer audit across all six repos in the report; genetics-results-munge has zero hits and is not a consumer.

TYPES: one read-only SELECT from genetics_results.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS, applied by script, with a round-trip assertion that columns/examples/categorical_columns are byte-identical afterwards.
REVIEW RE-DERIVED THEM INDEPENDENTLY AS A FULL CENSUS, not a spot check: 292 of 292 non-HLA columns match EXACTLY, zero disagreements, and column_types key order is identical to columns key order in every one of the 15 views. The cases the bead names are all correct - chr INT64, cs_id STRING, gene_group_ids ARRAY<INT64>, gene_group_names ARRAY<STRING>, and the FLOAT64/INT64 pairs (cs1_log10bf/cs2_log10bf FLOAT64 vs cs1_size/cs2_size INT64; clpp FLOAT64 vs cs_overlap INT64).
The five HLA columns could NOT come from INFORMATION_SCHEMA because the live view still emits the pre-rename names. They were derived from the columns they alias, on the ground that a SELECT alias cannot change a type, and review verified the live base columns (mlogp, sebeta, af_alt, af_alt_cases, af_alt_controls) are all FLOAT64. So the recorded FLOAT64 is right and nothing was invented.

ONE PREMISE CORRECTION: gene_group_ids was NOT actually undiscoverable - its description already said "ARRAY<INT64> ... match with <id> IN UNNEST(gene_group_ids)". The bead's general point stands (chr, cs_id, and pip vs cs_size had nothing), but that specific example was already covered in prose.

FAIL-CLOSED, PROVEN BY MUTATION AND RE-PROVEN BY REVIEW. gen-sandbox-docs.py RAISES rather than emitting a blank type cell; test-sandbox-docs.py goes 13 -> 17 checks and wraps the render call so a generator refusal surfaces as a named FAIL instead of a bare traceback. Five mutations all caught: a dropped column_types entry, a dropped block, INT64 -> INT, a description pasted where a type goes, and - the decisive one - the generator degraded to render a blank cell instead of refusing.
WORTH KNOWING: only _missing_type_fails_closed catches that last one. Review confirmed _types_in_docs stayed `ok` under that mutation, because with a complete datasets.yaml no blank ever renders. A check that merely proves the type APPEARS WHEN PRESENT fails open, which is the exact defect class this session keeps finding. The property rests on one check and that check works.
Live type verification is deliberately NOT in the harness, and the reason is in the code: it gates scripts/build.sh on a build host with no BigQuery credentials, and every other check there is a pure function of repo files - a live comparison would turn `docker build` into something that breaks when a service account rotates. The offline substitute is a grammar validator that also rejects stale entries naming columns `columns` no longer documents. Re-deriving from INFORMATION_SCHEMA is instead a documented step in adding-datasets.md, where the person who changed the view is.

FINDING, FILED SEPARATELY AS AN OPERATOR ACTION: the DEPLOYED hla_associations_v does not match its committed SQL - it still emits mlogp/sebeta/af_alt/af_alt_cases/af_alt_controls, so ALL FIVE HLA worked examples in datasets.yaml and in sandbox/schema/hla_associations_v.md FAIL against production TODAY with "Unrecognized name: mlog10p". This is NOT drift: it is the deliberate contract-phase state from 4277ffc (genetics-results-suite-5wm), whose message ends "NOT APPLIED to any cluster or to BigQuery" and which added the rollout runbook naming this exact gap. THIS COMMIT LEAVES IT UNCHANGED - configs/datasets.yaml has +327 and -0 lines, purely additive.
Nothing executes the worked examples, which is why it goes unreported: test-sandbox-docs.py contains no bq/bigquery/Client()/dry_run/subprocess reference, and its only example check asserts the SQL's FIRST LINE appears textually in the rendered markdown.

ALSO FIXED: configs/datasets-schema-example.yaml documented colocalization_v as cs_id1/cs_id2 where the live view has cs1_id/cs2_id. Pre-existing, and the new block had repeated it - so it was briefly wrong in two places. Corrected in both. Confirmed nothing reads that file (deploy.sh's `for f in configs/*.yaml` runs after a cd to k8s/, so it iterates k8s/configs/, not the top-level one).

KNOWN AND UNCHANGED: test-sandbox-docs.py cannot run in this checkout at all - genetics-mcp-server has no src/genetics_mcp_server/sdk/ on master, so the harness exits 2 ("harness could not run") before reaching any check. Pre-existing and documented, but it means these new checks GATE NOTHING TODAY; they start gating when the 4h6 sandbox work lands. Review had to stub the directory to exercise them.

title: Document per-view BigQuery partitioning and clustering in configs/datasets.yaml
description:
The sandbox schema docs (genetics-results-suite-4h6.13) now state the partition column for credible_sets_v, colocalization_v and coloc_credsets_v, but nothing documents CLUSTERING for any view. An agent writing SQL cannot see that filtering on a clustering key is nearly free while filtering on a non-key column is a full partition scan.

NOT done in 4h6.13 on purpose: genetics-results-suite-4h6.18 is about to change credible_sets's clustering, and genetics-results-suite-5p5 will rewrite credible_sets_v's variant/chr guidance the moment that swap runs. Anything written today goes stale on swap, and the whole point of the generated-not-transcribed design is that stale rules are the failure mode.

Do this AFTER 4h6.18 and 5p5 land. Derive the values from INFORMATION_SCHEMA (clustering_ordinal_position in genetics_results.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS on the BASE tables, not the views) rather than from memory, and put the text in tables.<view>.description in configs/datasets.yaml so gen-sandbox-docs.py carries it into the image. Add a marker to RULES in scripts/test-sandbox-docs.py so it cannot silently leave the canonical file again.

title: results-api has no per-execution aggregate budget, request-count limit or concurrency limit
description:
Follow-up from the genetics-results-suite-4h6.28 fix round; deliberately out of scope there.

db-api bounds a sandbox execution in aggregate: SANDBOX_AGGREGATE_BYTES_BUDGET is 200 GB per jti, now charged across all four of its BigQuery paths (/query, /schema, /stats, /tables/{t}/sample). results-api has no equivalent. Its SandboxResponseCapMiddleware bounds ONE response at 16 MiB; a script has ~120 seconds of wall clock and nothing limits how many requests it issues, in what concurrency, or how many bytes it accumulates in total.

Concretely missing on results-api:
1. a per-jti aggregate response-byte budget (the analogue of db-api's counter), answering 429 once spent;
2. a per-jti request-count limit;
3. a per-jti (or per-pod) concurrency limit — results-api runs replicas: 1 with an 8Gi limit and preloads the gene maps and the search index, and every in-flight capped request buffers up to 16 MiB.

Note the upstream teardown fixed in 4h6.28 (raising out of send so StreamingResponse's generator is abandoned) bounds what a SINGLE rejected request costs to produce, not what a loop of accepted ones costs.

Production impact today is nil: no sandbox Deployment exists and SANDBOX_ENABLED is "false" on both db-api and results-api. This is the control to add before the sandbox is deployed.

An in-process counter keyed on jti, as in db-api's api/main.py _jti_bytes, is sufficient while results-api stays at replicas: 1 — and would make results-api's replica count load-bearing the same way, so k8s/deployments/results-api.yaml would need the same comment db-api.yaml now carries.
close_reason:
Landed as genetics-results-api 01bcd03 and suite e2ba5d9. Nothing applied - no sandbox Deployment exists and SANDBOX_ENABLED is "false" on both services, so production impact is nil today. THE BEAD'S PREMISE HELD; no correction needed, which was unusual for this session.

FOUR COUNTERS PLUS A MAP BOUND, all keyed on jti, all checked before the handler, all declared as env vars on the Deployment so they are tunable without a rebuild:
  SANDBOX_AGGREGATE_RESPONSE_BYTES_BUDGET  1 GiB  = 64 responses at the 16 MiB cap
  SANDBOX_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_EXECUTION       1000   the byte budget does not bound a loop of SMALL responses
  SANDBOX_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS          4      4 x 16 MiB buffered against an 8Gi pod at replicas: 1
  SANDBOX_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_TOTAL    8      unreachable while the sandbox is concurrency: 1; insurance against raising it
  SANDBOX_MAX_TRACKED_EXECUTIONS           4096   backstop on the accounting map
1 GiB and 1000 are round backstops, not derived from measured script behaviour - the module says so. A reviewer noted the 4 x 16 MiB arithmetic understates real peak (the handler's rendered bytes and its object graph coexist with the middleware buffer), but the conclusion survives easily against 8Gi.

REJECT, NEVER QUEUE. Queueing holds the request while the sandbox's ~120s clock runs - indistinguishable from slow data, unactionable by the script - and can admit work that finishes after its execution is dead, which is the waste 4h6.28 removed. Every rejection carries code/limit/observed so an operator knows WHICH bound was hit; six distinct codes.

CLEANUP DELIBERATELY DIVERGES FROM db-api, and this is the one place the bead's "mirror db-api" instruction was not followed. db-api's 1024-entry LRU can evict a RUNNING execution and silently reset its budget - the fail-open direction. Here eviction requires BOTH past exp + LEEWAY_SECONDS (so no further request can present that jti) AND in_flight == 0. Verified by driving _sweep_locked directly: expired+idle dropped, expired+in_flight=1 SURVIVED, fresh survived. expires_at comes from the signature-covered exp, not anything client-settable.

VALIDATED BY TWO INDEPENDENT AGENTS, sighted and blind. The counting machinery came through clean and the numbers are worth keeping:
- Lock discipline: check-and-reserve is ONE critical section under threading.Lock with no await inside, so there is no check-then-act gap. 200 racing coroutines admitted EXACTLY 4 against a limit of 4; 4000 admit/release pairs across 8 OS threads left requests 4000 / bytes 40000 / in_flight 0 / pod 0.
- No slot leak on the normal path, handler exception, cap rejection, send raising mid-stream, or task cancellation - release is synchronous inside finally, so CancelledError cannot skip it.
- The two token-decode paths cannot disagree: eight header variants (lowercase bearer, double space, duplicate Authorization, non-ASCII latin-1 bytes, uppercase header name, RS256, absent) all agreed or diverged only as middleware=None/auth=401. Forged, expired, aud=db-api, empty-jti and a bare {"alg":"HS256"} stub all 401 with the tracker EMPTY - no free DoS on the map.
- Non-sandbox hot path: 0.27us with no auth header, 0.83us for an opaque bearer, 8.4us for a Google RS256 token (JOSE header parse only - is_sandbox_shaped returns False before any HS256 work), no lock taken, no map entry. Single uvicorn worker confirmed from run_server.py and the Dockerfile entrypoint; replicas: 1, no HPA - so the in-process counters are genuinely per-execution today, and results-api.yaml now carries the same load-bearing comment db-api.yaml has.

THE BLIND VALIDATOR FOUND TWO THINGS THE SIGHTED REVIEW MISSED, which is exactly the case it earns its cost on.

1) NON-2xx RESPONSES WERE NEITHER CAPPED NOR CHARGED. state["capped"] was `caps.enforced and 200 <= status < 300`, so an error body passed through unbuffered - bytes uncharged AND the 16 MiB cap not applied at all. MEASURED: 200,014 bytes delivered under a 500-byte cap; ten such requests delivered 2,000,140 bytes with bytes_sent still 0. The justification in the docstring and three docs was "an error body is small" - false, because FastAPI's 422 handler ECHOES the offending input, so a 100,000-char query param produced a 100,144-byte response, i.e. 1:1 attacker-controlled amplification. The real egress bound via that path was request-count x whatever fits in a URI, not 1 GiB.
FIXED: every status is buffered, bounded and charged. One concrete constraint found while fixing it - an existing test pins that the cap must not rewrite a 404 into a 429 and lose the real answer - so an over-cap non-2xx keeps its OWN status with a bounded stub body. Three new tests, all confirmed FAILING before the change.

2) A TEST NAMED THE DESIGN'S CENTRAL PROPERTY AND DID NOT OBSERVE IT. test_a_stream_is_charged_and_releases_its_slot asserted in_flight == 0 AFTER the request fully returned - terminal state - so it would have passed even if release moved into a FastAPI dependency teardown, the exact mistake the middleware placement exists to prevent.
AND MY OWN PRESCRIBED REPAIR WAS WRONG. I asked for an observation during the streaming body. In FastAPI 0.136.1 a dependency teardown runs AFTER the response body, so that sample reads 1 under BOTH placements and kills nothing - measured by building the mutant. The real discriminator is that admit runs in MIDDLEWARE for every request while a dependency is solved only for a MATCHED route: an unmatched path 404s out of the router with no dependency entered, stranding the slot permanently, and _sweep_locked can never reclaim it because it refuses to evict with in_flight > 0. Mutation table: during-stream [1,1,1] under both; unmatched-route in_flight 0 shipped vs 1 mutant. Both tests kept - the during-stream one still kills handler-return and response.start placements.
The false "generator outlives every dependency's teardown" rationale had been repeated in the middleware docstring and three docs; all corrected.

THE PERIMETER IS DOCUMENTED, NOT PATCHED - and this is what a reader must know:
(a) THE COUNTERS ONLY BIND REQUESTS THAT VOLUNTEER A TOKEN. With no Authorization header the middleware resolves no principal and never calls admit. Seven @is_public routes (/api/v1, /healthz, /api/v1/auth, /api/v1/variant_sets, /api/v1/variant_sets/{name}, GET+POST /api/v1/rsid/variants) answer 200 with no credential - MEASURED 20/20 served with _executions == {} - and the sandbox's NetworkPolicy egress reaches results-api:4000 DIRECTLY, bypassing auth-gateway. So a script that omits the header gets unbounded request rate, egress and concurrency on those routes. app/core/limits.py argued omitting the header cannot buy a looser limit; that holds for the per-response byte cap and is now FALSE for the four counters, and its comment is corrected. FILED SEPARATELY - closing it needs a design decision about identifying sandbox traffic without a token, not a fix round.
(b) sandbox_execution_tracker_full and the pod-wide concurrency limit are CROSS-TENANT denial surfaces. The "23 chat turns/hour" figure is an argument about honest volume, not a bound on an attacker. Also filed.

ALSO FIXED: the module docstring said "Three counters, not one" and "all three limits answer 429" while implementing four plus a map bound and emitting five codes - the suite docs said four correctly, so code contradicted docs on day one. Same stale count in a test name. _env_int now rejects non-integers, empty strings, 0 and negatives (0 turned any limit into "reject everything") and a module-level check rejects TOTAL < PER_EXECUTION, both failing loudly at import.

KNOWN AND LEFT: the over-cap stub response is uncharged, matching the rule that only payload bytes on the wire are charged; state["sent"] is assigned after await send, so a disconnect on the final send undercharges by up to one response; there is no request timeout, so a hung request pins a slot and its map entry - the anti-eviction rule that closes the fail-open direction has no counterpart bounding how long an entry may stay unevictable; no Retry-After on the 429s; no admission metric, so the numbers cannot be tuned from production data; and nothing asserts the jti-uniqueness the whole design rests on - if chat-backend ever minted per-session rather than per-execution, two executions would silently share one budget.

208 -> 218 passed in the credential-free offline lane; test_sandbox_budget.py 19 -> 30, test_response_caps.py 18 unchanged and all still passing. ruff clean on every touched file (21 pre-existing errors elsewhere in the repo, untouched).

title: db-api: compare_digest on str 500s on a non-ASCII bearer, and PyJWT is the only unpinned validator dep
description:
Two small hardening items in genetics-results-db, both noticed during genetics-results-suite-4h6.9 review and both deliberately left out of that change.

1. api/main.py require_auth does hmac.compare_digest(token, INTERNAL_API_SECRET) on str, which raises TypeError on a non-ASCII bearer - a 500 rather than a 401. genetics-results-suite-fad fixed exactly this in results-api (app/core/auth.py compares as bytes with an explicit comment), and th2 found the same bug a third time in chat-backend's api_tokens.py. This is the last known instance in the suite.
   NOT currently reachable: the sandbox branch runs first and a non-ASCII string is not sandbox-shaped (verified: is_sandbox_shaped('a.o.u' with non-ASCII) returns False without raising). So it is latent, not live.

2. pyproject.toml pins PyJWT>=2.10 while the siblings pin exactly (genetics-mcp-server pyjwt[crypto]==2.11.0, genetics-results-api PyJWT==2.12.1). The floor is correct - 2.10 is where PyJWT started rejecting a future iat as ImmatureSignatureError, which the sandbox token's anti-backdating property depends on - but an open upper bound on the one dependency doing credential validation is inconsistent with the other two repos and could drift on a rebuild.
notes: Correction (fix pass): (1) this was NOT the last known instance. A fourth lives in genetics-mcp-server mcp_server.py:_wrap_with_bearer_auth._token_is_valid, which compared MCP_API_KEY on str; api_keys is non-empty whenever that wrapper is installed, so every non-ASCII bearer hit a comparison, and it is raw ASGI middleware, so the TypeError was a bare 500. Fixed to bytes, plus the same line's headers.get(b'authorization').decode(), which raised UnicodeDecodeError -> 500 on a non-UTF-8 header and now yields 401. Both pinned by tests in tests/test_mcp_server.py (raw ASGI scope with byte headers; httpx refuses to encode a non-ASCII header value). (2) the db-api instance was reachable, not latent - measured HTTP 500 pre-fix, in-process and over a real socket. (3) the PyJWT >=2.10 floor gives rejection of a FUTURE iat (post-dating), compensated by sandbox_auth.LEEWAY_SECONDS; ANTI-backdating is enforced by sandbox_auth's own iat < now - MAX_TOKEN_AGE_SECONDS check and is version-independent. Conclusion (keep the floor, pin exactly) unchanged.
close_reason:
Landed as db 997a5e7, mcp 7787b89, suite 65ccddc. Batched with genetics-results-suite-r0l. Nothing applied to any cluster.

THIS BEAD'S OWN PREMISE WAS WRONG, IN THE UNSAFE DIRECTION, and correcting it is the substance of the work. The bead asserted "NOT currently reachable ... latent, not live" because is_sandbox_shaped() returns False for a non-ASCII bearer without raising. That observation supports the OPPOSITE conclusion: returning False is the hand-off. The sandbox branch DECLINES the token, and declining is exactly what drops it into the shared-secret comparison.
MEASURED, not argued, by two independent validators: reverting the comparison and driving a real request returns HTTP 500 on every non-ASCII bearer - confirmed in-process AND over a real socket on a free port (not 4000, which is held by a different service). So db-api had a live 500 on attacker-controlled input where a 401 belongs. An authenticator that crashes on the input it exists to reject is never acceptable, even though it is a DoS/error-oracle rather than a bypass (the request still never reaches a handler).

THE BEAD ALSO SAID THIS WAS THE LAST OF THREE INSTANCES. IT WAS THE THIRD OF FOUR. A blind validator grepped the siblings on the reasoning that after the same bug appeared three times in three repos a fourth was more likely than not - and found it: genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/mcp_server.py:277, inside _wrap_with_bearer_auth's _token_is_valid. Always reachable when that wrapper is installed, because the wrapper is only installed when API keys are configured, so api_keys is non-empty and any() always evaluates at least one comparison. That repo's auth/core.py had ALREADY been fixed to bytes; this call site was simply missed, and the suite spec asserted mcp-server did not share the bug - true only of the identity-header half th2 fixed.
Fixed in the same session, plus a SECOND 500 on the same path: the .decode() of the raw ASGI header raises UnicodeDecodeError on a non-UTF-8 header such as b"Bearer \xff". It now falls through to the existing 401 branch as an absent header does.

TEST TECHNIQUE THAT MATTERS BEYOND THIS BEAD: httpx REFUSES to encode a non-ASCII header value, so a test written the obvious way dies inside the CLIENT and reads as a pass. The bearer must be sent as raw bytes - which is what a non-httpx client puts on the wire and what starlette latin-1-decodes back into a non-ASCII str. Both repos' tests do this: db via a bytes-encoded header, mcp via the hand-built ASGI scope in TestBearerAuthMiddleware. This is how a security test becomes decorative without anyone noticing, and it is the third such trap this session.

ALL FIXES MUTATION-PROVEN ON DISK, each twice over by separate agents. db: reverting the comparison fails all three parametrized cases with `assert 500 == 401`. mcp: reverting the comparison fails the non-ASCII test with TypeError, reverting the decode guard fails the undecodable test with UnicodeDecodeError, and each leaves the other passing (so they are independent, not one test wearing two hats).

PYJWT PINNED at the installed 2.13.0 (was >=2.10), matching the siblings' convention - each pins exactly, to a different version (mcp-server 2.11.0, results-api 2.12.1). No lockfile in this repo to regenerate; the Dockerfile installs from pyproject.toml so the pin binds at image build.
THE COMMENT JUSTIFYING THE FLOOR WAS INVERTED and is corrected in both the pyproject and the suite spec. >=2.10 is where a FUTURE iat became ImmatureSignatureError - post-dating - which is precisely why sandbox_auth.LEEWAY_SECONDS exists. ANTI-BACKDATING, rejecting an OLD iat, is a separate and version-independent property enforced by sandbox_auth's own `int(claims["iat"]) < time.time() - MAX_TOKEN_AGE_SECONDS`, which does not involve PyJWT at all - PyJWT will happily accept an arbitrarily old iat while exp is future. The conclusion (keep the floor, pin exactly) was right; only the reasoning was wrong, and it was inherited from this bead's description.

DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED, filed instead:
- genetics-results-suite-ctq: starlette decodes headers as LATIN-1, so token.encode("utf-8") is not byte-exact with what the client sent. Harmless today - the secret is ASCII and an ASCII str encodes identically under both codecs - and the failure direction would be a 401 for the LEGITIMATE holder, not a bypass. Three repos share the idiom and must move together, so changing one alone would create a real inconsistency where there is currently only a shared latent one.
- genetics-results-suite-tzi: mcp_server.py's query_string.decode() (~line 349, MCP_ALLOW_QUERY_TOKEN branch) has the identical undecodable-bytes 500. Gated off by default. The bead notes that "latent" was also claimed of THIS bug and was false, so it asks for the gating to be verified rather than trusted.

Tests: db 131 passed (baseline 128 + 3); mcp 1299 passed / 74 deselected (baseline 1297 + 2).

PROCESS INCIDENT, my error, recorded so it is not repeated: I ran the sighted reviewer and the blind validator CONCURRENTLY, and both do mutation testing by editing source in place. They collided in the same worktrees - one agent's restore of api/main.py was reverted underneath it after it had verified it, and it observed a mutation applied and restored by something other than itself. Both caught it and both trees were verified byte-identical to the captured baseline afterwards (I re-verified independently with a diff against the pre-review capture). No damage, but mutation-testing agents MUST be serialized on a shared tree.

title: create-secrets.sh blanks eight optional secrets when re-run without them exported
description:
Pre-existing footgun, surfaced by genetics-results-suite-4h6.9's deploy gate and deliberately not fixed there.

create-secrets.sh implements reuse-or-generate for only internal-api-secret, sandbox-token-signing-key and the three oauth2-proxy-secrets. Everything else is --from-literal=x=${X:-}, so a re-run with only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY exported silently BLANKS all eight of:
  openai-api-key, tavily-api-key, perplexity-api-key, mcp-api-key,
  cohere-api-key, external-mcp-servers, admin-users, slack-webhook-url

Consequences: admin page membership collapses (admin-users), gnomAD/Open Targets tool proxying stops (external-mcp-servers), Slack alerting goes silent, and the search API keys die.

4h6.9 mitigated the immediate trigger by changing deploy.sh's missing-secret error to emit a targeted kubectl patch instead of telling the operator to re-run the script. The underlying script is unchanged.

FIX: extend the reuse-then-generate pattern to the eight optional keys, so a value already in the cluster survives a re-run whether or not it is exported. Also add SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY to the script's header comment block, which documents every other overridable secret env var and omits it.

RELATED, same class: the reuse path is kubectl get ... 2>/dev/null | base64 -d || true, so ANY kubectl failure - wrong context, RBAC, transient - is indistinguishable from 'no such key' and silently regenerates. For sandbox-token-signing-key the blast radius is only sandbox executions; for internal-api-secret it is every service.
close_reason:
Landed as suite 86c73ac. Never run against a cluster - all behaviour proven with a fake kubectl in a scratch dir.

BEAD ACCURATE on the list of eight, with one WORDING CORRECTION that matters: it said 'extend the reuse-then-generate pattern to the eight optional keys'. That would be wrong. They are reuse-then-EMPTY. A random API key is worse than an empty one - syntactically plausible, fails at call time rather than at startup - and admin-users and external-mcp-servers have no meaningful random value. The five existing keys keep reuse-then-generate, and one run can do both: measured with openai + admin-users + sandbox-token-signing-key all absent, the first two wrote empty and the third generated.

MEASURED PRE-FIX, so the fix is proven against observed behaviour rather than asserted: cluster seeded with LIVE values, re-run with only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY exported -> all eight blanked. After: all eight preserved. Explicit env still wins.

THE RELATED FAILURE MODE WAS FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE, not deferred, because extending reuse makes it eight times more consequential. Old path: kubectl get ... 2>/dev/null | base64 -d || true, so any kubectl failure was indistinguishable from 'no such key'. MEASURED pre-fix under a simulated RBAC denial against a cluster with intact values: exit 0, internal-api-secret AND sandbox-token-signing-key both REGENERATED, all eight blanked. Post-fix: aborts at the first read, 0 applies, quoting the real kubectl stderr. Same for a connection timeout and for kubectl exiting 127.

REVIEW CAUGHT TWO THINGS, both worth remembering.

1) The first draft used 2>&1, which poisoned the SUCCESS path. kubectl writes to stderr while exiting 0 routinely - gcp auth-plugin deprecation, 'Warning: ... is deprecated', kubelogin notices - and that text landed in the value. MEASURED: warning on stderr + valid base64 on stdout -> abort with a bare 'base64: invalid input', 0 applies. Fail-closed on GNU coreutils, so nothing was destroyed, but it made the script UNRUNNABLE in ordinary GKE environments. INFERRED and the reason it was treated as blocking rather than cosmetic: busybox base64 -d skips non-alphabet characters instead of erroring, so on an Alpine runner the identical input would have decoded to garbage and been written back over the live value. Now captured to a separate temp file (one mktemp at script scope, truncated per call, trap-cleaned) and read only when rc != 0. The decode failure also names the key and secret now.

2) THE SAME BUG AS THIS BEAD'S, two lines further down and missed by the bead: keycloak db-user and admin-user were hardcoded ${KC_DB_USER:-keycloak} / ${KC_ADMIN_USER:-admin} with no reuse. A non-default username was silently overwritten while its password was faithfully reused, leaving Keycloak unable to reach Postgres. Both now reuse-then-DEFAULT - empty is not an option for a username. MEASURED both directions: db-user=custom_kc_user round-trips; an empty cluster still yields keycloak/admin.

VERIFIED BY REVIEW, so do not re-derive: the abort propagates from ALL SEVEN secret_key call sites, not just the one the implementer described - bash DOES propagate a command-substitution failure inside ${VAR:-...} on the RHS of an assignment (measured: rc=7). No write follows a failed read for the same secret. Partial applies can occur across DIFFERENT secrets, but every value in them is the correct reused one - notably cookie-secret is not regenerated when a later read fails, so sessions survive.
Hostile cases all measured: values containing %, $(id), backticks and backslashes round-trip (printf '%s' with a fixed format, no injection); trailing whitespace preserved; a value that IS the string 'Error from server (NotFound)...' is not mistaken for an error, because the NotFound match only runs when rc != 0; a legitimately empty value stays empty; malformed base64 aborts.

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, deliberate: the ENABLE_RAG=true -> COHERE_API_KEY check moved after the reuse block, so a value already in the cluster now satisfies it. Previously it aborted even though the key was present. Confirmed it cannot silently proceed with RAG on and no usable key - an empty cluster value still trips the :? guard.

ALSO CORRECTED, because this change made them false: deploy.sh's stderr remediation text and docs/code-execution-security.md's runbook step both told operators NOT to re-run create-secrets.sh on the grounds that it blanks optional keys, which would now steer them away from the correct fix toward hand-rolled kubectl patching. Both keep the caveat that survives - safe for the optional keys, still aborts without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The stale rationale comment at deploy.sh:184 fixed too. 4h6.9's targeted-patch mitigation itself is still correct and was not reworked.
anthropic-api-key remains env-only and :?-required - fail-closed, aborts rather than blanks - and the header comment now says so instead of claiming 'every key'.

NEAR-MISS WORTH KNOWING, no harm done: an agent simulating 'kubectl missing' used PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, but a REAL kubectl lives at /usr/bin/kubectl, so the pre-fix script ran against the live GKE endpoint 34.76.35.166. It failed client-side at credential acquisition because gcloud was not on that PATH, so no API call reached the cluster and nothing was mutated - but the outcome depended on gcloud being absent, not on care. Every later run used a stub kubectl FIRST on PATH with command -v verified. Any future work on this script must do the same.

FILED SEPARATELY: create-secrets.sh:33 derives PROFILE by grepping terraform/terraform.tfvars, which under set -euo pipefail kills the script with exit 2 and NO MESSAGE when the file is absent - the normal case in a worktree. Fail-safe (0 kubectl calls, 0 applies) but zero diagnostic, and it runs BEFORE deploy.sh in the normal flow, so it is what an operator hits first. Pre-existing, same worktree/tfvars family as genetics-results-suite-82s.
