NOT DONE: trailing-newline stripping by $(...) - a key created via --from-file loses its trailing newline on rewrite. Pre-existing, identical in the old code, not a regression.

title: test-network-policies.py has three residual fail-open paths
description:
Left undone deliberately in genetics-results-suite-4h6.8 after the harness's two blocking holes (inferred policyTypes, namespaceSelector peers) were closed. None is exploitable against the manifests as they stand today; all three require a manifest shape nobody has written yet, which is exactly why they will not be noticed.

1. selects() subset-matches in the wrong direction for sandbox_policies(). It asks whether a policy's selector matches a pod whose labels are EXACTLY {app: sandbox}. A future policy with matchLabels {app: sandbox, tier: untrusted} WOULD select the real pod but is not returned by sandbox_policies(), so every check silently skips it. Fail-open, and mutation testing on the current manifests cannot surface it.

2. The 4h6.7 label-contract check guards on the literal path k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml. If 4h6.7 lands it as sandbox-deployment.yaml, or splits Deployment and Service across files, the check stays inert FOREVER while printing a reassuring 'note:' that scrolls past in deploy output. Consider a glob.

3. any() short-circuits peer evaluation in rules_reaching, so in from: [podSelector chat-backend, ipBlock 0.0.0.0/0] the ipBlock raise is never reached when evaluating chat-backend. Not a hole today because the layer-2 check scans mcp-server and does reach it, but the fail-closed guarantee is weaker than the docstring claims.

Also worth revisiting: the 'sandbox policy exists at all' check is a dead check. default-deny-ingress has podSelector {} and selects() returns True for an empty selector, so it can never fail. Deleting sandbox-policy.yaml entirely is still caught by three other checks, so this is dead weight rather than a hole - but its message asserts something it does not test.
close_reason:
Landed as suite dcb72aa. Nothing applied to any cluster.

THE BEAD NAMED 3 FAIL-OPEN PATHS PLUS A DEAD CHECK. Review found the same shape in SIX more places, so 10 were fixed. Every one was demonstrated on disk as HEAD-exit-0 vs fixed-exit-1, not argued - 33 probes in the final round, all expected. That evidence standard is the only reason these are believable, because the harness reported "checks passed" in every single case beforehand.

FROM THE BEAD:
1. selects() subset-matched the wrong way, so a policy with matchLabels {app: sandbox, tier: untrusted} - which WOULD select the real pod - was skipped by every downstream check. Added may_select(); sandbox_pod_labels() now reads the REAL pod labels once a workload exists instead of assuming the contract subset forever.
2. The label-contract check guarded on the literal path k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml, so under any other filename it would have stayed inert FOREVER while printing a reassuring note. Now discovers the workload.
3. any() short-circuited peer evaluation, so a fail-closed raise on a later peer was never reached.
4. The "sandbox policy exists" check was DEAD - default-deny-ingress has podSelector {} and selects() returns True for an empty selector, so it could never fail. KEPT and made falsifiable rather than deleted: the property is load-bearing, it was merely untested. It now catches a workload whose labels drift out from under every named policy.

FOUND BY REVIEW, SAME CLASS:
5. THE PEER SIDE HAD THE IDENTICAL BUG the bead only fixed on the policy side - peer matchLabels {app: mcp-server, role: tools} did not register as reaching the sandbox, silently uncovering layer 2 of the MCP exclusion at exit 0. THE KEY INSIGHT, and the part worth remembering: the fix is NOT may_select everywhere. Widen/narrow belongs to the ASSERTION POLARITY, not the function. Must-not-reach checks widen (an undecidable peer counts as reaching); must-reach checks narrow, because widening there is fail-OPEN once the pod's full label set is known. `widen` is keyword-only with NO default so every call site must state its polarity. Proved load-bearing in both directions - forcing widen=True on a must-reach check makes it pass, and an undecidable chat-backend peer gives `got set()` -> exit 1.
6. Discovery RELOCATED the bug instead of fixing it: keying on the substring "sandbox" meant a workload named code-exec.yaml went inert again at exit 0, with sandbox-policy.yaml selecting nothing and the sandbox unrestricted.
7. Matching a STRINGIFIED label dict adopted unrelated pods as the sandbox. Giving chat-backend a `sandbox-client: "true"` label - exactly what a future sandbox-client policy peer would use - gave exit 1 with 7 FALSE failures, so deploy.sh would abort a production deploy and point the operator at the security doc. A harness bug blaming a security control is the exact mistake already made once in this epic. Now reads labels["app"] only.
8. LIVE FAIL-OPEN, not hypothetical: the "admits chat-backend and nobody else" sweep iterated POD_LABELS (8 apps) while the file's own inventory listed 11, so a sandbox ingress admitting frontend, keycloak, keycloak-postgres or oauth2-proxy passed everything. Sweep is now the union of all three sources INCLUDING apps derived from the manifests, so it cannot go narrow as a hardcoded list rots.
9. Repo-parse failures exited 1 ("a control is broken") when the truth was 2 ("the harness could not run"). Distinct HarnessError now. Manifests that PARSE but are undecidable still exit 1 - that distinction is the point.
10. WORKLOAD_KINDS omitted Job, CronJob and bare Pod, so a sandbox landing as any of those was invisible to discovery AND to the catch-all meant to backstop discovery, while ordinary Deployments paid the cost. Added, with the CronJob pod template read from spec.jobTemplate.spec.template (a naive addition yields app: None and trips both real CronJobs).

DESIGN DECISION I MADE, on the reviewer's measured recommendation. The inventory catch-all first fired on any workload whose app label was not in a hardcoded list. That taxes every ordinary new service, and since deploy.sh frames exit 1 as "refusing to apply network-policies", a correct answer to "I added a service" would arrive dressed as a policy breach - which is how a check gets deleted instead of fixed. Measured rate: ~2 trips in 4.5 months (k8s/deployments/ history), small but the wrong shape.
Re-keyed on what docs/code-execution-security.md OBLIGES the sandbox to carry: runtimeClassName, a sandbox.gke.io/runtime toleration, automountServiceAccountToken false, or a serviceAccountName present and not genetics-suite. Doc lines 106, 303-305, 1668, 1840 were read and confirmed before relying on them. Unlike a filename these are FORCED - GKE taints the gVisor pool so a sandbox without them does not schedule, and one on genetics-suite forfeits the metadata-credential guarantee the isolation story rests on. Absent-vs-present matters: treating an absent serviceAccountName as a tell fires on the five workloads that declare none.

THREE INDEPENDENT LOCKS on an undiscovered sandbox remain, each proved separately: name/label discovery, the tell-based catch-all, and SANDBOX_ENABLED=true with no discoverable workload.

Real manifests: exit 0, 13 checks (12 before; the dead check was tightened not dropped, and the catch-all is new), 19 policies. Exit-code contract verified against deploy.sh:366-378. PyYAML missing still exits 2.

DELIBERATE DEVIATION, flagged: sweep_labels() also derives apps from k8s/deployments/, beyond the literal KNOWN_APPS union asked for. With the catch-all re-keyed, nothing else enforces KNOWN_APPS membership, so a list-only sweep would silently go narrow as the list rots. The extra source can only widen a widen=True sweep, i.e. only fail closed.

LEFT UNRESOLVED, honestly:
- KNOWN_APPS is now enforced by nothing. The manifest-derived source keeps the sweep complete regardless; the list is a fallback and its comment says so.
- A sandbox that evades name AND label discovery AND declares none of the four tells is still invisible to the catch-all. That is the intended trade - the tells are the forced ones - with the SANDBOX_ENABLED lock as the third guard.
- scripts/test-sandbox-docs.py exits 2 in this worktree (no SDK staged at sandbox/.sdk-src). Pre-existing, out of scope, untouched.

HANDOFF TO 4h6.7: the label contract (app: sandbox, containerPort 8080/TCP, Service sandbox 8080->8080) and flipping SANDBOX_ENABLED to "true" on BOTH db-api and results-api must land in the SAME commit as the workload manifest, or the harness exits 1 and aborts the deploy. That coupling is now enforced from three directions rather than one, and the checks activate on whatever filename and workload kind 4h6.7 chooses.

Stopped after 2 fix rounds per the loop's limit; nothing outstanding was a defect, only the trade-offs recorded above.

title: auth-gateway sets no securityContext on any container, and project-spec claims it does
description:
k8s/deployments/auth-gateway.yaml contains zero securityContext blocks. The existing nginx container never had one, and genetics-results-suite-th2 added a second container (the render-config initContainer) to the same file, so the gap now covers two containers.

docs/project-spec.md asserts 'every application container sets allowPrivilegeEscalation: false ...'. That claim was already stale for this file before th2; it is enumeration rot of exactly the kind CLAUDE.md flags.

auth-gateway is the internet-facing pod, so it is the one that least deserves the exception. Add allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, capabilities drop ALL and RuntimeDefault seccomp to BOTH containers, or correct the doc if nginx genuinely needs something. Note nginx:alpine binds :8080 (unprivileged) so NET_BIND_SERVICE should not be needed - verify before dropping ALL.

Deliberately not fixed inside th2: a one-container fix would have left the file internally inconsistent, and touching the running gateway's security posture is a separate risk decision.
close_reason:
Landed as suite 13f074c. NOT APPLIED to the cluster.

THE BEAD'S PREMISE WAS WRONG IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION. It said 'nginx:alpine binds :8080 (unprivileged) so NET_BIND_SERVICE should not be needed - verify before dropping ALL'. NET_BIND_SERVICE is indeed unnecessary, and that was verified (the only listen is 8080, and neither of deploy.sh's injectable fragments adds a listener - ${LEGACY_REDIRECT} is an `if`, ${KEYCLOAK_SERVER} is a `location`). But a bare drop: [ALL] would still have CRASHLOOPED THE INTERNET-FACING GATEWAY, for an unrelated reason the bead did not consider: nginx:alpine is built --user=nginx --group=nginx and the mounted config has no `user` directive, so the root master chowns its compiled-in temp paths to uid 101 and setuids its workers.

MEASURED with docker against the REAL rendered ConfigMap (extracted from the manifest, run through deploy.sh's substitution with both fragments populated, all eight cluster-local names stubbed via --add-host so nginx actually parses it):
  drop ALL                        exit 1, chown("/var/cache/nginx/client_temp", 101) failed
  drop ALL + CHOWN                master alive holding :8080, setgid(101) failed, worker cannot be respawned, HTTP 000
  drop ALL + CHOWN,SETUID,SETGID  HTTP 200, worker running as nginx
Each of the three is individually load-bearing. The initContainer needs ONLY CHOWN: `nginx -t` is not a dry run - it creates and chowns the same paths - but never forks a worker, so no SETUID/SETGID.
DAC_OVERRIDE is not needed: the rendered config lands 0644 root-owned in a root-owned tmpfs and the master reads it as root; the worker writes only to temp dirs the master already chowned, and to /dev/stdout.

THE SUBTLE ONE, DEMONSTRATED NOT REASONED: allowPrivilegeEscalation: false does NOT break the master's setuid(101). Measured with NNP on and off - identical results, HTTP 200 both ways. no_new_privs gates privilege GAIN through execve of setuid/setgid binaries, not a capable process voluntarily dropping to an unprivileged uid.

Exercised under the shipped cap set with real traffic through stub upstreams on a docker network: /healthz 200, / (auth_request subrequest -> oauth2-proxy stub, then proxy to frontend stub) 200, the Authorization: Bearer -> @api_bearer bypass 200, and a 20 MB POST forcing a client_body_temp file write as uid 101 (the client_max_body_size 50M path) 200. Error log clean.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY BUYS - the honest accounting, because the first draft's framing overclaimed and this is the part worth carrying forward. The WORKER, the process that parses internet traffic, was ALREADY Uid 101 / CapPrm 0 / CapEff 0 under the empty securityContext, because setuid() from root without PR_SET_KEEPCAPS clears the capability sets. Measured in both states. What this change hardens is the MASTER, which never touches attacker input: CapEff 0xa80425fb (the 14-cap default) -> 0xc1, NoNewPrivs 0 -> 1, removing DAC_OVERRIDE, NET_RAW, MKNOD, SYS_CHROOT, SETPCAP, SETFCAP, KILL, FOWNER, FSETID, AUDIT_WRITE. Real - it shortens the post-exploitation chain - but it does NOT reduce the privileges an nginx RCE lands in, and the master is still uid 0 on a writable rootfs. Not meaningfully harder to exploit; less useful once exploited.

THE DOC HALF FAILED THE SAME WAY THE ORIGINAL DID, ONE ROUND LATER. Replacing 'every application container sets allowPrivilegeEscalation: false ...' with an explicit enumeration produced a list that was WRONG ON DAY ONE: it missed k8s/cronjobs/keycloak-postgres-backup.yaml (google/cloud-sdk:slim, Postgres password from keycloak-secrets, no securityContext at any level) - seven listed, eight exist. And the self-check shipped alongside it told future editors to re-derive with `grep -rn allowPrivilegeEscalation k8s/deployments/`, which BY CONSTRUCTION cannot see k8s/cronjobs/. The check carried the identical blind spot that produced the error.
Fixed: eight named, grep widened to k8s/, plus the caveat that the grep only re-derives the HARDENED side - the non-hardened side is the COMPLEMENT of the workload inventory and must be derived by listing and subtracting, never by grepping.
Final classified inventory, re-derived twice independently: HARDENED = results-api, chat-backend, mcp-server, bff, db-api, auth-gateway x2, plus the sandbox pods. NOT HARDENED = frontend, oauth2-proxy, keycloak, postgres, rag-service, monitor CronJob, analyze-conversations CronJob, keycloak-postgres-backup CronJob. The only other securityContext hits in the tree are pod-level fsGroup (chat-backend:24, monitor-cronjob:19), which is not hardening.
The SANDBOX pods were in neither column and are the most hardened containers in the cluster (runAsNonRoot, uid 65532, allowPrivilegeEscalation false, readOnlyRootFilesystem). They are created dynamically with no manifest in k8s/, so no grep of this repo will ever find them - a second, independent reason the grep instruction alone is insufficient.

THE RETIRED SENTENCE SURVIVED VERBATIM IN A THIRD DOC, and that one is load-bearing: docs/code-execution-security.md:90-91 anchored the sandbox isolation-boundary argument on 'every application container sets ... drop: [ALL]'. After this change it is false twice - once for the eight unhardened workloads, again because drop: [ALL] is no longer flatly true even where set, since auth-gateway adds three back. Now scoped to the suite's own service containers, stated as not cluster-wide, both falsifiers named, and pointing at project-spec for the list rather than being a third copy. Three copies is how this rotted.
JUDGEMENT CALL by the fix agent, worth knowing: it kept the NOUN 'baseline' rather than retiring it, because section 2's decisions table has four rows justified entirely by 'Matches baseline' / 'Exceeds the cluster baseline'. Retiring the term would have left those dangling and repairing them was out of scope.

ROLLOUT RISK IS LOW BY CONSTRUCTION, and this is why it was safe to ship unapplied: replicas: 1 with no strategy block gives default RollingUpdate maxUnavailable = floor(0.25 x 1) = 0 and maxSurge = 1, so the new pod must reach Ready before the old is deleted. A CrashLoop or a failing initContainer leaves the CURRENT gateway serving. Now stated in the spec.
WATCH ON FIRST ROLLOUT ANYWAY: the live pod still runs the pre-th2 single-container manifest as uid 0 with securityContext {}, so this rollout introduces the initContainer AND the constraints at once. `nginx -t` resolves every proxy_pass hostname at parse time, so a Service missing in the target profile stalls the rollout - safely, but deploy.sh runs `kubectl rollout status ... || true`, so a stall does not fail the deploy loudly. Same for a live internal-api-secret containing anything outside [A-Za-z0-9+/=_.-], which hard-fails the init container.
Also observed: when the initContainer fails at chown, its error handler takes the wrong branch and prints 'FATAL: nginx rejected the config template itself, independently of the secret' followed by the chown message. Unreachable with CHOWN granted, but if caps are ever tightened again the diagnostic will point at the config rather than the capabilities.

NOT VERIFIED: that the rendered PRODUCTION config behaves identically - upstream resolution was stubbed via /etc/hosts rather than the real `resolver kube-dns`, though nginx resolves proxy_pass names at parse time either way so this is not capability-sensitive. No TLS, no GFE. GKE node support for seccompProfile RuntimeDefault is INFERRED (GA since 1.19 on COS/containerd), not checked against the live cluster.

NOT DONE, filed separately: running the pod as uid 101 with an emptyDir over /var/cache/nginx, which would remove all three capabilities AND make the master non-root - the part that actually matters. Measured that --user 101:101 with the unchanged config fails at mkdir("/var/cache/nginx/client_temp") (13: Permission denied), because /var/cache/nginx is root:root 0755 in the image, so the emptyDir is genuinely required. Out of scope here and a separate risk decision on the internet-facing pod.
Also not done: hardening the eight unhardened workloads.

title: _process_download_hints swallows every download failure, which has now hidden two identical defects
description:
Found during genetics-results-suite-buc on 2026-08-10, and it is the reason that bead and genetics-results-suite-bef both went unnoticed in production.

src/genetics_mcp_server/llm_service.py:367 (genetics-mcp-server):

    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f'Failed to create download: {e}')

then falls through to 'return result' with _download_data ALREADY POPPED. So any failure in building a download produces:
- no download link in the response
- no error visible to the user
- no error visible to the model
- only a warning in a log nobody reads

TWICE NOW this has hidden the exact same defect class. _convert_to_tsv's 'results' branch does results[0].keys(), which is an AttributeError on a positional list. bef found it for the five by-gene BigQuery tools; buc found the identical thing in get_hla_by_allele months later. In both cases the tool APPEARED to work - the model got an answer, the user got prose - and only the download silently vanished.

There are roughly 25 _download_data producers. Any future shape defect in any of them fails exactly this way.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: the failure is indistinguishable from 'this result did not warrant a download link', so nobody reports it as a bug. A user who wanted the TSV assumes the feature is inconsistent rather than broken.

FIX OPTIONS, roughly in order of preference:
(a) narrow the except to what is genuinely expected (disk/IO on the download store) and let a shape error propagate, since a shape error is a programming defect and should be loud
(b) keep the catch but surface it - append an INCLUDE_IN_RESPONSE note saying the download could not be prepared, so the user knows the link is missing rather than not offered
(c) at minimum, log at ERROR with the tool name and the observed shape, so the log line is greppable and identifies the producer

(a) and (b) are complementary. Do not do (c) alone - a louder log is still a log nobody reads.

Consider also whether _convert_to_tsv should accept both shapes rather than requiring callers to pick, since 'which shape does this consumer want' is what both defects got wrong. Note bef deliberately chose shape-per-consumer for a real reason - the {columns, rows} form avoids materialising up to 100k dicts for the download - so unifying the shapes is NOT automatically right. Read bef's reasoning (commit 45c729e) before changing that.
close_reason:
Landed as genetics-mcp-server 3947d20. 1299 -> 1336 passed, 74 deselected, ruff clean.

THE CATCH IS NOW AN ALLOW-LIST, (OSError, UnicodeEncodeError), derived by PROBING what the download store actually raises rather than by guessing a tuple. That distinction was load-bearing: csv.Error derives from Exception, NOT TypeError, and {"columns": [...], "rows": [1, 2]} raises exactly that - so the bead's suggested exclusion list (AttributeError, TypeError, KeyError, IndexError) would have LEAKED it. Probed and confirmed: PermissionError/FileExistsError/ENOSPC from the store are all OSError; UnicodeEncodeError is reachable from genuine upstream data, since json.loads decodes lone surrogates that utf-8 cannot encode - a data defect, not a programming defect, so it should not kill a turn.
_convert_to_tsv now validates both shapes UP FRONT and raises DownloadShapeError naming expected vs observed, before csv sees anything.

THE FIRST DRAFT GOT THE CENTRAL JUDGEMENT WRONG, and this is the part worth carrying forward. It let DownloadShapeError PROPAGATE - the bead's option (a) read literally - on the stated grounds that a malformed payload is 'a defect in the producing tool, never a runtime condition'.
THAT CLAIM IS MEASURABLY FALSE. executor.py:1095-1099 builds _download_data from resp.json(), the RAW PARSED HTTP BODY of the sibling results-api, never shape-checked. Same at executor.py:2274-2283 (summary_stats) and across MOST of the ~25 producers; only the six BigQuery-backed tools (executor.py:548, :1606) and the UniProt helper (which explicitly pre-validates) build the shape locally.
So a shape defect is often UPSTREAM DRIFT, not a local bug. Propagating would have coupled chat-turn success to another repo's response shape: chat_api.py:577 converts it to an SSE error event, so a user asking a genetics question gets NO ANSWER where before they got a correct answer minus a link. This repo's own docs already record one instance of exactly that cross-repo drift (results-api silently ignoring data_types), and CLAUDE.md's cross-repo section exists because sibling changes are undetectable from here.
RESOLVED as catch-and-surface for both paths. The bead's (a) and (b) are complementary as it said, but 'loud' must mean loud in CI and in logs, not fatal in production - the regression test already provides the CI loudness that (a) was reaching for.

BOTH PATHS ARE LOUD, with DISTINCT greppable ERROR tokens carrying tool name and observed shape: DOWNLOAD_SHAPE_DEFECT (with exc_info) and DOWNLOAD_FAILED. The separation matters operationally, not cosmetically - the suite's scripts/monitor/alerter.py queries severity >= WARNING on k8s_container logs and pushes new alerts to Slack, so the warning -> ERROR promotion plus a stable token is the actual mechanism by which these get noticed. A reviewer called that the single highest-value line in the diff.
Each path surfaces its own INCLUDE_IN_RESPONSE note. The shape note explicitly does NOT suggest re-running - a deterministic shape defect fails identically every time, and the original wording would have had the model tell the user to do something futile. DOWNLOAD_FAILED_NOTE was also reworded: it said 'server-side storage error', true of OSError and wrong for UnicodeEncodeError.

A SECOND SILENT HOLE, NOT IN THE BEAD, was found and closed: {} and {"data": [...]} and a bare list previously returned b"", which fell through `if tsv_bytes:` and dropped the download just as quietly as the exception path did. Confirmed real by mutation - under HEAD both returned with no exception, no link and no note. {"results": []} still returns b"" with no spurious note.
Also validated `filename`, the one field reaching json.dump unchecked. A non-str filename raised TypeError, escaped the allow-list, killed the turn AND left an ORPHANED .tsv on disk, because the data file is written before the sidecar. Unreachable today (every producer passes an f-string or str) but it was a NEW fatal path that HEAD had swallowed.

_convert_to_tsv DELIBERATELY NOT UNIFIED. Read bef (45c729e) as the bead instructed: it chose shape-per-consumer because {columns, rows} carries up to 100k positional rows and re-materialising them as dicts only to flatten them again is pure waste. That reasoning holds, so the mismatch fails loudly and early instead, with the 'results' branch error explicitly telling the caller that positional rows belong in the {columns, rows} form. Validation costs one isinstance per row and materialises nothing.

THE REGRESSION TEST IS THE ACTUAL DELIVERABLE and it was MUTATION-TESTED, not asserted. HEAD's _convert_to_tsv and _process_download_hints were exec'd back into the live module namespace from a pytest plugin: 22 of 48 tests FAILED. Every new class fails when the swallow is restored.
test_malformed_payload_never_returns_quietly is the guard that generalises - it makes the SWALLOW itself the failure (no exception => there must be an INCLUDE_IN_RESPONSE note), so it catches a future regression whatever exception type a new defect produces, rather than matching an enumerated list. Verified against 18 NOVEL payloads the test file does not enumerate (results as str/generator/list-of-None, columns as str, rows as generator, payload as None, non-str dict keys, ...): ZERO swallows. So the code generalises and the 9 enumerated payloads are illustrative, which is the right split. Two of them are verbatim reproductions of the bef and buc production payloads, so this would have caught both.

KNOWN AND ACCEPTED: two degenerate-but-valid payloads ({"results": [{}, {}]}, {"columns": [], "rows": []}) still produce a link to a 1-3 byte file. Pre-existing, harmless, deliberately not 'fixed'.
Subagent downloads still store owner=None (pre-existing, unchanged).

title: No git hooks are installed, so check-doc-drift.sh has never run
description:
Found during validation of genetics-results-suite-262 on 2026-08-07.

CLAUDE.md documents a documentation-ownership table and states: 'scripts/check-doc-drift.sh warns (never blocks) on commits that violate this; it runs from the pre-commit hook.'

It does not run. $(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/hooks/ is EMPTY - no pre-commit hook, no hooks of any kind, in the main checkout or any worktree. There is no CI and no yamllint either.

So the entire doc-drift mechanism has been inert for however long the hook has been missing. That is consistent with what this epic keeps finding: docs/project-spec.md asserted a node-pool pinning that was never applied AND surge arithmetic (3951m / 13.60 GiB from a '2651m / 7.91 GiB steady state') that no profile has ever produced; the datasets/phenotypes docs carried a stale ~33k row count; the ALL_VIEWS list was one short. Every one of those is exactly what check-doc-drift.sh exists to catch.

Note the script only WARNS by design, so installing it would not have blocked any of those commits - but nobody saw the warning either, which is the part that matters.

FIX:
1. Add an installer so the hook is actually present - either scripts/install-hooks.sh run once, or core.hooksPath pointed at a tracked directory, which survives clone and worktree creation without a manual step. Prefer the latter: a hook that must be installed by hand is a hook that is missing on the machine that needs it.
2. Verify it fires from a WORKTREE, not just the main checkout. This epic runs in three worktrees across three repos, and git resolves hooks via the common dir - confirm the path logic inside check-doc-drift.sh works when the working tree is <repo>/.claude/worktrees/<name>. Bead genetics-results-suite-e47 documents the same class of worktree path bug in sync-datasets.sh, which resolves siblings from the repo root and silently skips.
3. Consider whether warn-only is still the right call given the hit rate. A warning nobody reads and a check nobody runs are the same thing.

Related: genetics-results-suite-e47 (worktree path resolution in sync-datasets.sh).
notes:
PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-08-11 by direct investigation. THE HOOK DOES RUN. Do not act on this bead as written.

The description says ".../hooks/ is EMPTY - no pre-commit hook, no hooks of any kind". That checked .git/hooks/, which does contain only .sample files - but it did not check core.hooksPath. BEADS SETS core.hooksPath to <repo>/.beads/hooks, and .beads/hooks/pre-commit is present, executable, and TRACKED IN GIT (git ls-files .beads/ lists all five hooks).

Its last 5 lines are, verbatim:
  # --- doc-drift warning (not managed by beads) ---
  # never blocks: || true keeps a broken check from stopping a commit
  if [ -x ./scripts/check-doc-drift.sh ]; then
    ./scripts/check-doc-drift.sh || true
  fi

OBSERVED FIRING, not merely read: committing configs/datasets.yaml from the db-only-architecture WORKTREE on 2026-08-11 printed "doc-drift warning - this commit changes code the docs describe", naming datasets-yaml-schema.md and adding-datasets.md. So item 2 of the FIX section - "verify it fires from a WORKTREE, not just the main checkout" - is already answered YES. git runs hooks with cwd at the top of the working tree, so the ./scripts/ relative path resolves correctly in a worktree.

WHAT REMAINS REAL, and is the whole of this bead now:
1. core.hooksPath is LOCAL git config and is NOT tracked, so a fresh clone has no hooks at all until beads sets it. The tracked hook files survive a clone; the setting that points git at them does not. Anyone cloning this repo and committing gets no doc-drift warning and no beads export, silently.
2. THE DOC-DRIFT BLOCK IS APPENDED BELOW A BEADS-MANAGED MARKER BLOCK headed "BEADS INTEGRATION v1.0.3 - This section is managed by beads. Do not remove these markers." The version number implies beads rewrites this file on upgrade. If it regenerates rather than patching between the markers, the appended doc-drift section is lost silently - and the failure mode is exactly the one this bead was filed about, with nobody noticing.
3. Unverified: whether the sibling repos (genetics-results-api, -db, -browser, -munge, genetics-mcp-server) have any equivalent. This repo is the spec of record, but a cross-repo change can leave a sibling's docs stale.

SO THE FIX IS NOT "add an installer". It is: make the doc-drift block survive a beads hook regeneration (e.g. move it to its own tracked script invoked from a location beads does not own, or verify beads patches between markers rather than overwriting), and document/automate the core.hooksPath setting for a fresh clone.

The description's third point - whether warn-only is still right given the hit rate - stands unchanged and is a judgement call for the user. Note the warning DOES get seen: it fired in this session and was read and acted on.

The evidence cited in the description for the mechanism being inert (stale node-pool claims, surge arithmetic, ~33k row count, ALL_VIEWS one short) is still real drift, but it is NOT explained by a missing hook. check-doc-drift.sh only warns on path->doc mappings; it cannot detect a doc that enumerates something the code no longer matches, which is what every one of those was. That is a limitation of the check itself, worth its own bead if the user wants it.
close_reason:
Landed as suite 418457f. Worked as RE-SCOPED IN THE NOTES, not as the description asked - see the notes field for the premise correction.

THE DESCRIPTION WAS WRONG. It claimed no hooks are installed and check-doc-drift.sh has never run, based on .git/hooks/ holding only samples. It does not check core.hooksPath, which beads points at .beads/hooks, where a tracked, executable pre-commit runs the drift check - observed firing from a worktree on 2026-08-11. So FIX items 1 (add an installer) and 2 (verify it fires from a worktree) were already satisfied before this bead was picked up.

RISK 1 TURNED OUT FALSE TOO, and it is worth having measured rather than left as a standing worry. The doc-drift block sits below a marker headed 'BEADS INTEGRATION v1.0.3 - managed by beads', and a version number implies regeneration. MEASURED in a throwaway repo: beads PATCHES between its markers and preserves everything outside them. Sentinel survived `bd hooks install`, `bd hooks install --force`, a simulated upgrade (markers forced to v0.9.0 then reinstalled - re-stamped to v1.0.3, sentinel intact), and `bd hooks uninstall` (only the beads section is stripped, file kept). `bd hooks install --help` documents it: 'any user content outside the markers is preserved across installs and upgrades.' Confirmed independently by a second agent.
The installer's re-append is therefore redundant belt-and-braces, kept because it costs nothing and does not depend on a third party's implementation detail staying true.

RISK 2 IS REAL AND IS WHAT THIS BEAD ACTUALLY FIXED. core.hooksPath is LOCAL git config and is not tracked. The tracked hook FILES survive a clone; the SETTING that points git at them does not. A fresh clone gets no doc-drift warning and no beads export, silently. `bd init` is what sets it, so it only appears once someone runs beads.
scripts/install-git-hooks.sh sets it and re-appends the block if missing; --check reports without repairing and exits 1 loudly.

THE WORKTREE DETAIL IS THE POINT, given this is the fourth instance of the class this session (sync-datasets.sh/e47, terraform.tfvars/82s, bd's own issues.jsonl export/0xs). `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` returns a path RELATIVE TO CWD from a subdirectory - '../../.git' from a main subdir, absolute from a worktree - so the value is absolutised with cd+pwd before use. Without that it produces garbage from any subdir. VERIFIED from four positions: main root, main subdir, worktree root, worktree subdir; correct hooks_dir in all four, and commits in both the main checkout and the worktree ran the drift script.
The config lands in the SHARED .git/config (measured via git config --show-origin; extensions.worktreeConfig is not enabled), so one install wires every worktree - while each worktree still runs its OWN copy of check-doc-drift.sh, because git sets cwd to the working-tree top and the hook's path is cwd-relative. Both halves are correct.
ABSOLUTE path chosen deliberately, not by default: `bd hooks install` itself writes an absolute path (measured: bd 1.0.3 wrote /.../t3/r/.beads/hooks), so a relative value would ping-pong between the two tools and make --check report a spurious problem on every run. A relative path does otherwise work and would survive a repo move.

THE TRIPWIRE: deploy.sh and build-all.sh call `install-git-hooks.sh --check || true` near the top, so an unwired checkout surfaces on the first build or deploy rather than never.
--check IS GENUINELY READ-ONLY - important, because I told other agents it was safe to run against the real repo. Every write (git config, mkdir -p, cat >>, chmod) sits below an unconditional early exit in check mode. Proven, not just traced: a full find of the tree before and after is byte-identical, md5sum of .git/config unchanged, core.hooksPath still unset, exit 1 with the warning on stderr.
NO CONFLICT with the two other beads that touched deploy.sh in the same hour: the call sits at line 19, after SCRIPT_DIR and the .env load, before `cd terraform` and before both hi0's profile-identity guard and 82s's tfvars guard. It reads nothing they write. `|| true` on a plain command neutralises set -e regardless of exit code, including the 127 if the script is missing - verified. A hooks warning cannot abort a deploy or a build.

ALSO FIXED: deploy.sh:401's comment claimed 'there are no git hooks and no CI', 382 lines below the tripwire this same commit added - the exact drift class the check exists to catch, in the file that gained the check. Now matches the corrected sentence in project-spec.

SIBLING REPOS CHECKED (read-only, nothing installed): all five - genetics-results-api, -db, -browser, -munge, genetics-mcp-server - are configured IDENTICALLY. Each tracks its own scripts/check-doc-drift.sh and all five .beads/hooks files, each has core.hooksPath set as untracked local config, each has the doc-drift block wired into its pre-commit, and NONE has an installer. So the coverage gap the bead feared does not exist, but every one shares the fresh-clone hole. Two spot-checked directly; three INFERRED by uniformity. Only genetics-results-browser has CI at all and it does not run the drift check. Porting install-git-hooks.sh to the siblings is a five-line copy if wanted - deliberately not done here.

LEFT TO THE USER, unchanged: whether warn-only is still right given the hit rate. Note the warning DOES get seen - it fired in this session and was acted on.
FILED SEPARATELY: check-doc-drift.sh does path->doc mappings only and cannot detect ENUMERATION rot - a doc that lists something the code no longer matches. That is what every drift this epic found actually was (the node-pool pinning, the surge arithmetic, the ~33k row count, ALL_VIEWS one short - and, this session, an enumeration that was wrong on the day it was written). Recorded as a Known limits paragraph in project-spec.

NITS LEFT: main_root=$(dirname "$common") assumes the git dir is named .git inside the worktree root, so a --separate-git-dir or bare-main layout resolves wrongly - commented, not handled. And the installer's heredoc is a second source of truth for the doc-drift block; nothing enforces that it matches .beads/hooks/pre-commit, so an edit to one silently diverges - commented.

title: SDK functions backed by results-api lose their schema on an empty result
description:
Recorded as a DELIBERATE DEVIATION from genetics-results-suite-4h6.25's ticket text, 2026-08-07. Verified empirically: hla(phenotype=...) on a no-hit phenotype raises ColumnNotFoundError 'mlog10p' not found when filtered.

Task .11 established, and .25 restated as a requirement, that an SDK function must preserve column names on an empty result so a script filtering a no-hit query does not hit ColumnNotFound. The BigQuery-backed branches honour this - db-api derives 'columns' from the BigQuery job schema, which is populated even for a zero-row result (genetics-results-db/api/main.py:574).

The results-api-backed branches CANNOT: results-api returns rows only, so an empty response carries no schema to recover names from. This is SDK-wide, not introduced by .25 - every results-api-backed SDK function behaves this way.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN .25: the only fix available there was hardcoding results-api's 15-column HLA schema into the SDK, across a repo boundary, where it would rot silently the next time that endpoint changed. That is a worse failure than the one it prevents.

Real fix options, in rough order of preference:
(a) have results-api return column names alongside rows on the affected endpoints, the way db-api already does, and carry them through - fixes the whole class in one place
(b) derive the schema from the same source results-api does (_HLA_HEADER_SCHEMA and its siblings) via a generated, checked-in artefact rather than a hand-copied literal, so drift fails loudly
(c) have the SDK return an explicitly-typed empty frame only where a schema is already known locally

Scope it as the class, not as hla() alone - count how many SDK functions are results-api-backed before choosing.

Impact on the epic: a script hitting an empty result gets an exception rather than an empty frame, costing a retry iteration. That inflates the code-execution arm's iteration count in genetics-results-suite-4h6.23, in the same direction as genetics-results-suite-5wm.
close_reason:
Landed as genetics-results-api 49c1692, genetics-mcp-server b5e12a7, suite 477d9f5. Nothing applied to any cluster.

THE BEAD'S "SCOPE IT AS THE CLASS" INSTRUCTION WAS RIGHT AND hla() WAS THE TIP. Census done first, mechanically, by walking each SDK method -> its ToolExecutor methods -> base_url vs bigquery_url, transitively: 25 public functions (22 returning frames). 16 results-api-only, 5 branch-dependent, 3 db-api-only, 1 LD server. So 19 of 22 frame-returning functions have a results-api branch, and 16 were ACTUALLY EXPOSED - the other three (lookup_phenotype_names, get_dataset_display_names, normalize_gene_symbols) build frames from column literals they already hold.

OPTION (a), and the key realisation is that results-api ALREADY HAD THE SCHEMA AND WAS THROWING IT AWAY. tsv_stream_to_list reads the file's own TSV header line, and reads it EVEN FOR A ZERO-ROW FILE, then discards it. The JSON range responses are BARE ARRAYS, so an envelope would have been breaking - hence an X-Columns RESPONSE HEADER instead. One edit in range_response covers all 23 call sites across 11 routers.

WHY NOT (b): unsound, not merely awkward. header_schema is a VALIDATING SUPERSET - tsv_stream_to_list only asserts every file column is IN it - so a generated artefact from _HLA_HEADER_SCHEMA and its siblings would OVER-CLAIM columns for any file carrying fewer, and would add a cross-repo build dependency. genetics-results-suite-7yg proved exactness for HLA only. 4h6.31's column_types is NOT a precedent: those are BigQuery views with an INFORMATION_SCHEMA ground truth, which results-api endpoints do not have.
WHY NOT (c): re-imports exactly the hardcoded-literal rot 4h6.25 rejected, and reaches 1 of 16 functions.

ADDITIVE, PROVEN PER CONSUMER rather than asserted:
- body byte-identical, pinned by test_body_is_unchanged_by_the_header;
- browser: the only two .headers reads in its entire src/ are content-type on the chat-backend SSE stream - ZERO results-api response-header reads - and X-Columns is not in CORSMiddleware's expose list, so browser JS cannot see it even if it tried;
- mcp-server: resp.json() everywhere, the only resp.headers read is the new one;
- TSV path untouched, per what 7yg established (a byte pass-through that never reads header_schema; buffering the header out would add latency and a new 500 mode on the download route).
Header size: widest is coloc at 41 columns / 397 bytes against auth-gateway's proxy_buffer_size 16k - ~40x headroom, and even nginx's 4k default would pass. The SDK path never touches nginx anyway (sandbox egress is pod-to-pod to results-api and db-api only).

THE TRAP, caught during implementation: a ToolExecutor result dict IS the MCP tool payload - register_mcp_tools returns it verbatim and it is the chat backend's model input - so the first pass, which added column_names unconditionally, would have violated the epic's frozen-MCP-output rule. Now gated on ToolExecutor(expose_columns=False) and spliced with ** so an off path is byte-identical.
VERIFIED TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS by review: (i) mechanical - git diff -U0 of executor.py decomposes into 33 hunks, 31 of them pure insertions of the same `**self._columns_meta(resp),` token and 2 pure additions, and {**{}} preserves insertion order in CPython; (ii) runtime - the service's executor built exactly as mcp_server.py:79 does, driven through six tools with a stub returning X-Columns, leaked nothing and kept key order. The only expose_columns=True in the repo is sdk/client.py:148 inside GeneticsClient's own fallback; an INJECTED executor keeps its own setting. Review tried and COULD NOT construct a path where a True executor reaches the MCP surface.
column_names is deliberately kept distinct from db-api's `columns`: db-api's is REQUIRED to read positional rows, this one is advisory, and routing results-api's named dicts through the positional constructor would give up from_dicts' strict=False fallback for the mixed-type columns upstream produces. _frame consults it ONLY when the result is empty.

ALSO FIXED, found in review: columns_header's fail-open guard tested only for a comma and non-ASCII, but "\r".isascii() is True, so CR and LF passed it - and the docstring claimed a name that cannot survive the round trip drops the header. Unreachable today (streams.py raises for any header column not in header_schema, and all 137 distinct schema column names across app/config/ match [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+), so SCHEMA VALIDATION was the only thing standing between a malformed TSV header and response splitting - not the guard. Now rejects non-printable characters too, with a test.

NOT COVERED, and this is the honest residue: 4 of the 16 exposed functions are NOT fixed - gene_burden/gene-based, gene_annotations, gene_disease, search. Their endpoints compute JSON rather than streaming a TSV, so they never pass through range_response and have no file header to advertise. They degrade to today's bare empty frame - no regression, no fix - and that degradation is pinned by a test so an absent header can never raise something new. Fixing them means each router declaring its own output columns, which is (b)-shaped work.
A doc slip worth recording: gene-based results was named in the handoff but omitted from the "not covered" list in ALL THREE repos' docs, and the results-api spec claimed 34 call sites where there are 23. Both corrected - counts are exactly what CLAUDE.md flags as rotting.

TESTS: results-api 226 -> 227 passed offline (9 in tests/test_columns_header.py). mcp-server 1360 passed / 74 deselected, 24 in tests/test_sdk_empty_result_schema.py, driven through a MockTransport so all three layers are exercised rather than a fake executor, including the literal bead reproduction and a 16-case parametrize over the wired branches. Mutation-proven: forcing expose_columns=False at the SDK's construction site fails 18 of 24, and review reproduced that independently and confirmed the 6 survivors are the tests that SHOULD survive (non-empty, no-header degradation, byte-identity, and the _frame units). ruff clean on every touched file.

IMPACT ON THE EPIC: a script hitting an empty result no longer costs a retry iteration, which was inflating the code-execution arm's iteration count in genetics-results-suite-4h6.23.

title: SDK covers 40 of the 44 API-category tools - decide whether the last four are gaps or deliberate
description:
Found while fixing a doc count during genetics-results-suite-4h6.25 on 2026-08-07.

Counting category == 'api' in TOOL_DEFINITIONS gives 44. Cross-referencing those names against every .py under src/genetics_mcp_server/sdk/ finds 40 referenced. These four have no SDK wrapper:

  analyze_variant_list
  get_phenotype_report
  get_credible_sets_stats
  get_myvariant_annotations

WHY THIS MATTERS AND IS NOT MERE COMPLETENESS: the SDK is the entire surface a sandboxed script gets. Anything absent from it is unreachable from the code-execution arm, so genetics-results-suite-4h6.23 would score that arm as unable to answer those questions - a measurement artefact, exactly the failure genetics-results-suite-4h6.25 was filed to prevent for HLA.

FIRST determine, per tool, which of these it is:
(a) genuinely unreachable from a script - a real gap, needs an SDK function
(b) reachable but un-named, because the SDK collapses a {shape} x {product} grid so names deliberately do not map one-to-one
(c) deliberately tool-only because a script can compose it from primitives - analyze_variant_list and get_phenotype_report look like orchestration over things the SDK already exposes, in which case the right answer is to leave them out and say so, not to wrap them
(d) out of scope for the sandbox by design - get_myvariant_annotations calls an EXTERNAL service, and the sandbox egress allow-list in docs/code-execution-security.md may deliberately not permit it. If so, the benchmark must account for that rather than the SDK papering over it.

The measurement decision follows from the answer, so settle it before genetics-results-suite-4h6.23 runs.

docs/project-spec.md:269 now honestly states 40 of 44 rather than claiming full coverage.
notes:
ANSWERED 2026-08-07 by review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.25, verified two independent ways (regex over executor.\w+ calls in sdk/client.py intersected with category=='api'; and cross-referencing tool names against every .py under sdk/). Count confirmed: 44 api tools, 40 referenced.

The four resolve as follows - the bead asked which of (a)-(d) each is, and they differ sharply:

analyze_variant_list -> (b) MERELY UN-NAMED. Hits /v1/credible_sets_by_variant and /v1/nearest_genes; the SDK wraps BOTH as credible_sets(variant=) and gene_annotations(nearest_to=). It is a canned 257-line rollup over data a script already has. Reproducing it in polars is precisely what the code-execution arm is for. NO coverage hole.

get_credible_sets_stats -> (b)/(c) REACHABLE, LESS CONVENIENT. Calls /v1/credible_sets/{resource}/stats, a server-side aggregate the SDK cannot hit directly - but sql() reaches credible_sets_v, so the same counts are a GROUP BY away. NO coverage hole.

get_phenotype_report -> (c) UNREACHABLE AS AN ARTEFACT, but no data is out of reach. /v1/phenotype/{resource} returns a MARKDOWN NARRATIVE, not rows; the SDK has no generic HTTP escape hatch. Its underlying numbers all come from products the SDK exposes. Already on the deliberate presentation-tools exclusion list at docs/project-spec.md:332. NO coverage hole.

get_myvariant_annotations -> (d) GENUINELY UNREACHABLE DATA, and the ONLY one of the four that is. Goes out through external_client to myvariant.info; neither sql() (BigQuery views only) nor any SDK function touches it. A sandboxed script cannot obtain ClinVar/CADD/dbNSFP-style clinical annotations AT ALL.

SO THE REMAINING WORK IS NARROWER THAN THE BEAD ASSUMED - it is one tool, not four.

THE DECISION LEFT: get_myvariant_annotations is a REAL benchmark asymmetry. If any benchmark question needs clinical variant annotation, the code-execution arm cannot answer it while the tool arm can - the same class of artefact HLA was. It is excluded from the sandbox deliberately (docs/project-spec.md:332 lists myvariant in the excluded external/third-party group, and the sandbox egress allow-list in docs/code-execution-security.md does not permit third-party egress), so the answer is probably NOT to wrap it but to make genetics-results-suite-4h6.23 account for it: either exclude such questions from the benchmark set, or record them as a known, explained loss rather than letting them silently depress the arm's score.

It is only in the 44 at all because it is categorised 'api' rather than 'external'. Recategorising may be the cleanest fix and would make the coverage number self-maintaining.

title: get_hla_by_phenotype tool description names a column that endpoint does not return
description:
Found by review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.25 on 2026-08-07.

tools/definitions.py:1278 tells the model, for get_hla_by_phenotype: "Read `mlogp`, NOT `pval`".

The advice is right in spirit - that endpoint has no pval column and the guidance exists to stop the model inventing one - but the spelling is wrong for this branch. get_hla_by_phenotype goes to results-api /v1/hla/{resource}, whose _HLA_HEADER_SCHEMA (genetics-results-api/app/routers/hla.py:39) spells it mlog10p. It is get_hla_by_ALLELE, which reads hla_associations_v, that spells it mlogp.

So the description points the model at a column that does not exist in the payload it is describing.

This is what makes genetics-results-suite-5wm bite: a model primed on this description writes pl.col('mlogp') against the phenotype= branch of the SDK's hla() and gets ColumnNotFoundError.

NOT fixed inside genetics-results-suite-4h6.25: it edits a live MCP tool description, and per CLAUDE.md changes unrelated to the task at hand get asked about first. It is a one-word fix.

Fix alongside genetics-results-suite-5wm - if that bead decides to harmonise the SDK's column names, the right spelling here depends on which way it goes.
close_reason:
Landed as mcp 3da9f43, alongside genetics-results-suite-5wm (batched - same files, same defect class).

IT WAS TWO SITES, NOT ONE. The bead named the tool description. Grepping found the same wrong advice in src/genetics_mcp_server/config/defaults.py:77-81, the system prompt that is present in EVERY conversation. Fixing only definitions.py would have left the STRONGER signal telling the model to rank HLA results on `pval` - the tool description is read once when the tool is considered, the system prompt is always in context.

Both now say to rank on mlog10p. definitions.py:1278 (get_hla_by_phenotype) and :1310 (get_hla_by_allele, "Ranked by mlog10p"), plus the system prompt line.

Why the advice was actively harmful rather than merely stale: the HLA tools do not return `pval` in a form the model can rank on usefully, and a model told to rank on pval either invents the column or sorts the wrong direction - mlog10p sorts DESC for significance where pval sorts ASC. So the failure mode was silently inverted rankings, not an error.

VERIFIED no straggler: grepping src/ for mlogp now returns only min_mlogp occurrences, which are correct - min_mlogp is a tool PARAMETER and part of the public input schema, deliberately untouched. Its description at definitions.py:1317-1320 wisely names no column at all.

Batched with 5wm because 5wm renamed the very column this advice should point at; doing them separately would have meant two passes over definitions.py and defaults.py with a window where the advice named a column that did not exist yet.

Tests: mcp 1297 passed / 74 deselected (unchanged).

NOT APPLIED to any cluster - the system prompt ships in the mcp-server image and the tool descriptions with it, so this reaches users only at the next build/rollout, which is covered by 5wm's rollout section.

title: sync-datasets.sh resolves sibling repos from the repo root, so it silently skips when run from a worktree
description:
Found 2026-08-07 while fixing genetics-results-suite-bnb. Out of that bead's scope, left alone, but it will bite the next person.

scripts/sync-datasets.sh copies the canonical configs/datasets.yaml into the sibling service repos for local dev. It resolves them relative to the repo root as ../genetics-results-db, ../genetics-mcp-server and so on.

Run from a git worktree the repo root is <repo>/.claude/worktrees/<name>, so those relative paths point outside the tree entirely and resolve to nothing. The script WARNS and SKIPS rather than failing, so the sync silently does not happen.

Consequence seen for real: the genetics-results-db worktree's local datasets.yaml (gitignored, generated) predated master's HLA commit and had metadata for 14 of 15 views, missing hla_associations_v entirely. Anything reading it - including the API at startup, which raises without it - would have been working from a stale registry. The agent had to copy the canonical file by hand.

This matters more now that the epic runs in worktrees across three repos, and deploy.sh calls sync-datasets.sh best-effort before building the ConfigMap, so a stale copy can reach a deployment.

FIX: resolve the sibling paths from the git COMMON dir rather than the working tree - git rev-parse --git-common-dir gives the main checkout's .git even from a worktree, so its parent is the real repo root. Or resolve via git rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree / an explicit SUITE_ROOT env var. Whichever is chosen, make a failed sibling resolution LOUD rather than a warn-and-skip: a silent no-op sync is how a stale registry reaches a deployment.
close_reason:
Landed as suite cdc044f. Batched with genetics-results-suite-6o3 (same defect class).

PREMISE CONFIRMED AND WORSE THAN WRITTEN. The bead said the script warns and skips from a worktree. It does - but MEASURED in a throwaway layout, if a directory of a sibling's name happens to exist BESIDE THE WORKTREE, the old script COPIES THE CANONICAL FILE INTO IT while the real sibling stays stale. Both halves in one run: `WARN: repo not found, skipping .../wt/../genetics-results-api` AND `OK: copied to .../wt/../genetics-results-db/configs/datasets.yaml` (the decoy), with both real siblings left at 14 views and no hla_associations_v.
HONEST QUALIFICATION, since I overstated this once: that requires a worktree literally named `genetics-results-db` under .claude/worktrees/, and none exists (only db-only-architecture). It is a demonstrated CAPABILITY of the naive relative path, not an observed event. check-worktree-paths.sh had flagged this inverse case as undetected; it is now impossible rather than undetected.

FIX: siblings resolve from `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, absolutised with cd+pwd before dirname. That absolutisation is the actual bug at the heart of this - with -C, a relative answer is relative to THAT directory, so it must be absolutised there or the result is garbage from any subdirectory. Same incantation install-git-hooks.sh (rxw) needed.

FAILURE MODES SPLIT, so that "loud" does not mean "breaks the deploy":
  sibling not checked out on this machine  -> SKIP,  exit 0
  sibling root unresolvable                -> ERROR, exit 1
  directory of the right name, wrong repo  -> ERROR, exit 1, other siblings still sync
Verified by REPRODUCTION rather than by reading that this cannot fail a deploy: deploy.sh:338-341 invokes it as `... || echo "WARN: ... (continuing)"`, and under set -euo pipefail errexit is suppressed on the left of ||, no pipeline is involved so pipefail is irrelevant, and the list's status is echo's 0. Lab: script exits 1 -> WARN printed -> deploy continued, rc=0.
The wrong-repo check reads pyproject.toml's name. First version used `grep -q "^name = \"$sib\""`, which is formatter-brittle - a TOML reformat, single quotes or removed spaces would turn a working sync into exit 1. Now tolerant of spacing and quote style but still anchored on the closing quote, so genetics-results-db-fork is still rejected. Verified both directions. It passes for every real sibling today (both have `name = "<repo>"` on line 2), so this was prevention, not repair.
SUITE_SIBLING_ROOT added for layouts where .git does not sit beside the repo root.

check-worktree-paths.sh (0xs) loses its sync-datasets case - nothing left to detect once the script resolves correctly - and now covers three. The count in project-spec was corrected: it said "one preflight for all four" four lines below a table row saying it no longer checks the fourth.

ALSO CORRECTED, a false claim in THREE places: the sibling configs/datasets.yaml copies are described as "committed". MEASURED FALSE - gitignored in both siblings (genetics-results-api/.gitignore:186, genetics-results-db/.gitignore:39, both under a comment saying they are synced from here) and `git ls-files configs/` returns nothing. deploy.sh's comment additionally justified the sync as preventing drift in copies "baked into freshly built images", which is IMPOSSIBLE - build.sh clones from GitHub, so a gitignored file cannot reach an image. datasets-yaml-schema.md's section was written PRESCRIPTIVELY ("should be committed ... lets CI compare"), so rather than silently deleting an intent it now records that committing them for a CI drift check was intended, never implemented, and would first require these repos to have CI at all - verified there are no .github/workflows in either sibling, and the only CI in the suite is genetics-results-browser's, which runs no drift check.

TESTED ONLY IN A THROWAWAY LAYOUT - the script writes into sibling checkouts, so it was never run against the real repos. Seven cases covered: old-from-worktree (the decoy write), new-from-worktree, new-from-main-checkout, sibling absent, wrong-repo directory, non-git copy, and SUITE_SIBLING_ROOT.

title: genetics SDK does not cover the HLA tools
description:
Found 2026-08-07 after merging master into the epic worktrees.

Master added get_hla_by_phenotype and get_hla_by_allele (genetics-mcp-server commit c8d8aa3, with tests/test_hla_tools.py). The genetics SDK built by genetics-results-suite-4h6.11 predates them, so its 17 functions cover 42 of the now-44 api-category tools.

That matters beyond completeness: the SDK is the surface a sandboxed script gets, so anything missing from it is unreachable from the code-execution arm. A benchmark comparing that arm against the full MCP tool surface would score it as unable to answer HLA questions - a measurement artefact, not a real difference.

FIX: add an hla() function collapsing both tools the way every other product does, with the shape as an argument: hla(phenotype=...) and hla(allele=...), exactly-one-selector enforced by the existing _one_of, and _reject on any argument the chosen branch cannot honour.

Follow the conventions .11 established and its review found necessary:
- percent-encode every caller-controlled URL path segment via _seg (61 were unencoded before; httpx normalises ../ so an unencoded segment reaches arbitrary endpoints with the internal bearer attached)
- return polars.DataFrame, raise GeneticsError rather than returning {'success': False}
- preserve column names on an empty result so a script filtering a no-hit phenotype does not hit ColumnNotFound
- raise on truncation rather than returning a silent prefix
- if it goes through db-api rather than results-api, carry columns through and build the frame from them: db-api returns rows POSITIONALLY, which is what produced transposed stringified frames on five other paths

Check first WHICH backend the two tools use - results-api (commit 21034cf added an /hla endpoint) or BigQuery (hla_associations_v exists) - and follow the matching precedent. Also check whether the trait column spelling ('phenotype', a third convention) needs surfacing in the SDK's docstring.
close_reason:
Landed as genetics-mcp-server 5d0ac78. 1223 -> 1244 passed, 74 deselected, ruff check clean. Reviewed + fix round + re-verification; no blocking findings survived.

WHAT LANDED: sdk/client.py gains hla() with _one_of(phenotype=, allele=) and per-branch _reject (genes refused on allele=; min_mlogp/min_info/limit refused on phenotype=). min_* default to None and are substituted in-branch so min_info=0, which meaningfully DISABLES the imputation filter, is forwarded rather than eaten. SDK coverage of api-category tools goes 40/44 (see below - it was never going to be 44).

TICKET PREMISE CORRECTED - it asked WHICH backend the two tools use and assumed one answer. It is BOTH, ONE EACH: get_hla_by_phenotype -> results-api /v1/hla/{resource}; get_hla_by_allele -> BigQuery hla_associations_v. The per-phenotype tabix files cannot span 2,712 phenotypes, so the reverse question has no file to read. This is the only SDK collapse whose branches read different stores, so the db-api positional-rows guidance applied to the allele= branch only.

CONSEQUENCE THE TICKET MISSED: the two branches return DIFFERENT COLUMN NAMES for the same quantities - results-api mlog10p/se/af/af_cases/af_controls vs the view's mlogp/sebeta/af_alt/af_alt_cases/af_alt_controls. Both spellings verified against the real schemas (genetics-results-api/app/routers/hla.py:30 and configs/datasets.yaml:831), not inferred. Kept as ONE function and documented rather than renamed: harmonising asserts the two backends' quantities are semantically identical, which needs checking against the munge code, not assuming from the name. Filed as genetics-results-suite-5wm and made a blocker of .23, since it biases the code-execution arm's iteration count.

TWO FINDINGS I ESCALATED ABOVE THE REVIEWER'S NIT LABEL AND FIXED:
1. resource was the ONE caller-controlled SQL literal in executor.py not passed through quote_literal (line ~1439), and /v1/hla/{resource} was the one unencoded URL path segment (that endpoint landed in c8d8aa3, after the _seg sweep). The reviewer rated it NIT because db-api restricts to read-only SELECT anyway. Escalated because this epic's entire purpose is to put prompt-injectable LLM-authored strings into these arguments, and get_hla_by_allele is the exact method this task modified. Also moved LIMIT {int(max_rows)} to sql_int(maximum=_MAX_SQL_LIMIT), which was safe only because query_database happens to strip the trailing LIMIT.
   Verified: 11 hostile resource values and 6 bad max_rows values reach the SQL builder ZERO times (counted awaits, not assert_not_awaited), and surface to a script as GeneticsError rather than an empty frame, because GeneticsClient._payload raises on success=False. MAX_ROWS renders LIMIT 100000, exactly sql_int's inclusive maximum - no off-by-one that would make every default SDK call fail.
   37 real resource ids validated against the allow-list, zero rejected. The load-bearing argument is not the enumeration though: four other executor paths ALREADY gate resource names through quote_literal, so a live name this rejects would already be breaking asm_qtl, open_chromatin, mpra and mpra_pip_concordance.
2. docs/project-spec.md claimed the SDK replaces '42 API-category tools'. Re-derived from TOOL_DEFINITIONS: 44 exist, SDK reaches 40. Per CLAUDE.md's counts-rot-silently rule this belonged in the same commit.

DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE TICKET TEXT: an empty result on the phenotype= branch does NOT retain its schema (verified: ColumnNotFoundError). The ticket required preserving column names on empty results. results-api returns rows with no schema to recover names from, and the only fix available here was hardcoding its 15-column schema across a repo boundary where it rots silently - a worse failure than the one it prevents. SDK-wide, not introduced here. Filed as genetics-results-suite-6uk with three real fix options. The BigQuery-backed branches DO honour it, because db-api derives columns from the BigQuery job schema, which is populated even for a zero-row result.

MCP OUTPUT UNCHANGED, as the epic requires: get_hla_by_allele gained with_metadata: bool = False routed through _query_metadata so columns/truncated reach the SDK. definitions.py:2274 passes five positional args, so nothing in the tool surface can set it. Default-path payload keys verified byte-identical, pinned by a test in both directions.

LEFT UNDONE ON PURPOSE, both from c8d8aa3 landing beside 45c729e rather than through it, both changing live MCP output which this epic forbids until the profile flips:
- genetics-results-suite-buc (P1): get_hla_by_allele hands the model unlabelled positional lists. Confirmed empirically - results[0] == ['K11_COELIAC','HLA-DQB1','DQB1*02:01',1596.65,...] with no columns key. Exactly the defect bef fixed for the by-gene tools. Also needs the _download_data hole checked.
- genetics-results-suite-84o (P2): get_hla_by_phenotype's description says 'Read mlogp' while that endpoint returns mlog10p. One word, but it is what makes 5wm bite.

ALSO FILED: 5zz (SDK covers 40/44 - resolved per-tool during review; only get_myvariant_annotations is genuinely unreachable data, so the remaining decision is one tool not four, and it belongs to .23 rather than the SDK), bi1 (batched nits: raw-vs-normalized resource echo, two doc redundancies, the ruff-format drift on executor.py).

ENVIRONMENT: the 6o3 trap bit again and is now confirmed as a standing hazard in this repo - the editable install points at the MAIN CHECKOUT, so bare python/pytest in a worktree imports genetics_mcp_server from /home/jkarjala/suite/genetics-mcp-server/src, which has no _seg at all. Only the worktree's own .venv/bin/python resolves correctly. The test-runner agent correctly refused to proceed on this. Every number above was produced by an agent that asserted the resolved path first.

title: Agents dispatched into a sibling repo cannot read this beads database
description:
Orchestration defect found 2026-08-07 while fixing genetics-results-suite-bef. The fix agent flagged it; earlier agents did not.

Each repo in the suite has its OWN beads workspace. Verified:
  genetics-results-suite/.beads   -> 179 issues (this epic lives here)
  genetics-mcp-server/.beads      -> 127 issues
  genetics-results-db/.beads      -> 7 issues

bd resolves the workspace from the working directory. So an agent working in /home/jkarjala/suite/genetics-mcp-server/.claude/worktrees/... running 'bd show genetics-results-suite-4h6.1' gets 'no issue found matching'.

Every implementation and review agent dispatched into the mcp-server or db worktrees during this epic was instructed to 'bd show <bead> and read its notes field'. None of them could. Only the last one said so.

IMPACT WAS CONTAINED because every prompt restated the task detail inline - which is why the work came out correct. But it means:
- the notes fields written as durable cross-task handoffs (e.g. .4's 'secret=true now also means no metrics row', .19's user authorization and constraints) reached agents only because they were repeated in the prompt, not because they were read
- an agent could silently proceed without the context it was told to fetch, and several did without flagging it

FIX, pick one:
(a) Orchestrator stops telling cross-repo agents to run bd, and always inlines the bead text and notes. Simple, works today, but the notes stop being a durable channel and become prompt-authoring discipline.
(b) Give agents the suite path explicitly: 'run bd from /home/jkarjala/suite/genetics-results-suite'. bd would then resolve the right workspace.
(c) Consolidate: track cross-repo epics in one workspace and reference it from the others.

Also worth deciding: the sibling repos' beads databases (127 and 7 issues) are separate backlogs that this epic has been ignoring. Check whether anything in them conflicts with or duplicates the epic's work.

title: usage SSE chunk folds cache reads and creations together, so cost cannot be computed exactly
description:
Found building the replay harness (genetics-results-suite-4h6.4) on 2026-08-07. Small change, disproportionate value.

llm_service.py emits a per-iteration 'usage' StreamChunk carrying iteration, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_input_tokens, total_output_tokens, context_window, context_percent.

TWO PROBLEMS for anything measuring cost off the stream:

1. The chunk's input_tokens is NOT the billed input. llm_service.py ~786 sets it to input_tok + cache_read + cache_create - i.e. the whole context - while total_input_tokens accumulates only raw input_tok. Anyone reading input_tokens as billed input overstates it, badly, on a cache-heavy turn.

2. Cache READS and cache CREATIONS are folded into that single number and never separated. They differ by more than 12x in price (Opus: ~0.50 vs ~6.25 per M tokens). So an exact USD figure cannot be derived from the stream at all.

The replay harness works around (2) by reporting an INTERVAL - cost_usd_min pricing all cached tokens as reads, cost_usd_max pricing them all as creations - rather than fabricating a single number. That is honest but it weakens the primary metric that genetics-results-suite-4h6.23 gates the whole code-execution rollout on. Production data shows the cache-read share swinging 11% -> 52% across a turn's iterations, so the interval will not be narrow.

FIX: add cache_read and cache_create to the usage StreamChunk payload in llm_service.py. Both values are already computed and logged one line above (the 'API call iteration=' log line carries cache_read= and cache_create=), so this is exposing what already exists, not new instrumentation. Then the harness can compute exact cost and drop the interval.

Note chat_turn_metrics (task .1) DOES store cache_read_tokens and cache_create_tokens separately - but the benchmark runs with secret=true, which writes no row, which is why it reads the stream instead. This is the gap between those two paths.

title: Worktree venv trap: uv run resolves to the pyenv shim and tests the main checkout
description:
Discovered 2026-08-07 while implementing genetics-results-suite-4h6.1.

In a freshly created git worktree of genetics-mcp-server, 'uv run pytest' resolved to the PYENV SHIM (/home/jkarjala/.pyenv/shims/pytest) rather than the worktree's own venv — pytest was never installed in the worktree .venv. That global interpreter imports genetics_mcp_server from the MAIN CHECKOUT at /home/jkarjala/suite/genetics-mcp-server/src.

Consequence: a test run in the worktree silently exercises MAIN CHECKOUT source against WORKTREE tests. Edits made in the worktree are invisible, and the run reports green. The baseline established this way (977 passed) happened to be numerically correct only because both trees were at the same clean commit b2a1df4 — had the main checkout been dirty, every result would have been meaningless.

FIX for any agent working in a genetics-mcp-server worktree:
1. Run 'uv sync --extra dev' in the worktree (installs the declared dev extra into the existing venv; does not create a new one).
2. ASSERT resolution before trusting any result:
     uv run python -c "import genetics_mcp_server, sys; print(genetics_mcp_server.__file__); print(sys.executable)"
   Both paths must be under the worktree.

Corrected baseline after the fix: 977 passed, 74 deselected, 0 failed (~150s), verified under two pytest-randomly seeds. pytest-randomly 4.1.0 IS installed and active, so the suite is genuinely shuffled and order dependence is tested.

Worth considering whether to make this fail loudly rather than relying on every agent remembering — e.g. a conftest.py assertion that the imported package path is under the rootdir.
close_reason:
Landed as genetics-mcp-server 91349bf, genetics-results-api 0c63ce7, genetics-results-db a79c816. Batched with genetics-results-suite-e47.

The bead's own suggestion - "a conftest.py assertion that the imported package path is under the rootdir" - implemented in all three python repos. It raises pytest.UsageError from pytest_configure, so the run aborts BEFORE COLLECTION rather than surfacing as a buried test failure, and the message names both resolved paths plus the fix.

THE THREE REPOS ARE NOT SYMMETRIC, AND ASSUMING THEY WERE WOULD HAVE SHIPPED THE WRONG GUARD IN TWO OF THEM. Install modes established empirically, not assumed:
  genetics-mcp-server   EDITABLE install (.venv/.../_editable_impl_genetics_mcp_server.pth points at one tree's src/). A foreign interpreter imports a foreign tree - the exact trap. Guard compares the package's __file__ against rootdir.
  genetics-results-api  NOT installed; `app` is a NAMESPACE package
  genetics-results-db   NOT installed, no [build-system] at all; `api` is a namespace package
For the latter two __file__ IS None (verified: app.__file__ is None, type(app.__path__) is _NamespacePath), so the mcp-shaped assertion would have been LITERALLY INAPPLICABLE. They compare every __path__ entry instead.

THAT ASYMMETRY SURFACED A REAL, CURRENTLY-SILENT LEAK in the two namespace repos, and it is the more valuable finding here. Namespace packages MERGE every matching sys.path entry, so PYTHONPATH pointing at the main checkout adds its app/ to __path__ alongside the worktree's. MEASURED: app.__path__ ends up [<worktree>/app, <worktree>/app, <main checkout>/app]. A module present only in the main checkout imports from there, and a deletion made in the worktree is invisible. PYTHONPATH=<checkout> is exactly what a bare `python scripts/...` run needs in results-api, so this is reachable by ordinary use, not just by the pyenv-shim accident the bead described.

NO SPURIOUS FIRE, checked where it could plausibly happen rather than assumed: both sides of every comparison are Path(...).resolve(), so symlinks, trailing slashes, .. segments and /home-vs-realpath all normalise - there is no string comparison to attack. rootdir inference holds when running pytest from tests/ in api and db (all three repos have pyproject.toml at the root). And there is no CI, Dockerfile or tox/nox anywhere in the three repos that installs non-editable and then runs pytest, so no existing workflow trips it.
Guards proven to catch the REAL trap in all three: running the worktree's tests with the MAIN CHECKOUT's interpreter fired the mcp guard at configure with both paths named, exit 4, zero tests collected; PYTHONPATH=<main checkout> fired the api and db guards.
Suites unaffected: mcp 1360 passed / 74 deselected, api 236 passed offline, db 140 passed, --collect-only clean in all three.

KNOWN LIMIT, stated rather than papered over: _NamespacePath recomputes on sys.path change, so a conftest, plugin or test that mutates sys.path AFTER pytest_configure is not caught - measured, a post-import append does grow __path__. The realistic vector (PYTHONPATH) is present at configure time, so this is a documented boundary rather than a hole.
NIT LEFT: the mcp guard would abort a legitimate future "pip install . and test the installed wheel" workflow, and its message asserts unconditionally that the interpreter is not this tree's .venv, which would be wrong in that case. Nothing does that today.

STRAY FILE NOT COMMITTED: a uv.lock appeared untracked in the genetics-results-db worktree as a side effect of an agent running uv there. It is new (no git history) and was not part of this work, so it was deliberately left unstaged rather than swept into the commit. Decide whether that repo should have a lockfile on its own merits.

title: Backfill phenotype and dataset metadata into BigQuery
description:
Highest-leverage single backfill. Phenotype/trait metadata and the dataset registry exist today only as per-dataset metadata_file JSONs (datasets.yaml:1190+) plus the resources/profiles blocks, reachable only through results-api. That is why a phenotype question costs a search call, a lookup call and then the real query.

Load them as BigQuery tables (phenotypes, datasets) with a phenotype_v view, so trait-code resolution becomes a JOIN inside a single query rather than a separate roundtrip. Tens of thousands of rows - small.

This unlocks lookup_phenotype_names, get_resource_metadata, get_dataset_display_names, list_datasets and the FILTERING half of search_phenotypes. Fuzzy ranked search stays on results-api - BigQuery cannot replace it and it remains the entry point of most conversations.

Files: genetics-results-db/schemas/phenotypes.sql + phenotype_v.sql (new), scripts/load_phenotypes.sh (new), api/main.py VIEWS allowlist, configs/datasets.yaml, docs/adding-datasets.md.
notes:
USER DECISION 2026-08-07: authorized to run against production BigQuery. This work is ADDITIVE - it creates new tables and views and touches no existing data - which is why it is cleared ahead of .18.

Still required: dry-run every statement first and report estimated bytes before executing. Do not TRUNCATE or REPLACE anything that already exists.

Highest-leverage backfill in the epic: phenotype/trait metadata and the dataset registry exist today only as per-dataset metadata_file JSONs (configs/datasets.yaml:1190+) reachable through results-api, which is why a phenotype question currently costs a search call, a lookup call and then the real query. As BigQuery tables with a phenotype_v view, trait-code resolution becomes a JOIN inside a single query.

Fuzzy ranked phenotype search STAYS on results-api - BigQuery cannot replace it and it is the entry point of most conversations. This backfill unlocks the FILTERING half only, plus lookup_phenotype_names, get_resource_metadata, get_dataset_display_names and list_datasets.
