close_reason:
Phenotype and dataset metadata backfilled into production BigQuery. genetics-results-db worktree 52e9175, genetics-results-suite worktree d96a913. phenotypes 32,611 rows, datasets 888. 47 tests pass. One reviewer verified against production, one fix round.

ADDITIVE ONLY - review confirmed no TRUNCATE/DROP/ALTER/DELETE touched any of the 12 pre-existing tables; the loader writes WRITE_TRUNCATE to two new names and is idempotent.

TICKET FRAMING WRONG TWICE, both found by VERIFYING rather than reading:
1. The join key is trait_original, not trait. trait is a display string (Height,_inverse-rank_normalized); trait_original holds the phenocode (HEIGHT_IRN). The first table keyed on trait and joined ZERO rows SILENTLY. Verified live after the fix: FinnGen_R14 1380/1425, kanta 328/328, Open Targets 20312/20312, genebass 4501/4501 in both exome tables - and five datasets still go to zero on trait.
2. Neither resource nor the registry id can be the key - the relation to the results-view dataset value is many-to-many in BOTH directions (pgc_scz+pgc_bip inside PGC; genebass_exome+genebass_gene_based inside genebass; finngen_pqtl is FinnGen_Olink in credible_sets but FinnGen_Olink_3K in colocalization). That mapping exists in NO config - it is baked into munge-produced TSVs - so BQ_DATASETS_BY_DATASET_ID owns it.

CAUGHT IN REVIEW - the same silent-wrong-answer class, twice more:
- db-api /query auto-qualifier did a bare string replace. Adding two common English words to the allow-list corrupted string literals: a LIKE pattern containing the word datasets had the fully-qualified table name spliced into it, which RUNS and returns zero rows. authorize_query cannot catch it - the SQL is valid and touches only allowed tables. Renaming the table was REJECTED as the fix: it repairs one word and leaves phenotypes, variant_annotation, gene_annotations, open_chromatin. The replace now rewrites only FROM/JOIN positions. All 47 examples across all 14 views verified to still qualify AND dry-run clean. Known residual, documented and pinned by a test: FROM/JOIN inside a string literal is still rewritten.
- phenotypes.dataset_id was documented as joining datasets.dataset_id but resolved to NOTHING for every registry entry that lost a merge (388 kanta rows). Now labelled provenance, not a join key, naming the two ids that match nothing.
- The drift cross-check disabled ITSELF: a bq failure yielded an empty string that read as falsy, so validation was skipped and the load proceeded anyway. Now refuses unless ALLOW_UNVALIDATED=1.
- validate() was missing the mapped-minus-live direction. Added; found 7 registry entries in no results table (IIBDGC plus 6 QTD sub-studies). Suppressed deliberately via ABSENT_FROM_RESULTS with a reason each, emitted with dataset NULL, and SELF-EXPIRING - the build fails if a suppressed name goes live. All four checks are now fatal, not advisory; the previous advisory warning for IIBDGC had been emitted and ignored.

VERIFIED CORRECT BY REVIEW: schema NOT NULL choices against real data; unpartitioned plus clustered matching gene_annotations and peak_to_gene; the generate_resource_sql.py ALL_VIEWS and monitor/bq_summary.py exclusions, because their resource is a real registry column rather than a name-derived CASE so a coverage check would be circular; cross-repo docs complete in both repos; 0 duplicate keys in either table, joins 1:1 with no fan-out.

DELIBERATELY OUT: eQTL Catalogue QTD ids are sub-STUDIES occupying the dataset column, so they are datasets rows - putting them in phenotypes would produce rows that never join. Chromosome encoding N/A, neither table carries coordinates.

title: Materialize variant/resource as stored columns and re-cluster credible_sets
description:
Pure win, independent of which agent interface wins - do it regardless.

credible_sets_v derives BOTH variant and resource in the view (schemas/credible_sets_v.sql) while the base table clusters on dataset, data_type, gene_most_severe, most_severe (schemas/credible_sets.sql:26-27). So the two filters the agent is told to use prune NOTHING. datasets.yaml:237 already documents the workaround ('Always add the chr filter next to variant ... without it the same query scans ~20x more data').

Store variant and resource as real columns (variant_effect, mpra and variant_annotation already do this) and re-cluster to resource, data_type, trait, pos. pos and trait are not clustering keys today despite region and QTL-by-gene being dominant shapes.

Measure scan bytes before and after on the ten commonest queries from genetics_api_logs and record the numbers in the issue.

Files: genetics-results-db/schemas/credible_sets.sql, credible_sets_v.sql, scripts/setup_bigquery.sh.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-10. STOPPED at step 4 as authorized. Nothing existing modified - no DROP/ALTER/CREATE OR REPLACE ran, no repo file changed, credible_sets and credible_sets_v untouched.

TWO TICKET PREMISES FAILED.
(1) 'the ten commonest queries from genetics_api_logs' - that table does NOT record SQL. Its only log_type is endpoint_access and all 223k rows come from the FILE/TABIX api (genetics-results-api), which never touches BigQuery. The only place BigQuery SQL is logged is genetics_api_logs.stdout, whose jsonPayload carries sql/bytes_processed/dry_run: 538 rows over 2026-05-21..2026-08-10, 375 referencing credible_sets_v. Small and agent/MCP-dominated - state that whenever these numbers are cited.
(2) 'QTL-by-gene is a dominant shape' is NOT supported. trait equality is 19.2%, and HALF of all trait filtering is LIKE '%..%', which no clustering can prune.

REAL FILTER FREQUENCY over 375 queries: data_type 52.5%, resource 46.7%, chr 30.1%, pos 29.1%, trait/trait_original equality 19.2%, trait LIKE 19.2% (unprunable), variant 10.1% (36 of 38 WITHOUT a chr filter), gene_most_severe 6.1%, most_severe 4.8%, dataset 3.5%.
BYTE ATTRIBUTION: 96.5% of all bytes come from queries with NO chr filter - 67.3% 'other, no chr' plus 29.3% 'variant, no chr' (36 queries, 426 GB). Region queries are only 3.5% of bytes.

CORE PREMISE CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT: WHERE resource='finngen' on credible_sets_v scans 4,176,706,833 B versus 2,520,802,636 B unfiltered - MORE than unfiltered, because it must additionally read dataset to evaluate the CASE. Zero pruning. Meanwhile WHERE dataset='FinnGen_R14' (a real cluster key) prunes to 347,487,447 B. The datasets.yaml:237 11.5x variant/chr warning also confirmed exactly.

METHODOLOGY TRAP WORTH KEEPING: --dry_run is NOT usable for this comparison. On the live table dry-run equals actual, but on a freshly-created CTAS table the dry-run estimate IGNORES CLUSTERING until BigQuery's storage optimiser has processed it. Observed: resource+data_type dry-ran at 4,492,232,401 B and actually processed 517,406,337 B. A first benchmark pass using dry-run showed the new tables as uniformly WORSE - a pure artefact. All recorded numbers are real total_bytes_processed with use_query_cache=False. Measurement cost ~350-400 GB scanned, roughly USD 2-2.50.

THREE EXPERIMENT TABLES BUILT, all clearly non-live, all CREATE TABLE (no OR REPLACE), all with OPTIONS(description='EXPERIMENT genetics-results-suite-4h6.18 ... NOT LIVE. Safe to drop.'), all PARTITION BY RANGE_BUCKET(chr, GENERATE_ARRAY(1,23,1)), all 115,043,095 rows, all with stored variant and resource:
  credible_sets_exp_rdtp  resource, data_type, trait, pos    <- the ticket's proposal
  credible_sets_exp_rdvp  resource, data_type, variant, pos
  credible_sets_exp_drvp  data_type, resource, variant, pos

WEIGHTED TOTAL over the top-10 shapes, weighted by log frequency: before 333.14 GB; rdtp 47.00 GB (-85.9%); rdvp 43.48 GB (-86.9%); drvp 43.45 GB (-87.0%).

THE TICKET'S OWN KEY CHOICE IS THE WORST OF THE THREE, and it carries the only in-set regression: Q9 (region + data_type + trait LIKE) is +12.0% under rdtp and improves under both alternatives. And R5 (data_type='eQTL' AND trait='SORT1' - the QTL-by-gene shape the ticket names as its justification for putting trait in the key) gets essentially NOTHING under rdtp: -2.3%, because trait at position 3 is not on a filtered prefix when resource is omitted. drvp gives it -18.0%.

pos as key 4 is doing nothing measurable. rdvp/drvp match or beat rdtp on every region shape despite putting variant ahead of pos.

REGRESSIONS AGAINST THE OLD CLUSTER KEYS - real and material, weighted by how often those columns are filtered:
  dataset='FinnGen_R14' (old key 1, 3.5% of queries): 0.560 -> 1.559 rdtp (+178%) / 1.691 rdvp (+202%) / 2.053 drvp (+267%)
  gene_most_severe='SORT1' (old key 3, 6.1%):         6.161 -> 9.014 (+46%) / 8.854 (+44%) / 8.850 (+44%)
  most_severe IN (...) (old key 4, 4.8%):             9.509 -> 10.259 (+8%) all three
  no filter at all:                                   2.373 -> 1.971 (-17%) all three

SIZE DELTA +13.5% logical (23.74 -> 26.96 GB). Stored variant 1.96 GB, stored resource 1.25 GB. Both are CHEAPER TO READ THAN TO DERIVE - deriving variant needs chr+pos+ref+alt = 2.57 GB, deriving resource needs dataset = 1.66 GB - which is why the unfiltered scan got 17% BETTER despite the bigger table. Storage cost is negligible against the scan saving.

CROSS-REPO CONSEQUENCE, reported not changed: after this change the datasets.yaml:237 workaround ('always add the chr filter next to variant') becomes WRONG - adding chr goes from an 11.5x saving to marginally counterproductive (ratio 0.94-0.95x). That is the canonical configs/datasets.yaml in the SUITE repo and belongs to a different task.

WHY NO REPO FILE WAS TOUCHED: scripts/setup_bigquery.sh auto-creates a table for EVERY schemas/*.sql that is not *_v.sql, so adding a schema file would have created the experiment table on the next production setup run. Editing any of the three listed files IS the swap.

IMPLEMENTATION PATH FOR THE EVENTUAL SWAP: scripts/load_data.py already has the staging-table indirection (const_columns / convert_chr / strip_cell_type_prefix) used to project computed columns, so variant and resource can be materialised there without changing the source TSVs.

CLEANUP OWED once a decision is made: drop credible_sets_exp_rdtp, credible_sets_exp_rdvp, credible_sets_exp_drvp in phewas-development.genetics_results.
close_reason:
PREPARED ONLY, landed as genetics-results-db 68b4c40 (verify with git log). Nothing swapped. No live BigQuery object created, dropped, altered or written. The live credible_sets table (115,076,906 rows) and credible_sets_v view are untouched. Reopen or file a follow-up when the swap is actually executed.

USER DECISION 2026-08-10: clustering is data_type, resource, variant, pos. Weighted total over the ten commonest logged shapes 333.14 GB to 43.45 GB, -87.0%.

THE TICKET'S OWN KEY ORDER WAS THE WORST OF THE THREE BENCHMARKED. Its stated justification for putting trait in the key was that QTL-by-gene is a dominant shape; measured, a QTL-by-gene query that omits resource gets -2.3% under that order because trait at position 3 is not on a filtered prefix, versus -18.0% under the chosen one. trait equality is only 19.2% of queries and half of all trait filtering is LIKE with leading wildcards, which no clustering can prune. The ticket's order also carried the only in-set regression, +12.0% on region plus trait LIKE.

THE TICKET WAS ALSO WRONG ABOUT WHERE TO LOOK. genetics_api_logs records NO SQL - its only log_type is endpoint_access and all 223k rows come from the file/tabix API, which never touches BigQuery. The only BigQuery SQL is in genetics_api_logs.stdout: 538 rows over 2026-05-21..2026-08-10, 375 referencing credible_sets_v. Small and agent/MCP-dominated - say so whenever these numbers are cited.

CORE PREMISE CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT: WHERE resource='finngen' on the view scans 4,176,706,833 B versus 2,520,802,636 B unfiltered - MORE than no filter at all, because it must additionally read dataset to evaluate the CASE. Zero pruning.

ACCEPTED COSTS, weighed against how often those columns are actually filtered: dataset= +267% at 3.5% of queries, gene_most_severe +44% at 6.1%, most_severe +8% at 4.8%, logical size +13.5%. The completely unfiltered scan gets 17% BETTER despite the bigger table, because both stored columns are cheaper to read than the columns needed to derive them (variant 1.96 GB stored vs 2.57 GB to derive; resource 1.25 GB vs 1.66 GB).

METHODOLOGY TRAP, recorded in the runbook: --dry_run CANNOT verify this. On a freshly-created table the estimate IGNORES clustering until BigQuery's storage optimiser has processed it - observed 4,492,232,401 B dry-run against 517,406,337 B actual. A first benchmark pass using dry-run showed the new tables as uniformly WORSE, entirely as an artefact. All recorded numbers are real total_bytes_processed with use_query_cache=False.

setup_bigquery.sh IS DANGEROUS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND NEITHER PERFORMS THE SWAP. Without --recreate the DDL is CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so editing a schema file and re-running prints 'Creating table credible_sets...', creates nothing and exits 0 - someone could believe they had swapped. With --recreate it bq rm's EVERY table in the dataset, not the one whose schema changed. It now prints what it is about to destroy with row counts and requires the dataset name typed. The guard is advisory - the row-count query fails open - and what is really wanted is a scoped --recreate <table>.

resource is GENERATED from datasets.yaml at load time rather than transcribed, so the mapping keeps one source of truth. Zero mismatches for both columns across all 115,043,095 benchmark rows. Declared NOT NULL, deviating from the CTAS-built experiment table, because api/main.py:499 reads a view column's mode from the base table and NULLABLE would flip /schema from REQUIRED for every MCP agent. No live row can violate it: the CASE ends ELSE LOWER(dataset) and chr/pos/ref/alt are all REQUIRED. View output schema verified byte-identical against the LIVE view: 22 columns, same names, order and types.

PERMANENT REGRESSION, documented in three places: resource is frozen at load time, so changing a dataset_to_resource_rules entry no longer takes effect by recreating the view - it needs a reload or an UPDATE backfill.

TWO REVIEW ROUNDS ON THE RUNBOOK, and the second earned its place. Round 1 found: the committed view SQL makes setup_bigquery.sh abort at credible_sets_v under pipefail, silently leaving the ELEVEN views sorting after it unapplied; the cutover left the view pointing at a renamed-away table for however long the operator takes to paste the next command, not 'a second'; a loader run during the soak DELETEs from the old table and then fails to re-append, destroying the rollback target; and the last-resort recovery used FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF, which does not work on a DROPPED table - it failed at exactly the moment it existed for.

THEN THE COLD RE-READ FOUND THIS BEAD'S OWN DEFECT CLASS IN ITS VERIFICATION SECTION: nothing asserted the new table actually HAS the target clustering. Since the DDL is IF NOT EXISTS, a leftover credible_sets_new from an aborted attempt would be reused with the wrong layout and pass every check - and the next section tells the reader that disappointing scan numbers are expected and to wait for the storage optimiser, which is precisely the explanation that would mask it. The layout is now asserted BEFORE cutover. Also fixed: no guard against running the 115M-row INSERT twice, an unguarded backfill UPDATE rewriting a clustering key table-wide with no preflight, a non-standard sed in one step that muscle memory would apply to the live table name, and a row count baked in as a literal in three places.

CROSS-REPO WORK STILL OWED, measured but NOT changed here: after the swap the note at configs/datasets.yaml:237 in the SUITE repo becomes WRONG. Re-measured with real execution: variant without chr goes 7,606,541,126 B to 253,707,488 B, and the chr-filter ratio goes from 0.048 (a 20.8x saving, so the note is exactly right today) to 1.136 (13.6% WORSE, so it becomes exactly wrong). Line 237's text and line 242's example SQL both need changing, and line ~1137 should switch to cs.variant = '5:1104823:C:T' instead of the four-column form. LEAVE ALONE the range-scan examples at 272, 304, 315, 1196, 1283 - they genuinely need chr = N for partition pruning - and 1033, 1052, 1082, which concern other tables. This must land in the same window as the swap.

NOT DONE, worth a bead if the swap proceeds: no test covers DERIVED_COLUMNS, resource_case_sql or the MATERIALIZED_RESOURCE_VIEWS lint branch. For a mechanism that bakes a value into 115M rows that is cheap insurance. Also noted: load_data.py and generate_resource_sql.py default to DIFFERENT datasets.yaml files (local generated copy vs canonical sibling); the rules blocks are identical today but drift is live, and a stale local copy would now silently mislabel an entire load.

TEST COUNT DISCREPANCY: the implementer reported 65 passing, the reviewer reproduced 49 - tests/test_build_phenotypes.py fails collection on missing fsspec, a pre-existing environment issue unrelated to this change. The reviewer asserted the worktree module path, so the 6o3 trap did not fire.

CLEANUP OWED: genetics-results-suite-4ci - drop credible_sets_exp_rdtp, credible_sets_exp_rdvp and credible_sets_exp_drvp. Keep drvp until the real swap is verified against it. Measurement cost was roughly 350-400 GB scanned, about USD 2-2.50.

title: Rewrite the system prompt for a code-first workflow
description:
defaults.py:185 currently says 'Prefer API tools over the database' and defaults.py:134 plus definitions.py:1477 mandate a get_database_schema call before any query. Under a code-first surface these are actively wrong - the mandated schema call is a guaranteed extra roundtrip, and the API-preference line inverts the intended routing.

Replace the per-tool routing guidance with code-first workflow guidance: how to discover capabilities, how to compose one script instead of several calls, when to print a summary rather than raw rows. Keep the substantive domain distinctions that are NOT about routing (the open_chromatin vs caQTL vs variant_effect vs mpra distinction at defaults.py:70-76 is real science and must survive, relocated into the SDK docs).

Files: genetics-mcp-server/src/genetics_mcp_server/config/defaults.py.

title: Implement list_capabilities and read_artifact
description:
list_capabilities(module?) returns SDK stub signatures for one module, so the catalogue costs zero context until asked for. This is the mechanism that makes adding a dataset free in context terms.

read_artifact(path) pulls a file the script wrote (a plot, a TSV) out of the sandbox scratch dir. Reuse the existing path validation (_validate_path, sandbox_tools.py:26) - it exists because path traversal was already a concern in the in-process version.

Files: genetics-mcp-server/src/genetics_mcp_server/tools/definitions.py, tools/executor.py.

title: Generate schema markdown and .pyi stubs into the sandbox image at build time
description:
This is how the agent learns the schema without any of it being front-loaded into context - the progressive-disclosure half of Alt 3, and the reason it needs no prompt-cache breakpoint (genetics-mcp-server/docs/project-spec.md:420 records that there is no spare breakpoint).

Generate from the canonical configs/datasets.yaml at image build: /genetics/schema/<view>.md (one file per view, columns + descriptions + the worked examples already in the tables.<view>.examples blocks) and /genetics/sdk/*.pyi signature stubs. A script reads them on demand like a developer would.

Include the hard-won correctness rules as prose in the relevant schema files: the peak_to_gene join warning (datasets.yaml:204-210), the chr-alongside-variant partition-pruning rule (datasets.yaml:237), and the credible-set key being (resource, dataset, trait, cell_type, cs_id) not cs_id alone.

Files: genetics-results-db or genetics-mcp-server build script (new), sandbox Dockerfile.
close_reason:
Landed as suite 3e4425f and genetics-mcp-server efc77a2. Files only; NOTHING applied to any cluster, no docker push. Validation: mechanics review + CONTENT validation in parallel, two fix rounds, a targeted re-review, then a final correction round. No blocking findings survived.

THIS UNBLOCKS A REAL IMAGE BUILD. 4h6.6 deliberately made the build REFUSE while PLACEHOLDER files were staged, so this is the first point where the sandbox image actually builds: docker build succeeds locally with all ten of that bead's assertions passing, and NO Dockerfile change was needed - the 4h6.6 contract held exactly as written (sandbox/schema -> /genetics/schema, sandbox/stubs -> /genetics/sdk, verbatim, 65532:65532, /genetics/sdk NOT on PYTHONPATH).

WHAT LANDED. scripts/gen-sandbox-docs.py renders 15 view files plus an index into sandbox/schema/ and three .pyi stubs into sandbox/stubs/, from canonical configs/datasets.yaml and the SDK source. scripts/test-sandbox-docs.py is a 13-check harness now gating build.sh. SUITE has no pytest suite; the convention is standalone scripts/test-*.py with a check() decorator and exit 0/1/2, which this follows.

GENERATED, NEVER TRANSCRIBED, AND ENFORCED. The generator names no view and no SDK function in its executable code; the harness proves it by AST-stripping the generator's own comments and docstrings and asserting on what remains. That constraint is load-bearing: 5p5 will rewrite the variant/chr guidance the moment the credible_sets clustering swap runs, and a transcribed rule would then be silently wrong inside the image while datasets.yaml said the opposite. Views come from yaml.safe_load, not a regex - 15, cross-checked against db-api's own VIEWS. Stubs are read with ast, never imported, since importing would execute config.settings and the build host has no polars or httpx.

DELIBERATE EDIT TO THE CANONICAL configs/datasets.yaml. The credible-set key was the one rule not expressible from any existing field - columns.cs_id said only 'groups variants in the same causal signal'. Written into that description rather than hardcoded in the generator. Verified against live BigQuery, not asserted: chr22 alone has 41,412 distinct cs_id against 122,322 distinct 5-tuples, a 3x silent merge; trait is load-bearing (dropping it gives 120,761); the key does not over-merge because cs_id is itself region-qualified. Doc-ownership judged and confirmed: datasets-yaml-schema.md documents columns.<name> as free-text, no enum/field/view list changed, so no doc was made stale. No sibling repo TRACKS a datasets.yaml copy - all are gitignored - and all four generated copies were synced by hand because scripts/sync-datasets.sh is worktree-unaware and exits 0 having copied nothing.

TWO DEFECTS THAT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED WRONG ANSWERS, both found by validating CONTENT rather than code - asking whether an LLM reading these files would write correct SQL. Neither was visible to the mechanics review.

1. coloc_credsets_v documented a join key that is NOT a key. On (dataset, cs_id), UKB_PPP's chr22:42428847-45428847_1 spans 71 distinct traits, because for GWAS and pQTL cs_id encodes the fine-mapping REGION, not the trait. The doc's own worked example returned the right answer BY LUCK - the top hit landed in a region no other FinnGen_R14 trait occupies. In a dense region it silently mixed dozens of unrelated proteins' PIPs into the answer. It also contradicted credible_sets_v.md, which had it right.
   THE OBVIOUS REPAIR WAS ALSO WRONG and only measuring caught it: joining on trait works for GWAS and DESTROYS the QTL side, because colocalization_v.trait2 is a gene symbol where coloc_credsets_v.trait is the molecular feature id - zero rows for 3,574 of 3,785 eQTL sides and 469 of 473 sQTL. Shipped join uses trait_original with cell_type IS NOT DISTINCT FROM, verified across all five verticals: GWAS 1174/1174 with the NULL-safe form vs 0/1174 with plain equality, caQTL 3723/3723, pQTL 258/258, eQTL 4442/4466, sQTL 469/473.
2. All 54 worked examples used unqualified view names. NOT a live 400 on the sql() path - db-api's _qualify_tables rewrites them before authorize_query - but that fallback is a regex whose own docstring records it cannot see inside string literals, and an agent copying an example anywhere else gets 'must be qualified with a dataset'. 69 references qualified at the source, zero double-qualifications, CTE names and aliases untouched, all 52 examples dry-run clean.

THREE THINGS WRITTEN DOWN BACKWARDS AND CAUGHT BY RE-MEASURING - worth noting because each was produced by a careful agent and refuted by data:
- The residual unmatched sides are FinnLiver, DATASET-WIDE (24/24 eQTL, 4/4 sQTL), not an eQTL Catalogue tail - that resource contributes zero - and the suffix is on coloc_credsets_v, not colocalization_v. An earlier round asserted a SPLIT fallback does not recover them; it recovers all 28 with zero ambiguity, but ONLY if both sides are split (splitting one side gives 947/4466 and breaks the 3.5k pairs that already matched).
- The example demonstrating the bad join was pinned by ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1 over 47 rows tied at PP_H4_abf = 1.0, so its numbers were irreproducible and both joins returned identically. With a deterministic tiebreak: 2 credible sets against 18 under the shortened join.
- coloc_credsets_v repeats a variant on 4,443 of 20,050 keys (22%, against credible_sets_v's 2.4%), so its variant-intersection example double-counted. Now documented with the SELECT DISTINCT remedy.

The cs_id wording ALSO had to name IS NOT DISTINCT FROM explicitly: cell_type is NULL for GWAS on 282,195 of 2,489,585 chr22 rows, so a plain equi-join on the five columns silently drops every GWAS row. The first version said 'grouping, joining or counting' without qualification, which is right for GROUP BY and wrong for JOIN.

HARNESS HARDENING after mutation testing found two ways to pass on bad output: _stub_surface was NAMED 'exactly the SDK's exported surface' and cited 4h6.6's equality precedent while asserting CONTAINMENT, so a FABRICATED function in genetics.pyi passed all 13 checks - the model would have been shown an SDK function that does not exist. And categorical_columns had NO coverage, so dropping the whole block regenerated cleanly. Both closed. The harness was also wired to nothing; it now gates build.sh (hard fail) and folds into build-all.sh's skip branch, and returns exit 2 rather than 0 when the SDK source is absent instead of silently running 9 of 13.

MAX_ROWS is DERIVED by following client.py into ToolExecutor._MAX_SQL_LIMIT and SystemExits if unresolvable. 6uk's empty-result warning moved from hla()'s docstring alone to the SDK module docstring covering all nine results-api-backed functions. sql() raises rather than returning a prefix at its ceiling; now stated.

VERIFIED: 13/13 harness checks, with the two new ones confirmed to FAIL on their mutations; all 52 examples dry-run clean; docker build 10 assertions ok / 0 failures; column lists exact for all 15 views against INFORMATION_SCHEMA (same columns, count and order, zero undocumented, zero nonexistent, no post-swap credible_sets shape leaked); stub fidelity exact by AST diff of all 26 GeneticsClient methods; MCP 1285 passed / 74 deselected, unchanged.

LEFT UNDONE, filed: 4h6.30 (per-view partitioning/clustering docs - deliberately NOT written, because 4h6.18 is about to change credible_sets's clustering and anything written today goes stale on swap; deps added on 4h6.18 and 5p5), 4h6.31 (column TYPE field - a datasets.yaml schema change requiring datasets-yaml-schema.md and adding-datasets.md updates; an agent currently cannot know cs_id is STRING, that chr is INT64 so chr = 'chr5' fails, or that gene_group_ids is an ARRAY needing UNNEST), 4h6.32 (SDK truncation message names 100,000 when a sandbox execution is capped at 25,000), fml (adding-datasets.md says two views are excluded from ALL_VIEWS; there are four).

NOTE FOR ANYONE RUNNING THE SCRIPTS BY HAND: both refuse to run from a worktree without --sdk-src, since they look for sandbox/.sdk-src. A bare invocation reports 'harness cannot run' (exit 2) rather than passing. Pre-existing to this bead's wiring, not a regression.

title: Instrument every SDK function call so the audit trail survives
description:
Today each data access is a tool call, logged as 'Executing tool: <name>' (llm_service.py:869) and countable per conversation. Once access moves inside a script, that trail disappears and analyze_conversations' per-tool statistics lose their meaning.

Emit a structured log line per SDK function call from inside the sandbox, carrying session id, function name, arguments summary and row count, mirroring the existing format so existing log queries keep working. This is both an observability requirement and a security requirement (the security doc needs to answer 'what did that script actually read?').

Files: genetics-mcp-server/src/genetics_mcp_server/sdk/ (instrumentation decorator), scripts/analyze_conversations.py (consume SDK-function stats alongside tool stats).

title: Re-derive the node pool budget and grow capacity for the sandbox
description:
min_node_count == max_node_count == 2 on e2-standard-4 is pinned deliberately (docs/project-spec.md:274-310): an autoscaler with room to move evicted chat-backend mid-SSE. A full deploy already overshoots one node on BOTH axes (3951m vs 3920m allocatable CPU, 13.60 vs 12.97 GiB), and the spec explicitly warns that adding a service re-breaks this.

The user has approved more resources but expects little extra need - measurement supports that (peak 23 turns/hour, so one small sandbox replica).

Re-derive the surge total including the sandbox against the chosen pool. Note machine_type is ForceNew on google_container_node_pool: changing it in place DESTROYS and recreates the pool, so a machine-type change must be done as a new pool plus cordon/drain migration, not a tfvars edit. Keep min == max whichever option is chosen.

Update the sizing table in docs/project-spec.md in the same commit.

Files: terraform/terraform.tfvars, terraform/gke.tf, docs/project-spec.md.
notes:
USER DECISION 2026-08-07: gVisor on a DEDICATED node pool. Confirmed as the design doc specifies.

The pool is pinned min==max==1 and is SEPARATE from the primary pool, so it contributes nothing to the primary surge budget. Note the original 'this is nearly free' argument is now WEAKER than when written: it assumed the primary pool was pinned at 2, and genetics-results-suite-262 established it is actually autoscaling 1-3 with one node running. The user chose gVisor anyway, on isolation grounds - untrusted LLM-authored code gets a userspace syscall boundary, and chat-backend can never be co-scheduled with it. Accepted cost: one permanently-running node.

MUST INCLUDE (from the security review - the pool spec is where the central isolation claim actually lives or dies):
- workload_metadata_config { mode = 'GKE_METADATA' } UNCONDITIONALLY. Without it the pool defaults to GCE_METADATA, exposing the raw metadata server, and a script reading 169.254.169.254/.../service-accounts/default/token gets a project-level token. Workload Identity is irrelevant in GCE_METADATA mode.
- This ALSO requires google_container_cluster.primary's workload_identity_config to become unconditional. It is currently inside dynamic ... for_each = var.manage_iam ? [1] : [] in terraform/gke.tf, so under manage_iam=false there is no workload_pool and an unconditional GKE_METADATA pool is rejected by the GKE API AT APPLY, not at plan. Making workload_pool unconditional is an in-place cluster update; it does not recreate pools or change existing pools' metadata mode.
- A dedicated node service account: NOT genetics-suite, NOT the Compute Engine default (which typically carries roles/editor). Mandatory input, no null fallback.
- Explicit oauth_scopes: devstorage.read_only, logging.write, monitoring, monitoring.write, service.management.readonly, servicecontrol, trace.append. devstorage.read_only is REQUIRED for Artifact Registry image pulls - roles/artifactregistry.reader alone is not sufficient. Add roles/stackdriver.resourceMetadata.writer to the node SA.
- Note the scope reduction is NOT load-bearing in GKE_METADATA mode (pod tokens come from the IAM Credentials API, not node scopes); it defends the GCE_METADATA misconfiguration case and the escape-to-node case only.

Do NOT gate the sandbox pool on manage_iam to escape an apply failure - that reintroduces the metadata hole verbatim.

UNVERIFIED, confirm before relying on it: runsc sentry memory overhead against the pod's 3Gi limit, and GKE Sandbox's machine-type requirements for the chosen type. Listed in genetics-results-suite-5r2.

Still blocked on genetics-results-suite-262 for the docs half.

title: Add the sandbox Deployment, Service and container hardening
description:
New k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml. Non-root, readOnlyRootFilesystem, allowPrivilegeEscalation false, capabilities drop ALL, RuntimeDefault seccomp, explicit CPU/memory limits, no volume mounts at all (definitely not chat-data).

Sizing is settled by measurement (2026-08-07): peak load is 23 chat turns/hour, p95 8/hour, mean 3. One small always-on replica is sufficient; do not build for concurrency that does not exist. Use an emptyDir for script scratch space with a size limit.

Update the services table in docs/project-spec.md and README.md in the same commit (documentation-ownership rule for k8s/**).

Files: k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml (new), docs/project-spec.md, README.md, scripts/deploy.sh.
notes:
DECISION 2026-08-07: Alternative 3 (code execution) selected by the user, who also wants code execution in production independently.

MEASUREMENT that informed it (production, 916 turns since 2026-05-01 + chat_history.db 5,464 messages / 959 sessions):
- Tool surface: log line confirms 'Including 80 MCP tools (profile=all, 60 local, 20 external)'. Local schema alone = 18,263 tokens.
- Tool calls per turn: median 4, p90 12, max 58. Per session: median 13, p90 51, max 220.
- Model roundtrips (iterations) per turn: median 2, p75 4, p90 6, p95 8, max 25. 13.5% over 5; 2% over 10.
- Cost: mean 2.01 USD/turn, ~1,842 USD total. The 13.5% of turns with 6+ iterations burn 35% of spend.
- Context accumulation: median 39k tokens at iteration 1 -> 117k at iteration 7+, uncached share 11% -> 52%.
- Load: peak 23 turns/hour, p95 8/hour. One small sandbox replica suffices.

HONEST READ: the MEDIAN turn is not pathological (2 roundtrips, 4 calls), so code execution's median ceiling is 2 -> 1. The justification is the tail (35% of spend) and the context-accumulation curve, which is the one thing only code execution fixes - Alt 1 and Alt 2 reduce call counts but every result still lands in context. Expect the win as cost and tail latency, NOT a dramatic median tool-call drop.

USER CONSTRAINTS: security must be examined carefully and properly sandboxed; the MCP service is retained but code execution must NOT be reachable via MCP; more compute is available but little is expected to be needed.

DEFERRED, NOT DISCARDED: the Alt 1 / Alt 2 tool-consolidation merges (search_entities, the LD pair, the summary-stats pair) remain worthwhile independently of the sandbox and can be revisited if the benchmark disappoints.

LABEL CONTRACT — fixed by genetics-results-suite-4h6.8, do not choose differently.
k8s/network-policies/sandbox-policy.yaml selects the sandbox by these exact values, and the
Deployment/Service in this task MUST match them:

  pod label:      app: sandbox   (Deployment .spec.template.metadata.labels, and the
                                  Service selector)
  container port: 8080/TCP       (NetworkPolicy `ports` are POD ports, not Service ports)
  Service name:   sandbox        (ClusterIP, port 8080 -> targetPort 8080)

WHY THIS IS NOT A STYLE PREFERENCE: a NetworkPolicy whose podSelector matches no pod is not
an error, it is silent no-coverage. sandbox-policy.yaml carries the namespace's ONLY egress
policy (there is no default-deny-egress anywhere), so a label mismatch here produces a
sandbox with UNRESTRICTED egress — internet, s3://, DNS tunnelling — and nothing anywhere
reports a problem. scripts/test-network-policies.py cross-checks k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml
against this contract as soon as the file exists; run it after creating the manifest.

Also fixed by 4h6.8 and required of this task:
- hostAliases pinning db-api and results-api ClusterIPs in all four name forms. There is NO
  DNS egress rule and there will not be one; 53/UDP is DROPPED, so an unpinned name is a
  multi-second stall, not a fast error.
- automountServiceAccountToken: false. (Note it is a Kubernetes-API control and does nothing
  about the metadata server; that defence is 4h6.10's node pool mode.)
- Do NOT add the sandbox to k8s/network-policies/monitor-policy.yaml. Kubelet probes are
  exempt from NetworkPolicy on this cluster's Dataplane V2, so no probe rule is needed either.
- The sandbox must NOT receive INTERNAL_API_SECRET. Both db-api and results-api will return
  401 to it until 4h6.9 lands the scoped credential; that is expected, not a bug to work
  around.

SANDBOX_ENABLED MUST BE FLIPPED IN THE SAME COMMIT — added by genetics-results-suite-4h6.9.
scripts/test-network-policies.py now gates deploy.sh and asserts: if k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml
exists, then k8s/deployments/db-api.yaml AND k8s/deployments/results-api.yaml must both set
SANDBOX_ENABLED to a literal "true". Both ship "false" today, so ADDING sandbox.yaml WITHOUT
flipping both flags ABORTS EVERY DEPLOY with exit 1. Verified on a scratch copy: sandbox.yaml
present + flag false -> exit 1; both flipped -> exit 0.

That coupling is deliberate. SANDBOX_ENABLED=true is what makes db-api and results-api
sys.exit(1) when either INTERNAL_API_SECRET or SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY is unset. With it
false, db-api keeps its PRE-EXISTING fail-open branch, where an unset INTERNAL_API_SECRET
disables auth entirely with only a startup warning - so a sandbox script that simply omits
the Authorization header would reach it. The flag is the whole fail-closed guarantee.

Ordering inside deploy.sh is already correct and needs nothing from this task: the secret
gate runs BEFORE the policy harness, so the signing key is guaranteed present before the flag
can make either pod exit.

Also from 4h6.9: the sandbox must receive NEITHER INTERNAL_API_SECRET NOR
SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY. The token is minted by chat-backend per execution and injected by
4h6.14; the sandbox holds no signing material at all. Exactly three Deployments mount the
signing key - chat-backend, db-api, results-api - and sandbox.yaml must not become a fourth.

UPDATED BY genetics-results-suite-r22 (suite dcb72aa) -- TWO CLAIMS ABOVE ARE NOW STALE.
The harness NO LONGER keys on the literal path k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml. Both statements
above that say "as soon as the file exists" / "if k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml exists" were
themselves a fail-open bug: under any other filename the checks stayed inert FOREVER while
printing a reassuring note.

It now DISCOVERS the sandbox workload by file name, OR object name, OR pod labels being a
superset of {app: sandbox}, across Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job, CronJob and bare
Pod. So name the manifest whatever you like -- the checks activate regardless.

THE CONTRACT ABOVE IS UNCHANGED AND IS NOW ENFORCED HARDER, from three independent directions:
  1. name/label discovery (above),
  2. a catch-all keyed on the pod-spec tells the security doc obliges the sandbox to carry --
     runtimeClassName, a sandbox.gke.io/runtime toleration, automountServiceAccountToken false,
     or a serviceAccountName present and != genetics-suite,
  3. SANDBOX_ENABLED=true on db-api or results-api with NO discoverable sandbox workload.

Note lock 2 fires on automountServiceAccountToken: false, which the contract above already
requires of you -- so a manifest meeting this contract is discovered by lock 2 even if you
somehow evade lock 1.

Still true and still the thing that aborts every deploy: label app: sandbox, containerPort
8080/TCP, Service "sandbox" 8080->8080, AND SANDBOX_ENABLED flipped to "true" on BOTH db-api
and results-api, ALL IN THE SAME COMMIT as the workload manifest.

Run scripts/test-network-policies.py after writing the manifest. Real manifests today: exit 0,
13 checks, 19 policies. Exit 1 = a control is broken and deploy.sh aborts; exit 2 = the harness
could not run and deploy.sh only warns.

=== HANDOFF FROM genetics-results-suite-0lf (2026-08-12), REQUIRED, NOT OPTIONAL ===
THE SANDBOX POD MUST NOT RECEIVE INTERNAL_API_SECRET. This Deployment is one of the two things that actually closes 0lf's hole; the other is 4h6.14.

WHY: results-api's four per-execution counters are only charged when _sandbox_principal resolves an HS256 sandbox token. MEASURED against the real ASGI app with SANDBOX_ENABLED=true:
    Authorization: Bearer <INTERNAL_API_SECRET>  ->  200, user_email=mcp-tool, sandbox_budget._executions == {}
is_internal_caller admits that credential, so the request reaches the handler with NO ACCOUNTING AT ALL. sdk/client.py states outright that the client attaches INTERNAL_API_SECRET to every request and that a script which can import the module can also read os.environ. So while the sandbox holds that secret, a script sheds all four counters by sending it instead of no header - 0lf closed "omit the header" and left "send the other header" open.

SO: do not mount, project or env-inject INTERNAL_API_SECRET into the sandbox pod, and do not let it arrive via a shared ConfigMap/Secret pulled in wholesale. Verify it is genuinely absent from the container's environment, not merely unset in the manifest.

A TEST WILL FAIL WHEN YOU GET THIS RIGHT, and that is the intended signal:
  genetics-results-api tests/test_anonymous_surface.py::test_an_internal_secret_caller_is_served_but_not_accounted
It encodes today's behaviour deliberately. Update it in the same commit rather than working around it.

title: Build the hardened sandbox container image
description:
New build context in genetics-mcp-server (or a dedicated sandbox/ dir in the suite repo - decide in the security doc). Contents: a minimal Python base, no shell, non-root uid, the genetics SDK pre-installed, plus polars/scipy/matplotlib for analysis. Pre-warm the interpreter so marginal script cost is a fork, not a pod schedule.

Also carries the generated schema docs and .pyi stubs (see the stub-generation task) at /genetics/schema/ and /genetics/sdk/.

Must satisfy every control in docs/code-execution-security.md. Wire into scripts/build-all.sh and scripts/build.sh alongside the existing local monitor and keycloak build contexts.

Files: sandbox Dockerfile (new), genetics-results-suite/scripts/build-all.sh, scripts/build.sh.
close_reason:
Landed as suite 0e52747. Image builds; no docker push, nothing applied to any cluster. Adversarial review, fix round, re-verification by rebuild: all five blockers closed, no new blocking findings.

CLOSED WITH --force BECAUSE IT IS BLOCKED BY 4h6.13, AND THAT BLOCK IS NOW LITERALLY TRUE BY DESIGN. This task's own deliverable - the Dockerfile, the build checks, the build-script wiring - is complete and reviewed. But the image CANNOT BE BUILT FOR REAL until 4h6.13 lands, because blocker 4's fix makes the build refuse while PLACEHOLDER files are staged, and also until 4h6.11 reaches master, because the SDK is installed from a clone of MCP_SERVER_BRANCH (default master) and .11 currently exists only on the worktree branch. Both couplings are deliberate: an image asked for by name that silently lacks the SDK or ships placeholder schema docs is worse than a failed build. Do not treat this closure as 'the sandbox image exists'.

WHAT LANDED: sandbox/ build context in THIS repo (the security doc decided that, not me). Distroless python3-debian12:nonroot, uid 65532, no shell, no CMD, genetics SDK plus polars/scipy/matplotlib, wired into build-all.sh and build.sh beside monitor and keycloak. Ten build-time assertions, up from six.

FOUR WAYS THE BUILD ASSERTED A PROPERTY IT WAS NOT CHECKING, all found by adversarial review, all closed:

1. polars ships the entire Rust object_store - a GCS/S3/Azure client with its own HTTP/TLS stack and its own GCP metadata-token path compiled into native code. The doc's control is 'no google-auth-based client in the image'; the check grepped PYTHON DISTRIBUTION NAMES, so it reported green while pl.scan_parquet('gs://...') minted tokens against 169.254.169.254. NEITHER branch of the control was satisfied and no other bead owned it. Now pinned to the literal IP (the doc's own named fallback) and the check greps native objects, failing unless the pin is present. MEASURED: 86.7s hanging on an unresolvable metadata name, 7.4s against a blackholed pin, 2.0s with no network. WHAT THE PIN DOES NOT DO, now stated in the doc: s3:// reaches bucket.s3.amazonaws.com in 0.0s with no metadata step, so pl.write_parquet('s3://...') remains an exfiltration primitive independent of httpx, closed only by 4h6.8's NetworkPolicy.

2. pip and setuptools shipped in the final image. The check named 'no shell or package manager in the final rootfs' walked only the distroless base, never /opt/venv or the staging tree, and its ban list omitted pip. TWO DOC SENTENCES ASSERTED THE OPPOSITE AS FACT. Both corrected; walk widened to /dl, /opt/venv and /out; packaging tooling and /opt/venv/bin deleted. Re-verified WITHOUT -S, the way the image actually runs and the way the checks do not: pip/setuptools/pkg_resources/_distutils_hack/ensurepip all ModuleNotFoundError, and sys.path puts the venv ahead of the stdlib with no system site-packages to leak in.

3. The whole genetics_mcp_server package shipped - 42 modules including auth/core.py, whose docstring is the recipe for forging the identity header that genetics-results-suite-fad confirmed works TODAY against results-api from any pod in the namespace. Pruned to the SDK's measured import closure of 13 modules, 84 files removed. The assertion is EQUALITY with the allow-list, not containment, so the list grows deliberately. auth/core.py, chat_api, llm_service, db/chat_history_db and skills/sandbox_tools are all gone.
   RESIDUAL, filed as genetics-results-suite-l41: config/settings.py CANNOT be pruned from here. Chain verified against the real branch, all module-level: sdk/__init__ to sdk/client to tools/executor to tools/uniprot to config/settings. So the image still names every internal env var and still carries executor.py's f-string SQL sites. Recorded in the doc rather than left implicit.

4. The 4h6.13 placeholders reached the image with nothing detecting them - silent degradation, since run_analysis runs and the pod is healthy while the model gets a file saying PLACEHOLDER instead of the schema. The build now refuses. build-all.sh skips loudly so a suite build stays green; build.sh sandbox fails hard.

5. prewarm.py documented matplotlib as falling back silently when MPLCONFIGDIR is unwritable. It RAISES OSError - verified. That file is what 4h6.14's implementer reads for the contract, and prewarm() returned failures instead of raising, so a supervisor ignoring the return value would start with matplotlib un-imported and every plotting script would fail in the child while the pod looked healthy. Now raises PrewarmError naming every failure.

THE --no-deps DRIFT PREDICTED WHEN THE SDK INSTALL WAS WRITTEN ARRIVED IMMEDIATELY: with 4h6.11 landed, importing the SDK fails on dotenv through that same settings chain. The build check caught it, which is what it is for. Pinned python-dotenv==1.2.2, genetics-mcp-server's own pin; it brings in nothing else.

DEVIATION FROM THE SECURITY DOC: builder is python:3.11-slim, not 3.12. Distroless python3-debian12:nonroot ships CPython 3.11.2, so a 3.12 venv puts cp312 native wheels in front of a 3.11 interpreter. The doc's spec is unbuildable as literally written; intent preserved and the doc records it.

WHAT 'NO SHELL' DOES NOT BUY, verified by execution and consistent with the doc: ctypes reaches libc, arbitrary native code runs (mapped RWX and executed injected x86-64), arbitrary syscalls are available. It buys no curl/wget/nc, no LOLBin, and os.system returning 127. The doc does not overclaim - it says the boundary is the pod, the network policy and the kernel, full stop. gVisor (4h6.10) and the egress policy (4h6.8) carry the entire load.

PRE-WARMING is split deliberately: the forking supervisor is 4h6.14's, and a placeholder would be indistinguishable from a real one at runtime, hence NO CMD. The image owns only what a fork cannot amortise - compileall of the venv, mandatory under a read-only rootfs, and a baked font cache. Cold import of the full stack measured at 2.99s.

CONTRACT FOR 4h6.13: sandbox/schema/ to /genetics/schema/ (GENETICS_SCHEMA_DIR), sandbox/stubs/ to /genetics/sdk/ (GENETICS_STUBS_DIR), copied verbatim, owned 65532:65532, no Dockerfile change needed. .13 must delete the PLACEHOLDER files and must not leave either directory empty. /genetics/sdk is deliberately NOT on PYTHONPATH - the importable SDK is the real package in /opt/venv, and two copies of those names would shadow silently.

ADDED TO THE 4h6.14 HANDOFF: the nsswitch STARTUP assertion the doc requires as a backstop (no other task owned it), the obligation to let PrewarmError crash the pod, and the verified requirement that the supervisor copy the matplotlib cache and set MPLCONFIGDIR before importing matplotlib.

NOTED, NOT ACTED ON: 607 MB image against a pinned 1-node sandbox pool means a pull on every node replacement. build.sh had NO local build contexts before this - monitor and keycloak live only in build-all.sh, contrary to the ticket's premise - and I added handling for sandbox only.

title: Export full ordered turn sequences for replay
description:
export_eval_dataset() (analyze_conversations.py:970) exports only first_user_message, which cannot drive a multi-turn replay. Extend it to emit every user turn in order per session, with the options in force at each turn (verbosity, tool_profile, instruction_set_id, literature_backend) so a replay reproduces the original conditions.

Files: src/genetics_mcp_server/scripts/analyze_conversations.py.
close_reason:
Both landed in genetics-mcp-server worktree commit 89c4e79. Suite 999 -> 1024 passed, 74 deselected, 0 failed. Single reviewer (light tier), one fix round.

.2 counts tool_use blocks from content_json with the marker regex as an explicit pre-migration fallback, and reports coverage next to every aggregate (>=N per session when it fell back, tool_count_caveat under each table). A row with content_json present but zero tool calls deliberately does NOT fall back - project-spec.md:1216 documents the model imitating the marker notation as prose and fabricating results.

.3 exports every user turn in order, untruncated, with the options in force, ordered on (created_at, rowid).

CAUGHT IN REVIEW - and this one I had endorsed as correct before it was checked: the first implementation carried option values forward on the premise that null means 'unchanged'. FALSE. ChatPage.tsx:402 passes all four option keys on every saveMessage, explicitly null when unset; chatHistoryApi.saveMessage.test.ts exists solely to pin that; add_message writes exactly what the request carried with no merge. And null is a REAL VALUE - tool_profile IS NULL means all tools (definitions.py:1587), useChatOptions.ts:140 says verbatim 'a null toolProfile is all, which is a real choice rather than a gap', and 'all' is unpersistable as a string. Effect: a user who ran turn 1 on tool_profile='api' then switched back to all-tools exported as 'api' - corrupting exactly the replay conditions .3 exists to preserve, with .4 as the direct consumer.
Now: each row's own values are the options in force, nulls included; carry-forward only when ALL FOUR columns are null, which cannot be a current-client write since verbosity and literature_backend always coerce to non-null defaults.

Also fixed: is_exact was vacuously true on an empty dataset; four report tables printed unmarked totals.

VERIFIED, not assumed: no double counting (fixture built at the real production shape 2731/1960/9435/2075 with deliberate overlap); build_session_tool_stats really does drop tool-less sessions (812 vs 911), justifying the separate coverage pass; load_data really selects rowid AS _rowid; no write path introduced; nothing in any sibling repo consumes eval_dataset.json.

ANALYZER_VERSION deliberately NOT bumped - the LLM cache keys on _format_conversation_for_eval which reads none of this; bumping would force a full re-judge at real API cost for identical inputs.

LEFT UNDONE: _format_conversation_for_eval still sorts on created_at alone, so a tie can show the judge a user turn after its own reply - genetics-results-suite-jr1. load_data opens the DB read-write - genetics-results-suite-8kt.

title: Feature: code-execution agent — genetics SDK in a hardened sandbox, minimal tool surface
description:
Reduce the chat/MCP agent's tool surface (currently 63 tools, 42 of them API-bound) by making BigQuery the primary data path, keeping genetics-results-api as a specialist backend for what BQ cannot serve (summary statistics, LD, fuzzy search index, streaming downloads) and for the browser/BFF.

Motivation:
1. Tool-count bloat: 63 tools is far above the 5-15 practical ceiling where tool-selection accuracy degrades; the 42 API tools dominate per-turn schema overhead.
2. BigQuery is strictly more capable than the tabix API for the verticals it already holds, because it can JOIN (cis/trans, caQTL peak->gene, gene groups).
3. Reduce tool calls per conversation - table/schema design and front-loaded example SQL directly drive round-trip count.
4. Fill BQ data gaps and revisit partitioning/clustering for latency.

Hard constraints discovered during examination:
- Summary statistics cannot move to BQ (~10^11 rows, source buckets not owned by the suite).
- LD is panel-computed, not tabular.
- Fuzzy phenotype/gene search is an in-memory ranked index; BQ cannot replace it.
- The API's largest consumer is the browser via BFF, independent of chat - API retirement is NOT in scope, only tool retirement.

Gate: a benchmark built from real production conversations (chat_history.db) must be in place BEFORE migration, measuring tool calls/turn, latency, token cost and answer quality.
notes:
DECISION 2026-08-07: Alternative 3 (code execution) selected by the user, who also wants code execution in production independently.

MEASUREMENT that informed it (production, 916 turns since 2026-05-01 + chat_history.db 5,464 messages / 959 sessions):
- Tool surface: log line confirms 'Including 80 MCP tools (profile=all, 60 local, 20 external)'. Local schema alone = 18,263 tokens.
- Tool calls per turn: median 4, p90 12, max 58. Per session: median 13, p90 51, max 220.
- Model roundtrips (iterations) per turn: median 2, p75 4, p90 6, p95 8, max 25. 13.5% over 5; 2% over 10.
- Cost: mean 2.01 USD/turn, ~1,842 USD total. The 13.5% of turns with 6+ iterations burn 35% of spend.
- Context accumulation: median 39k tokens at iteration 1 -> 117k at iteration 7+, uncached share 11% -> 52%.
- Load: peak 23 turns/hour, p95 8/hour. One small sandbox replica suffices.

HONEST READ: the MEDIAN turn is not pathological (2 roundtrips, 4 calls), so code execution's median ceiling is 2 -> 1. The justification is the tail (35% of spend) and the context-accumulation curve, which is the one thing only code execution fixes - Alt 1 and Alt 2 reduce call counts but every result still lands in context. Expect the win as cost and tail latency, NOT a dramatic median tool-call drop.

USER CONSTRAINTS: security must be examined carefully and properly sandboxed; the MCP service is retained but code execution must NOT be reachable via MCP; more compute is available but little is expected to be needed.

DEFERRED, NOT DISCARDED: the Alt 1 / Alt 2 tool-consolidation merges (search_entities, the LD pair, the summary-stats pair) remain worthwhile independently of the sandbox and can be revisited if the benchmark disappoints.

title: PUT tool-descriptions is auth_required, not admin_required
description:
Found by the blind validator while fixing genetics-results-suite-uog. PRE-EXISTING and currently DORMANT, but it is a latent global prompt-injection channel.

genetics-mcp-server routers/llm_config.py:557-565 - PUT /chat/v1/llm-config/tool-descriptions/{tool_name} is gated by auth_required, not admin_required. Any authenticated user can overwrite a GLOBAL tool description with unbounded free text, persisted and versioned in tool_description_history.

Why it is dormant: nothing loads those stored rows into the chat path. chat_api never passes custom_tool_descriptions to llm_service.stream_chat, so the parameter is always None and the stored text never reaches a model. Verified during the s5y.5 work as well.

Why it still matters: the moment anything wires those rows in, one user's edit reaches every user's turn. Tool descriptions are the instructions the model uses to decide WHEN to call a tool, so a hostile or careless edit is more consequential than an instruction set, which is per-user and presentation-scoped.

Fix: change the dependency to admin_required, matching the other global-configuration endpoints. Check the DELETE and any sibling write on the same resource. Note this is an authz change on a route that currently has no legitimate non-admin user, so it should break nothing - confirm no client calls it (the browser's llmConfigApi.ts only calls the comments endpoints).

Also from the same review, weaker and separate: request.model is unvalidated against any allowlist - a cost and scope question rather than prompt text.
close_reason: Fixed in genetics-mcp-server 1b973a1. All four legacy /llm-config/tool-descriptions* endpoints now Depends(admin_required), not just the PUT: the two GETs return changed_by (an admin email), and admin-to-write/world-to-read invites the write gate being read as accidental. No DELETE exists on the resource. Confirmed no caller outside tests across all six repos. Consequence worth knowing: admin_required 404s when ENABLE_ADMIN_PAGE=false; prod sets it true in k8s/deployments/chat-backend.yaml. The suite runs REQUIRE_AUTH=false where admin_required waves everyone through, so pre-existing tests would have passed unchanged and proved nothing - added TestToolDescriptionAuthGuards which moves REQUIRE_AUTH/ADMIN_USERS itself, plus an admin_client fixture enabling ENABLE_ADMIN_PAGE for the existing cases. Mutation-checked: reverting the PUT to auth_required fails the guard. request.model allowlist split out to a separate bead.

title: test suite has order-dependent failures under pytest-randomly
description:
Found while validating genetics-results-suite-2cl/-qdf. PRE-EXISTING and reproducible on pristine HEAD — confirmed NOT caused by that work (a reviewer built a tree differing only by a test-fixture move and got byte-identical failure sets).

genetics-mcp-server: with pytest-randomly active, TestAdminAuthGuards::test_dev_mode_allows_any_user (expects 200, gets 404) and ::test_non_admin_denied_when_auth_required (expects 403, gets 404) fail under some seeds. Measured: seeds 12345 and 20260804 FAIL; seeds 1, 42, 999, 7 PASS. Roughly a 1-in-3 hit rate. With -p no:randomly the suite is green.

The tests pass when test_admin_router.py runs alone under the failing seed, so the leak comes from OTHER modules running first, and no single module reproduces it in isolation — it needs a combination.

Diagnosed causes (not fixed):
- config/settings.py get_settings() is @lru_cache'd; tests that call it without clearing the cache leave a stale Settings instance behind, and admin_required then sees enable_admin_page=False and 404s.
- auth/dependencies.py:14 evaluates _require_auth = os.environ.get('REQUIRE_AUTH', ...) at IMPORT time, so patching os.environ later does not update it.

Fix likely means an autouse fixture clearing get_settings.cache_clear() between tests, and reading REQUIRE_AUTH through settings rather than at import time.

This matters beyond flakiness: every 'full suite green' claim in this epic's task history was measured on whatever seed happened to run.
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit adb57ef. Suite 810 passed / 74 deselected on -p no:randomly and on seeds 12345, 20260804, 1, 987654321 — the first two being the known-bad ones.

THE TICKET'S DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG and was corrected during implementation. It blamed a stale @lru_cache on get_settings(); the two failing tests already call cache_clear() themselves. The real cause: test_temperature.py called importlib.reload on the settings module, rebinding config.settings.get_settings to a new function object with its own empty cache while config/__init__.py kept re-exporting the old one. admin_required reads the package handle, the tests cleared the submodule handle. A reviewer proved causality by re-injecting the reload into the fixed tree and reproducing the exact failure set.

The reload was never needed (every Settings field reads os.environ in a default_factory) and was latently harmful (the module calls load_dotenv() at import, so a reload resurrects an env var a test just removed).

SEPARATE FINDING, now fixed: pytest-randomly was neither installed nor declared, so -p no:randomly was a silent no-op and every seed sweep in this epic ran against ad-hoc installs. Declared and pinned exactly (the seed-to-order mapping moves between versions), with shuffling left on by default — an undeclared plugin is how this went unnoticed.

Follow-up filed for the REQUIRE_AUTH two-sources-of-truth test trap.

title: llm_config_db: write accessors leave the transaction open on failure
description:
PRE-EXISTING, found while reviewing genetics-results-suite-s5y.4. In genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/db/llm_config_db.py, none of these write accessors roll back on failure: save_tool_description, add_user_comment, delete_user_comment, save_user_setting, delete_user_setting, create_api_token, revoke_api_token, validate_api_token.

Each is a single DML, so SQLite has already backed out that statement's own changes and no partial data is pending. But the transaction stays OPEN and holds the write lock against every other writer of llm_config.db until that thread happens to commit something else. Connections are thread-local and cached for the process lifetime, so a long-lived server thread can hold the lock indefinitely.

The instruction-set accessors added in s5y.4 have rollback guards and a _discard_stale_transaction helper that incidentally cleans this up whenever one of them next runs on the same thread — nothing else does.

Fix: mirror the try/except BaseException -> rollback; raise pattern from create_instruction_set, and move conn.commit() inside the try.
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit 56f2341. Suite 770 passed / 74 deselected, stable over 6 repeat runs; 20 of 21 new tests verified to fail against the unfixed source.

DELIBERATE DEVIATION on the auth path, verified security-neutral by two independent reviewers: validate_api_token swallows a failure of its trailing bookkeeping UPDATE (last_used_at + rolling expiry) and returns the user anyway, rather than raising. Revocation (is_active=1 in the SELECT's WHERE) and expiry are both decided BEFORE the try, from committed state, so no invalid/expired/revoked token can authenticate. The deadline is frozen rather than pushed on failure, so a persistently failing write ages a token out rather than keeping it alive. Old behaviour was strictly worse: the raise became a 500, mcp-server read that as 401, and the poisoned connection failed every subsequent validation on the same thread — one transient SQLITE_BUSY became a lasting 401 outage for all API-token users until pod restart.

Scope note: read accessors also got _discard_stale_transaction (12 methods the ticket did not name). Kept as defence-in-depth and documented as such, not as a live bug fix.

Follow-up filed: genetics-results-suite-4um (chat_history_db.py has the identical bug class).

description: genetics-results-browser src/features/chat/LLMChat.tsx. A compact Select (not a RadioGroup — the row already holds literature backend, Tools and Answer brief/detailed) after the Answer box (~lines 909-970). State near ~line 196, seeded from the stored selected_instruction_set; send instruction_set_id in the request body (~lines 589-606); add to the send callback deps (~lines 719-746). Include a 'None' option and a link into InstructionsDialog.
notes:
REVIEW DEPTH (user decision, 2026-08-04): frontend tasks use a SINGLE reviewer, not the three-validator pattern. The full pattern is reserved for anything touching the auth path or a live database.

FROM .15-.17 REVIEW - handle this or the selector breaks:
Archiving a set does NOT clear the stored selected_instruction_set pointer. That is deliberate and matches the epic's 'unknown id is ignored, never 422' rule on the server side - but .18 must handle a stored id that no longer appears in listInstructionSets(), or the selector renders a blank or dangling value. The selection helpers already exist and are currently unused, waiting for you: getSelectedInstructionSetId / setSelectedInstructionSetId / clearSelectedInstructionSet in src/features/chat/instructionSetsApi.ts. close_reason:
Landed in genetics-results-browser commit 11cf754 (batched with .19). typecheck 0, 228 tests pass. Review APPROVED.

Most consequential finding, fixed: LLMChat remounts on every session switch (key={chatKey}), so the selection reset to null until two fetches resolved - a message sent in that window silently went WITHOUT the user's instructions, with no visual cue since the options row is collapsed by default. State hoisted into a zustand store (this repo's existing cross-remount pattern, and it keeps the four bare-render LLMChat tests working where react-query would have needed a provider in each).

Dangling pointer: a stored id whose set has been archived drops to None and clears the setting. Reviewer verified the clear cannot fire on a FAILED fetch - it runs only inside the try after both promises resolve - so a network hiccup cannot delete a valid user setting.

Shared-session isolation verified: the options row and dialog render only under !readOnly, every call is auth_required + credentials:include, and the server scopes the body to the authenticated caller, so a shared-session viewer can never see or send another user's set.

Cover: id scoping across users (user A cannot resolve user B's set), unknown/archived id is ignored rather than 422, char and count caps enforced on write and re-checked on read, the two-block system shape, envelope ordering (guardrail postamble after the body), a DB error degrading to no instructions rather than failing the turn, and the same-second settings tiebreak. Do NOT duplicate that coverage — .14 should cover only what those two files do not: the two-block system prompt shape, envelope ordering, unknown/archived id ignored at the chat layer, and a DB error degrading to no instructions rather than failing the turn.
close_reason:
CLOSED AS ALREADY SATISFIED - no new work needed. This task was trimmed early on (see its notes) once .3 and .4 landed their own test files, leaving four items: the two-block system prompt shape, envelope ordering, unknown/archived id ignored at the chat layer, and a DB error degrading rather than failing the turn. A reviewer checked each against the tests that exist today and found all four covered by work landed in .7/.8:
- two-block shape: TestTwoBlockSystemPrompt (4 tests, drives the real _stream_anthropic, asserts block order, both cache_control markers, block 0 byte-identical across users, single block with no instructions, no system field with neither)
- envelope ordering: TestInstructionEnvelope (preamble<body<guardrail, rindex beats a body quoting the postamble, appends after verbosity) plus the cross-block assertion in TestInstructionSetWiring
- unknown/archived id: TestInstructionSetResolution::test_unknown_id_is_ignored_not_raised / ::test_archived_id_is_ignored / ::test_another_users_id_does_not_resolve, and ::test_unknown_id_still_streams at the HTTP layer

In several cases the coverage is tighter than this ticket asked - the envelope tests include fence-escape and postamble-mimicry attacks the ticket never named.

title: Add instruction-set CRUD endpoints
description:
genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/routers/llm_config.py, in the user-settings region (~lines 185-296), all Depends(auth_required) and user-scoped:

GET    /chat/v1/llm-config/user/instruction-sets -> [{id,name,body,updated_at}]
POST   /chat/v1/llm-config/user/instruction-sets {name, body} -> created set; 400 empty, 413 over char cap, 409 over count cap
PUT    /chat/v1/llm-config/user/instruction-sets/{id} {name?, body?, comment?}; 404 if not owned
DELETE /chat/v1/llm-config/user/instruction-sets/{id} -> archive, 204
GET    /chat/v1/llm-config/user/instruction-sets/{id}/history?limit=20 (mirrors the tool-description history endpoint ~lines 388-413)

Selection reuses the live GET/PUT/DELETE /user/settings/selected_instruction_set — no new endpoint for it.
notes:
From .4: the accessors raise typed errors so you can map them without string matching — InstructionSetBodyTooLong -> 413, InstructionSetLimitReached -> 409. create_instruction_set's -> InstructionSet annotation is now honest (it raises RuntimeError rather than returning None).
update_instruction_set now returns None for an ARCHIVED set as well as an unowned one, so PUT on a set the user just DELETEd must 404, not 200.
InstructionSet.body_over_cap flags a set whose stored body predates the cap; update() rejects an echoed-back over-cap body with InstructionSetBodyTooLong.
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit a617edf. Reviewer probed cross-user isolation empirically with a two-identity client: status, detail string and response shape are byte-identical for a foreign id versus a nonexistent one on all three id-taking endpoints, so there is no existence leak. Ownership is checked BEFORE the length cap, so an over-cap body aimed at a foreign id still 404s rather than 413ing. Error mappings come from the typed exceptions, not string matching. PUT on an archived set 404s.

A new accessor get_instruction_set_history plus an InstructionSetVersion dataclass were added; verified to meet all three of this file's hard-won conventions (_discard_stale_transaction on entry, _as_utc_or_epoch parsing, changed_at DESC + id DESC tiebreak) with user_id in the WHERE clause rather than a post-filter.

BLOCKING BUG CAUGHT IN REVIEW: the history endpoint's limit was unvalidated. ?limit=-1 returned the ENTIRE history because SQLite treats a negative LIMIT as unbounded, and a limit past 64 bits raised OverflowError out of the driver as an uncaught 500. Fixed with Query(20, ge=1, le=100). The pre-existing get_tool_description_history endpoint had the identical hole and was fixed in the same commit.
