title: Emit a two-block cached system prompt
description:
genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/llm_service.py. stream_chat/_stream_anthropic (~lines 425-438, 519-531) gain user_instructions: str | None. Build system as two blocks at ~lines 577-581: block 0 = default_system_prompt + verbosity_prompt with cache_control (shared across all users, one entry per verbosity value), block 1 = instruction_envelope(body) with cache_control on the spare 4th breakpoint.

Measured: shared block is ~7.4K tokens; a full refragmentation costs ~$0.043 per event vs ~$0.0025 for the incremental per-user block, and leaving it uncached costs ~$0.05 across a 25-iteration turn. This uses the last of Anthropic's four breakpoints (tools, shared system, user system, last message) — update the cache-breakpoint comment at ~lines 549-556 to say so.
close_reason: Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit 1b0cf83 (batched with .7). Reviewer counted cache_control markers on the ACTUAL emitted request params rather than trusting the summary: 2 with neither tools nor instructions, 3 with either, exactly 4 with both - never more. Block 0 confirmed byte-identical across two users with different instructions, and the no-instructions path emits the identical single-element list as before, so nothing regresses for users without a set. All four Anthropic breakpoints are now in use (tools, shared system, user system, last message); any future breakpoint must displace an existing one, and the comment says so.

title: Resolve instruction_set_id in ChatRequest
description:
genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/chat_api.py. Add instruction_set_id: str | None to ChatRequest (near the verbosity field, ~line 221). In stream_chat (~line 383) resolve it to a body scoped to the authenticated user and pass it to service.stream_chat as a SEPARATE argument, not concatenated.

An id that does not resolve for this user is ignored, not 422'd — same rule as verbosity: a presentation preference must never fail a chat turn. A DB error must degrade to 'no instructions', never to a failed turn. Log the set id and name only, never the body.
notes:
HANDOFF FROM .4: .7 OWNS bounding the instruction body length - nothing below it clamps any more.
- get_instruction_set/list_instruction_sets return the AUTHORITATIVE stored body, which CAN exceed the cap (the .3 legacy import writes uncapped bodies, and a lowered cap strands existing rows).
- Truncate to INSTRUCTION_SET_MAX_BODY_CHARS yourself; import the constant from db.llm_config_db, do not hardcode 4000.
- InstructionSet.body_over_cap is a computed bool telling you it happened.
- Truncating must never fail the turn - degrade to the first N chars, consistent with the ignore-unresolvable-id rule. len() is code points, pinned by a test.
- Log the set id and name only, never the body.

FROM .6: instruction_envelope() now exists in config/defaults.py. Call it; do not rebuild the wrapper. Its fence length is computed from the body, which is what makes truncation safe - so truncate BEFORE wrapping and let the envelope fence the result.

FROM .6's review: chat_api.py:379-382 currently says the verbosity fragment 'is appended last so it reads as the final instruction'. That becomes FALSE the moment you append the envelope after it. .7 owns that file - update the comment in the same change.
close_reason: Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit 1b0cf83 (batched with .8). Suite 884 passed / 74 deselected across two seeds. Reviewer verified cross-user scoping empirically across 11 identity/id combinations (guessed uuid, null/empty user, case-variant, SQL-injection shaped, archived set) - only the owner resolves. The user comes from Depends(auth_required), never from the request body. Truncation-before-wrapping verified against 6 fence-straddle cases. Three nits fixed because they contradicted the task's own acceptance criteria: the try did not cover the slice or the envelope call so a non-str body could still raise; secret mode logged the user-authored set name; and 'Applying' was logged for a body that resolved to nothing.

title: Add instruction_envelope() to config/defaults.py
description:
genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/config/defaults.py, beside _VERBOSITY_PROMPTS (~lines 264-294). Build the fragment as: '## Your instructions (user setting)' preamble, the user body in a fence, then a guardrail postamble.

The postamble MUST follow the body — recency wins, and the existing comment at chat_api.py:379-382 reasons about the verbosity fragment being 'the final instruction', which inverts once arbitrary user text follows it. The envelope scopes the text to tone, audience, depth, units, default resources and language; it may not relax grounding, citation, truncation or out-of-scope rules, and says explicitly that the rules above win on conflict.
close_reason: Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit a18e3a2 (batched with .9). Suite 863 passed / 74 deselected across two seeds. Review found one BLOCKING issue: the envelope used a fixed three-backtick fence and interpolated the body verbatim, so a body containing ``` closed the wrapper early and could inject a heading at the same structural level as the real system sections; a body ending in a bare fence left the guardrail paragraph reading as fenced content rather than as an instruction. Not merely adversarial - .7 truncates the body before wrapping, so a cut landing in a backtick run does the same to a benign body containing a code snippet. Fixed with a fence computed from the longest backtick run in the body, verified against a CommonMark-accurate fence walker with both escape variants demonstrated contained.

title: Fix same-second tiebreak in user-settings reads
description: genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/db/llm_config_db.py get_user_setting/get_user_settings (~lines 452-506). They join on MAX(changed_at), but SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP has 1-second resolution, so two saves to the same key in the same second both match and an arbitrary winner is kept. Add ORDER BY changed_at DESC, id DESC (id is a true AUTOINCREMENT sequence). Needed because the selected-set pointer will live in this store.
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit 416e961. Suite 785 passed / 74 deselected across 5 runs including 2 random orderings. Blind validation killed all 8 mutants (HEAD revert of each of the 5 queries, MAX->MIN on both grouped forms, and dropping the user_id scope); 11 of 12 new tests fail against HEAD, the survivor being the one that pins preserved NULL behaviour.

The bug was user-visible, not latent: the index is scanned rowid-ascending within a tie, so get_user_setting returned the OLDEST tied write every time. Two clicks inside one second kept the first.

TWO ROUNDS OF REGRESSION CAUGHT IN REVIEW: (1) the first rewrite lost the index on both plural accessors — measured 26ms->1124ms at 60k tool rows and 5.5->214ms at 10k settings rows/user. Replaced with a grouped MAX(id) form that restores the plan and matches or beats HEAD. (2) A comment asserted a query plan that only occurs after ANALYZE; neither repo ever runs ANALYZE, so it was wrong in the deployed state. Two reviewers contradicted each other on it and the disagreement was resolved empirically across 44 database states.

SCOPE BEYOND THE TICKET, needs the user's awareness: the ticket named only get_user_setting/get_user_settings. Three tool-description accessors carried the identical defect and were also fixed — fixing only the singular one would have made it disagree with the history listing an admin reads as current, and a tie there could drop the NEWEST versions from a limited listing. Deliberately NOT touched: get_user_comments/list_all_user_comments (tie permutes a display list, no current value derived) — filed as genetics-results-suite-qdf instead.

Follow-ups filed: genetics-results-suite-2cl (singular accessors crash on NULL/blank changed_at while plural drop the key), genetics-results-suite-qdf (admin feedback pagination boundary shift).

title: Add instruction-set accessors with caps
description: genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/db/llm_config_db.py. Add list/get/create/update/archive_instruction_set. Every query scoped by user_id. update appends to user_instruction_set_history and updates the row. Caps enforced at write time AND re-checked at read time (a legacy row can exceed a later-lowered cap): ~4000 chars per body, ~20 non-archived sets per user.
notes:
From .2's review: SQLite DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP on updated_at fires only on INSERT, never on UPDATE. update_instruction_set MUST set updated_at explicitly, or the (user_id, archived_at, updated_at DESC) index orders by creation time and the 'newest first' listing is silently wrong. Also insert timestamps by omission rather than explicit NULL — the columns lack NOT NULL (consistent with every other table in the file) but the dataclass types them non-optional.

From .3's review: the legacy import's re-entry guard depends on the epic's archive-rather-than-delete decision. Do NOT add a hard delete accessor — a hard DELETE would let the legacy import re-run and resurrect an imported set the user deliberately removed.
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit 937cd74. Full suite 748 passed / 74 deselected, stable across 8 repeat runs; each new test mutation-verified to fail only against its own reverted fix. Three fix rounds; both round-3 reviewers concluded nothing blocked shipping.

Blocking bugs caught and fixed in review: (1) read-time body clamp destroyed 5000 chars of a 9000-char legacy set on an edit-form round trip; (2) the per-user count cap was a TOCTOU that 4 concurrent creates walked through, leaving 23 rows against a cap of 20; (3) BEGIN IMMEDIATE outside the try permanently poisoned a thread's cached connection after any failed DML; (4) update/archive lacked rollback guards, so a failed write was silently committed by the next successful one, breaking the append-only history invariant; (5) update returned success while persisting nothing and appending a phantom history row when racing an archive.

Responsibility moved OUT of this task: bounding the body length for the prompt now belongs to .7 (see .7 notes). InstructionSet.body_over_cap reports it.

Pre-existing defects found but deliberately NOT fixed here, filed separately: genetics-results-suite-y5d (the class's other 8 write accessors leave transactions open on failure) and genetics-results-suite-do8 (llm_config.db has no WAL, unlike chat_history.db).

title: Import and retire the orphaned user_instructions_history table
description:

Its one-blob-per-user shape cannot express many named sets.

In _migrate_to_history_tables, do a one-shot idempotent import (guarded on user_instruction_sets being empty) of the latest surviving row per user into a set named 'Imported'. Stop creating the legacy table for new databases. Leave existing rows in place; do not drop the table in the same release.

Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit 5ac15b9. Full suite 686 passed (664 baseline + 22 new migration tests), review APPROVED round 2, blind validation found no functional defects.

DELIBERATE DEVIATION from this task's text: the guard is per-user (NOT EXISTS for that user_id), not 'guarded on user_instruction_sets being empty'. The literal reading was found to be a blocking bug — one user owning one set would have silently stranded every other user's legacy text forever, and nothing orders .11 after .3. Do not re-litigate.

Two round-1 blocking bugs fixed: one-arg SQLite TRIM strips spaces only so newline-only bodies were being imported; NULL changed_at suppressed the column DEFAULT and lost the ORDER BY comparison.

Known pre-existing issue found but NOT fixed (out of scope, needs user sign-off): docs/project-spec.md's Testing table is also missing test_credible_set_summary.py, test_disabled_thinking.py and test_stream_truncation.py, and CLAUDE.md's doc-ownership table has no tests/** row, so that table has no drift guard.

title: Feature: user-authored Instructions for chat
description:
Users can create and store multiple named sets of additional instructions (like Claude Desktop 'profiles', e.g. 'I'm a statistician') and select one per chat use case. The selected profile's text is appended to the LLM system prompt on each chat request.

UI lands beside the existing brief/detailed Answer selector in the chat options row (genetics-results-browser src/features/chat/LLMChat.tsx). Storage is per-user in the DB (genetics-mcp-server SQLite llm_config_db, which already has user_settings_history and an orphaned user_instructions_history table). Backend prompt assembly mirrors the verbosity_prompt() pattern in config/defaults.py + chat_api.py.

Spans repos: genetics-mcp-server (API + DB + prompt), genetics-results-browser (UI + types), genetics-results-suite (docs of record).

Naming to be decided as part of planning.
design:
Alternative 2 selected: first-class entity, server-resolved by id, split cached system block.

Name: UI label 'Instructions', code noun instruction_set. Rejected 'profile' (already means tool_profile in the same options row, the daly/finngen deploy config_profile, and results-api app/config/profiles/), 'persona' (the suite spec uses it for the APP_NAME assistant persona, and the text describes the user not the assistant) and 'context' (the same row renders a 'Conversation context' usage bar).

Key decisions:
- The chat request carries an id only; the server loads the body scoped to the authenticated user, so prompt text is never client-supplied and an answer is always attributable to a stored set.
- System prompt splits into two cached blocks: shared default+verbosity (one global cache entry per verbosity value) and the per-user envelope on the spare 4th breakpoint. ~$0.0025 per incremental write vs ~$0.043 for full-block refragmentation vs ~$0.05 per 25-iteration turn uncached.
- Selection: global-per-user default in user_settings_history, overridden per request, recorded per message on chat_messages. Per-session storage rejected: it needs a session-mutation endpoint and makes 'which wins' unanswerable when the selector moves mid-conversation.
- Archive rather than delete, so historical chat_messages rows stay resolvable.
- Unknown id is ignored, never 422 — same rule as verbosity.
- Folded in from the other alternatives: seeded clonable example sets in the dialog (from Alt 3), and the ORDER BY changed_at DESC, id DESC settings fix (from Alt 1).

Out of scope, documented rather than built: subagents (their reports are intermediate artifacts the main agent rewrites) and the MCP server path (no server-side system prompt, _validate_user_token discards identity, no llm_config.db volume mounted).

Not part of this epic, but decide separately: ChatRequest.system_prompt (chat_api.py:209) lets any authenticated user replace the entire system prompt with no gate — a strictly larger hole than the feature going in beside it.
close_reason:
All 21 subtasks closed. Feature complete and documented across genetics-mcp-server, genetics-results-browser and this repo's spec of record.

Shipped: users author named instruction sets, pick one per chat, and the selected set's text is appended to the system prompt in its own cached block. Named 'Instructions' rather than 'profiles' because tool_profile already sits in the same options row and the deploy config_profile and results-api app/config/profiles/ take the word twice more.

Architecture as chosen (Alternative 2): a first-class entity, resolved server-side by id so prompt text never travels on the request, with the system prompt split into a shared cached block and a per-user one. That keeps one cache entry per verbosity value instead of fragmenting per user, and consumes the fourth and last Anthropic breakpoint.

Blocking bugs caught in review that a green test suite did not: a read-time clamp that destroyed 5000 chars of a 9000-char legacy set on an edit round-trip; a per-user cap four concurrent requests walked straight through; BEGIN IMMEDIATE outside a try permanently poisoning a thread's cached connection; a fixed markdown fence a body could close early to inject a fake system section; an unvalidated LIMIT that returned entire histories on ?limit=-1 and 500'd past 64 bits; and a selector that silently reset on every session switch so messages went without the user's instructions.

Also fixed along the way, all pre-existing: rollback guards across both SQLite modules, WAL on llm_config.db, a same-second tiebreak that returned the OLDEST write, malformed-timestamp crashes, admin feedback pagination that could duplicate or skip an item, REQUIRE_AUTH read from two sources, and an importlib.reload that split the settings cache and made the suite's own green signal unreliable.

Deliberately not built, documented instead: instructions do not apply to subagents or to the MCP server path. Filed rather than fixed: genetics-results-suite-b3v (OpenAI branch drops instructions silently), -uvh (batched comment/doc accuracy), -eis (admin UI timestamp format), -avt (INTERNAL_API_SECRET), plus the still-open question of ChatRequest.system_prompt letting any authenticated user replace the entire system prompt with no gate.

title: [mcp-server] Serve MCP OAuth discovery (.well-known/oauth-protected-resource + WWW-Authenticate)
description:
Repo: ../genetics-mcp-server. File: src/genetics_mcp_server/mcp_server.py, in the ASGI auth_middleware (same place /healthz is special-cased).

Implement RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata so MCP clients (Claude connectors, ChatGPT, brainzzz) auto-discover the authorization server:
- Serve GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (and the path-suffixed /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp) returning JSON: { resource: OAUTH_RESOURCE_URL, authorization_servers: [OAUTH_ISSUER], scopes_supported: [...], bearer_methods_supported: ["header"] }. - On a 401 from the bearer middleware, add header WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="<resource>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource" so clients know where to look.
Only enable these when OAUTH_ISSUER is configured. The authorization-server metadata itself (/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server) is served by Keycloak, not here.

title: Feature: Direct OAuth (Keycloak) auth for MCP server — GeneGenie / brainzzz
description:
Let external web applications (first: brainzzz) connect to the GeneGenie MCP server via a standard OAuth 2.1 flow, instead of a shared api-token. Add this as a FOURTH bearer-validation path alongside the existing three (MCP_API_KEY shared secret, Google Identity Token JWT, per-user API token) — nothing existing is removed.

WHY: IAP/Google ID-Tokens don't fit a third-party app acting on behalf of its own users (audience-bound, no consent/refresh, users not on our email allow-list). MCP's HTTP transport defines an OAuth 2.1 profile where the MCP server is an OAuth *resource server* and clients auto-discover the *authorization server*. The daly/GeneGenie deployment already runs Keycloak as a full OIDC AS (https://auth.<domain>/realms/genetics, ENABLE_KEYCLOAK on for daly), so Keycloak is the authorization server and a 'web application type' OAuth client registered there is exactly what's needed.

SCOPE: GeneGenie (daly profile) only for now. finngen/FinnGenie has Keycloak OFF (Google-direct) and is out of scope.

DESIGN CONTRACT (shared across subtasks):
- Authorization server = Keycloak realm 'genetics'; issuer https://auth.<domain>/realms/genetics.
- MCP resource canonical URL (RFC 8707 resource indicator / RFC 9728 resource identifier) = https://genegenie.broadinstitute.org/mcp.
- Keycloak issues access tokens (JWT) with aud including that resource URL (via an audience mapper / dedicated client scope on the brainzzz client).
- MCP server validates: signature via Keycloak JWKS, iss match, aud includes resource URL, exp; THEN the existing email/domain allow-list (settings.allowed_emails / allowed_email_domains, already fed by the bearer-auth-allowed ConfigMap).
- Discovery: MCP server serves /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (RFC 9728) pointing at the Keycloak issuer, and returns WWW-Authenticate: Bearer with resource_metadata=... on 401. The authorization-server metadata itself is served by Keycloak (already on auth.<domain>).

Code work is split between the sibling repo ../genetics-mcp-server (validation + discovery + settings) and this repo genetics-results-suite (deployment env + auth-gateway routing + docs). Plus Keycloak client config (ops).

title: Phase 0: finalize EpiMap 18-state storage + open/active state set
description: Decide how the ChromHMM 18-state label is stored (score_type=chromhmm_18state + state token placement) and which states count as open/active (TSS/enhancer/transcribed). Gates the EpiMap munge task.
design:
EpiMap ChromHMM 18-state modeling for the open_chromatin product.
Model = Roadmap/EpiMap 18-state (observed_aux_18), 833 biosamples, hg38 CALLS.
INCLUDE (accessible/active regulatory subset) as open_chromatin rows:
  active promoter: TssA, TssFlnk, TssFlnkU, TssFlnkD
  active enhancer: EnhA1, EnhA2, EnhG1, EnhG2, EnhWk
  poised/bivalent (accessible, tagged): TssBiv, EnhBiv
EXCLUDE (not open peaks): Tx, TxWk, ZNF_Rpts, Het, ReprPC, ReprPCWk, Quies.
State storage (NO schema change): encode the exact state in score_type as chromhmm:<State> (e.g. score_type=chromhmm:EnhA1); assay=chromHMM; score=NULL (presence-based — ChromHMM is a categorical segmentation, so row existence = state called in that biosample).
Agent-facing regulatory_class grouping (map in the MCP tool description, NOT stored): Tss* -> promoter, Enh* -> enhancer, *Biv -> bivalent.
Labels: cell_type = verbatim EpiMap biosample name; tissue from EpiMap sample metadata (GROUP/Anatomy column); life_stage=adult unless the biosample metadata marks it fetal/embryonic; condition=unknown.
Do NOT import EpiMap DNase layer (that is the Meuleman DHS index, which was dropped).
close_reason: Resolved: EpiMap active/accessible state subset + state-in-score_type encoding decided. Decision recorded in --design.

title: Phase 0: confirm genome builds & liftOver needs

design:
Genome-build decision — platform standard = GRCh38/hg38 (GENCODE).
- marderstein (scATAC peaks + ChromBPNet + FLARE): hg38, native, no liftOver.
- li_brain_atac (Li 2023 Science): hg38, native.
- catlas (Zhang 2021 Cell): hg38, native (verify cCRE BED header at download).

- calderon_immune (Calderon 2019): hg19 -> liftOver to hg38 (UCSC hg19ToHg38.over.chain); drop unmapped and split/multi-mapping intervals, then re-sort.
- rosmap_brain (Xiong 2023): hg38, native.

title: Feature: Google token authentication for MCP server

title: tfvars sed uses GNU-only \s, and build.sh warns about nothing from a worktree
description:
Found while fixing genetics-results-suite-1xp; pre-existing, left untouched there deliberately.

TWO SMALL PORTABILITY/DIAGNOSTIC GAPS in the tfvars-parsing scripts, both non-urgent:

1. `\s` IS A GNU SED EXTENSION. scripts/deploy.sh:39, scripts/create-secrets.sh, scripts/build.sh and scripts/build-all.sh all extract tfvars values with `sed 's/.*=\s*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/'`. BSD/macOS sed does not understand `\s`, so the substitution simply does not match and the variable comes back as the WHOLE LINE rather than the value - silently, with exit 0. On Linux this never fires, which is why it has never been noticed. Fix is `[[:space:]]*`, which is POSIX and works on both. Four call sites, one spelling.
   Not urgent: everything today runs on Linux. It matters the first time someone runs deploy.sh or build.sh from a Mac.

2. scripts/build.sh DOES NOT CALL check-worktree-paths.sh, while scripts/build-all.sh:25 does. After 1xp, a build from a worktree with no terraform.tfvars falls back to APP_NAME=FinnGenie - correct behaviour, but with NO warning at all when a single service is built directly. build-all.sh warns; build.sh does not. Decide whether build.sh should get the same preflight call or whether single-service builds are deliberately quieter.

RELATED, DECIDED AND ACCEPTED IN 1xp, recorded so it is not rediscovered as a bug: an UNREADABLE (chmod 000) tfvars is now masked by `|| true` into the FinnGenie fallback with exit 0 and no message. Measured. On daly that bakes the wrong brand into images. Accepted because the prior behaviour on that exact path was a silent exit 2, which is not better - but if a third case ever needs handling here, this is the one to revisit.

title: Four SDK functions still lose their schema on an empty result; their endpoints do not stream a TSV
description:
Split out of genetics-results-suite-6uk, which fixed 12 of the 16 exposed SDK functions and deliberately left these four.

6uk made results-api advertise a JSON range response's columns in an X-Columns header, which the SDK consumes so an empty result keeps its column names. That works because those endpoints STREAM A TSV and range_response can read the file's own header line - even for a zero-row file.

These four do not:
  gene_burden / get_gene_based_results  (app/routers/gene_based.py)
  gene_annotations                      (app/routers/genes.py, gene_groups.py)
  gene_disease                          (app/routers/gene_disease.py)
  search                                (app/routers/search.py)
Their endpoints COMPUTE JSON and return StreamingResponse/TimedJSONResponse directly, never passing through range_response, so there is no file header to advertise. They degrade to a bare pl.DataFrame() - no regression, and 6uk pinned that degradation with a test so an absent header can never raise something new.

WHY THIS IS A DIFFERENT SHAPE OF WORK: fixing them means each router DECLARING its own output columns, rather than reading them off a file. That is the option (b) 6uk rejected for the streaming endpoints, and the reason it was rejected there does not apply here - there is no file header to be a superset of, so a declared list IS the ground truth. But it means a hand-maintained list per router, which is exactly the thing that rots. Whatever is chosen needs a check that fails closed when a router's declared columns and its actual output disagree - see 4h6.31 for the pattern (a generator that REFUSES rather than degrading, plus a test that mutation-proves the refusal).

Do not just hardcode the lists. 4h6.25 rejected a hand-copied schema across a repo boundary and 6uk rejected a generated superset; a third variant with no check would be worse than either.

Low priority: the failure is a script getting a bare empty frame and having to guess column names, which costs a retry iteration rather than producing a wrong answer.

title: The sandbox tracker bound and pod-wide concurrency limit are cross-tenant denial surfaces
description:
Found by a blind validator during genetics-results-suite-4h6.29; documented there, not fixed.

Two of results-api's new limits deny service to OTHER executions rather than only to the caller that exceeded them:

1. SANDBOX_MAX_TRACKED_EXECUTIONS (4096). The accounting map is global and entries are created by ANY valid token, living up to one token lifetime (~305s). A caller able to start 4096 executions inside that window locks out every other user's NEW execution with sandbox_execution_tracker_full. The module argues 23 chat turns/hour makes this unreachable - that is a statement about honest VOLUME, not a bound on an attacker.
   Note this is the direct cost of the (correct) fail-closed eviction choice: because a live entry is never evicted, a full map must refuse newcomers.

2. SANDBOX_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_TOTAL (8) against SANDBOX_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS (4) means TWO misbehaving executions can deny every other execution pod-wide. Moot while the sandbox is concurrency: 1 - the per-jti limit binds first - but it becomes live the moment sandbox concurrency is raised, which is precisely the scenario the pod-wide limit was added for.

RELATED AND COMPOUNDING: there is no request timeout anywhere (none in run_server.py's uvicorn.run, none in the manifest). A request hung in a GCS read holds a per-execution slot, a pod-wide slot, AND pins its map entry permanently, because _sweep_locked refuses to evict anything with in_flight > 0. So the anti-eviction rule that closes the fail-open direction has no counterpart bounding how long an entry may stay unevictable. A handful of hung requests is enough to reach case 2 without any attacker.

TO DO, roughly in order:
1. Add a request timeout, which is worth doing on its own merits and removes the compounding path. Decide where - uvicorn's timeout, an ASGI middleware, or a per-request asyncio deadline - and note that whatever is chosen must still run release() in a finally.
2. Add per-caller fairness to the pod-wide limit, or drop it in favour of a memory-based admission check, so one execution cannot consume every slot.
3. Consider whether tracker-full should shed the OLDEST idle entry rather than refusing the newest - it changes which party is harmed, and the current choice harms the innocent newcomer.
4. Emit a metric or ERROR log on tracker-full and on pod-wide rejection. Today only logger.warning fires on rejection and nothing logs admissions, so an operator cannot tell a denial from quiet traffic, nor tune 1000/4/8 from production data.

Not urgent: production impact is nil until the sandbox is deployed. Do it in the same window as genetics-results-suite-4h6.7.

title: check-doc-drift.sh's sandbox mapping fires on generated schema docs, where it cannot apply
description:
Observed firing on suite 74bfc7f (genetics-results-suite-4h6.31), which regenerated sandbox/schema/*.md to add a column-type column.

SANDBOX_PATHS in scripts/check-doc-drift.sh is '^(sandbox/|k8s/deployments/sandbox\.yaml$|k8s/network-policies/sandbox-policy\.yaml$)' and maps to docs/code-execution-security.md, whose listed concerns are "isolation boundary, egress+ingress allow-lists, the three MCP-exclusion layers, sandbox token claims".

sandbox/schema/*.md are GENERATED schema documentation. They cannot affect any of those four things, so the warning can never apply to them - yet it fires on every regeneration, and the schema docs are regenerated whenever a dataset or column changes, which is often.

WHY THIS MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TIDY-UP: a warning that fires when it cannot apply is how the check teaches people to ignore it. That is the same failure mode fixed in genetics-results-suite-0xs, where a preflight's beads detection fired in every worktree regardless of staleness and would have turned a four-item check into wallpaper. This check is warn-only, so the cost of ignoring it is exactly the cost of the drift it exists to catch.

FIX: narrow the code-execution-security.md mapping to the paths that can actually change the isolation boundary - the sandbox image, its Dockerfile and entrypoint, k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml, k8s/network-policies/sandbox-policy.yaml - and exclude sandbox/schema/. Decide separately whether sandbox/schema/ should still map to docs/project-spec.md; it plausibly should, since the spec summarises what the sandbox exposes.

CHECK THE OTHER MAPPINGS FOR THE SAME SHAPE while you are there - any rule whose path pattern is broader than the doc concern it names will do this. The CLAUDE.md ownership table and this script are supposed to mirror each other, so fix both or neither.

title: db-api reads INTERNAL_API_SECRET at import time, so a module-scope import in any new test breaks test_api_auth
description:
Found while validating genetics-results-suite-tcs, in genetics-results-db.

api/main.py reads INTERNAL_API_SECRET at MODULE IMPORT time. tests/test_api_auth.py sets the env var at FIXTURE time (line 21) and imports api.main at line 23 - but pytest imports every test module during COLLECTION, before any fixture runs. So any future test module that does `from api import main` at module scope freezes INTERNAL_API_SECRET to '' for the whole session and breaks test_api_auth with a failure that points nowhere near the cause.

DEMONSTRATED, not theorised: importing api.main with the env var unset, then setting it and re-importing, leaves INTERNAL_API_SECRET as '' - the module-scope read happens once.

tests/test_endpoint_access_log.py (added by tcs) works around it by importing lazily inside a fixture, with the reason in the fixture docstring. That is a workaround, not a fix, and it only holds as long as every future author notices the docstring.

FIX, pick one:
(a) a conftest.py that sets INTERNAL_API_SECRET before collection - smallest, keeps the module-scope read;
(b) read the secret at REQUEST time rather than import time - removes the global-state hazard entirely and is the honest fix, but touches the auth path, so it needs the same care genetics-results-suite-zyi's compare_digest work did;
(c) leave it and rely on the docstring - not recommended, since the failure mode is a confusing error in an UNRELATED test file.

Prefer (b) if the auth path is being touched anyway; (a) otherwise. Note that whichever is chosen, a test should pin it - the current arrangement passes for a reason no test states.

title: check-doc-drift.sh cannot detect enumeration rot, which is what every drift found so far actually was
description:
Split out of genetics-results-suite-rxw, which established the limitation while fixing a different half of the problem.

scripts/check-doc-drift.sh warns when a changed PATH has a mapped DOC that was not changed in the same commit. That is all it does. It cannot detect the failure mode CLAUDE.md actually warns about:

  "A doc is stale the moment it ENUMERATES something the code no longer matches.
   Counts and lists rot silently - view lists, endpoint tables, env-var tables,
   service inventories - so re-derive them from the code rather than trusting them."

EVERY drift this epic has found was enumeration rot, not a missing doc update:
- docs/project-spec.md asserted a node-pool pinning that was never applied
- surge arithmetic (3951m / 13.60 GiB from a '2651m / 7.91 GiB steady state') that no profile has ever produced
- the datasets/phenotypes docs carried a stale ~33k row count
- the ALL_VIEWS list was one short
- genetics-results-suite-eau (2026-08-11) replaced a rotted 'every application container sets ...' claim with an explicit enumeration THAT WAS WRONG ON DAY ONE - it missed k8s/cronjobs/keycloak-postgres-backup.yaml - and shipped a self-check instruction (`grep k8s/deployments/`) that by construction could not see the directory the missed file was in
- genetics-results-suite-re3 (2026-08-11) had two investigations cite a BigQuery table that turned out to be a different machine's log

The eau case is the sharpest evidence: a human-written enumeration and its own re-derivation instruction were BOTH wrong at the moment of writing, and the doc-drift hook fired correctly on that commit while being structurally incapable of noticing.

WHAT A CHECK COULD ACTUALLY DO, roughly in order of value for effort:
1. Assert that named inventories match a derivable source. Start with the ones that have rotted: the container-hardening lists in project-spec/README vs `grep -rn allowPrivilegeEscalation k8s/` PLUS the complement of the workload inventory; ALL_VIEWS vs configs/datasets.yaml; the service table vs k8s/deployments/*.
2. Assert that any fenced code block or table cell claiming to be a command's OUTPUT can be regenerated and still matches.
3. Fail on a doc that cites a BigQuery table, k8s object or file path that does not exist.

Note (1) is the only one that addresses the actual hit rate, and it needs each enumeration to declare its source - e.g. an HTML comment marking the block and the command that regenerates it. That is a real design task, not a grep.

DECIDE FIRST whether this is worth building or whether the discipline belongs in review instead. The honest counter-argument: every instance above was caught by a human or an agent reading carefully, not by tooling, and a check that covers three enumerations while the docs contain fifty may create false confidence in the other forty-seven. If it is built, it should say plainly which enumerations it covers.

RELATED, unresolved and the user's call: whether check-doc-drift.sh should block rather than warn. Recorded in rxw's description; the warning does get seen, so blocking may not be the lever.

title: Eight workloads still have no container securityContext
description:
Split out of genetics-results-suite-eau, which hardened auth-gateway and enumerated the rest rather than fixing them.

Re-derived from k8s/ twice during eau, so this list is current as of suite 13f074c:
  Deployments: frontend, oauth2-proxy, keycloak, postgres, rag-service
  CronJobs:    monitor (pod-level fsGroup: 1000 only), analyze-conversations, keycloak-postgres-backup (k8s/cronjobs/)
None sets a container-level securityContext. The only other securityContext hits in the tree are pod-level fsGroup at chat-backend.yaml:24 and monitor-cronjob.yaml:19, which is not hardening.

DO NOT DO THESE AS ONE CHANGE. eau proved the failure mode: a bare capabilities.drop: [ALL] would have CrashLooped the internet-facing gateway, for a reason the bead had not anticipated (the image's root master chowns temp paths and setuids its workers). Each image needs the same empirical treatment - run it locally under docker with --cap-drop=ALL --security-opt=no-new-privileges against its real config, and find out what it actually needs before shipping a drop.

Prioritise by exposure: oauth2-proxy sits in the request path; postgres and keycloak hold credentials; rag-service and frontend are lower; the three CronJobs are lowest but keycloak-postgres-backup runs google/cloud-sdk:slim with a Postgres password from keycloak-secrets.

Expect the same trap eau hit twice: several of these images run a root process that drops to a service user, so drop-ALL alone breaks them and the honest fix is runAsUser plus writable-dir emptyDirs rather than capability juggling. Also expect the docs to need updating in the same commit - docs/project-spec.md and README.md both ENUMERATE this list, and docs/code-execution-security.md defines a 'suite baseline' term that these workloads are explicitly outside of.

title: results-api logs no response size, so the endpoint_access sink can never answer size questions
description:
Found while validating genetics-results-suite-re3, and it corrects a premise that bead inherited.

re3 said httpRequest.responseSize was 'non-null on 0 of 2,812 rows', implying the sink drops it. It was never there to drop. MEASURED: httpRequest is NULL on all 278,757 rows across BOTH tables in genetics_api_logs. genetics-results-api/app/middleware_usage_logging.py calls logger.info() with a plain dict, which produces a jsonPayload-only entry; Cloud Logging populates the httpRequest struct only when a caller sets it, and nothing here does. The column exists in the schema because the Logging export schema is fixed, not because anything writes it.

So no sink configuration change can produce response sizes. It needs a middleware change.

WHY IT MATTERS: docs/code-execution-security.md's truncation analysis wanted exactly this data and had to fall back to reasoning about caps instead of measuring. That fallback is sound (see the code-execution-security re-measurement bead) but it means the question 'has any response ever approached the cap' is currently unanswerable from logs.

TO DO (sibling repo genetics-results-api):
Add a response_bytes field to the endpoint_access payload in app/middleware_usage_logging.py - capture Content-Length where present, or accumulate body bytes in the send wrapper for streaming responses. Note that most of results-api's large responses ARE streaming (TimedStreamingResponse), so Content-Length alone will miss precisely the cases the size question is about.
Then update this repo's docs/project-spec.md log-sinks bullet, which currently states that httpRequest is never populated.

Low priority: nothing is broken, a capability is simply absent. Raise it if the truncation question comes up again.

title: Three independent DatasetMapping() constructions in results-api, one mapping-file read each
description: Flagged during genetics-results-suite-917, deliberately left alone there as out of scope. app/core/streams.py (now behind get_dataset_mapping()), app/core/service_container.py:149, and app/services/data_access_coloc.py:203 each construct their own DatasetMapping. Each construction calls _init_dataset_to_resource_mapping -> read_file(path) over dataset_mapping_files, and read_file handles gs://, so that is three reads of the same mapping file per process where one would do. It was previously awkward to consolidate because streams.py's was EAGER at module import; 917 made it lazy, so all three are now lazily constructed and pointing them at the single container instance is a clean change. Check whether the three actually receive the same configuration before merging them - if any is constructed with different dataset_mapping_files or options, that difference is load-bearing and consolidation would change behaviour. The suite is now a real signal (564 passed, and pytest -m offline runs 182 tests credential-free), so this is verifiable in a way it was not before genetics-results-suite-w09.

title: mcp_server.py query_string.decode() has the same undecodable-bytes 500 as the bearer header
description: Found while fixing genetics-results-suite-zyi's fourth compare_digest instance, deliberately left out of that change as out of scope. genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/mcp_server.py ~line 349, the MCP_ALLOW_QUERY_TOKEN branch, does query_string.decode() with no guard. A non-UTF-8 query string raises UnicodeDecodeError inside raw ASGI middleware, where there is nothing above it to turn the exception into a response, so the caller gets a bare 500 instead of a 401. This is the identical shape just fixed on the same file's authorization-header decode (~line 335), which is now wrapped in try/except UnicodeDecodeError falling through to the existing 401 branch. NOT REACHABLE BY DEFAULT: the branch is gated on MCP_ALLOW_QUERY_TOKEN, which is unset in every k8s manifest and script in the suite, so this is latent unless someone enables query-token auth. Note that 'latent' was ALSO claimed of the zyi bug and turned out to be false, so verify the gating rather than trusting this description. FIX: same treatment as the header decode, plus a test sending a non-UTF-8 query string through the hand-built ASGI scope in tests/test_mcp_server.py's TestBearerAuthMiddleware (which is how the two new bearer tests avoid httpx refusing to encode non-ASCII values).

title: compare_digest bearer comparison encodes utf-8 but starlette decodes headers as latin-1
description: Raised by review during genetics-results-suite-zyi; deliberately NOT changed there because it is a suite-wide consistency question, not a solo change. Starlette decodes raw header bytes with LATIN-1, so a wire bearer of b'Bearer s\xc3\xa9cret' arrives as the str 'Bearer sA-cret' (mojibake). Re-encoding that with utf-8 yields b's\xc3\x83\xc2\xa9cret', so the comparison never sees the bytes the client actually sent. token.encode('latin-1') would be byte-exact. HARMLESS TODAY AND FAIL-CLOSED: INTERNAL_API_SECRET is ASCII, and an ASCII str encodes identically under both codecs, so every genuine caller still matches. It becomes a real bug only if the secret ever contains a non-ASCII character, and then the failure is a 401 for the LEGITIMATE holder - the safe direction, not a bypass. THREE REPOS SHARE THE SAME utf-8 IDIOM and must be decided together: genetics-results-db api/main.py (~line 136-138), genetics-results-api app/core/auth.py:66-68, and genetics-mcp-server's chat-backend auth. Changing one alone creates a real inconsistency where today there is only a shared latent one. DECIDE: either switch all three to latin-1 for byte-exactness, or document that the secret MUST be ASCII and add a startup assertion to that effect - the latter may be better, since a non-ASCII shared secret has no upside and an explicit constraint is easier to reason about than an encoding subtlety. Related: genetics-results-suite-zyi, which fixed the str-vs-bytes TypeError on this same line.

title: adding-datasets.md HLA checklist does not mention the explicit-column decision

title: ToolExecutor's client property has four latent descriptor sharp edges after the l41 lazy-resolution change
description:
All four are latent - a reviewer grepped both repos and confirmed nothing does any of them today. Filed so the next person to touch ToolExecutor does not discover them the hard way.

genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/tools/executor.py:

1. del executor.client RAISES (:273). The client property has a setter but no deleter, so del gets AttributeError: property 'client' of 'ToolExecutor' object has no deleter. cached_property allowed it once cached. Fix: add a @client.deleter doing self.__dict__.pop('client', None).

2. hasattr/getattr on client is a CONSTRUCTION TRAP (:246). hasattr(e, 'client') returns True AND leaves a live client in __dict__. The previous cached_property had the same trap, but nobody now expects client to be absent-able, and close() deliberately reads __dict__ rather than the attribute for exactly this reason. Worth a line in the property docstring.

3. _client_lock exists only via __init__ (:204). Any construction bypassing it - object.__new__, Mock(spec=ToolExecutor), a subclass overriding __init__ without super() - AttributeErrors on first client access. No such site exists today.

4. Order dependency between base_url shadowing and public_url (:234-239). public_url's default is self.base_url and cached_property is a non-data descriptor, so executor.base_url = X propagates into public_url only if assigned BEFORE public_url is first read. Probed both orders. No production or test code assigns any of the three URLs on an executor.

NOT a regression and confirmed as such: deepcopy/pickle fail on _thread.lock, but _ResilientAsyncClient already made deepcopy fail with TypeError before this change, and nothing copies or pickles an executor.

Cosmetic, could fold into a formatting pass: ruff format --check would reformat executor.py, but it would have reformatted the pre-change file too - there is no CI workflow, no pre-commit config and no ruff format in any script, and the enforced ruff check passes clean. Also base_url is annotated -> str while _endpoint_env returns str | None; unreachable since a default is always supplied, and no type checker is configured.

title: SDK truncation error names the 100,000-row transfer cap, but a sandbox execution is capped at 25,000
description:
On the sql() path, GeneticsClient._check_truncation (genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/sdk/client.py:162-172) never reaches the message that names 100,000. executor.py:492 sets truncated = len(all_rows) > max_rows or download_capped, so the 'truncated' branch (:162-167) always fires first, and its text names NO number at all: 'result was truncated, so the rows returned are a positional prefix'. The download_capped_at_100k branch (:168-172), which is the only string naming db-api's 100,000-row transfer cap, is unreachable from sql().

Substantive problem, verified: db-api resolves SANDBOX_MAX_ROWS = 25,000 for a SandboxPrincipal (api/main.py:252, min(request.max_rows, caps.max_rows)) and sets truncated = total_rows > max_rows (api/main.py:850). So a sandbox execution is cut at 25,000 and the SDK reports that cut with an error that gives the agent no ceiling to design around — it cannot tell 25,000 from 100,000 from the message, and raising max_rows does nothing. 100,000 is the relaxed MAX_ROWS, reachable only by a caller holding INTERNAL_API_SECRET.

Fix in the SDK: have db-api return the cap it applied in the /query response and quote that number in the truncated-branch message. Do not hardcode 25,000 in the SDK - it is db-api's constant. Separately, decide whether the download_capped_at_100k branch is dead code on this path or whether executor.py should stop folding download_capped into truncated.

title: docs/adding-datasets.md undercounts the views excluded from ALL_VIEWS
description:
Found 2026-08-10 while re-deriving the view list for genetics-results-suite-4h6.13 (the sandbox schema-doc generator), which the ticket asked to verify rather than trust.

RE-DERIVED, not read off a doc:
- configs/datasets.yaml tables: = 15 views (yaml.safe_load, not a regex).
- genetics-results-db api/main.py VIEWS = the same 15. The queryable surface and the documented surface agree.
- genetics-results-db scripts/generate_resource_sql.py ALL_VIEWS = 11.

docs/adding-datasets.md:184 says 'The two metadata views - phenotypes_v and datasets_v - are deliberately **not** in ALL_VIEWS.' There are FOUR views outside ALL_VIEWS, not two: phenotypes_v, datasets_v, gene_annotations_v and variant_annotation_v. The doc's stated reason (they carry resource as a real column from the registry) may or may not be the reason the two annotation views are excluded - that needs checking against schemas/gene_annotations_v.sql and variant_annotation_v.sql before the sentence is rewritten, which is why this is a bead rather than a one-word fix.

WHY IT MATTERS: the sentence reads as an exhaustive account of the exclusions, and CLAUDE.md's documentation-ownership table names exactly this list as a rot risk. Someone adding a view and reasoning 'mine is not a metadata view, so it belongs in ALL_VIEWS' gets the wrong answer for an annotation view.

NOT FIXED IN 4h6.13 because it is unrelated to that task's change (which touched one column description) and the correct replacement wording needs the schema check above.

Files: docs/adding-datasets.md:182-188.

title: chat-backend allow-list does not accept oauth2-proxy's leading-dot subdomain form
description:
genetics_mcp_server/auth/core.py:_email_allowed handles exact domain match and a literal '*', mirroring what genetics-results-api does. oauth2-proxy additionally accepts a leading-dot form: --email-domain=.example.com matches any subdomain.

A deployment setting oauth_email_domain = '.example.com' would have oauth2-proxy admit u@sub.example.com through the gateway, and chat-backend would then 401 it - the two allow-lists diverge silently and the user sees a logged-in UI where every call fails.

Does NOT affect the current profile (finngen.fi, no leading dot), which is why th2 shipped without it. results-api has the same gap and should be fixed in the same pass so the two stay identical.

Files: genetics-mcp-server auth/core.py, genetics-results-api app/core/auth.py.

title: Drop the three 4h6.18 experiment tables once the swap lands
description:
Cleanup owed from genetics-results-suite-4h6.18's measurement phase, 2026-08-10.

Three experiment tables in phewas-development.genetics_results, ~27 GB logical each, all created with OPTIONS(description='EXPERIMENT genetics-results-suite-4h6.18 ... NOT LIVE. Safe to drop.'):
  credible_sets_exp_rdtp   resource, data_type, trait, pos
  credible_sets_exp_rdvp   resource, data_type, variant, pos
  credible_sets_exp_drvp   data_type, resource, variant, pos   <- the chosen key order

Do NOT drop drvp until the real swap has landed and been verified - it is the reference for confirming the production table came out with the same pruning behaviour. Drop rdtp and rdvp at any time.

Note setup_bigquery.sh auto-creates a table for every schemas/*.sql that is not *_v.sql, so these must never gain schema files.

title: Batched nits from the SDK HLA work
description:
Nits found during genetics-results-suite-4h6.25 and deliberately not fixed in-cycle, per the batching rule. None affects behaviour in a way a user or script would notice today.

1. executor.py:1462 echoes the RAW resource value, not the normalized one.
   sql_safety.normalize_literal's own docstring instructs callers that also use
   the value outside SQL to use the normalized form, 'so the raw one can still
   carry leading/trailing CR/LF that the allow-list never saw'. The sibling site
   at executor.py:1506 does gene = normalize_literal(gene, name='gene') before
   quoting, for exactly this reason.
   Verified reachable: resource='finngen\n' returns success=True and echoes
   'finngen\n'.
   NIT rather than substantive because this resource value only lands in a JSON
   payload field - unlike the gene case it is not used in a download filename or
   a Content-Disposition header, so there is no header-injection surface.
   Fix for uniformity: resource = normalize_literal(resource, name='resource')
   before quote_literal.

2. docs/project-spec.md - the new '40 of 44' sentence enumerates the same four
   tools that are already listed as deliberate exclusions about 60 lines further
   down at project-spec.md:332. Self-consistent, just redundant. Consider making
   the sentence point at that list rather than repeating it, so the two cannot
   drift apart.

3. docs/project-spec.md:386-389 - the _reject enumeration for SDK functions does
   not list hla()'s rejections (genes on allele=; min_mlogp/min_info/limit on
   phenotype=).

Explicitly NOT a defect, checked and dismissed: resource='finngen--' is accepted
since '-' is in the allow-list, but the '--' sits inside a literal whose quote
cannot be closed (the allow-list excludes the apostrophe), so it cannot start a
SQL comment.

Also worth folding in here: ruff format --check wants to reformat executor.py
entirely, but the diff is pre-existing whole-file drift (line-length rewraps,
slice spacing) - the file has never been ruff-formatted and the project gate is
ruff check, which passes. Decide whether to format it once deliberately rather
than letting each task trip over it.

title: No test proves URL path segments round-trip against a real ASGI server
description:
Coverage gap found during the re-review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.11 on 2026-08-07. The behaviour is CORRECT - this is about the suite not proving it.

Task .11 applied urllib.parse.quote(value, safe='') to 61 caller-controlled URL path segments in tools/executor.py. Since every identifier in this suite is colon-separated (variants are chr:pos:ref:alt, regions are chr:start-end), that encodes ':' as '%3A' on essentially every call.

The reviewer verified round-tripping empirically by standing up a real uvicorn + FastAPI server with routes mirroring the real signatures, and confirmed every realistic identifier survives byte-identically: variants with all four documented separators, regions, HLA-DRB1, MT-CO1, IGH@, Open_Targets_26.06, and values containing spaces, plus and percent. It also confirmed uvicorn unquotes scope['path'] before Starlette routing, that no route uses a path converter or custom regex, and that auth-gateway's proxy_pass has no URI part so nginx forwards the request URI verbatim.

But the SUITE only asserts containment: tests/test_bigquery_gene_tools.py:84 checks the URL still starts with the right prefix. Nothing asserts a positive round-trip for a colon-bearing identifier. So a future change to _seg(), to a route signature, or to the nginx proxy_pass could silently break every by-variant and by-region tool while the suite stays green.

FIX: add a test that runs a minimal ASGI app with the real route shapes and asserts the executor-built URL delivers the exact original value as the path parameter, for at least a variant with each of the four separators, a region, a gene symbol with punctuation, and a dotted dataset id.

title: SDK: int(limit_sql) re-parses a SQL token and would raise uncaught if a range floor is dropped
description:
Found in the re-review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.11 on 2026-08-07. LATENT - not reachable today. Filed rather than fixed in-cycle.

executor.py:974, 1130, 1203, 1294, 1364 each do:
    limit = int(limit_sql)

That silently assumes _token() returned a BARE integer string - which is exactly the assumption _token exists to break. sql_safety._token() parenthesises NEGATIVE values (e.g. '(-5)') so that a leading minus can never render as a SQL line comment in an expression like 'g.gstart - {window_sql}'.

Safe today only because every one of those five call sites passes minimum=1 to sql_int, so a negative can never be produced. If a future call site drops that floor, int('(-5)') raises ValueError - and the enclosing 'except SqlValueError' at executor.py:981 does NOT catch ValueError, so it escapes as an unhandled exception rather than the intended {'success': False, 'error': ...}.

Verified: int(sql_int(-5, name='x')) -> ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '(-5)'

FIX: stop round-tripping the value through its SQL rendering. Either keep the validated int the caller passed and use that for max_rows, or have sql_int return both the token and the number (the fix agent considered a (token, number) tuple and chose not to). Do not parse the SQL token back into a number.

title: analyze_conversations opens the live chat DB read-write on a shared RWO PVC
description:
Pre-existing, found reviewing genetics-results-suite-4h6.2/.3. NOT introduced by that work.

scripts/analyze_conversations.py load_data (~line 55) opens chat_history.db with a plain read-write sqlite3.connect, while load_instruction_set_names (~line 104) correctly uses a file:...?mode=ro URI.

The analyzer runs nightly as a CronJob against the LIVE chat_history.db on the chat-data ReadWriteOnce PVC, co-scheduled with chat-backend (podAffinity, because RWO). It only reads today, so nothing is wrong right now - but it is the one place where a future bug in the analyzer could write to the production conversation database, and it holds a write-capable handle while chat-backend is serving.

Fix: open read-only via file:...?mode=ro like the sibling function already does. One line, no behaviour change today, removes the class of accident entirely.

title: analyze_conversations: judge input sorts on created_at alone, so ties can invert a turn
description:
Found reviewing genetics-results-suite-4h6.2/.3, deliberately NOT fixed in-cycle.

_format_conversation_for_eval (scripts/analyze_conversations.py ~700-702) still does .sort('created_at') with no tiebreak. created_at has one-second resolution, so a user turn and its own reply can share a timestamp and be presented to the LLM judge in the wrong order.

.2/.3 added message_sort_keys() -> ['created_at', '_rowid'] and applied it to the export path, but deliberately did NOT apply it here, because changing judge INPUT changes judge OUTPUT and would warrant an ANALYZER_VERSION bump - forcing a full Opus-5 re-judge of every conversation at real API cost.

Fix: apply message_sort_keys in _format_conversation_for_eval AND bump ANALYZER_VERSION in the same change, so the re-judge is deliberate rather than a side effect. Worth batching with any other change that already requires a bump.

title: chat_turn_metrics: session_id is client-supplied and unvalidated
description:
Found by re-review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.1 on 2026-08-07. NOT blocking - filed rather than fixed in-cycle.

The user_id guard added in .1 stops user B overwriting user A's metrics row. But session_id on the same write path is still client-supplied and never checked for ownership, so:

1. B can INSERT new chat_turn_metrics rows tagged with A's session_id, poisoning per-session cost attribution.
2. delete_session's first DELETE clause is 'session_id = ?' with no user scope on the metrics rows themselves (it is gated on the ownership-scoped chat_sessions delete succeeding, so A must own the session - but any row carrying that session_id is removed regardless of who wrote it). Reproduced: B recorded a row with A's session id; A deleting that session deleted B's row.

Impact today is contained: get_turn_metrics has NO production caller (tests only), so nothing reads these rows yet. It becomes real the moment per-session cost aggregation ships - which is exactly what genetics-results-suite-4h6.23 (the benchmark) intends to do.

Requires the attacker to volunteer their own row, so this is telemetry pollution and self-inflicted loss, not disclosure.

Fix when a reader ships: scope the metrics DELETE by user_id as well as session_id, and validate on write that the session_id belongs to the authenticated user (or drop session_id from the write path and derive it at read time from message_id).

File: src/genetics_mcp_server/db/chat_history_db.py ~437-444 (delete) and the record_turn_metrics call path.

title: Doc-accuracy pass: batched nits from the sandbox security design review
description:
Batched wording/accuracy nits from both reviewers of genetics-results-suite-4h6.5. Deliberately NOT fixed in-cycle. Fix these together in one pass.

docs/code-execution-security.md:
- section 2 KSA row omits roles/artifactregistry.reader from the GSA role list (terraform/iam.tf:26). An enumeration that no longer matches the code is stale per CLAUDE.md.
- section 2 and 7 state the Workload Identity binding and its roles unconditionally; every one is count = var.manage_iam ? 1 : 0. The manage_iam=false deployment is precisely where the metadata-server default bites, so this needs a clause.
- 'its full 60-tool surface' (section 3) and 'the existing 60-tool surface' (6.2) hardcode a count in a repo whose CLAUDE.md says counts rot silently. Re-derive or drop.
- section 4 block quote is attributed to both docs/project-spec.md and main.py's require_auth docstring; it matches project-spec verbatim, the docstring wording differs. Attribute to project-spec, paraphrase the docstring.
- 'Every other pod uses serviceAccountName: genetics-suite' is true of the six backend deployments and the cronjobs only; frontend, bff, auth-gateway, oauth2-proxy and keycloak set none and run as default. Say 'every suite backend deployment'.
- sandbox_tools.py full path is src/genetics_mcp_server/skills/sandbox_tools.py, not tools/. Give it once on first mention.
- section 2 CPU row: 1500m against ~1930m allocatable on e2-standard-2 is not 'well under'. Reword.
- header scopes the doc to .6-.10 and .14 but the handoff table also binds .16 and section 1 assigns _validate_path reuse to .15. Align.
- e2-standard-2 + gvisor: confirm the runsc sentry memory overhead against a 3Gi limit and GKE Sandbox machine-type requirements before .10 relies on it.

Other repos:
- bead genetics-results-suite-4h6.15 names the wrong directory for sandbox_tools.py (tools/ instead of skills/). Fix the bead text.
- genetics-mcp-server/docs/project-spec.md:247 says the general tool category has 16 tools; the code has 18 (omits get_resource_metadata and get_dataset_display_names).
- scripts/check-doc-drift.sh was not updated for the new CLAUDE.md ownership row: sandbox/** is uncovered, and k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml matches only the generic ^k8s/ rule which never points at code-execution-security.md.

title: Backfill gene expression and gene-disease associations into BigQuery
description:
Two small backfills that close the remaining feasible data gaps.

gene_expression: GTEx v10 median TPM plus HPA IHC, two long TSVs referenced from genetics-results-api app/config/profiles/finngen/expression.py.
gene_disease: GenCC and Monarch, two TSVs from profiles/finngen/gene_disease.py.

Explicitly NOT backfilled, with reasons recorded in the docs: summary statistics (~10^11 rows in gs://finngen-production-library-green, buckets the suite does not own), LD (panel-computed, not tabular), rsID lookup and gnomAD sites (point tabix at ~0.3s beats the BigQuery job-submission floor, and the BFF needs them anyway).

Files: genetics-results-db schemas and loader scripts for gene_expression and gene_disease; api/main.py VIEWS allowlist; configs/datasets.yaml.

title: Apply the same stored-column and clustering fix to the other view-derived tables
description:
Repeat the credible_sets treatment for coloc_credsets, exome_variant_results and asm_qtl, whose views also derive variant and/or resource that the base tables do not cluster on.

Do this only after the credible_sets change has measured scan-byte improvement, so the approach is validated on one table before three more are migrated. gene_burden_results is ~343M rows - check whether it needs the same treatment and size the migration accordingly.

Files: genetics-results-db/schemas/ coloc_credsets, exome_variant_results and asm_qtl table plus view SQL; scripts/setup_bigquery.sh.

title: request.model is unvalidated against any allowlist
description:
Split out of genetics-results-suite-bq3, where it was noted as weaker and separate.

genetics-mcp-server: ChatRequest.model is client-supplied and passed through without checking it against any allowlist. This is a cost and scope question rather than a prompt-injection one: a caller can select a model the deployment did not intend to pay for, and provider is client-selectable too (OPENAI_API_KEY is wired into the pod).

Check what happens with an unknown model string - whether it 400s from the provider SDK or surfaces as an uncaught 500 - and decide between an allowlist and a documented pass-through.

title: _validate_latest_message does not bound assistant-role or replayed message length
description:
Found while fixing genetics-results-suite-uog. PRE-EXISTING, weaker than the bug it was found beside.

genetics-mcp-server chat_api.py:90 _validate_latest_message inspects only the newest role == 'user' message, so a client-sent ASSISTANT-role message is length-unbounded, as is any older user turn in replayed history.

The system-role variant of this gap is now closed - uog constrained ChatMessage.role to Literal['user','assistant'], so a system-role message cannot exist in the request at all and there is nothing unbounded for the check to miss.

What remains is a general request-size concern rather than an authority one: a forged assistant turn carries no system authority, and the Anthropic path's _sanitize_tool_blocks / _strip_tool_use_markers already touch those messages. Worth bounding total request size or per-message length regardless.
close_reason:
Fixed in genetics-mcp-server 904284f. Added _validate_request_size: total text across ALL messages (MAX_REQUEST_CHARS, default 2M) and message count (MAX_MESSAGES_PER_REQUEST, default 500), 413 before any model call.

Deliberately NOT the tighter rule of applying max_message_chars to every message: replayed tool results are routinely larger than any typed message, so that would reject ordinary long conversations. A test pins that a 40-turn conversation with 20KB tool results per turn still passes.

Inline image data is excluded from the text budget - images are bounded by max_attachments_per_message, and counting their base64 would reject ordinary image use. Test covers that too.

title: the OpenAI provider branch silently drops user instructions
description:
Found reviewing genetics-results-suite-s5y.8. Matches that task's stated Anthropic-only scope, so not a defect in it.

genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/llm_service.py:471 forwards user_instructions only to _stream_anthropic. The OpenAI branch ignores it with no log line.

Consequence: a user who has an instruction set selected and whose request routes to the OpenAI provider gets their instructions dropped invisibly - the UI shows a set applied, the model never sees it. The docstring does say Anthropic-only, but nothing surfaces it at runtime.

Options: implement the equivalent for the OpenAI path, or log once per turn when instructions are dropped, or surface it in the UI. At minimum it should not be silent.
close_reason: Fixed in genetics-mcp-server 904284f. Implemented rather than logged: the UI showed the set applied, so a log line would have left the user misinformed. _stream_openai now takes user_instructions and concatenates it after system_prompt into one system message - the two-block split exists to give each half its own prompt-cache breakpoint, which the OpenAI path has no equivalent for. Order matches Anthropic's. Six tests in TestOpenAIUserInstructions, including one pinning the DISPATCH (that is where the drop was, not in _stream_openai). Docs corrected: project-spec.md said the branch silently drops them.

title: INTERNAL_API_SECRET has four independent reads, two snapshotted at import
description:
Same defect class as genetics-results-suite-pol, different variable. Out of pol's stated scope.

genetics-mcp-server reads INTERNAL_API_SECRET in four places:
- auth/dependencies.py:13 — import-time snapshot
- routers/api_tokens.py:18 — import-time snapshot
- tools/executor.py:108 — live per call
- mcp_server.py:245 — live per call

The import-time snapshots run before load_dotenv() in some import orders, so a value set only in .env is silently ignored there. Fail-closed today: an empty secret skips the bearer branch and falls through to requiring the IAP header, so it is not a hole — but it is the same test trap pol removed, and the four reads can disagree.

Fix: add Settings.internal_api_secret and route all four through it.
close_reason:
Fixed in genetics-mcp-server 6bac696, documented in 14988a7. Added Settings.internal_api_secret and routed all four readers through it: auth/dependencies.py and routers/api_tokens.py (were import-time snapshots, module globals now gone rather than aliased), tools/executor.py and mcp_server.py (were live os.environ reads). Removed the now-dead 'import os' from the first two.

One trap found on the way: executor.py had a function-local 'from config.settings import get_settings' LATER in __init__ than the line I was changing, so referencing get_settings earlier in the same function would have raised UnboundLocalError at construction. Hoisted to a single local import + one settings instance at the top of __init__.

Coverage: nothing in tests/ referenced INTERNAL_API_SECRET at all, so the four could have disagreed silently. New tests/test_internal_api_secret.py covers all four consumers plus the fail-closed empty-secret behaviour; every case sets the env AFTER import, which is what a snapshot cannot see. Mutation-checked: reintroducing the module-global snapshot in dependencies.py fails test_auth_dependency_accepts_the_bearer_form.

Note /chat/v1/auth is @is_public and reports status rather than gating - it answers 200 whatever is presented. The gated route is /chat/v1/me; a test aimed at /auth would prove nothing.

title: batch: correct inaccurate comments and close small coverage gaps in the chat backend
description:
Batched doc/comment accuracy pass. All found during review of genetics-results-suite-y5d/do8/s5y.4/s5y.5/2cl/qdf/ni9/4um/pol, and deliberately deferred rather than fixed in-cycle.

COMMENTS THAT ASSERT SOMETHING UNTRUE (CLAUDE.md treats these as defects):
1. auth/dependencies.py:21-22 — claims importing get_settings per call means 'a reload of the config module does not leave this holding the pre-reload cache'. Measured false: after reloading config.settings the package __init__ keeps re-exporting the pre-reload function, so auth_is_required() returned the STALE value. It also contradicts tests/conftest.py:23-26, which describes the same asymmetry correctly.
2. docs/project-spec.md:718-720 — claims routing the gate through Settings 'also means it sees .env rather than only the real environment'. chat_api.py:25 calls load_dotenv() before importing the auth dependencies at line 31, and chat_api is the sole importer, so the old global already saw .env. The true statement is that a Settings instance cannot exist before config/settings.py's load_dotenv(), so the ordering hazard is now structurally impossible rather than merely untriggered.
3. docs/project-spec.md:~711 — says pol 'production never disagreed (nothing in src/ writes os.environ at runtime)'. The premise is true but the conclusion is not: the divergence came from import order vs load_dotenv(), so in a .env-driven dev/compose deployment with REQUIRE_AUTH=true the gate held False while /chat/v1/auth reported True. pol was a real dev-only divergence, not purely a test trap.
4. tests/conftest.py — settings_env's two-handle clear_all loop is a no-op duplicate today (the package and module get_settings are the same object). The sibling clear_settings_cache fixture documents this; settings_env does not.

COVERAGE GAPS:
5. Nothing guards the ni9 invariant. TestAdminFeedbackPaginationStability would still pass under a half-move (dialog items would sort consistently above session items, so the key stays total and pagination stable). Add an assertion that both sources' created_at isoformat strings have the same shape, or an explicit cross-source same-second tie order assertion.
6. test_the_reported_is_admin_matches_the_gate_on_the_admin_endpoints omits the unauthenticated rows (REQUIRE_AUTH=true/no user -> 401; false/no user -> 200). Both verified correct by hand; two more parametrize rows would pin them.
notes:
FROM .7/.8 REVIEW:

title: admin feedback timestamps gained a +00:00 suffix — check the browser admin UI
description:
Consequence of genetics-results-suite-ni9 (commit 47c59ca). NOT a defect, but user-visible and unverified on the client.

GET /chat/v1/admin/feedback now emits created_at and latest_at with a +00:00 suffix where session_comment items previously had none. The values were always UTC; only the rendering changed.

Risk: the JS Date constructor parses a bare 'T12:00:00' as LOCAL time and the offset form as UTC, so admin-UI feedback times will shift by the viewer's offset. That is a correction, but it is visible.

Check genetics-results-browser/src/features/admin/adminApi.ts:201, which consumes latest_at - confirm it is not string-compared against a stored value, since a format change would fire one spurious 'new feedback' signal on first load after deploy.
close_reason:
Verified, no client change needed. genetics-mcp-server 96adba3 adds the guard.

The bead's stated risk does not exist: latest_at is consumed only by AdminPage's feedbackLabel via formatRelativeTime, never string-compared against a stored value and never persisted, so there is no spurious 'new feedback' signal on first load after deploy.

Rendering: adminApi maps created_at straight to new Date(...).toLocaleDateString/String. With the +00:00 suffix JS parses as UTC and renders local, which is CORRECT; the bare form was parsed as local, i.e. UTC values were being shown as if local. The change is a fix and the only visible effect is the shift the bead predicted.

Confirmed both feedback sources now emit the same shape, and added the guard uvh item 5 asked for - a half-move would have kept the existing pagination tests green because every offset-bearing string sorts above every bare one. Mutation-checked with .replace(tzinfo=None) on one source.

title: REQUIRE_AUTH has two sources of truth in the chat backend
description:
Found while fixing genetics-results-suite-8r4. PRE-EXISTING, not a production bug, but a live test trap.

genetics-mcp-server reads REQUIRE_AUTH twice:
- src/genetics_mcp_server/auth/dependencies.py:14 snapshots it at IMPORT time into the module global _require_auth, used by auth_required and admin_required.
- src/genetics_mcp_server/chat_api.py:260 re-reads os.environ['REQUIRE_AUTH'] per request.

Safe in production: nothing in src/ writes os.environ at runtime (verified — no assignment, setdefault, putenv or update anywhere), and in k8s the value is fixed for the process lifetime, so the two always agree.

The problem is in tests: patch('...dependencies._require_auth', True) moves one and not the other, while patch.dict(os.environ, {'REQUIRE_AUTH': 'true'}) moves the other and not the one. So /chat/v1/auth's is_admin can disagree with admin_required's gate under test — exactly the class of test-isolation trap 8r4 was about.

Fix: route both through settings rather than reading os.environ in two places.

Also worth knowing: seeds quoted in bug reports are only meaningful while pytest-randomly stays pinned at the version 8r4 set. Bumping it resets that history.
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit 47c59ca (batched — three small fixes in one repo, one cycle). Suite 850 passed / 74 deselected, green on seeds 12345 and 20260804. Review APPROVED; blind validation of the auth change returned no blocking issues and confirmed via a full six-combination security matrix that nothing reaches an endpoint it could not before.

Notable: the blind validator reproduced that the OLD pol code had a real hole — with the gate pinned to an import-time False and the live value true, a non-admin got 200 on /chat/v1/admin/sessions. Under the new code the same request is 403.

Also corrected during implementation: an earlier reviewer's claim that making the comment reads timezone-aware would leave the admin feed's merge order identical. It would not — admin.py sorts isoformat STRINGS, and a naive stamp renders 19 chars against an aware 25, so a naive string is a prefix of an aware one and a same-second cross-source tie is settled by the suffix before (source, id) is reached. Both halves of the feed were moved together to preserve the qdf guarantee.

Nits filed rather than fixed in-cycle: see the batched comment-accuracy bead, the admin-UI timestamp bead, and the INTERNAL_API_SECRET bead.

title: llm_config_db: comment/session-comment reads still crash on a malformed timestamp
